“Inwardly clinging to the Annihilation View” (In the mind, truly holding the Annihilation View): In the mind, holding on to the mentality of the Annihilation View, that is, the doctrine of Emptiness without being thorough, it becomes the View of Obliteration. The Emptiness in Prajna is not empty like nothingness, it is not the End of Views! “False self-titled Mahayana” (Irrelevant, claiming to be Mahayana): Those who study Mahayana dharma, think that all dharmas are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, like dew, like lightning, regarding eating meat, drinking alcohol, getting married, getting married, claiming that there is no problem, I am Mahayana, not entangled, not attached, [no need to follow the precepts anymore]. Is it okay to eat meat and drink alcohol? This body is entangled, that's an example. In his mind, that person holds the thought of Doan Kien, still saying that he is Mahayana. "Not protecting the three sinful karmas, destroying the true Dharma" (Not preventing sins in the three karmas, disrupting our true Dharma): For the three karmas of body, speech, and mind, the Ten Evil Karmas, not preventing them at all, creating the Ten Evil Karmas, destroying the Dharma. After that person dies, he will definitely fall into the Uninterrupted Hell.

“Try to contemplate the basis theory, the object is not a fake weapon” (So you must observe the basis when speaking the Dharma, don't talk to someone who is not a Dharma device): Regarding the Mahayana Dharma, you must consider whether that person is a Dharma device or not, you must contemplate the mechanism! When we speak the Dharma, we cannot contemplate the foundation. We do not know what good roots that person has created several hundred years or many eons ago. We cannot contemplate the foundation. How to do this? First of all, we must repent. First, visualize that this is Śākyamuni Buddha speaking, it is the Buddha speaking, not me speaking. Every time you dedicate and repent of your sins, you must add one thing: "If you preach the Dharma, the Buddha will bless you. It is the Buddha who speaks, not you." You must definitely contemplate. Then, repent for your sins, what sins are you repenting of? If one speaks wrongly, one does not gain any benefits, but after listening to the Dharma but still cannot be liberated, that means one is guilty.

The speaker is guilty, it has nothing to do with the listener.

“ Arrogant, uncompassionate, cruel, vile” (Arrogant, uncompassionate; cruel, vile): Very arrogant, without compassion. Preaching the Dharma must be filled with compassion. The purpose of preaching the Dharma is to help others achieve liberation, to let others hear it and become enlightened, at least to plant good roots, it must be complete! If you are arrogant and do not have compassion, that is contempt for living beings and low ambition. Therefore, a wise person should know, what is holding on to Duan Kien, and how is it to hold on to Duan Kien?

“Arrogant, uncompassionate, cruel and even inferior, wise people are aware of it, slandering the Duan Kien, non-Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha, non-Great Vehicle, slandering Buddhas, bound to fall into the Infinite Hell” (Arrogant, uncompassionate, cruel, vile, wise people should be know, the person who holds the Complete View is not a Sravaka or a Pratyekabuddha, nor is he a Mahayana Dharma instrument. That person flatters and slanders the Buddhas and will surely fall into the Unbroken Hell): You are neither a Sravaka, a Pratyekabuddha, nor a Mahayana, neither of the three vehicles! Just a person who flatters the evil king, flatters the great ministers, and slanders the Buddhadharma will surely fall into the Hell of No Interruptions. There are officials who in their hearts do not want to slander the Mahayana, but because of the forces of evil, the evil kings oppress and order them, making it impossible for them not to do so. They do so for their own benefit and peace in the present life, while slandering and denouncing others. Because you only think about benefits, for the sake of profit, that crime becomes serious!

“Upholding the precepts mocks the noise, defies the dharma, avoids suffering and evil, the wise man is like a willow, named Thanh Van Thua” [meaning]: That person who wants to maintain the precepts must go to a pure place, a quiet place, and dare not stay in urban areas. If one is noisy, that person is afraid that keeping the precepts will not be successful, opening his eyes will also violate the precepts, hearing evil music with his ears, watching TV will violate the precepts, everywhere will be a transgression! How to do this? Go to a place where there is no trace of humans, away from the noise. “Forgive the Dharma, fear suffering and evil” (Regret the Dharma, fear suffering and evil): That person refuses to preach the Dharma, what is he afraid of? Fear of being infected by others, fear of preaching the Dharma and suffering. “Wise people can accept the willow” (Wise people should know clearly): People with wisdom will know Thanh Van is like that!

“ Mocking almsgiving, contemplating birth and death, often enjoying the single-minded state of tranquility, the wise person accepts it, is known as the Single Enlightenment Vehicle” (Likes giving alms, contemplates birth and death. Often likes to be alone in a quiet place. Wise people should know. That is called the Single Enlightened Vehicle): The Single Enlightened Vehicle also likes to give alms, contemplates the dharma of birth and death, All dharmas are impermanent, contemplating birth and death is contemplating causes and conditions; but they also like to practice alone. Why is it called Doc Giac? Sitting quietly alone is called the Single Sense Vehicle. “Complete with all good roots, protect the original compassion” (Complete with all good roots, protect the root of compassion): That is the mind of great compassion, protecting compassion. “Often mocks taking advantage of things, claiming the name Mahayana” (Often likes to receive, benefit sentient beings, that is called Mahayana): Always joyfully accept sentient beings, using the Four Dharmas of Reception to benefit sentient beings. “Sacrifice your life and life to protect the precepts, without harming sentient beings” (If you give up your life and life to protect the precepts, and do not care about harming sentient beings): It is better to give up your life and life to protect and uphold the Buddha's forbidden precepts. “Diligently seeking the Emptiness Dharma, understanding the Mahayana” (Diligence seeking the Emptiness Dharma, one should know that it is the Mahayana): Seeking Prajna wisdom, since all conditioned dharmas cannot be Emptied, one practices the unconditioned Dharma, completely without harming sentient beings.

“The mind is patient with all dharmas, good speech has no secrets, the dharma is often mocked, it accepts the Mahayana” (The mind is patient with all dharmas, does not hold back good words, often enjoys all dharmas, should be known as Mahayana): The mind is patient, “forbearance” means “admit”, all dharmas are good. Bodhisattva does not abandon even worldly dharma. Without worldly dharma, there is also no Buddha dharma. Why do we often use worldly dharma as an example when preaching Dharma? If the Dharma is beyond the world, sentient beings will not be able to enter it. So tell them the Dharma of the world, sentient beings will understand the Dharma of the world, use the Dharma to reveal the Dharma that is beyond the world, then they will be able to enter! Don't be stingy. The Dharma has no secrets, saying that the Buddha Dharma is a secret is wrong. The Buddhadharma has no secrets, there is no dharma that cannot be told to sentient beings, but everything can be said; But if the base is not right, then for this sentient being it is Secret, for other sentient beings it will be Manifest. Secret is Show, Show is Secret, you must understand this principle. In all the teachings spoken by the Buddha, a mind of faith and joy must always arise. That is Mahayana.

“ Dharma tools, non-dharma tools, benefit the mind equally” (Equality of mind benefits both dharma tools and non-dharma tools): Not because it is a dharma tool, or not a dharma tool, intelligent people with wise great disciples are extremely happy, but for stupid and confused disciples, they feel hatred and even contempt. usually. That is not a Bodhisattva. Dharma objects are the same, they are of equal benefit to them, and non-dharma objects are also equally beneficial to them. Equality of mind to benefit sentient beings. “Untainted by worldly dharmas” (Untainted by worldly dharmas): Although not contaminated with worldly dharmas, it is said that Bodhisattvas do all merit but have no merit. Why is there no merit? They do not immerse themselves in the appearance of merit. That is Mahayana.

“A wise person, universally speaking of the three vehicles, without worrying about the monkhood, will quickly attain Supreme Enlightenment” (Therefore, a wise person will respectfully speak all three vehicles, without harming my Sangha disciples, quickly attain Supreme Enlightenment): Don't harm my disciples, don't harm the monks who destroy them. world!

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! Those who are truly good at the Kshatriya, the true Brahman, the true official, the true layperson, the true elder, the true monk, the true Vaisya, the true Thudatta, the weak male, the weak female, achieve the ten races of the Wheel of Virtue and Virtue. If you appear in the body, you can quickly feed on the Sravakayana seed, your spirit will not retreat, or you can manifest into the Sravakayana saints, non-Practice Enlightenment, Mahayana holy weapons. Ha class vi ten? One person, one has pure faith, one must necessarily have good and evil karma. The second person, the old man is self-sufficient and noble, far away from all evil friends and evil views. The three monks, abide in the rules of discipline, stay away from killing, and indulge in alcohol. Four, stay calm Inkindness in the mind, far away from all anger and anger. The five beings, abiding in compassion, save all weak sentient beings. Six people, stay in the happy mind, stay away from all negative karma. Seven people, stay calm and let go, abandon all greed and jealousy. The eight false ones, specifically take refuge, far away from all attachments to evil and evil, and do not take refuge in evil spirits or pagans. The nine practitioners are diligent, steadfast, and courageous in cultivating good dharmas. Ten people, often mocking tranquility, seeking Dharma meaning, rejoice in all things.
Brahman, the true good official, the true layman, the true elder, the true monk, the true Vaisya, the true Thu-datta, whether male or female, who achieves the ten types of Virtue and Virtue Wheel, will be able to quickly plant in their present body the seed of the Thanh Van Vehicle without retreating, or in their present body, they will become the dharma weapon of the status of saints in the Thanh Van Vehicle, not the dharma weapon of the Single Sense Vehicle and the Mahayana ten? is to be completely pure in faith, to believe in all good and evil karma. Two is to be completely away from all evil friends and evil views. Third is to stay away from killing, even to drink alcohol. Four is to stay away from all anger and anger. Five is to stay away from all weak sentient beings. Six is to stay away from all negative karma Seven is to stay calm and let go of all greed, jealousy, and hatred. Eight is to have true refuge, to stay away from all attachments to evil and false thoughts, and not to take refuge in evil spirits or heretics. Nine is to be diligent, steadfast, and courageous in cultivating good dharmas.

Vo Y Hanh Luan has ten dishes, Huu Y Hanh Luan also has ten dishes. In the present life, it is possible to quickly plant the seed of the Sravaka Vehicle, so that the seed does not retreat, or in the present life, one can achieve the dharma weapon of the saints in the Sravaka Vehicle. The main saint statuses are First Fruition, Second Fruition, Third Fruition, and Four Fruition, [but that person] is not the dharma weapon for the saint statuses in the Single-Buddha Vehicle and the Mahayana, nor is it the dharma weapon of the Single-Buddha Vehicle!

“What are the ten? What are the ten? One is complete and pure faith), that is, believing in good and evil cause and effect. “Second person, the first person is self-sufficient” (Second is complete shame): Often feel that oneself is not enough, [that is] not enough practice, not enough listening to the Dharma, not enough wisdom. You must stay away from evil beings and evil views. "Third, abide in the law of ritual" (Third is to abide in the law of ritual): "Abide in the law of ritual" is to stay away from killing, up to and including drinking alcohol. At least stay in the Three Refuges and Five Precepts.

great compassion. “Compassion” is the wish to eliminate all the suffering of sentient beings. Seeing them suffer is our own suffering, which is also a kind of “replacement” mind, which means wishing for them to suffer. In the dedication vow of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva's ten great vows, [Bodhisattva] vowed to endure all sufferings for sentient beings, causing them to be liberated. That is the Bodhisattva's great compassion, far from all anger, resentment, and harm. Tieu Thua only needs himself to be free from anger, anger, and harm to living beings. It's okay to be kind like that! But now these ten good wheels are the Avalokiteshvara (have a place to rely on to give rise to good roots and merit), called the Avalokiteshvara. The Wheel of Medicine is based on the Ten Wheels, all three vehicles are present, depending on what mind you use. The Mahayana mind will believe in Mahayana and have great compassion. Nhi Thua's compassion is not as vast.

“Five, abiding in compassion” (Five is abiding in compassion): Saving weak sentient beings.

“Six, abide in the heart of joy” (Six is ​​to abide in the heart of joy): Stay away from all four evil karma in food and speech. When speaking, don't lie, don't deceive others, don't speak harshly and hurt others. The ancients said: “A good word makes the listener feel warm even though the weather is cold): Hearing a good word makes the heart feel very refreshed, very comforted, very warm. “Evil words of six-month-cold merchants” (Evil words hurt the listener, making them feel cold even though it is June): June is so hot, one of your words hurts people like pouring a bucket of ice water on their head, it's cold, it will hurt them, that's what it means! This is specifically talking about speech karma in the ten evil karmas. Don't gossip or say useless words to others. Things like bad language, or performing General Thanh[7] have created a lot of karma.

“Seven false, abiding in a mind of equanimity” (Seven is abiding in a mind of equanimity): Often there is a mind of renunciation. That mind of renunciation is the mind of renunciation of the world. If it is Mahayana, then it is renunciation of the Second Vehicle, but ["disengagement" as the main scriptures say is] separation from all stinginess, greed, and jealousy. These things are all said according to the Second Vehicle.

“The eight false refuges, the correct refuge” (Eight is the true refuge): Taking refuge in the Buddha, taking refuge in the Dharma, taking refuge in the Sangha is the “right refuge”. Stay away from all attachments to good, bad, evil, and do not take refuge in evil spirits or pagans.

“Nine, fully diligent, steadfast, courageous, cultivating good dharmas” (Nine is fully diligent, steadfast, brave, cultivating good dharmas): Regarding the Ten Good Karmas, we say one thing without saying bad words. You should never say bad words, that is, say words of praise and maintain a good conduct. Not just in one life, but in countless lives, all maintain the same virtue.

“Ten, often mocking tranquility, seeking the meaning of the Dharma” (Ten is often fond of tranquility, thinking, searching for the meaning of the Dharma): Often prefers tranquility; Here it is a quiet mind, not a request for a quiet environment. [Just seeking] a quiet environment is still not enough? Do you want to stay in the mountains for peace and quiet? The mountain is still not quiet! A person cultivating the Way in a grass hut in the mountains and forests, while entering Concentration, his mind is very calm. Small birds outside chirping and chattering, that person gives rise to the evil thought: "In the future I will turn into a bald eagle that will eat those birds." His merit is completely redirected. One angry thought arises, evil thoughts arise, hundreds of thousands of barrier doors open, that person immediately falls, turns into a bald eagle, specializing in eating small birds. Is it a crime to stay in the mountains or forests? Very important concept!

(Sutra) Good man! The weak one is the true good King of the Sat-de-li king, the one with the true good will is the Thu-atta-la-class, the weak male, the weak female, so the ten races of All-Yeared Hanh Luan, appearing in the middle body, can quickly feed on the Sravakas, the spirit never retreats.
Animals, etc., whether male or female, who have accomplished these ten types of Virtue and Virtue, can quickly sow in their present body

seeds of Shravakayana, causing no retreat).

That Sravakayana nature has not been withdrawn, and can also attain all the holy dharmas of the Sravakayana in the present life. These ten types of Medical Wheels are said according to the Shravaka Vehicle. Just now [in the main sutra] there were a few direct statements about the dharma weapon belonging to the saints (status of saints) in the Shravaka Vehicle, which is not the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle, not the attainment of the Mahayana dharma, [because, due to the ten Wheels of Medicine above, it will] not be possible to attain [the Mahayana dharma], nor can the [practitioner] become the dharma weapon of the Single-Buddha Vehicle and the Mahayana.

(Sutra) Or the incarnation, witness the Shravakayana possessing the holy dharma, become the Shravakayana's holy dharma weapons, non-realization Single Enlightenment, the Mahayana holy dharma, will not become Single Enlightenment, the Mahayana holy weapon. Seeking to know the test of Doc Giac, Mahayana, the stage is like the theory. Good man! Such as the ten races of Yāṇāhāna, necessarily Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, Tathagata Buddhas, all living together.
Saints belonging to the Sravaka Vehicle, do not attain the holy Dharma of Pratyekabuddha or Mahayana, it is not a dharma weapon for saints of Pratyekabuddha or Mahayana. You should know that for Pratyekabuddhas and Mahayana people, it is said like this, O good man! Such sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Tathagata Buddhas all have the same ten types.

The meaning of this passage is absolutely not a correspondence with Shravakayana.

(Sutra) Good man! Resurrection of the ten races of Bodhisattva and Tathagata, non-Sravaka, Solitary Enlightenment, Bodhisattva, Tathagata, in the same community. The weak one has the true goodness of the Sat-de-li king, the one with the true good will of the Beast-atta-la class, the weak male, the weak female, thus forming the ten races of All-Yeared and Virtuous Wheels, appearing in the body, quickly feeding on the Single-Enlightenment seed, the spirit never retreats. Or incarnate, attain the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle, possess the holy dharma, and become the Single-Enlightened Vehicle of the holy dharma weapons. Ha class vi ten? One, practice to purify body, speech, and mind. The second person, the old man, is self-sufficient and noble. The three hypocrites, the Five Aggregates, are deeply born of fear. The four false beings, seeing birth and death, are extremely difficult. Five people, often mocking tranquility, stay away from the chaos. The six people mocked Ah Luyen Nha and lost their lives. The Seven, protect the senses, the mind is always calm. The eight falsehoods, virtuously contemplate dependent origination, examine cause and effect. Nine scholars often mock the need to practice Dang Tri and Tinh Lu. The ten practitioners should practice to initiate the dharma and be good enough to eliminate it.
Enlightenment, Bodhisattva, Tathagata are all in common. If there is a truly good Kshatriya king, even a truly good Thudatta, etc., whether male or female, who achieves these ten types of Virtue and Virtue, they will be able to quickly plant the seed of the Single-Enlightened Vehicle, so that they will not retreat. Or in the present body, they will realize all the holy dharmas of the Single-Enlightened Vehicle and become the holy objects of the Single-Enlightened Vehicle mười? Một là tu hành thân, ngữ, ý nghiệp thanh tịnh. Hai là trọn đủ hổ thẹn, chán nhàm thân mình. Ba là sanh lòng sợ hãi sâu xa đối với Ngũ Thủ Uẩn. Bốn là thấy sông sanh tử tột bậc khó vượt. Năm là thường thích tịch tĩnh, lìa các ồn náo. Sáu là thích A Luyện Nhã, chẳng chê bai lỗi lầm của người khác. Bảy là thủ hộ các căn, tâm thường tịch định. Tám là khéo quán duyên khởi, xét kỹ nhân quả. Chín là thường Like to diligently practice Dharma Tri and Tinh Lu. Ten is to deal with the dharmas that gather and arise, and can be skillfully eliminated).

The previous part talks about the ten types of Friendship and Virtue of Shravakayana; Next, [in this section] we talk about the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. Huu Y Hanh Luan in this section specializes in Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas, the heavenly Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas, different from Arhats. The ten wheels in the previous section (the wheels are discussed in the second chapter), Mahayana Bodhisattva and Pratyekabuddha are complete. There are also ten types of the Wheel of Virtue and Virtue that the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, Bodhisattva, and Tathagata all complete together. If there is a king who is a good person and also seeks the dharma of liberation, up to the lowest seed of nature (Animal-dala) among the four types of seed, whether male or female, if he can achieve these ten types of wheel, then in his current life, he can cultivate the seed of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle so that he will not retreat, but also rely on the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle to enter the Dharma and attain enlightenment. That is the Middle Vehicle.

Sravakayana is Hinayana, Bodhisattva is Mahayana; Either in the present life, that person can attain it, or he may not attain it in the present life, but in the future he will also attain it. If you sow the seed, you will become a dharma weapon for a saint in the Single Sense Vehicle, [a dharma weapon] is also a tool to hold the dharma. “What are the ten?” (What are the ten?): What are the ten types of wheels?

“The one who practices pure body, speech, and mind karma” (One is to practice pure body, speech, and mind karma): Body karma is to have no acts of killing, stealing, or lust. Linguistic karma means not having the behavior of "lying, embellishing, double-talking, or speaking harshly". Thoughts do not give rise to greed, anger, or ignorance. This is called “purity of body, speech, and mind”.

“Second, full of self-respect, full of self-pity” (Second, full of shame, disgust with self): Always feel that you are very far from the holy path, unable to be pure, unable to free yourself from the afflictions of the world, bored with your own body and mind. That person is bored with his own body and mind, not caring about where he eats, dresses, or behaves.

“The Three False Aggregates, the Five Aggregates of Attachment, deeply give birth to fear” (The third is the deep fear of the Five Aggregates): Form, Feeling, Perception, Actions, Consciousness, these are called the Five Aggregates of Attachment. Because of those five types, people will hold on to evil and not do good. As for Form Dharma, that is, for all forms and forms, one is greedy for it. The mind dharma is Feeling, Perception, Action, Consciousness, these four dharmas all belong to the mind dharma. This is the third Huu Y Luan.

“Four falsehoods, view of birth and death, extremely difficult” (Fourth is seeing the river of birth and death, extremely difficult to cross): When that person relies on this fourth type to observe, [realizes] the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death is very difficult to overcome. It's like we're floating in the river of birth and death, dying here, being born there, being dead and then being born again, being born and then dying again. If immortal, there will be no birth; If not born, will be immortal. That sea of birth and death is very difficult to cross, you will be immersed in the sea of birth and death!

“Five people, often ridicule tranquility, stay away from chaos” (Fifth is often like tranquility, far from noise): That person often wishes for tranquility, mind away from noise and bustle, in the world but wants to find the mountains and forests, find a place of leisure.

“ Six people, mocking A Luyen Nha, will never lose anything” (Six is ​​liking A Luyen Nha's place, not criticizing other people's mistakes): Because he opposes noise, he longs for A Luyen Nha (A Lan Nha), which is a quiet place. Therefore, regarding the mistakes of others, that person does not criticize, slander, or sting others!

“The seven, protect the senses, the mind is always calm” (Seven is to preserve and protect the senses, the mind is always calm): Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, must always be carefully guarded, don't make mistakes. The mind always abides in silence, in Concentration, neither fluttering nor drowsiness.

“The eight are good at contemplating dependent origination, examining cause and effect” (Eight is skillful in contemplating dependent origination, carefully examining cause and effect): Starting to practice like that, skillfully observing the dependent origination of all dharmas, but this person is a Single Enlightenment, born at a time when there is no Buddha in the world, is a Single Enlightened One. When a Buddha appears in the world, this person is called Pratyekabuddha, relying on the twelve causes and conditions to contemplate the dharma of the twelve causes and conditions, contemplating their arising and passing away. Why do we have four seasons in a year? Why do trees grow in Spring, grow in Summer, shrink in Autumn, and hide in Winter? Contemplate those conditions that arise. Why can they grow and develop? Why did they disappear? Contemplate all cause and effect retributions in human life, retribution for good and evil, cause and effect. What cause results in what result? If we sow good causes, we will definitely reap good results. If you sow evil, you will absolutely suffer retribution. Observe why this person is so miserable? Why did that person have such good blessings? [Saying] “why” implies observation. Look at what that person has done, has accomplished; That can only be said in the present life. A single-sensed person entering Samadhi in the mountain can see eighty thousand great kalpas, how many events there are in ten thousand years, ten thousand koṭi years. From the Concentration, He can see clearly what that person has done in many lifetimes; But he has one flaw: he doesn't save sentient beings and doesn't tell others!

“Nine people often mock the need to cultivate, Dang Tri, Tinh Lu” (Nine is often fond of diligently cultivating Dang Tri, Tinh Lu): Tinh Lu is Concentration, that person can maintain it equally, causing Concentration not to be lost. There are many types of Concentration. A person's Concentration is Equanimity, such as cultivating the Seven Factors of Enlightenment, the Eightfold Path, the Five Faculties, the Five Strengths, the Four Right Efforts, and the Four Fulfillments of the Mind, so one always diligently [practices], without slacking off!

“The ten, practice starting the dharma, good and eliminate it”: “Train” means “gathering”. When the Single Enlightened One cultivates the path, from within his body and mind, various causes arise. As for the causes, He can destroy them and eliminate them. Evil people must definitely disappear, good people must be made to grow.

(Sutra) Good man! The weak one is truly good, the King of Sat-tara, the one who is truly good, the Beast-atta-la class, the weak male, the weak female, thus forming the ten races of Virtuous Medicine and Virtue. If you appear in the body, you will be able to quickly feed on the seed of the Single Sense Vehicle, your spirit will not retreat, or if you appear, you will attain the Single Sense Vehicle and possess the holy dharma, becoming a Single Sense Vehicle with all the holy dharma weapons. Good man! Thiet Thiet Thanh Van, Doc Giac Huu Y Hanh Luan. Necessarily Thanh Van, reaching the Single Enlightenment, he only tries the wheel, the speed surpasses the three great oceans, the speed of beast enters the Prajnaparamita city.
Thu-datta, etc., whether male or female, who achieves these ten types of Virtue and Virtue Wheel, will be able to quickly realize all the holy dharmas of the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle, and become the dharma weapon for the saints in the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle. This is called the Wheel of Virtue and Virtue of All Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, and will be able to quickly escape the ocean of the three existences. quickly enter the citadel of Bat Nirvana).

“Good man” is the name Buddha used to call Vajragarbha Bodhisattva. This Dharma was requested by Vajragarbha Bodhisattva. If there is a good king, up to four types of good nature, regardless of whether the person is male or female, if he achieves these ten types of Virtue Wheel of Being, while he practices, or in life, can destroy his karma and Or (defilements), can cultivate the seed of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, causing that nature not to be lost, in this life he has not achieved the path and fruition of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, then in the future, he will be able to attain it. Either in this life, one can become the dharma weapon of the saintly positions, or one can attain [those positions] in this life.

“Good man! The name of the Sravakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, the Pratyekabuddhas and the Pratyekabuddhas” (Hey good man! That is called the Pratyekabuddhas and Pratyekabuddhas of all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas): All Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, following this instruction, will be able to quickly cross the ocean of the Three Realms (three worlds), can quickly quickly enter Bat Nirvana, that is, can reach the state of birthlessness, immortality, and attain Nirvana. That Nirvana is not ultimate, it is not the Buddha's ultimate Nirvana, so there is a difference!

(Kinh) Good man! Huu Y Hanh Luan Thi Ha's meaning? Words have false clothes, names have attachments, egos have clothes, things have feelings, things have attachment. The conduct of the Aggregates of Conduct, the Conduct of Precepts, the Origin of Conduct, and the Subsequent Relations of Conduct. Wheel of teachings, wheel of teachings. Like the Chakravarti of the Chakravarti, or the practice wheel. Such as Thanh Van and Doc Giac, he only tries the wheel and seeks Nirvana. Try to try the two types of Mahayana energy. The reason why it's fake? Because the medicine only lowers the behavior, not the Mahayana energy. Because of clinging to the Aggregates of Conduct, fear, suffering, self-seeking liberation is necessarily suffering, not seeking liberation necessarily sentient beings practice hard, not Mahayana energy. Because the medicine refers to the precepts, precepts, sutras, and eunuchs, those who seek liberation must necessarily suffer from suffering, but those who do not seek liberation must necessarily practice with effort, without Mahayana energy. Because of accepting the teachings of the Dharma Places, sutras, and eunuchs, those who seek liberation must necessarily suffer from suffering, but those who do not seek liberation must necessarily practice with effort, without Mahayana energy. Because the biological system belongs to the living system, all sentient beings, do not mock and receive, non-existent compassion, the living system belongs to the fixed system, not the Mahayana energy. Due to the constant contemplation of others and the sufferings of others, letting go and not being able to save them, one tries to seek liberation on one's own, without the Mahayana energy. By using the word to cut off all attachments of afflictions, without mocking all sentient beings, all afflictions are eliminated, without Mahayana energy. Due to the inability to control the Mahayana wheel, the Bodhi beast tries to escape the Mahayana energy. Due to the inability to rely on the great light wheel of the Bodhi beast, the Mahayana energy is lost. Because of the joy and mockery of the only non-traveler, he entered Nirvana and became a child, practicing and practicing without Mahayana energy.
(Sutra: Hey good man! What is the meaning of Huu Y Hanh Luan? When you say Huu Y, it's called Huu Y. There is something to hold on to, something to rely on, there is a system to follow. The conduct is the Aggregate of Conduct, the Virtue of Virtue, the Chain of Virtue, the cycle of "teaching and teaching", like the wheel (Luan Bao) mounted by the King of Wheels, or the wheel of action (the wheel of action). This kind of [energy] is not a Mahayana energy. Because they only practice lowly, it is not a Mahayana energy. Because they hold on to their own Aggregates of Conduct and are afraid, disgusted, seek to liberate all suffering, and do not practice, they are not a Mahayana energy. If they practice to liberate all sentient beings, it is not a Mahayana spirit. Because they accept their own Paths of Conduct and are afraid, disgusted, seek to liberate all suffering, and do not practice to liberate all sentient beings, it is not a Mahayana spirit. Because they are bound and dependent on the Attachment of Beings, they do not like to receive and do not have compassion for sentient beings, because they have attachments. Because they contemplate others suffering all kinds of things and ignore them, just to seek liberation for themselves, they are not the Mahayana energy. Because they do not want to eliminate the oligarchic afflictions for all sentient beings, they are not the Mahayana energy It is not a Mahayana spirit. Because they enjoy being alone, without friends, entering Nirvana to practice, so it is not a Mahayana spirit).

“Good man! Huu Y Hanh Luan is the synonym?” (Hey good man! Huu Y Hanh Luan is the synonym[8]?): What is the meaning of that linguistic nomenclature? Which? “The language of Huu Y fake” (Speaking of Huu Y): Regarding the term Huu Y Hanh Luan, first talk about Huu Y. What is Huu Y? It is “attachment” , that is, attachment to taking or giving up. First there must be a Self, then there is a dharma for us to rely on, that is, the scene. Any dharma that is good is accepted (captured, held), “there is something that is accepted, there is something that is dependent on” (there is something that is accepted, there is something that is bound, dependent). That is called Huu Y. What is Huu Y? Depending on that person's attachment and holding, there will be a Self (ie the Self to be the subject of the holding action). Whenever there is a Self, there is a Self (what belongs to us), a Self is also called a Self. For example, our lives are not separate from dressing, living, and traveling. In the cold winter, we need to keep warm, this is called Huu Y in life. Just because you are attached to these things, you become attached to them, [so] there will be a feeling, there will be a relationship. These things bind you, making it impossible for you to escape.

Simple explanation of the word “Hanh”. In Huu Y Hanh, what is Hanh? [Hands of conduct include] Aggregates of Conduct, Precepts, Places of Conduct, and Subsequent Virtues. The Aggregates are the Five Aggregates, which are Form, Feeling, Perception, Actions, and Consciousness. Those five types are constantly in motion, that is Hanh. “Hanh” means “movement”, constantly moving. All things are objects, including your body. Your body is made up of four great elements (Earth, Water, Fire, Wind), all movements in your body do not leave the Five Aggregates.

Tho means “to receive”. The external realm is no longer there, but the inside receives the realm from one's own Dharma Chen and is in contact with it; That is Uan Hanh. The precepts are eighteen precepts. The eighteen realms include eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind (those are the six senses), Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma (these are called the six senses), Eyes, Ears, Tongue, Tongue, Body, Consciousness (called the six consciousnesses, ). Six senses, six objects, six consciousnesses, these three types combined, three times six equals eighteen. “Precepts” means that each dharma has its scope and limits. The land is twelve places, that is, the eyes observe colors, the ears hear sounds, the tongue knows tastes, and the consciousness absorbs the dharma. Each realm [consists of] six sense objects in contact with six consciousnesses, which are called the Twelve Places. Chen and Consciousness come into contact with the Base, the six senses. The six senses and the six senses come into contact, that is where Consciousness operates.

What is Subordination? Means “to bind”. Again, there is No Dependent Conduct, which means that once liberated, there is no dependent conduct. In each practice, there are many “relatives” that depend. Speaking of form outside the body, just like our body inherently belongs to ourselves, but the form outside our body is the [object] for us to enjoy. Some things are dependent, some things are boring. That is, the colors you don't like and then get bored of them are of the type of love and hate. Whenever you love it, you want to keep it as your own; Whenever I hate it, I hope to escape it. That is “having a relationship”; this is called Huu Y Hanh.

Luan is “the teachings, the teachings of the precepts” [meaning] the Buddha preaches the Dharma to us, teaches and admonishes us on what we should do. This is like the wheel (Luan Jewel) that the Holy King Chakravarti sits on [to fly around the four continents], just like we sit in a car, it can transport us. But Luan has the ability to crush. Whenever there is an obstacle under the wheel, whatever is small, it can crush it. All Shravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, relying on the Wheel of Virtue and Virtue, will be able to attain Nirvana.

What does “Or follow the wheel” mean? “Thu” means “head”, that is, the end of afflictions. This is beheading afflictions, cutting off afflictions, and skillfully attaining Nirvana. These two types of [Happy Clothing] belong to Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha. The Sutra originally only talked about Pratyekabuddha; Here, Thanh Van in the previous section has been combined. The person who practices this Wheel of Virtue is not a Mahayana dharma vessel, is not a Bodhisattva, is not a container for the Mahayana, but is a Hinayana. Their aura is only that big. Why say so? "Because they point to the Precepts and Conduct, they are shocked and miserable" (Because they refer to their own Precepts, they are afraid and disgusted): That person points to the Wheel of Virtue, thinks only of himself, does not want to be bound by all kinds of suffering and pleasure, does not want to be bound by all kinds of suffering. Regarding birth, old age, sickness, and death, love must be separated, hatred must be met, and prayer cannot be achieved. That person is very afraid and hates those tribulations. Especially the disease, I hate it very much. Also “pray without success”, you seek but cannot achieve, want to let go but cannot! Love must be separated, hatred must be met. He wants to be free from those sufferings, but only wishes to liberate himself. "Practice without seeking liberation for all sentient beings" (Practice without seeking liberation for all sentient beings): He practices for his own liberation, not for the sake of all sentient beings.

“Non-Mahayana weapon” (Not a Mahayana dharma weapon), does not belong to the Bodhisattva Vehicle, is not a Mahayana dharma weapon. That person belongs to Actions, Aggregates, Precepts, and Places, hoping to destroy them. That person does not care about all sentient beings' suffering. Seeing all sentient beings suffering, that person cannot be saved, so he must go to a quiet place, even away from everyone. That person "does not seek to liberate all sentient beings to practice" (does not seek to liberate all sentient beings to practice), so it is said that he "does not practice Mahayana energy, because of the dependent system of Being and Behavior" (not the Mahayana energy, because he depends on the dependent behavior): This dependence is related to predestined mindfulness, that is, his belief is dependent, because for something he does not believe in, he will reject it. “If you don't belong”, you won't accept other sentient beings, won't educate them, won't help others so they can escape suffering. “There is no compassion” (There is no compassion), why? That person only wishes to free himself from suffering, that is called "being attached", being bound, "not having the Mahayana energy".

“Due to the contemplation of others suffering, they let go and cannot save them” [meaning] that person sees all sentient beings endure a lot of suffering, but does not save, nor does he preach the Dharma to benefit sentient beings, only praying for self-liberation. Because I don't want to be in this world, "non-Mahayana energy" (not Mahayana energy). Because that person himself “cuts off the afflictions”.

“Unlikely to eliminate all sentient beings' afflictions” (Disliking to eliminate all sources of afflictions for all sentient beings): Not willing to eliminate afflictions for sentient beings, nor willing to help sentient beings, nor preaching the Dharma to benefit others. Therefore, we say “reciting sutras, reciting mantras, worshiping, and making vows are all dedicated to all sentient beings”; that is the Bodhisattva.

What does Thanh Van Nhi Thua do? They only dedicate it to themselves, without thinking about sentient beings. They don't even save their own relatives. Therefore, people think that monastics have no feelings and must practice like a piece of wood or a rock; but this is not correct. They refuse to save sentient beings, see death but do not save them, even though sentient beings are in the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death. They have attained enlightenment, such as achieving the six types of supernatural powers, attaining the Complete Contraception, and should preach the Dharma to sentient beings, but they refuse and stay in Zen to enjoy and enjoy themselves. Therefore, they are not of Mahayana energy.

“Unable to sit on the Mahayana wheel, the Bodhi path” (Unable to sit on the Mahayana wheel to move towards Bodhi path): Unable to control the Mahayana wheel. “Luan” means to crush. Mahayana wheel also has the function of transportation. The Mahayana wheel transports [practitioners] into the Mahayana, and the Mahayana must benefit sentient beings. Therefore, the self-realized realms of Mahayana and Hinayana are roughly the same, but one is willing to give the self-realized realm to give to sentient beings, while the other is not willing to give alms, for fear of falling into the pit of afflictions. They haven't finished saving themselves yet. When it comes to saving others, they don't dare to be clever! They "cannot follow the great light wheel" (cannot follow the great light wheel to enter): "Great light wheel" is wisdom, which means Prajna. Those in the Single Enlightened Vehicle and those in the Shravaka Vehicle cannot rely on the great wheel of light to enter Bodhi, in order to reach ultimate Nirvana and attain enlightenment. Therefore “is not the Mahayana energy”.

The Pratyekabuddha Vehicle is very lonely, they also do not associate with Dharma friends.

What is Doc Giac? They meditate on their own, contemplating the birth and death of all dharmas. From the appearance of birth and death, find the principle of non-birth and non-destruction. Once you have found the "no birth and death", then the difference between birth and death will disappear. Therefore, it is said that they are not of Mahayana temperament. In the above section, we talked about two types of Ten Medical Wheels, that is, Ten Existing Medical Wheels, one is Thanh Van, the other is Single Enlightenment. Are those dharmas good or not? Is it a dharma for us to directly move towards Mahayana?

(Sutra) Good man! All sentient beings, the Thanh Van Vehicle, the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, are working on the island, with the right effort to study, like these living beings, their faculties are mature, their faculties are weak, their diligence is minimal. The theory of weakness and taste is subtle and profound, the Mahayana Dharma is profound, the theory of hearing two causes, the plan is a great sin, and the heron is against all Buddhas. The reason why it's fake? Weak sentient beings like the Sravaka Vehicle, the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, who are active in the island, who diligently practice and study, whose faculties are mature, whose faculties are weak, who are diligently minimal, who hear and hear wonderfully, and who are even profound in the Mahayana Dharma. As for all sentient beings, they are truly foolish, self-centered, bound to cessation and cessation, depraved with crazy thoughts, and grasping at inhumanity. The effects of karma, the cessation of thought, the eight necessarily good actions, the evil actions, false teachings of the Mahayana, the destruction of self, phi dharma preaching, dharma teachings illegal. TActually non-monks, theory of monks; Truth is a monk, theory is not a monk; Truly non-Bhikkhuni, the theory is not Bhikkhuni; truly is Bhikkhuna, the theory is not Bhikkhunā.
If someone has not diligently and diligently practiced properly, such beings have not yet matured, their base is poor, and they have little diligence. If someone talks about the profound and profound Mahayana dharma, both the speaker and the listener are guilty of a great sin, and they are also going against all the Buddhas. cowardly, with little diligence, but immediately hear that the Mahayana Dharma is very profound and wonderful, such sentient beings are truly foolish, claiming to be omniscient, trapped in cessation, falling into crazy thinking, clinging to the theory of "there is no cause", regarding karma, giving rise to the idea of cessation, rejecting "there is no such thing as doing good or evil", blaspheming about Mahayana, destroying my dharma, saying the dharma is dharma, the dharma is saying it is not dharma, Treally not a monk but says it is a monk, really a monk but says it is not a monk, really not a Bhikkhu but says it is Bhikkhu, really a Bhikkhu but says it is not Bhikkhu).

Buddha talked about the wrong way of teaching [of teachers]: If [listeners] don't yet know how to walk, you tell them to run, [listeners] will stumble and fall. Therefore, there are sentient beings who have never worked hard on Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, and the twelve causes and conditions, "the isle" (have never worked hard), that is, they have never worked hard and are not skillful in practicing. That Dharma has not yet been successfully cultivated, and the Mahayana energy is not yet ripe. Such sentient beings have not yet practiced the Second Vehicle Dharma, but if they directly study the Mahayana Dharma, it will not be possible!

“ Low base, little effort” (Poor base, little effort): If in this life one does not listen to the Mahayana Dharma, that person will be slandered. The person's base is not yet ripe, that person's base is poor. There are also very few minds that are diligent in cultivating the Dharma, but they are not diligent, they just keep slacking off, indulging in the five worldly desires. Wealth, beauty, fame, food, drink, and sleep are the five roots of hell. That person is greedy for the realm of the five desires, eating, living, sleeping, and taking up a lot of time in a day. Let's think about it: Busy with food and clothing, tired and tired, we have to sleep. Twenty-four hours in a day pass, how much time do you still have to study religion? As for reciting sutras, we practice reciting sutras between lay people and monastics. Of course it can't be compared! Five hours of monastic practice is too few! Out of twenty-four hours, you only practice for five hours, what do you do for the remaining nineteen hours? Sleeping takes up a lot of time. In a person's life, sleeping takes up too much time. There are people who sleep eight hours and still think it's not enough!

Now we are repenting, including repenting to the holy name and sitting quietly, it only takes an hour to finish, everyone then chats. Of course, chatting is also discussing Buddhism. No matter what the table is, we have to be busy eating and drinking. From ten-thirty to eleven-thirty, for an entire hour, then there was a short break, almost an hour, so two hours arbitrarily passed by! Woke up and was busy with housework. If you arrange your time, there really is very little [time] for diligence! If such a person teaches them the very profound and subtle Mahayana Dharma, makes them meditate, makes them study, makes them practice and comprehend, it will be impossible! Both the speaker and the listener are guilty of a great sin! Why? If the speaker does not know the basis, the listener may incur the crime of blasphemy. Doing so is contrary to all Buddhas and is not in accordance with the Buddha's teachings. From Hinayana to Mahayana, you first need to know that this world is suffering, where does that suffering come from? Because we create karma, that is, the Collection (grouping of karma). Suffering and suffering are the cause and effect of the world. Cessation, Path: You must know that cessation is joy and achievement. You must know, you must observe, this is cultivating the Way in order to attain Nirvana, which is cause and effect beyond the world. Those are two layers of cause and effect. Speaking according to the Hinayana, this dharma is originally the dharma of the Four Truths, the Hinayana, but because that person benefits sentient beings, it is called the Mahayana. Not only must we cultivate the path ourselves, attain Nirvana, no longer create karma, and no longer experience suffering, [but] we must also make all sentient beings know. That is Mahayana.

The Dharma is neither big nor small, you are the one who receives the Dharma. You hear the Mahayana saying "all dharmas are Emptiness, cause and effect of good and evil do not exist, there is basically no existence", [if you do not understand clearly], you will fall into the Emptiness of Cessation and Cessation. Then, according to the realm of the five desires, this aspect seems to be empty, the other aspect is truly empty. Therefore, if one speaks the Mahayana Dharma, one is afraid that after hearing it, one will fall into the Dharma View, nor will one fall into the Eternal View. If we consider Nirvana as the Eternal View, we consider the meaning of Emptiness as the Ending View; that's a mistake!

Therefore, there is a class of sentient beings who have never officially practiced the Shravaka Vehicle or the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, have never put in the effort, have not practiced diligently, have not been diligent, and have not yet matured their faculties. “The base is poor” (The base is poor), only a little diligent, don't come to listen and receive the very profound Mahayana dharma. But that person believes that he has the Mahayana energy, considers himself to be wise and wise, but [after listening] only focuses on Annihilation, that is, the View of Annihilation. Duan Kien is that person who talks about Emptiness, [mistakenly thinking] "All dharmas are Emptiness, so what is there anymore suffering or happiness to achieve? In fact, they do not exist!" When we preach the Contemplation Sutra, the lower half of the volume says "both sides (Yes and No) are not established", but that person falls on the side of Duan Kien. Due to being infatuated with the realm of the five desires, that person is very diligent, but when it comes to cultivating the Six Paramitas, that person is very lazy and has little diligence. That's falling into "crazy thinking".

“Accepting to the theory of no cause” (Accepting to the theory of “there is no cause”)

that means not believing in cause and effect. As for all karmic consequences, doing evil karma will result in suffering, doing good karma will result in good karma, being born in heaven and enjoying joy, until attaining enlightenment. Those who do not believe in cause and effect, then give rise to thoughts of annihilation, rejecting all good and evil deeds, falsely calling themselves Mahayana. That person studies Mahayana, considers the Mahayana dharma to be the Cessation of Thought, is entangled in Emptiness, attached to Emptiness, considers all the good deeds, evil deeds, bad deeds, and good deeds of the Buddha's teachings to be exactly the same [because of misunderstanding the meaning] "The Mahayana always says equality, destroying both sides." In the Vimalakirti Sutra, Manjushri Bodhisattva asked layperson Vimalakirti: “What are precepts, concentration, and wisdom?” Layperson Vimalakirti replied: “Lust, anger, ignorance”. What does that mean? Lust, anger, and ignorance have no real substance. Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom also do not have a real entity. They are the same essence of the Dharmakaya and also the essence of the dharma nature. “Response” is reciprocity. This one says this half, that one says the other half, there is no good or evil. Suppose you do not practice Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and the Path, and then attain that meaning of Emptiness, you will fall into the Emptiness of Ending Cessation, and will refute that "there is no cause and effect!" Refuting that there is no cause and effect, destroying and disrupting the Buddha's teachings, in the end, regarding the Buddha's teachings, right becomes wrong! Lust, anger, and delusion are illegal, what that person says is right, what he says is Dharma becomes illegal, if what he says is illegal becomes Dharma!

“Destroying my Dharma” (Destroying and disrupting my Dharma): Which is not Buddhist Dharma, but that person says it is Buddhist Dharma. Originally it was Buddha Dharma, but that person said "it is not Buddha Dharma". He is not a monk, not a true monk, and is said to be a monk. As for a true monk, it is said that he is not a monk. That's crazy. Actually, it is not Bhikkhuni Da, that is, it is not a precept, as with Buddhism in Dong Do, the rules in temples and pagodas are not precepts, but are prescribed by the patriarch. These things are called Thanh Quy, they are said to be precepts. Therefore, [some people mistakenly maintain that] if you don't study the precepts passed down by the Buddha, you'll be fine if you study the Thanh Quy thoroughly. These are all "the dharma said is illegal", it's really not Bhikkhu Da but he says it's Bhikkhu Da, it's really Bhikkhu

Da says it's not Bhikkhuni Da.

(Sutra) Stupidity, madness, arrogance, jealousy, with the party's heart, the Mahayana dharma praises, supports protective, generous and generous. U Thanh Van Vehicle, Single Enlightenment Vehicle, blasphemy, obscenity, no spirit left behind, unable to truly follow the Thanh Van Vehicle, or Single Enlightenment Vehicle, or Supreme Vehicle, renounce worldliness, become a monk, receive the Complete Precepts, become an up-so-nature, practice the necessarily good dharma of cause and effect. The disciples, either with the dharma weapon or the non-dharma weapon, need to practice Learning, Unlearning, and wish to attain the ultimate fruit of true goodness and rebirth, upholding the precepts, breaking the precepts, having no precepts, pretending to have no precepts, types of destruction, haughtiness, confusion, seizing strange robes and bowls, not hearing and taking advantage of all the birth tools, system of blessings, and prohibitions.
(Sutra: The mind is foolish, crazy, arrogant, arrogant, jealous, sectarian. For the Dharma Mahayana, then praised, praised, supported, protected, and caused it to be widely circulated. As for the dharma of the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, it was slandered, obstructed, and not allowed to be transmitted. It is not possible to truly rely on the Sravaka Vehicle, or the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, to renounce the world, become a monk, attain full enlightenment, and practice the causes and conditions of all good dharmas. Whether it is a Dharma weapon or not a Dharma weapon, advise them to diligently practice Learning and Unlearning, until the truly good people attain ultimate ultimate results, uphold the precepts, or break the precepts, those who do not have the precepts, but use all kinds of slander, curses, reprimands, chaos, take away their robes and bowls, do not allow them to enjoy the things needed in life, tie them up, lock them up).

“ Stupidity, madness, arrogance, jealousy, the mind of the party” (The mind is foolish, crazy, arrogant, arrogant, jealous, ganging up): This temple slanders that temple, that temple slanders this temple. This group of lay people defames that group of lay people. In the end, who is right and who is wrong? Crazy right and wrong! Those who study the Shravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle then slander the Mahayana. Those who study the Mahayana dharma slander and obstruct the sravaka vehicle and pratyekabuddha dharma, do not allow it to be transmitted, [insisting] "this is the Hinayana dharma, do not let it exist". It is impossible to truly rely on the dharma of the Shravaka Vehicle, or the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, or the Supreme Vehicle to renounce worldliness and become a monk. After hearing the Dharma, you will enter the Dharma. Those who cannot do so, of course cannot become a monk, cannot receive the Full Precepts,

can't become a monk, can't become a monk.

“It is not as real as practicing all good dharma causes and conditions” (It is also not true as practicing all good dharma causes and conditions): Practice good dharma causes and conditions and then do good things. For all good dharmas, do not do them because they are small [and do not do them]. We can donate one coin to the suffering people, or we can donate one coin to a Dharma conference in a temple or pagoda. You can also donate one coin. That's called rejoicing. Not donating, but even destroying, means not practicing all good karma. “My disciple, either a dharma weapon or a non-dharma weapon” (For my disciples, it is either a dharma weapon or not a dharma weapon): A person who practices well and learns like that will be a tool to hold the dharma. “Or non-dharma weapon” is a person who breaks the precepts. Breaking the precepts will not be good! Bhikkhus, bhiksunis, upasakas, upasikas like that, that is, the four disciples [like that], cannot be called diligent in practice. “Need to practice” is diligent practice.

“Learned, Uneducated” (Learned and Uneducated): That is, the status of being educated and uneducated. The status of No Learner is to have attained Arhatship. What is Huu Hoc status? The seven statuses are all learned statuses, that is, First Fruition Direction, First Fruition, Second Fruition Direction, Second Fruition, Three Fruition Directions, Three Fruition Directions, Four Fruition Directions, all are called the Learned Fruition status. Achieving Arhatship is the status of No Learning, until "true and good differences give rise to attaining the ultimate fruit"; That is the attainment of Arhatship, the end of Thoughtful Thinking. That is a magic weapon.

Or one who breaks the precepts, “upholds the precepts, breaks the precepts, has no precepts” (upholds the precepts, breaks the precepts, those who have no precepts): There are those who maintain the precepts, there are those who break the precepts, or even do not have any precepts at all. That is [speaking of all kinds of people] studying the Mahayana dharma. Here, we are talking about the true goodness of the King of Sat-de-li, the true goodness of Thu-datta-la, that is, the four types of nature, with respect to Bhikkhus who break the precepts, Bhikkhus who maintain the precepts, or Bhikkhus who do not have any precepts, there is no distinction between them, all cursing, slandering, cursing, scolding, rebuking, being upset, and even depriving them of their robes and bowls without allowing them to use them. All the necessary items in their lives have been taken away, can they still survive? They will not be able to survive, until they are imprisoned in prison.

(Sutra) Like the eight-fold cause and effect, the Nihilism Commentator, although in the middle of the human body, is truly a Rakshasa, ugh In the next world, countless great kalpas, it is difficult to attain personal identity. Being in hell, experiencing immeasurable suffering, not dealing with human beings, giving birth to the View of Obliteration and Extinction. Like a benevolent monk, the non-nine-stepped body is emptied, the day is gone, the mouth is closed, the mouth is speechless, the pain and poison are endured, and pain is difficult to endure. At the end of life, one is destined to be born in the Infinite Hell. Evil beasts, reincarnating in the past, experiencing suffering, difficult to save, hundreds of thousands of kalpas, difficult to restore the human body. Although it is too immeasurable, countless kalpas, the human body is perfected, the child is born in the five impurities, the Buddha world, the birth is weak, the birth is weak, the warm, the ah, the loss is not real, the species is seriously ill, often suffering from hindrances, or the body is in trouble, the cause is not happy. The language is vulgar, the ears are evil. The mind is often confused, has no solution, is born in poverty, lacks dharma, does not conform to good beings, follows evil actions, mocks evil karma, holds evil views, creates the sin of the Uninterrupted, falls again and again into the Uninterrupted hell, reincarnates into the evil beast, and is extremely difficult to arise.
(Sutra: Those who reject all cause and effect, believe in such an Abhidharma, although within Humans are truly La Sat, in countless future lives, it is better to be in hell and suffer countless sufferings than to rise up to the Destroyer View! Such a foolish person will soon be crippled and crippled for many days and nights, unable to speak Evil, suffering, difficult to save, many hundreds of thousands of lives, difficult to be a human again. Although after countless countless lives, will be a human again, but will be born in the world of five impurities, without Buddha, blind and deaf from birth, speechless, speechless, with all kinds of serious diseases that often bind the body, or the body is short, ugly, people do not like to see, speech is clumsy, stuttering, ears hear bad things, mind is often confused and does not understand anything. Being born in a poor house, with shortcomings, not meeting good friends, following evil friends, liking to create bad karma, liking to hold evil views, committing the sin of the Uninterrupted and then falling into the Hell of the Uninterrupted, revolving in the evil destinies, with difficulty escaping.

“Eight not necessarily cause and effect, the argument of cessation of cessation” (Refutes the absence of all cause and effect, believes in the doctrine of cessation): [That is, the person who always insists that] “we do this without making mistakes, without incurring retribution”. “Like a benevolent benefactor who is eternally at ease with his crippled body” (Soon such a bewildered person will have his limbs crippled and lacking): Even though that person does not believe in cause and effect, cause and effect will find that person; When [karma] comes, that person will suffer. That kind of foolish person has no wisdom, his body in this life will "have no limbs" (not long after, the limbs will be disabled, lacking), or due to illness, they will be disabled or lacking, or as in the present, being in a car accident, or encountering a natural disaster, water disaster, or fire, can all cause that person's limbs to become disabled, but there are many disabled people due to illness. For a very long time, "nothing to say for many days and nights" (for many days and nights, tongue-tied, unable to speak): Can't even speak! For what reason? Suffering makes that person become like that. Karma transfers to that person's body; That is called retribution due to the arising of the View of Nihilism, causing the person to suffer deeply, making it very difficult to endure. After death, one will definitely be reborn in the Uninterrupted Hell.

“Evil beasts, revolving here and there” (Circulating back and forth in evil destiniess): “Evil beasts” are the three evil destiniess, ie hell, hungry ghosts, and animals. “Suffering all sufferings, difficult to save” (Suffering all sufferings, difficult to save), through how many lifetimes? “Many hundred thousand kalpas” (Many hundreds of thousands of kalpas): Not one hundred thousand kalpas, two hundred thousand kalpas, but many hundreds of thousands of kalpas. If you want to restore your human body, that is, to be reincarnated as a human in the human world, it's not easy! It must be necessary to go through countless eons to be able to take on a human body. For that number of countless kalpas, if we talk about small kalpas, it is also many tens of thousands of years. Countless lifetimes, if we use human time to calculate the time limit, it is very difficult to count. “You are born in the five defilements, without the Buddha world” (But born in the five defilements, without the Buddha): These are the Five Defilements, the Defects of the Evil World, the Defects of Views, the Defects of Defilements, the Defects of Living Beings, and the Defects of Life. At that time, [will be born in] a world without Buddha, that is, born in a time like us in the present.

A person lying on that bed confessing his sins saw his body filling up the entire bed. Ten thousand people is enough to fill the bed. That is the meaning “without interruption”. Having committed this type of crime, after being born in the human world, such a person's life span is still not long. I, oppressing, harming, and punishing my disciples who keep the precepts, break the precepts, and do not have the precepts, all cause them to not be able to peacefully cultivate good qualities. Due to that cause and effect, they have spent hundreds of thousands of lifetimes immersed in evil destiniess, from darkness to darkness, from which it is difficult to escape. All the sins of such sentient beings are because they have not sought to listen to the teachings and practice the Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha dharma, but have previously sought to listen to the teachings and practice the very profound Mahayana dharma. It is difficult for a foolish person to follow the Dharma of Extinction, not to mention being able to become a saintly dharma weapon? He cannot even attain Nirvana through the attainment of the Sravakas or the Pratyekabuddhas, let alone attain the vast and very deep Supreme Bodhi?

“Such a foolish person who follows the Nihilism Abhidharma” (Such a foolish person who follows the Nihilism Abhidharma): This is someone who believes in the Nihilism Abhidharma, rejecting there is no cause and effect. “Destroying, destroying my Dharma” (Destroying, causing chaos, destroying my Dharma), causing the Buddha's Dharma to be destroyed. If destruction means destroying the Dharma eyes of sentient beings, people will not have the true Dharma to be able to hear. That person hinders many people and prevents others from believing in the Buddha's path. “Forcing and punishing my disciples for keeping the precepts, breaking the precepts, and not having the precepts” (Forcing, harming, and punishing my disciples for keeping the precepts, breaking the precepts, and not having the precepts), for my disciples, regardless of keeping the precepts, breaking the precepts, and not having the precepts, it makes them unable to have peace of mind, practice good qualities, believe in cause and effect, practice the Dharma, worship Buddha, and worship. These causes and conditions do not exist. That evil person, because of the fate of punishment, destroys the Buddha Dharma, destroys the Sangha, defames the religion, "many hundred thousand kalpas, a group of evil beasts" (for many hundreds of thousands of kalpas, immersed in evil destiniess), often suffers in the three evil destiniess.

“From darkness to darkness, it is difficult to escape): Hoping to escape that kind of suffering is very difficult. All of the sins of living beings like that, as mentioned in the above section, there are so many sins and retributions, they make mistakes, suffer suffering and retribution, all because of "the one who sought to hear and practice the Sravaka Vehicle, the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, first sought to hear and practice the subtle and profound Mahayana Dharma" (did not seek to listen to the teachings and practice the Dharma of the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, but sought to hear and practice the subtle and very deep Mahayana Dharma). For that retribution, then point out the cause, what is the cause? Because I have not yet heard the Hinayana Dharma, I have not heard the Second Vehicle Dharma, but have first heard the Mahayana Dharma.

I remember when I first entered the Buddhist Academy, the old master Tu Chau[9] in the morning taught the Four Precepts, in the afternoon he taught the Avatamsaka Sutra, on one side was the Hinayana Dharma, the smallest Hinayana Dharma, on the other hand was the Mahayana Dharma. The most complete, Mahayana and Hinayana combined! Studying the Hinayana Dharma aims to review the things you have done throughout the day. What do you think about the actions of your body, mind, and heart? What did the body do? Can it be combined with the Avatamsaka Sutra? What if we cannot combine? Must repent! To study the Hinayana dharma, one must repent of one's sins, be vigilant, and remind one's body and mind not to be careless, not to be arrogant and arrogant; But that is not enough, it is necessary to study the Mahayana dharma in order to be able to put an end to birth and death, to be able to complete the twenty types of cessation, to attain Buddha's ultimate Nirvana. If you study the Mahayana dharma, you must recognize that the cause and effect of good and evil are not wrong at all. You should not, just because you study the Mahayana, consider that both worldly and extra-worldly cause and effect are destroyed. [If you think so], you're wrong! If you study the Mahayana dharma, then the Nirvana attained in the Sravakayana dharma and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle dharma must still be widely propagated, and you must also advise all sentient beings to study.

We study the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, the things said in the first half of the book and the second half of the book are indeed two different things. The first half of the book talks about good and evil, cause and effect. Contemplate good and evil cause and effect, that is, consider whether you do a lot of good or do a lot of evil. Contemplate for yourself! Your body, speech, and mind all have a lot of negative karma. Of course you know the present life, but you don't know the past life! We must contemplate what we did in countless past lives? Contemplating the next life, where will you be born in the future? That is judging from your determined karma, it will be transformed by your practice, not because of that destiny. You can contemplate Cham Luan at any time. Today, when you contemplate, you see that you may have to suffer retribution. Pray every day, and contemplate again the next morning, maybe [you will see] your karma has disappeared, your suffering has been finished, there is no more! Contemplation is this meaning!

“Good man! The vase is like a ruined vase” (Hey good man! For example, the vase has been destroyed). “Hoa vase” is a vase that has not been fired yet, has not been properly molded, and still has holes, cracks, and gaps. Will the [vessel] you use to store oil or milk leak? “All the leaks” (It's all leaked)! For what reason? It's not a [suitable] container to hold, it's not a very good container, whatever it holds will eventually be lost. That container is also damaged, that is, the item has defects. It also means that the person who preaches the Dharma to the person receiving the Dharma must consider what kind of energy the listener has and what Dharma should be spoken, so that person will be able to receive it. If that person is not that person, but is the Sravaka or Single-Enlightenment vehicle, he does not tell them the Dharma of the Sravaka or the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle, but instead arrogantly speaks of the Dharma of the Mahayana. That is called “non-qi” (not a vital element).

To give an example, like Chinese Zen Buddhism, due to the pressing times, there is no sutras that can be studied. During the time when Tam Vu destroyed Buddha, only Zen Buddhism flourished because there was no need to study any sutras, and there was no need to recite Buddha's name. [Hearing Trieu Chau say] “reciting Buddha's name for one hour, gargle for a day” [so I thought I really had to do that, because reciting Buddha's name would make] my mouth unclean for three days! The meaning is not like that! [Mr. Trieu Chau said so], because it is pure Mahayana [using self-reliance to practice], not relying on any means. That is research to gain enlightenment, clear the mind and see the nature. But what habits has this fostered? From the Tang Dynasty until now, people in the Zen Hall have rarely studied the Dharma. You preach the sutras there, but they don't listen, nor do they come to the Buddha's Recitation Hall. They stayed in the Zen Hall, besides eating well and sleeping well, they still slept well, ate well, and remained in a daze like that. Even when chanting and reciting public prayers, they avoid everything and don't believe in anything. That is very dangerous. It's still not as good as reciting Buddha's name in the Buddha's Recitation Hall, or studying the teachings in school, it's still better!

When studying teachings, any shaman who teaches you will teach from the Small to the Great. It's not like you just learned it, you immediately learned Mahayana. When you are in the Buddhist Institute, you must also talk about the eight consciousnesses, analyze your thoughts, and well control your three karma of body, speech, and mind to be able to enter the Mahayana. Otherwise, it will be like a cracked vase. What else can you expect to contain? The vase was damaged, the container was also lost. Therefore, it is said: When sentient beings "are in the Sravaka Vehicle, the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, are on the island, diligently practice" (regarding the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Dharma, have not yet diligently and diligently properly studied it), have not yet matured their faculties, are weak, and do not have the strength to be diligent, if the great profound and wonderful Dharma is spoken to them, "listening to two-cause talk, concluding a great sin" means that both the speaker and the listener are both guilty. “The heron is contrary to all Buddhas” (It is also contrary to all Buddhas), all the mistakes have been described in detail as in the previous section. For example, if a warehouse in the world is damaged and has holes, most of the precious things and goods placed in it will be lost. If your house is used to store goods [if it's torn up like that], not only will you store precious gems, but food will also be lost, because there are caves in there that other people can enter. That place is already ruined!

The person who studies that dharma "has a lot of attachment to the Second Vehicle dharma" (a lot of stinginess, jealousy, towards the Second Vehicle dharma) that person does not practice. “False name of Mahayana” that is false, claiming to be Mahayana. Because Thanh Van and Duyen Giac must talk about cause and effect, talk about retribution. The Mahayana principle is to say No View, but that person's Emptiness is actually the Cessation of Emptiness View, that is, the Cessation of View, not the real Emptiness View. Why did the Buddha preach sometimes not about Existence, but about Non-existence? Sometimes when talking about Emptiness, we don't say Emptiness, but say Non-emptiness? The intention is for you not to be attached. You should not be attached to Existence; That Existence is non-existence. You should also not be attached to Emptiness, that Emptiness is Non-emptiness, then there is also Existence and Emptiness. That's called the four sentences (four sentences): "No, yes; neither yes nor no; neither yes nor no"; four sentences like that. Like a blind person, you place all kinds of treasures in front of that person, but that person still cannot see or receive it. “Not stopping killing, up to wrong views” (Not stopping killing, up to wrong views): That person says “killing is not a sin”.
