He only sees the living enjoying pleasure, not the dead suffering from sin! That person has no wisdom, how can he see? This belongs to wrong view. Although that person still listens to the Mahayana very diligently, "cannot understand the profound dharma" means he cannot understand the very deep meaning of the dharma, so he cannot enlighten!

“It's like a field of stone” (Such as a field full of rocks): The field is full of rocks, how can you sow seeds? If you sow, you won't be able to produce seeds! Therefore, "living beings who are arrogant, arrogant, lazy, and arrogant about the Second Vehicle dharma, are lazy, and non-mocking, need to practice" (living beings who are arrogant, arrogant, and lazy about the Second Vehicle dharma and do not like to practice diligently): Why don't they like to practice diligently? “Desire for the five desires”: Being attached to the realm of the five desires, that person will relax, will not be bored, nor practice diligently. “Even though you are truly a Mahayana seed” means that you have sown the Mahayana seeds to those sentient beings, but they are all rocky fields, unable to grow, and they also do not study diligently. “Totally without accomplishment” (Completely without accomplishment): From beginning to end, there is no accomplishment. For example, when we read the Ksitigarbha Sutra, do we think that the Ksitigarbha Sutra is Mahayana or Hinayana? When it comes to Mahayana, the sutras all talk about suffering in hell. Speaking of Hinayana, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will bless you in everything. You can attain the Three Vehicles of Path and Fruition from the Ksitigarbha Sutra. Therefore, that sutra is neither Great, nor Small, but also Great, also Small, depending on the person who perceives it, depends on how you think, and what type of Dharma weapon it is?

We say Three Refuges, Five Precepts. The first step to enter Buddhism is to receive the Three Refuges and Five Precepts. Are the Three Refuges and Five Precepts part of the Mahayana or Hinayana? There is absolutely no one who judges that the Three Refuges and Five Precepts are Hinayana, and no one judges that the Three Refuges and Five Precepts are Mahayana. If you accept the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts until you develop the Bodhisattva mind to benefit sentient beings, then it will be Mahayana. After you have received the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, are tired of leaving the world, wish to leave the world, and first only care about yourself, not caring about anyone else, then you will be a Hinayana. All dharmas are neither big nor small, they just depend on how you use your mind? But here, in order, according to the Buddha's teachings, the A Ham Sutra is the Hinayana, the Prajnaparamita Sutra is the Mahayana. The Agama Sutra also has Mahayana meaning, but we cannot comprehend it. The Buddha's teachings are not simple, the whole is not Small, it is absolutely Small, Great is absolutely Great, it is not like that! There is no fixed dharma in Buddhism, it is based on the mind, based on the minds of sentient beings of those who study Buddhism like us to establish Mahayana or Hinayana dharma.

Because of them, if they have spent a lot of time, they still cannot understand. For example, if there is someone who does not wear armor, does not hold a sword or stick, and rushes into battle, they will be injured and suffer the same suffering. All sentient beings have never studied the Second Vehicle, their wisdom is weak, and they have not yet attained vitality, but because they speak of Mahayana, they will inevitably create false attachments Afterwards, you will be crippled and lacking limbs, for many days and nights, unable to speak, suffering from extreme suffering and pain, and will definitely be born in the Hell of No Intermittent, in evil destiniess, going back and forth.

“It's like cancer, it stores honey jelly” (Like a jar, first of all it contains honey jelly): You put a little poison in there, a little bit is enough, you still can't eat it, if you eat it you will be poisoned to death. "Such sentient beings, diligently practice the Second Vehicle, and thus achieve success" (Such sentient beings, diligently study the Second Vehicle, have not yet achieved success): Just like there are sentient beings who practice the Second Vehicle, because they are lazy, they do not succeed in whatever they practice. If you tell them the Mahayana dharma again, the Second Vehicle is already broken, the Mahayana is also broken, they cannot achieve it either way! “For example, if there is a person who is crazy and has a chaotic mind, he cannot understand because he is making music” (For example, if there is a person who is crazy and has a chaotic mind, because he plays music, [that person] cannot understand): That person's mind is already chaotic, you play the guitar or sing for him, nothing will reach his ears. Like a living being who has never practiced the Second Vehicle, greed, anger, and delusion are very strong, and afflictions disturb that person's mind. That person "is attached to no cause" (attachment to "there is no cause"), no matter what you say, that person will not listen, because that person is attached to the Commentary on Nihilism. For people like that, no matter what Dharma you say, it won't work. No matter how long you talk, that person still can't understand!

“For example, if there is a human being who does not wear armor, does not carry a sword, staff, or spear in battle, I will certainly pity him and experience suffering” (For example, if there is a person who does not wear armor, does not hold a knife or stick, and rushes into battle haphazardly, he will be injured and suffer hardships): That is said during war, so In battle, they must wear armor and also wear armor inside. “Pillar” is something worn inside. “Armor” is something worn on the outside. I was in Tibet and saw that every year in the Spring, they race horses, shoot archery, all wear armor, and wear quite heavy armor. The current horse is basically unbearable. That suit of armor weighed hundreds of pounds, and the body weighed another hundred pounds, and had to have someone come help to wear it. It was all made of real iron. Their acting is still just an imagination. Tibetan opera uses real armor and armor to draw bows and shoot arrows. If even with these things you don't protect carefully, you don't have a knife in your hand, and you don't have a bow or arrow, just two empty fists and rushing into battle, that's no good! Currently, it is even more impossible! Nowadays, guns are used, which is completely different from that time!

Therefore, if you speak the Mahayana Dharma to that person, if he does not fall into the View of Annihilation, he will also fall into the View of Permanence, and will be attached to both sides. Therefore, one after another, they create immense evil and create a lot of wrongs. A foolish person who does not have such wisdom will soon have crippled and defective limbs. Due to defamation of the Three Jewels, cause and effect is obscured, "for many days and nights, unable to speak, experiencing all kinds of suffering and poison, excruciating pain and suffering" (for many days and nights, tongue-tied, unable to speak, suffering poisons, extreme pain that is hard to bear). After death, one is bound to be reborn in the Infinite Hell. "Dear evil beasts, circulating here and now, understanding it like money, this is what I preach" (Circulating back and forth in evil destiniess, you should know as detailed in the order in the previous section): These things have already been said in the previous section, in hell, suffering, suffering endlessly.

(Sutra) Good man! The wise person first contemplates all minds and then preaches the Dharma. The first stage arises from the mind, the compassionate mind, the happy mind, the beneficial mind, the mind that is not complacent, the mind that is patient, the mind that is not arrogant, the mind that is not jealous, the mind that is not deceitful, the mind that leads to concentration, then altruistically preaches the Dharma, indifferent to all sentient beings, the text preaches the Dharma, the cycle of birth and death, and the great tribulation. The good Tathagata attains all sentient beings' minds and bodies, because of the Infinite Truth, the Infinite Elemental Wheel, and the one who preaches the Dharma. The great man is armored with all the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, selflessly preaching the Dharma, and the heron is obedient to him. Due to compassion, the spirit destroys all afflictions, the spirit transcends the three seas of existence, the sentient beings reach the middle of the three vehicles, depending on the mind's ridicule, depending on the pleasure of the One Vehicle, quickly completes the effort, the person preaches the Dharma, and in the final cycle of birth and death, falls into great danger.
(Sutra: Good man! Therefore, wise people should first observe the mind of all Everyone, then preach the Dharma. First of all, you should develop a heart of compassion, a heart of joy, a mind of benefit, a mind that is not complacent, a mind that can endure, a mind that is not arrogant, a mind that is not jealous, a mind that is not stingy, and a mind that is calm and focused, so that other sentient beings who listen to the Dharma will not wander into birth and death and fall into great danger beings, using the No-Tentrances, the No-Hand-Hand Wheel because they speak the Dharma. All the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas who are fully armored, preach the Dharma in the same way for others. Out of compassion, because they want to help sentient beings eliminate all afflictions, to help them escape the sea of three realms, because from within the three vehicles, sentient beings, depending on their preference, will quickly reach completion, because speaking the Dharma completely does not allow sentient beings to circulate. birth and death, falling into great danger).

A wise person must first observe living beings, observe what their thoughts are? This must require the attainment of Forgiveness of Mind and Fulfillment of Life. If you don't have all [those magical powers], what will you do? First of all, you must develop your mind. “Generating from the heart”: From the heart is to give all sentient beings happiness and eliminate suffering for sentient beings. “Great compassion” is seeing sentient beings suffering in the same way as yourself suffering. That is called developing Bodhi mind. All of these many types of minds give rise to the mind of joy, joy towards the dharma, joy towards sentient beings. Being “beneficial”, that is, determined to create benefits for sentient beings. “Do not entertain the mind”: Practicing the Dharma and preaching the Dharma must be diligent, able to endure the harm of sentient beings, and all kinds of defamation can be endured, because it will eliminate harm. “No pride and arrogance”: All sentient beings and I are equal. If you separate yourself from sentient beings, you will not be able to become a Buddha. One day, I was talking with everyone about repaying the four great graces. Do you know what the four great graces are? We only know father, mother, Buddha, and do not know the kindness of living beings. Repaying the four great kindnesses, the first is to repay the kindness of sentient beings. Without sentient beings, you will not be able to become a Buddha. Compassionate joy and forgiveness towards whom? Sentient beings achieve Buddhahood for you. Can endure, not arrogant, not arrogant, not even jealous, not stingy!

“Concentration of the mind”: That many minds must be fulfilled! Due to the power of concentration, joy arises in the body and mind, the body and mind are calm. That is called “isoconductivity”. Then, because he preaches the Dharma and speaks the great Dharma, it will not cause him to cycle through birth and death because of listening to the Dharma preaching. Just hearing the Dharma will make that person cut off the path of birth and death, at least cut off the suffering of the three evil destiniess. Before, I taught Avatamsaka and Dharma flowers. At first, studying the Dharma, went through two Buddhist Institutes, the first five years studying Hoa Nghiem at Co Son. Five years later, he was at Tram Son Tu, studying the four teachings with old magician Dam Hu, that is, taking the Lotus Sutra as his main subject. After coming to America, he changed to studying the Ksitigarbha Sutra and taught the Ksitigarbha Three Sutras. If anyone can recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, believe in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, see the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and worship the image of Ksitigarbha, the three paths will be completely cut off, and danger will no longer exist. That's what Buddha said. I think that by teaching this Dharma, sentient beings will no longer cycle through birth and death and fall into great suffering. After that, sometimes he also preaches the Samantabhadra Vows, preaches the three chapters of the Avatamsaka Sutra, and also preaches Manjushri Bodhisattva teaching us how to skillfully use the mind. We just need to know how to use our minds. If you use your mind wisely, you will end all evil. You know how to use your mind, whatever you encounter, you will make a vow, praying for all sentient beings to become Buddhas.

“The good Tathagata attains the mental form of all sentient beings, through the Infinite Elements, the Infinite Elemental Wheel, he preaches the Dharma” (The Tathagata skillfully understands the mental appearance of all sentient beings, uses the Infinite Elemental Elements, the Infinite Elemental Wheel to explain the true Dharma to them): Next, speaking of the Buddha Wheel, the meaning of these passages is very deep, You must listen attentively. “The great one is fully armored with all the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas” (All the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas are fully armored): That person is among living beings but is not infected by living beings, in battle wears armor, wears armor, is not injured, is a great Bodhisattva, only then can he preach the Dharma to others. That is "out of compassion, the spirit destroys all afflictions" (out of compassion, because he wants to eliminate afflictions): Pitying all sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to eliminate those afflictions. “The spirit transcends the three realms of existence” (Because it allows them to escape the ocean of three realms): the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm are collectively called the Three Existences. Usually, “three existences” refers to this!

“For sentient beings like the middle three vehicles, depending on the mind's derision, depending on the one vehicle" (Because it causes sentient beings from within the three vehicles, depending on their heart's preference, to follow one vehicle), that is to preach the Dharma completely, all three vehicles speak. If sentient beings have an affinity with any vehicle, learning that vehicle will be very good, so all three vehicles “great, middle, small” are said. “Quick completion of perfection” (Because of quick completion): If one preaches the Dharma according to one's base, because of the corresponding base, one will attain enlightenment. This will make that person reach perfection very quickly. "Those who preach the Dharma, at the end of the cycle of birth and death, fall into great danger" (Because they speak the Dharma, it does not cause them to cycle through birth and death, falling into great danger): The purpose of preaching the Dharma is to make sentient beings leave suffering, be happy, and no longer fall into danger. “Danger” is the danger in the three diagrams.

(Sutra) Van ha name Vo Tran Cau Hanh Luan? The one who teaches the Dharma at the same time, the non-existent Aggregates, the non-existent Bases, the non-existent Realms, the non-existent Desire Realms, the non-existed Form Realms, the non-existed Formless Realms, the non-existed beings in the world, the non-existences of others, the non-existents of other formations, the non-existent Feelings, the non-existent Thoughts, the non-existent Thoughts, the non-existences of Contact, the non-existed volitions, the non-existent ignorance, the non-existent will of old age and death, the non-existed formations, and the non-existing formations. inaction. The sentient beings preach the true Dharma, only the Aggregates, Places, and Precepts, speaking of the cessation of evil and non-action, the stage of cessation of attachment, the sentient beings preach the true Dharma. Di Thi Nghia Co, named Vo Tran Cau. The practitioner, with the ability to permanently cut off death, rebirth, and rebirth, preaches the Dharma to all sentient beings. Position: The ability to permanently cut off the Aggregates, Places, and Precepts, and to preach the Buddha's teachings. The ability to permanently cut off bad and inactive actions, and to all sentient beings to preach the Dharma. Thi vi Hanh. The wheel is like the light of the full moon, clear and unobstructed, filling the void, illuminating a realm without obstructions. Tathagata, up to the Bodhisattvas, possesses supernatural powers, theory, precepts, three types of transcendental wheel of unobstructed effect, transforms all worlds, benefits all sentient beings, the souls of all living beings do not return to different beasts, does not necessarily add to worldly beings, does not necessarily add to Sravakas, Solitary Enlightenment, has the power of sentient beings to destroy the dharma of birth and death, attain the peace and joy of Bodhi Nirvana. Thi Vi Luan's name. As the name of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Earthless Body of the Wheel of Action shows.
Aggregates, not because there is Base, not because there is World, not because there is Desire Realm, not because there is Formless Realm, not because there is this life, not because there is another life, not because there are Actions, not because there is Feeling, not because there is Perception, not because there is Thought, not because there is Contact, not because there is volition (arising of ideas), not because of ignorance, not because of aging, death, not because of action and non-action dharma, just because all the Aggregates, Places, and Worlds, in general, up to and including actions and non-actions, are extinguished, for sentient beings, it is said to be the true Dharma. Because of that meaning, it is called Non-Trinity. Actions means being able to permanently stop "death here, birth there". Because living beings declare the right dharma, that is, being able to permanently cut off actions and non-actions, for the sake of sentient beings. birth declares the true Dharma. This is called Action. The wheel is like the light of the full moon, clear and unobstructed, pervading all of space, illuminating all realms without hindrance. Likewise, all three types of the wheel are supernatural powers, teachings (speaking the Dharma in response to the wishes and thoughts of sentient beings), precepts (teachings), having an unobstructed effect throughout all worlds, benefiting all sentient beings, causing them to be taught. sentient beings do not follow any other path, but unlike all sentient beings in the world, not in common with all Sravakas and Solitary Enlightenment, can cause sentient beings to eliminate the sufferings of birth and death and attain the peace of Bodhi Nirvana.

This is called Infinite Cau Luan, which means Emptiness. [In the previous paragraph] it was just said that [speaking the Dharma without the right foundation will cause the listener] to fall into the View of Cessation of Cessation, but here the Dharma is taught wonderfully, without causing the listener to fall into the View of Cessation of Cessation. “Existence” is physical dharma, including mind dharma. “Aggregates of Being” are the Five Aggregates, which are Form, Feeling, Perception, Actions, and Consciousness. “No Existence of Place” (Not because there is a Place) is the twelve Places. “Unexisted Realm” (Not because there is a Realm) are the eighteen Precepts. Speaking of one thing in particular, “Unexisted Desire Realm”, “Unexisted Form Realm”, “Unexisted Formless Realm” (not because there is a Desire Realm, not because there is a Form Realm, not because there is an Immaterial Realm), that is, the three realms. “Non-existed Formless Realm”, “not because there is this life, not because there is another life,” “not because there is another life,” “not because there is another” is this life, “not because there are actions” refers to the future. “Not because there are actions, not because there is Feeling, not because there is Thought, not because there is Contact, not because there is volition” (Not because there are Actions, not because there is Feeling, not Because there is Perception, not because there is Thought, not because there is Contact, not because there is volition): These are Feeling, Thought, Action, Consciousness.

“There is no ignorance” (Not because there is ignorance), not even because there is old age or death. Those are the twelve causes and conditions. Of the twelve causes and conditions, Ignorance depends on Action, Action depends on Name and Form, Name and Form depends on the Six Places, until old age and death.

“The Impersonal Five Aggregates” (Not because of the Five Aggregates), the Five Aggregates[11] are Form, Feeling, Perception, Actions, Consciousness, [along with] Eighteen Precepts, twelve Places, there is no Volition, Thoughts, Thoughts, Feelings, Actions, all of them do not exist, like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, up to the Dustless Structures of Actions, up to actions and non-actions, all of these things are intended to show the meaning of the Middle Way, not falling into either side of Cessation and Permanence.

The next paragraph is intended to reiterate, why do we need to repeat it? Because this meaning is not easy to understand! The Buddha preached the Dharma as pure, “purity of the earthly structure” is what was done, what the teachings said were all pure. While preaching the Dharma, do not be attached to this, nor be attached to that. Everything is free from attachments, there is no here and there. This and that are both opposites. Wherever there is an opposite, there is an object, so the dharma has no opposite. Separated from both sides, revealing the Middle Way, separated from the four strokes, absolutely boundless.

If you want to end birth and death, you must practice this Wutang Cau Luan, causing everything to pass away and become pure. What we have just read above is all for the sake of cessation and teaching the Dharma to sentient beings. Because of that meaning, it is called Vo Tran Cau. The practitioner, if he does so, will be able to permanently put an end to “death here, birth there”, that is called Action. It is necessary to reach the eternal cessation of birth and death and attain ultimate Nirvana. That is the true Dharma, the ultimate Dharma, forever cutting off the Aggregates, Bases, Precepts, Five Aggregates, Twelve Places, and Eighteen Precepts.

If speaking broadly, all actions and non-actions must be completely cut off, there is no action, and there is also no non-action, that is called the Infinite Cau Luan. Wu Chen Cau Luan is like that, there is no action, but also no non-action. Action means non-action, non-action means action. The dharmas spoken by the Buddha have no beginning and no end. That's why it's called Vienna. If you look for a beginning you won't find it, if you look for an end you won't find it either. That is the meaning of Vienna. Currently, use this to display Vo Tran Cau Luan. Among them, there are ten types of armor. Luan is a simile, what simile is that? For example, Dharma uses the wheel to speak. The wheel can crush all obstacles under it. In Buddhism, compare what the Buddha said to Luan. That wheel is like the full moon, its light shines everywhere. If it's Summer, the moonlight at night is very cool. The meaning of comparing [Buddha's teachings] to light is to demonstrate that [those dharmas] are not obstructed. Light appears in the air, without obstacles, which means the realm is without obstacles. That is the visualization of all the outstanding effects of [the three types of teachings of the Dharma wheel:] supernatural powers, magical teachings, and the precepts of Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas are also unobstructed.

As for miraculous powers, in the Buddha's six senses, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind all turn into miraculous powers. So the heavenly eye and heavenly ear, [for each sense] add a word Thien. Thien [here] means natural. When you attain enlightenment, understand clearly, are enlightened, and restore your original nature, the realms that are deluded or obstructed will disappear, and you will have miraculous powers. Divine power is your natural wisdom. The Essence of supernatural powers is wisdom. “God” is not based on thinking. Another person saw a [miraculous] event, then said that person was a true god. A true god is like a magician, with the feeling that he or she is a god. Or swallowing a knife or spitting fire, you feel that [the person who can do that] is truly very strange, because you can't do it. When you see them do it, it feels very magical. Buddha's supernatural powers are very natural. He sees sentient beings, knows the appearance of sentient beings, knows the past lives of sentient beings, and what Dharma he should teach them to enable them to become enlightened. [That is supernatural power]. As for “the theory” is the great Bodhisattvas or Buddhas, for the things sentient beings think and remember in their minds, they remember, that is, remember the things that belong to the cultivator and the effects of that person's mind while cultivating, to preach the Dharma [corresponding to what they think and remember]. That is called “doctrine”. “Teacher precepts” (teaching): All dharmas spoken by the Buddha are called “religious precepts”. Like when we request precepts from a master, [precepts] means to “admonish, encourage, educate” you. Preaching means preaching the Dharma. Originally, the teacher taught you about the precepts and taught you how to act.

Those three types of supreme Dharma wheel have an unobstructed effect, that is, an unobstructed effect, not only saving a certain sentient being, not saving other sentient beings, or saving in this world, not being able to save in another world. [If that's the case] then there is discrimination! Therefore, it is said that [Buddhism] benefits all sentient beings, that is, it benefits all sentient beings who are saved, causing those sentient beings to practice the three vehicles together without any difference. You just need to practice according to the Dharma taught by the Buddha, starting with the Three Refuges and that's it! Using Mahayana faith to practice the Three Refuges, what you focus on is what you rely on, returning to your own mind. That's the end.

All dharmas have reached the ultimate, that is, your ordinary thought in the present is the ultimate. “Taking refuge” is taking refuge in your mind, taking refuge in the three vehicles of path and fruition, or taking refuge in Buddhahood. That is a place that is separate (not together) compared to all living beings in the world. This is specifically about Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, not only separate from all sentient beings in the world, but also different from all sentient beings belonging to the Sravaka Vehicle and the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle of the transcendent world. The Buddha is great and compassionate, immeasurable love, compassion, joy, and equanimity, unlike the Two Vehicles. Why not together (not together)? Next, [the main sutra] talks about the Second Vehicle. The Second Vehicle is only for oneself, not for sentient beings. Sentient beings suffer, they do not care, nor do they save them. Because Buddhas and Bodhisattvas can eliminate all the sufferings of birth and death for sentient beings. Birth and death are caused by the afflictions of sentient beings. In the cycle of birth and death, sentient beings have boundless suffering. [Buddhas and Bodhisattvas] make them stop and end the cycle of birth and death and suffering, and stop spinning in the six paths of reincarnation. So what will be attained? Achieving Nirvana, peace and Bodhi. Bodhi is enlightenment, because it is enlightened, because it is not born, it is not destroyed. Nirvana is unborn, immortal, achieving ultimate peace, that is called Luan. I explain this word Luan as "preaching the Dharma". That is what is called the ultimate, having reached the Vo Tran Cau. Without Hands and Actions, there is no power of action and no action (there is no doer or thing to be done), and there is no grasping. That is called "attainment". Such peace and happiness, "as an attendant, famous as the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas of the Infinite Elements of the Wheel of Action" (thus is called the Wheel of the Infinite Elements of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas).

Because of all dharmas, there are no strange obstacles. Because the sun's light shines all the way through, the three vehicles of energy, depending on their doubts, proclaim the Dharma without any attachments. The Tathagata and all sentient beings preach the Dharma as it is, because it is like space, with no different characteristics, and has immeasurable Concentration and solemnity as the abbot, and all sentient beings preach the wonderful Dharma, without any attachments. The great one, armed with all Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, preached the Dharma altruistically, with the egret serving as this, and preached the dharmas of non-existence, non-emptiness, non-emptiness The name Tathagata refers to Bodhisattvas, sentient beings who preach the wonderful Dharma of the middle land.
The sky shines all over. For the three vehicles, according to the appropriate basis, they preach the Dharma without attachment. That is, the Tathagata speaks the Dharma like that in the void, using immeasurable and dignified concentration, teaching the wonderful Dharma without attachment. That is, all Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas preach the Dharma in the same way non-existence, non-emptiness, non-existence of form, non-separation of emptiness, up to non-existence of emptiness of These are called Tathagata and Bodhisattvas who preach the wonderful Dharma in the Lands for all living beings.

“Van ha names the Wheel of No Hands?” (What is called the Wheel of No Hands?): [In the previous part], combine these two things to say; now separated. First let's talk about Vo Tran Cau Hanh Luan. Next, talk about the Wheel of Wushrin.

“Because all dharmas have no hindrances, because the sun's spectrum shines completely” (That is, they are not attached to all dharmas, like sunlight shines all over): In the previous part, use moonlight to visualize the elimination of our brain heat. In this section, use sunlight to visualize the elimination of darkness. Sunlight shines on everything. Regarding all the Sravaka Vehicles, Pratyekabuddha Vehicles, and Bodhisattva Vehicles, what dharma should that person use to attain salvation, then speak that dharma, appropriate to the capacity. Whatever dharma corresponds to that person, then speak that dharma. All sentient beings, up to the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, have attachments. The Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas no longer have Ego Clinging, they have cut off Ego Clinging, but still have Dharma Clinging. [They think] “The self is false, the Dharma is real.” Therefore, in the Vajra Sutra, the Buddha told Subhuti: “Knowing the self preaches the Dharma, like the Buddha's example, the above Dharma is satisfied with the Dharma, the other side is not the Dharma”, [meaning] you should know that the Dharmas I told you before are to save you from birth and death, like a boat to cross a river. Once you've crossed the river, you don't need a boat anymore, so why are you still attached?

Speaking of the Dharma, according to the basis for preaching the Dharma, [those mentioned dharmas] are all the Dharma, allowing them to attain salvation is called the Dharma. It's not true, no matter how much you talk about the Dharma, it still can't eliminate attachments, it can't eliminate suffering, it's still not the Dharma! Because they (listeners) don't understand. [Truth dharma is the dharma] that makes sentient beings no longer have attachments! The Tathagata Buddhas, for the sake of sentient beings, speak such dharma, what dharma is that? Next, [the text lists] such dharmas as spoken by the Buddha. “As it is” is a word to refer to dharma, to refer to certain things. What are such dharmas? That Dharma seems to be empty, with no distinct appearance. “General” is all things built in space. Emptiness itself has no distinct appearance. To all sentient beings of all paths in the three vehicles, the Buddha spoke of countless types of Concentration. There are countless types of Concentration. Concentration is not just sitting still and not saying anything, the six senses being motionless is Concentration! It's not like that at all! Concentration means all actions are in Concentration. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas see illusory beings, and the dharma spoken by the Buddha is also illusory. When saving sentient beings, it is like we are playing (“du hý”). What are you playing? “Freely and dignified abbot” means the Buddha preached the Dharma to abbot, abbot right in the Dharma, dignified that Dharma, but in reality, there is no such Dharma!

“The living beings who preach the wonderful dharma, have no attachments, have great support” (Because the living beings speak the wonderful dharma, have no attachments, have complete great support): “Fully have the great armor” is when fighting with the afflictions of living beings, there is no fear, no suffering from sentient beings. pollution. If the practice is not deep and has no concentration, the original purpose is to save sentient beings, but in the end it will turn out to be exactly like sentient beings, tainted by sentient beings! If you develop an attachment to the dharma, or develop an attachment to the appearance of sentient beings, that is not the ultimate meaning. At first, if [you say it] like that it won't work, you have to know when and what dharma to preach!

What is Vo Tran Cau Luan like? Buddhist practice of Wu Hanh Luan. The Wheel of Action is the Wheel of No Hand and Action, [which means] not holding on to all dharmas, that is, from within its movement, Action is "motion", in all its effects, wisdom and skillful means are not fundamental, but illusory. That kind of skillful means is the wonderful dharma.

What is the miraculous Dharma? Next, [the main sutra] explains the wonderful dharma. Don't be attached to anything, there's nothing to be attached to. “Great armored armor” (Complete large armored armor): What is a large armored armor? Meaning Emptiness, all are inactive! Therefore, it is said that Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, that is, Great Bodhisattva, [in Sanskrit] is Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, Ma Ha translated means Great, when saving sentient beings, or benefiting sentient beings, His compassion, joy and forgiveness is the greatest, the greatest of all dharmas, so it is called the Form. Sentient beings can clearly understand their own mind, [understand] the form of their own mind, and will preach the Dharma to sentient beings, that is, speak (preach the Dharma) like that. [Therefore, the main sutra says] “herons dress like thi” (same thing).

“The theory of the dharmas of non-existence, non-emptiness, non-emptiness that is form-emptiness, non-separation of form-emptiness, non-separation of emptiness, non-emptiness of consciousness, non-separation of emptiness” (Says the dharmas of non-existence, non-emptiness, non-emptiness, non-emptiness, non-emptiness, up to and including non-emptiness, non-emptiness): Dharma by the Buddha said not to be attached to appearance. Saying Yes, sentient beings are immediately attached to Yes. Speaking of Suffering, really suffering, three sufferings, eight sufferings, up to countless sufferings, birth, old age, sickness, death, suffering, love must be separated, five skandhas are illustrious, praying for nothing, what you wish for cannot achieve the goal, suffering because of death. Every individual has the suffering of not being able to pray! Birth suffering, illness suffering. [Sentient beings] have forgotten suffering. Regarding the suffering when you were born, you are confused and do not remember. You don't remember the pain of going back and forth. Speaking of the dharmas of Yes; If it says Yes, sentient beings become attached. The Buddha did not say Yes, in Mahayana teachings they all say “non-Existence”. That Existence is not Existence (non-Existence), non-Existence is not Emptiness! Non-emptiness is not Existence! That's not true! That is talking about the meaning of Emptiness. That Emptiness is not empty as you are attached to. Because of your attachment to [emptiness], it is said to be non-emptiness; As for your attachment to Existence, it is said to be non-Existence.

All dharmas have two aspects: Existence and Emptiness, non-existence and non-emptiness is the Middle Way. Not saying the decision is Yes, but also not saying the decision is No. No means Yes, Yes means No. Emptiness is in Being, Being is in Emptiness. That is “Form is Emptiness, Emptiness is Form”; that is in general. In general, “dharmas are neither Existence nor Emptiness”.

Next, differentiate each thing. First of all, we talk about Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness. We are not talking about the Five Aggregates. The Dharma of the Five Aggregates is also Emptiness. Form itself is Emptiness, right? Having left Form, do you say Emptiness in place of Form? Or is it the word that separates from Form to say Emptiness? Where Form says Emptiness, it is inherently Yes. For example, this flower, we say this flower is Emptiness, right? No is Yes, but it does not really exist, because it has no self. Saying it is “non-Existence” means from the place of Being that it is “non-Existence”, saying “non-Existence” is Emptiness, but non-emptiness! Currently there is still a specific truth that exists, why not? Regarding this issue, you must be enlightened and research!

Like this body of ours, yes or no? Authenticity is there. A person's name and appearance both exist, but that person is not something that truly exists, because it can change and has no nature of its own. Our bodies are composed of the Four Great Elements, i.e. Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind. The Shurangama Sutra speaks of seven elements, that is, with the addition of Emptiness, Base, and Consciousness. Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind make up the body, but without Emptiness it is not possible? Everyone can ask: Why does our body have empty space? In your abdomen, there are gaps between the five internal organs and six organs, between this organ and that organ. If there is no space and stick together into a mass, each organ will lose its effectiveness. Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind are separated. If there was no air in your stomach, could you still survive? Without water, nothing can exist. If there was no air, you would immediately stop breathing! When a person reaches the final moment of death, he/she neither eats nor drinks, and can still live for a few days, but once the qi is cut off, he/she will die. Therefore, Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Emptiness, Base, and Consciousness [are collectively known as the Seven Elements].

Therefore, for all dharmas, first state the Form dharma. Is form dharma Emptiness? Form is neither Emptiness nor Existence, is it “Form is Emptiness”, or “Emptiness is Form”? Both sides are crazy! Is that form Emptiness? Still can't say that! Form is not "itself Emptiness", and Emptiness is not "itself Form" either! Emptiness is Emptiness, Form is Form; Form is Form, Emptiness is Emptiness. It's not just the Physical Dharma that's like that, but Feelings, Perceptions, Actions, and Consciousness [are also like that], [the main sutra] summarizes the three categories of Perception, Actions, and Consciousness. “Nai chi” has the meaning of “reduced”.

“Non-emptiness is Feeling, non-action is Emptiness, Non-Perception” (Not “it is Emptiness of Feeling”, not “it is Emptiness of Actions”, not “it is Emptiness of Perception”): For these things there is no repetition. Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness are all like that. Speaking of the Aggregates, neither the Aggregates are Emptiness nor the Emptiness the Aggregates, that is the meaning. That is the Five Aggregates of Form. [So] when Being (existence) is it Emptiness, or when Separation (separation) is Emptiness? “Tie” is not correct, and “Ly” is also not correct! It's not Tuc, it's not Ly. Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, that is, talking about the six senses, so “not being the Eye of Emptiness, not being separated from the Eye of Emptiness”, “nau will” are again shortened [to speak directly to] “not being the Mind Emptiness, not being separated from the Mind Emptiness”. What is omitted? Eliminate the four intermediate senses, that is, omit the ears, nose, tongue and body, and use “nau chi” to [express the meaning of] “say it in passing”. For each group of dharmas, it is said in the same way. The six hundred volumes of the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra say it again and again, in such a twist. Because there is no simplification, there is no word “near will”, all six things are stated, each dharma is exposed; That's why the texts in the [Great Prajna] scriptures are many. That's what it means.

In other sutras, he used the two words “nai chi” to summarize. Therefore, in this passage, you understand one meaning in it, and then understand the whole, “non-Thing, non-lying”, that is the meaning of the Middle Way. “Tuc” is neither, nor is Ly! You read the Mahayana sutras, disassemble the four sentences, absolutely not[12], no matter how you say it, it's not correct. The Four Owls are “yes, no, neither yes nor no, neither yes nor no”. That's called Four Owls. That is, “Form is Emptiness” is not correct, “departing from Form is Emptiness” is also not correct, “departing from Consciousness is Emptiness” is also not correct, “Consciousness is Emptiness” is also not correct. That is the meaning of “separate four sentences” (separate from four sentences). “Non-emptiness is the emptiness of Form, non-separation from Form is emptiness”, until “Non-being is emptiness of Dharma, non-separation from emptiness of Dharma”, why say it again? There is no mention of Form and Mind Dharma (i.e. Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma). First talk about Form Dharma (Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste), then talk about Mind Dharma (Dharma). Mind is Dharma, when it comes to mind dharma, it is also “non-Consciousness, non-Less”. Then we talk about the Six Consciousnesses, “non-emptiness of Eye Consciousness, non-separation of Emptiness of Eye Consciousness”. Next, it is shortened, until the Eye, Ear, Tongue, Tongue, Body, Mind, six consciousnesses, “nothing even non-Consciousness, non-separation of Consciousness”: “Separation” is not possible, and “Consciousness” is also not possible. That is also the meaning of “non-Tinh non-ly”.

“Non-existence is emptiness of the Desire Realm, non-separation from the Desire Realm is emptiness, non-separation is the emptiness of the Boundless Land of Emptiness”, it has said quite a lot in general. The Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm are all omitted. The six heavens of Desire Realm and the eighteen heavens of Form Realm are omitted, immediately speaking of the Four Heavenly Emptiness, that is, the Heavenly Land of Infinite Consciousness, the Heavenly Land of Nothingness, the Heavenly Land of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception, and the Heavenly Land of Infinite Emptiness. The Four Heavens are neither Emptiness nor Existence. The Four Heavenly Emptiness is established in emptiness, should it be Emptiness? That's not true! Because they (the gods) reside in that heaven and are conscious. They think it doesn't exist, but in reality it still exists! The Land of Nothingness does not originally exist, but the word Land is added, [meaning] "still exists". Non-Existence means non-existence, the word Land is added because they believe that being born in heaven still means having a country, just like we have a place to live. The Four Heavens are pagan heavens, but [those who have attained] Arhatship are also in the Four Heavens. Abiding in different heavens, they enter that Concentration and abide in the right concentration, while the Four Meditations and Eight Concentrations are in the Concentration of Boundless Consciousness, the Land of Nothingness... Those who enter the Concentration will go to that heaven. [The Four Meditations and Eight Concentrations and the Arhat's Samadhi] are called [combined] the Nine Concentrations.

In the Dhamma of Existence, many such examples have been given. Here is to point out the holy path, the dharma taught by the Buddha such as the Four Foundations of Mindfulness, the Four Fulfillments of Mind, the Five Faculties, the Five Powers, the Seven Bodhisattvas (Seven Enlightenment Factors), the Noble Eightfold Path, the thirty-seven paths, these are all the holy dharma of Bodhi. [The main sutra says in general summary] “that is, the Four Mindfulness of the Land of Emptiness, or the separation of the Four Mindfulness of the Land of Emptiness”, then use the word “nau chi” to abridge, [say immediately] “the eight limbs of the noble path of emptiness, separated from the eight limbs of the noble path of emptiness” that is, to omit [the intermediate dharmas. To be specific, the Four Right Efforts, the Four Fulfilling Minds, the Five Faculties, the Five Strengths, and the Seven Bodhisattvas are all omitted and not discussed in detail. The Dharma taught by the Buddha is also like that. Not only are worldly dharmas emptiness, but the dharma spoken by the Buddha is also emptiness, but one cannot cling to emptiness. Anyone who is biased towards Emptiness is the View of Ending. Bias towards the Right is the Permanent View. If it is not the attachment to Permanence, it will be the attachment to Sections. It's not the attachment to Yes, it's the attachment to No. That is all the meaning of Prajna.

The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, which teaches about Existence and Suffering, wants to make you bored. It is impossible to determine whether a sutra is absolutely Mahayana or Hinayana. In that, there will be a part involved. For example, in the Prajnaparamita Sutra, everything is understood from “no Existence, no Emptiness”. Point out those signs because the Buddha spoke of those dharmas, the world has those signs, the three realms of twenty-five existences all have those signs! We must clearly understand Feelings and Lying from within. That is, from Form one can say Emptiness, from Emptiness one can say Form. Separation from Form and Emptiness, i.e. Form and Emptiness. Leaving the Four Mindfulness Pillars of Emptiness, or “that is, the Four Mindfulness Pillars of Emptiness” is not correct. It's okay to understand this meaning! That's called magic. Therefore, those who study Buddhism should understand the meaning of perfection. No matter how attached you are, it's not right. That is to destroy attachments, so tell them the dharma of attachments.

We often talk about dependent origination. Dharmas that arise dependently and arise without self-nature. The dharma of dependent origination is Emptiness and Existence. Thus, “non-dependent arising of emptiness”, it is not that the dependent arising of emptiness itself is Emptiness, nor is it “separation of dependent origination of emptiness”. Understand the nature of emptiness and dependent origination. These things are all talking about emptiness, talking about many things, all of which are emptiness. Why is there dependent origination? Dependent origination is all kinds of causes and conditions, made up of many kinds of conditions. If there is a lack of conditions, the dharma will not be successful, that is the meaning. If you understand the principle of dependent origination and emptiness, you will understand all of these principles. There are not many sutras that specialize in dependent origination anymore! The dharma of dependent origination, that is, the dharma of dependent origination is emptiness, leaving the dharma of dependent origination is emptiness. Before each dharma, add the word Phi (not), which means, as you say, "it's just talk, it has no real meaning". Dharma talk is not dharma. If you leave words and talk, is there Yes? Away from speech, what else is there to show? Cannot display! When it comes to Truth, when it comes to the end, there are no words.

“There is only talk, it has no real meaning”: Just say it, whatever you say is not that thing, but it is not false talk. Don't pay attention to that, it's not false talk, it's not like that! Whatever you talk about is not [really] that thing! When it comes to something, it is just a way of representing, a symbol. For example, when we talk about Fire, the Fire [in your words] is absolutely not [real] Fire. If there is Fire in that statement, it will burn you. You should understand this meaning, whatever you talk about is not that thing. When you talk about Truong Tam, Truong Tam is a symbol. “Truong Tam” [in your statement] is not Truong Tam himself, it is just a symbol for him. Since it's a symbol, Truong Tam is fine, Truong Tu is fine, you can change it to Truong Ngu, you can change it to anything. Symbols can be arbitrarily changed, they are not real entities. From this, you can understand!

Our original mind, our true heart, cannot be expressed in all languages. That is called “ly Chan Nhu”. The Mahayana Arising of Faith, the Mahayana scriptures all call it “separation from true speech”, separation from “language ceases, mental activity ceases”. If you want to think and observe, you will see that they are all non-existent. If you observe it, you will be wrong, “bach phi” means this meaning. As long as you stir up your thoughts, you are already wrong. This meaning is very deep, not the original meaning of this sutra!

[Words] Tam Bat Ho just talks about the Buddha, that is: Buddha's body, speech, and mind are three pure good karma. Whatever he does arbitrarily, whatever he does with his body is good, achieving truth, goodness, beauty, ultimate purity, forever free from mistakes, no need to prevent or preserve anymore. “Ho” [in Tam Bat Ho] means “to preserve and prevent”. Buddha does not need to prevent and preserve, but Arhats and Bodhisattvas still have to prevent and preserve. All actions of body, speech, and mind must be paid attention to, because the body, speech, and mind [of Arhats and Bodhisattvas] still have ignorance and subtle habits.

Once upon a time, in India there was a venerable man whose habit had lasted for countless eons

is now extremely heavy. Because from countless lifetimes up to now, if he is not a king, then he is a great rich man, infected with the habit of speaking for countless lifetimes, calling others “little servant” (lowly servant). He is not arrogant at all, but out of habit. He met the Buddha, heard the Dharma, attained enlightenment, and had supernatural powers. The dragon king, heaven, and ghosts all protect him. When he crossed the river, he could not get across, so he shouted: "Little monk! Stop the flow", telling the dragon king to stop the flow. The Dragon King knew that he had attained Arhatship, so he immediately stopped the water flow to let him pass. He didn't say a word of thanks, just leave! The Dragon King then came to tell the Buddha, saying that the Venerable was too impolite, too arrogant, and complacent. The Buddha told the dragon king that the Venerable did not have the heart to look down on him, but it was due to his past habits. Even though you have attained Arhatship, you can only cut off the current Views of Thought, cut off the gross Or, but the subtle Or is not cut off, you still have habit energy. It is very difficult for us to cut off habit energy. We carry habit energy from many lifetimes. As soon as a cultivator sees it, he immediately knows your habit. Everyone knows their own habits, but changing them is very difficult. Buddha immediately told the dragon king: "Okay! Let me tell him to apologize to you, tell him to repent to you." Immediately tell that Arhat to repent to the dragon king. That Arhat said again: "Little monk, don't be angry." Ha, ha! In front of the Buddha, he still called others “little servant”. The Buddha said it was his habit, there was no way to change it. If he can change that habit, he will be a great Bodhisattva.

We have a lot of problems, each person is different. A mother gives birth to nine children, nine different children. Each person has different habits, different seeds, absolutely not the same. Therefore, cultivators must preserve three karmas. That is called Tam Bat Ho. “The Three Realms are empty”: The Three Realms do not exist. Buddha's three karmas do not exist. Neither anger, nor emptiness, nor separation. Because we have left the three Unprotected things, it is said to be Empty. You say, What's wrong? Leaving the real entity, still saying No more? That is, the Three Realms are Emptiness. The Three Realms are the three karmas of Buddha's body, speech, and mind. The Buddha's body, speech, and mind karma are pure. Therefore, the Four Fearless Fears, the Ten Powers, the Eighteen Uncommunicative Dharmas, up to great kindness, great compassion, joy, and renunciation are all like that, until the Buddha attained Nirvana. Nirvana is not born, is not destroyed, is it not Emptiness? That is “that is, Nirvana is empty, separate from Nirvana is empty”, That is, it is not possible, but Ly is also not possible. Nirvana itself is "no emptiness, no death", "no birth, no death", no contamination, no purity.

Sattva declares for sentient beings. That's called Vo Tran Cau Luan. Depending on the previous acceptance, it will not be pure, there will be impurities. Therefore, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas save sentient beings but do not see sentient beings. They save sentient beings all day long but have no sentient beings to save. All day long he preached the Dharma, but he didn't say any Dharma, didn't say a single sentence, it contained such a meaning. That is not a truism. “Cutting meaning” is a separation from speech, but having speech is not cutting down teachings. Use this Wheel of No Hand to explain the wonderful dharma. When it comes to wonderful Dharma, then it is not possible to be Immediate, not to be able to Ly, it is not possible to say No, but it is also impossible to say Yes!

(Sutra) Good man! The Tathagata taught the Dharma to all sentient beings, like the full moon light, clear and unobstructed, filling the void, illuminating the realm of contact with absolutely no hindrances, widely preached. It is true that Wushand Luan teaches the wonderful dharma, because it is necessarily a dharma without any obstacles, because it is like the sun's rays shining all the way, the three vehicles of energy, depending on the season of doubt, proclaiming the true dharma, without any attachments. The Tathagata and the sentient beings preach the Dharma as it is, because it is like nothingness, with no different characteristics, and has immeasurable Concentration and solemnity as the abbot. The sentient beings preach the wonderful Dharma, with no attachments, and the spirit of the three vehicles can be entered at will. The great man is bound by all Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, altruistically preaching the Dharma in obedience to the Buddha, teaching sentient beings, reading the most profound and profound dharma, in the middle of the three vehicles, in accordance with the period of mockery, in accordance with the one vehicle, of the good roots of the species, of attaining maturity, in accordance with the one vehicle, in the midst of good abiding, In the midst of birth and death, the evil and unwholesome dharmas increase, and the spirit of Nirvana is solid and never regresses.
(Sutra: O good man! In the same way, the Tathagata uses the Earthless Elements for the sake of all sentient beings. The wheel to preach the Dharma is like the light of the full moon, clear and unobstructed, pervading all of space, illuminating all realms without obstructions. In general, using the Wheel of No Head to speak of the wonderful Dharma, it is unobstructed, like the light of the sun that shines throughout all the three vehicles, according to each appropriate air, the Dharma is declared without attachment. That is, the Tathagata speaks the Dharma like that, as if the void has no form In other words, using immeasurable Samadhi, he solemnly and solemnly presides, for sentient beings to speak wonderful and wonderful Dharma without attachment, causing the three vehicles to enter according to the appropriate temperament. All the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas who are fully equipped with great armor preach the Dharma for others in the same way. This causes sentient beings to listen to this very profound and supreme Dharma. From within the three vehicles, they will enter into one vehicle according to their liking. All good roots will be ripened, and they will abide perfectly in it. one vehicle, complete does not cause them to develop all kinds of evil, unwholesome dharmas in samsara, makes them steadfast and irreversible towards Nirvana).

Due to the Infinite Elements, the Elemental Wheel is like moonlight: The full moon is clear, unobstructed, the moonlight fills the entire void, illuminating all realms without obstructions. The moonlight shines brightly, the moon does not give rise to the idea of ​​shining brightly, but naturally it is like that. The receiver does not think to receive, nor does he have any thoughts of wanting to receive. Dharma is marvelous, in all dharmas there is no entanglement, no attachment. No entanglement, no hindrance, that is, “it is not existence, it is not non-existence, it is existence, it is emptiness” are all impossible. “Because the sun's spectrum shines all the way” (For example, the sunlight shines all over): The sun rises, the darkness on the earth disappears. The Buddha towards the Three Vehicles, namely Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas, according to the Dharma they relied on, the Buddha preached the Dharma not because He wanted to preach the Dharma, but because living beings needed it. Once the foundation is ripe, the Buddha will preach the Dharma. Every dharma that is said is "if you don't ask, you won't say it", and it has a cause and effect. Because he was invited, the Buddha spoke; There is also support, great Bodhisattvas come to help educate. Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, they do not need to listen to the Dharma, but they come to help the Buddha propagate and teach, to prove: The reason they attained enlightenment is because they practiced and attained [those mentioned dharmas].

“No attachment”: For all dharmas, there is no attachment. For the sake of sentient beings, speak such Dharma. The Dharma is like this “due to being like space, without difference in appearance” (like space, without difference in appearance). From the dharmas spoken by the Buddha, we know that there is worldly cause and effect, extra-worldly cause and effect, and good and evil retribution. These are all words that correspond to one's base. In emptiness, there is no this form, there is no that form. If there is a form, it is that form itself.

“Immeasurable Concentration traveling freely and dignified the abbot” means using immeasurable Concentration subjects to solemnly adorn the abbot. What abbot is that? Abbot of this wonderful dharma, abbot but not abbot! “Decorating living beings is really not dignified. Tin the name of being dignified” (Dorning living beings but really not being dignified. That's called being dignified): That's using a saying in the Diamond Sutra. Do not be attached to the words in this sutra. As for liberation, only with bondage can there be liberation. Without being bound, there can be no talk of liberation. If you don't bind, you won't untie it. Without bondage, there will be no liberation! Sentient beings end their afflictions and attain Bodhi. Are there afflictions that can be eliminated? There is no affliction to end, is there Bodhi to be realized? Layperson Truong Vo Chien[13] said the following two sentences: “If you eliminate afflictions and increase illness”, that is to say you want to eliminate afflictions, it will increase another level of illness! What's the increase? The affliction. That "break" is a disease. “Animals who turn to Chan Such Dec are evil”, evil knowledge and wrong views! If you want to aim (towards, enter) Truth to realize the True Form, then it is all wrong view. That is to reach the ultimate meaning. Just by opening your mouth, you're wrong, missing the four sentences, absolutely no. Is it right to say nothing? Why did the Buddha rebuke the dumb monks? The dumb monk doesn't know what to do! Only if you enter, you will know.

These are all true meanings in the Mahayana definitive meaning that you must realize. The meaning of the wonderful Dharma is to make you not attached to anything, aiming to achieve such a goal! Let sentient beings listen to anything without attachment; No attachment to anything. When the Buddha preached the Dharma, countless millions of sentient beings came to listen to the Dharma. Someone asked me: "Master, how many people were there in India at that time?" I said: "I don't know either, how do I know how many people India has? At least not as many as it is now!" That person asked again: "Are there that many people in the Buddha's sermon assembly?" I said: "That's not human!" That person asked: "If it's not human, then what is it?" "Gods and Bodhisattvas come from other worlds, in the void." “Can this world tolerate it?” I said: "That's your view." Such an explanation is completely wrong, it is called attachment. The Buddha preached the Dharma in the void, the sound of the Dharma spoken by Him filled all places.

There was a magician who preached the Dharma. As long as there were five or more people, he would stop speaking. We were at Phap Nguyen Pagoda, when the old monks preached the precepts, there was a group of every fifty people [ordaining precepts], still not in time. Doing so is not legal. Usually one on one. You see that the great virtuous ones are truly enlightened, all transmitting the precepts one-on-one. The precept teacher asks that person, speaking correctly according to that person's (the person receiving the precepts) abilities. We do not have the ability to "suit all three senses" like the Buddha. During the Buddha's time, the Buddha spoke a passage of Dharma, there would be many people who would become enlightened, attain enlightenment, and even develop Bodhi mind. We talk about it many times, but no one develops Bodhi mind. If you do develop Bodhi mind, you don't know it, but it's not really developed. Only by reaching the First Pillar can one truly develop Bodhicitta. That is called “preaching the Dharma at your discretion”.

“Altruism preaches the Dharma, the heron obeys it like this, the spirits of living beings test the supreme and profound Dharma” (Because others preach the Dharma in the same way, allowing sentient beings to listen to this supreme and very profound Dharma): The most profound and superior Dharma is the mind. Regarding “non-being, non-separation” as mentioned above, we should not think about the words, but must be understood by our mind. Tell me, what is the true shape of your mind? Thinking is not that mind. Separated from thinking, where is our mind? You must leave your conscious mind to investigate. Whenever you seek help, you will become enlightened. Using a discriminating mind, you go to the old monk and ask him to explain. If you develop a discriminating mind throughout your life, he will beat you. That is a very profound meaning!

Like Venerable Cau Chi, people came to question him, no matter who asked, he used a finger to teach Zen, whoever came to ask was enlightened. No matter who asked for the Dharma, he would raise a finger, and the person who came would immediately be enlightened, immediately bow their head and worship, thanking him. One day he was not at home, only one young disciple was present. Another person came to ask about the Dharma, [the disciple] said that the master was not at home, so that person asked: "What is the intention of the founder coming from the West?" The little disciple then stretched out his hand. Oh! That person was very happy, bowed his head in gratitude, and left, enlightened! Master returned and asked: "Is anyone coming?" The disciple replied: "Someone has come to request Dharma." The master said again: "How do you answer?" The little disciple replied: "I imitated the teacher. He asked what the founder's intention was from the West, so I immediately did this..." The teacher asked again: "What was his expression like?" "He bowed his head in thanks, saying he was enlightened." Venerable Cau Chi asked: "Are you enlightened or not?" “I don't know.” "Okay! I ask you, what is the intention of the founder coming from the West?" The disciple then raised a finger, and the teacher immediately slashed that finger off with a knife! The pain was so much that the disciple screamed and groaned. [Teacher scolded]: "Stop screaming, do it again!" The little disciple tried to endure the pain, but Venerable Cau Chi asked again: "What is the intention of the Patriarch coming from the West?" The disciples immediately became enlightened, but there was no pain!

Is everyone enlightened or not? What do you realize? First there is Yes, then there is No, not No, not Yes. It's not Yes, there's nothing, so I say No. Otherwise, what else can I say! Since it's nothing, let's talk about Nothing! Let's take our time and explore! In the above description, many reasons have been mentioned, but there is no reason to say. If you say it, you will fall into the Second Meaning, Third Meaning, forever mistaken, unable to understand. How to do it? Based on the teachings, based on the scriptures to see. This will be very tiring, reading, worshiping, and repenting. If you truly have the ability, you will immediately suddenly realize great enlightenment. Even if you are enlightened, you still have to learn from the beginning. Even though you are enlightened, you do not yet have the ability and are still not a Buddha. That is called "enlightening the Buddha's teachings".

In the three vehicles, depending on your heart's desire, "depending on the one vehicle, the good roots of the race, the stage of attaining maturity" (depending on which vehicle you want to move towards, all good roots will ripen): The good roots sown in the past have all matured. “Depending on the one vehicle, one is extremely good at abiding” means: Any vehicle is fine, extremely skillful in abiding, that is, that person can cut off Or, attain Truth, remain motionless, no longer experience the cycle of birth and death!

(Sutra) Good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva has immeasurable destruction, countless sentient beings circulate in birth and death, and altruistically preach the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac attained the position of self-destructing the cycle of birth and death and altruistically preached the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva is an immeasurable spirit, countless sentient beings save the four streams, altruistically preach the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac were born in the spiritual position of the fourth generation, altruistically preaching the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva eliminates immeasurable, countless sentient beings' afflictions and illnesses, and altruistically preaches the Dharma. Thanh Van and Single Enlightened One can self-eliminate all afflictions and diseases and preach the Dharma altruistically. Bodhisattva Mahasattva destroys sentient beings' Aggregates of afflictions and habit energies continuously and without residue, altruistically preaches the Dharma. Shravaka and Single Enlightenment attains the position of cutting off the Aggregates of afflictions and habit energies continuously and endlessly remaining, altruistically preaches the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieved great compassion and great compassion, great compassion for others, and altruistically preached the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac are extremely compassionate, extremely compassionate, without great compassion, and altruistically preach the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva, all sentient beings who have fixed thoughts, preach the Dharma. Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha, sentient beings without any thought, preach the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva means to altruistically forgive suffering sentient beings and altruistically preach the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac attained the position of selfishness, possessing suffering, and altruistically preached the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva fulfills the Dharma position of all sentient beings, altruistically preaches the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac were self-satisfied with their dharma status and altruistically preached the Dharma. Bodhisattva Mahasattva enlightens all sentient beings and altruistically preaches the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac attained the position of self-righteousness, triumphed over the Dharma, and altruistically preached the Dharma.
(Sutra: O good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat for the sake of ending the cycle of birth and death of nothingness Bodhisattva Mahasattva preaches the Dharma for others. Shravaka and Single Enlightenment preach the Dharma only for the sake of others to overcome the fourdfalls In order to eliminate the afflictions of countless sentient beings, Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas only teach the Dharma to eliminate their own afflictions and afflictions for others. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat preaches the Dharma to completely eliminate the continuous afflictions of the Aggregates of sentient beings Even if you have nothing left over, you preach the Dharma for others. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat teaches the Dharma for the sake of others. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat does not use great compassion as the cause. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat preaches the Dharma for them. Pratyekabuddha does not care for living beings but for them The Bodhisattva Mahasattva preaches the Dharma in order to end all suffering for all other sentient beings. Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha only preach the Dharma for the sake of others. Bodhisattva Mahasattva preaches the Dharma for the sake of others. Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha preach the Dharma for others Enlightenment preaches the Dharma for the sake of attaining the superior Dharma for oneself.)

We often say that the Second Vehicles also hold alms bowls, people invite them to preach the Dharma, they also preach the Dharma; But their purpose is only to end birth and death, to stop the cycle of birth and death for themselves. They preach the Dharma with no intention of causing living beings to eliminate birth and death. That is the difference between the Second Vehicle and the Bodhisattva. Everything they (the Second Vehicle) did was for themselves, not to preach the Dharma to save countless sentient beings who are in the cycle of birth and death. Bodhisattva Mahasattva causes all immeasurable and countless sentient beings to cross the four waterfalls and preach the Dharma for them. The four falls are the four basic types of birth and death, until the last type is “ignorance burst” (the cascade of ignorance). Thanh Van and Doc Giac are not like that, they only want to escape their own four waterfalls. They preach the Dharma to sentient beings purely for themselves, not for others.

The Bodhisattva who preached the Dharma never thought of himself. Everything the Bodhisattva does is for the sake of saving sentient beings. When we recite the Samantabhadra Vow, or recite the Pure Virtue, [we will see] that no matter what happens to Him, he always thinks of Buddha Dharma, that is, thinks of sentient beings, only hoping that sentient beings can become Buddhas. Every sentence is like that, whatever happens, “pray for sentient beings” (pray for sentient beings), pray for them to end afflictions, attain Bodhi, all are vows for them to cut off the stream of birth and death, enter Omniscience, it is all like that. Thanh Van and Doc Giac are not like that.

Bodhisattva Mahasattva preaches the Dharma in order to eliminate the diseases and afflictions of countless and countless living beings. The Bodhisattva preaches the Dharma with the aim of causing all sentient beings to attain the Truth and no longer cycle in birth and death. “The Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas themselves eliminate all afflictions and diseases, and altruistically preach the Dharma” [meaning] Bodhisattvas preach the Dharma to eliminate the illnesses and afflictions of sentient beings, not for themselves, while Practitioners and Sravakas preach the Dharma to eliminate their own illnesses and afflictions but for others. "Bodhisattva Mahasattva, by cutting off the continuous disturbing habits of living beings, the Aggregates of afflictions and habitual energies, without any residue, altruistically preaches the Dharma" (Bodhisattva Mahasattva, by cutting off the continuously afflicting habits of the Aggregates of sentient beings, causes them to be completely clean, with no residue remaining, but preaches the Dharma for others): Although he himself has not yet become a Buddha, he makes all sentient beings become Buddhas. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is always in the Bodhisattva position, but many of the sentient beings he has transformed have become Buddhas. In the Ksitigarbha Sutra, the Buddhas from the ten directions [attending the Dharma Assembly in the Dao Loi heaven] were all saved and taught by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to become Buddhas. He himself is still a Bodhisattva, that is the great Bodhisattva nature. Not only does it help sentient beings to cut off their afflictions, the Aggregates, that is, Form, Feeling, Thoughts, Actions, Consciousness, and the Five Aggregates of afflictions, but they also hope to cut off their habitual energies, not allowing habitual energies to continue, not allowing afflictions to continue, causing all afflictions to be completely wiped out, with no residue left. That's how he preached the Dharma to sentient beings!

“Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat achieved the result of great compassion at the same stream” (Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat because of the achievement of great compassion at the end stream): Great compassion as a cause, preaching the Dharma for others. His great compassion is equal. “Save”: The same type as Save, [implies] making all sentient beings be like Him, achieving perfect Bodhi. He used great compassion as the cause, hoping that all sentient beings would develop great compassion, and preach the Dharma to them in order to save all sentient beings. Thanh Van and Doc Giac preached the Dharma not because of great compassion and ultimate fruition. They are not for equality. “Equity” means making all living beings equal to us, all of the same type. “Save” is a type. Bodhisattva Mahasattva, thinking about sentient beings, preaches the Dharma. “Conscientious mindfulness” is “to protect, bless, receive blessings”, using a mind of great compassion, compassion, joy, and forgiveness to receive sentient beings. Receiving them like this, preaching the Dharma to them; What about Thanh Van and Doc Giac? They, for themselves, do not have great compassion, do not think, and are not like Buddha. After Śākyamuni Buddha became Buddha, whenever he met any great Bodhisattva, he would instruct him: "After I enter Nirvana, for my disciples in the Dharma-Ending Age, do not leave anyone behind, it is all for me to save them, causing them to leave birth and death". To each great Bodhisattva, he gave such instructions, whether Avalokitesvara, Ksitigarbha, Manjushri, Samantabhadra, He gave such instructions. At the same time, we set up all kinds of methods and methods to teach you the fate of reciting the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Three Jewels of Sangha. Thanh Van and Duyen Giac did not care like that. Bodhisattva, in order to end the suffering of all sentient beings, to end the suffering of all sentient beings, preached the Dharma to them, causing them to attain peace. Thanh Van and Doc Giac, in order to eliminate all their own suffering, preach the Dharma to others, not for others, but for themselves. They do what they need to do [to help themselves liberate] like that. For whom? For yourself!

“Bodhisattva Mahasattva fulfills all sentient beings' taste of the Dharma, altruistically preaches the Dharma" (Bodhisattva, in order to make all sentient beings perfect the taste of the Dharma, preaches the Dharma for them): Whatever we eat, we are greedy for its delicious taste. Dharma has a dharma taste, that is, the flavor of dharma. The great Bodhisattvas instruct us so that you can study the Dharma diligently, joyfully, and happily, which means you have achieved the taste of the Dharma, and achieved peace. Having achieved clear food, it will eliminate heat and famine for you. As long as we have the taste of dharma, we will have dharma. Bodhisattva preaches the Dharma like that. As for Thanh Van and Doc Giac, they only aim to satisfy their own dharma taste, not for the sake of sentient beings. They preach dharma to sentient beings to satisfy their own dharma taste.

“Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat of all sentient beings overcomes the dharma” (Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat for making sentient beings achieve the supreme dharma wisdom): From the dharma, the supreme light and wisdom are born. “Minh” is enlightenment, enlightenment means clarity. The triangle of complete enlightenment means self-awareness, awareness of others, and perfect enlightenment. Regarding those three types of enlightenment, now we can only seek self-realization. We don't have the intelligence, we don't have the strength! When the Bodhisattva preaches the Dharma to sentient beings, it will cause all sentient beings to attain the supreme Dharma and be able to give birth to light and wisdom. Because of that, we preach the Dharma to sentient beings. Thanh Van and Doc Giac preached the Dharma for others only because they achieved superior Dharma insight.

(Sutra) Good man! Of course, Bodhisattva and Mahasattva are boundless in their precepts and rules, with universal knowledge of eliminating all sentient beings' great ignorance, great fear of all things, all destruction, attaining great light, attaining great names, truly enlightening All-Wisdom, and altruistically preaching the Dharma. Thanh Van and Doc Giac have only a small portion of the law and doubt, have attained the position of eliminating the darkness of ignorance, attained a small amount of light, gained a small name, are truly enlightened and have a small portion of dharma wisdom, and altruistically preach the Dharma. Good man! Thanh Van, Doc Giac, non-existence u tha really longs for thoughts, non-existence u tha truly feels sorrow, non-existence u tha truly does not despise, non-existence u tha truly benefits, non-existence u tha truly exalts, non-existence u tha truly practices recommendation, non-existence u tha truly exclaims, non-existence u tha truly has no delusion, praises beauty, non-existence u tha is self-centered, flexible and peaceful, non-existence u tha does not arise enlightenment of body, speech, and mind. Good man! Mahayana practitioners of non-existence are self-centered, so longing for thoughts, they preach the desire of non-existence to forgive
(Sutra: Good man!
