In short, the countless precepts of Bodhisattva Mahasattva are all In order to completely eliminate the great darkness of ignorance, great fear, and all the depravities of all sentient beings, allowing them to attain great light and great name, truly enlightenment of the All-Wisdom, they preach the Dharma for others. Thanh Van and Doc Giac's teachings are only aimed at eliminating their own darkness and ignorance, attaining small light and great name, truly enlightening themselves with some Dharma wisdom, preaching this Dharma for others Good men! Thanh Van and Doc Giac do not truly care for others, do not truly care for others, do not truly care about others, do not despise or tease others, do not truly benefit others, do not truly do things to improve others, do not truly want to praise others, do not truly praise others, do not care about themselves to make others happy, and do not give rise to happiness. The wrong karma of body, speech, and mind towards others. Good man! A person who abides in the Mahayana does not think of himself, in general, he does not develop wrong karma of body, speech, and mind towards others).

Universal Wisdom refers to Buddha, only Buddha can be called “Universal Wisdom”. “Essential language” means in short. In general, Bodhisattva Mahasattva follows countless rules and regulations. “Law” is the precepts, “discipline” is the four postures, walking, standing, sitting, lying down. Doubt is the means of the law. So all of their dharmas, all of their rules, are aimed at eliminating ignorance and darkness for all sentient beings, to the point of making sentient beings forever fearless. People who live in darkness easily develop fear; in light, fear will not arise. If you have great wisdom, you will see clearly no matter what, and there will be no sense of fear. If you don't see clearly, you won't gain wisdom and will still have to grope on the dark path. Whether the front is a trap or not, you don't know. Walking on the road, fear will arise, there will be scary things, until the loss is reduced, that is, fear of good karma will be reduced, only fear of bad karma will increase.

Listen to the Dharma for the purpose of enabling yourself to achieve great light, up to a good name. Speaking from a social perspective, reputation is the second life. If you have a good reputation, everyone who sees you will respect you, praise you, and be happy. The bad news spreads far and wide, you will encounter obstacles. It is true that the enlightenment of Omniscience makes it possible for all sentient beings to become enlightened and become Buddhas. Preaching the Dharma to them like that, Bodhisattva wants all sentient beings to become Buddhas, will cause darkness and ignorance to gradually decline, lighten wisdom and name [increase], causing them to become enlightened, eventually growing until they achieve Omniscience.

As for some of the precepts of Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha, [if we look at the appearance], we only know that the Bodhisattva's precepts are ten important precepts, forty-eight are light precepts as said in the Brahma Net Sutra. That is the Bodhisattva's ritual rules. [Meanwhile], the Bhikkhu precepts include two hundred and fifty things, eighty thousand moral conducts, and eighty thousand things in the mind, the basic precepts are two hundred and fifty things. If [based on that appearance], one thinks that the Bodhisattva precepts are very few, while the monks Thanh Van and Duyen Giac have many forbidden precepts, such an explanation is wrong. Each precept in the Brahma Net Sutra contains countless and countless precepts. In addition to Chi, there is also Action. In the precepts of monks, many things are Tathagata, that is, things that should be done. Therefore, you must know that for Bodhisattvas, whoever develops Bodhi mind will receive the Three Pure Precepts:

1) All ritual rules are included in the Rules of Ritual Precepts. As long as the Buddha teaches that something is not allowed, it is the Law.

2) For Nhat Thien Dharma Realm, whatever the Buddha wants you to do is something that should be done, you must do it. The cause of benefiting sentient beings and all good dharmas you must perform. Regardless of whether it is the Ten Virtuous Dharma, the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, or the Shravaka Dharma, you must do it all. In all dharmas, as long as they are good dharmas, you must do them. [That is Nhiep Thien Dharma Realm].

Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas are not like that, just for themselves, eliminating the darkness of ignorance, that is, eliminating their own ignorance, achieving a small amount of light. Because their mentality is not great, the benefits are very small.

“Small name”: Not a big name. In the three thousand great thousand worlds and countries in other directions, countless worlds know great Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; That's called “great name”. Not fame in this world, fame in this world is very small! “As it really is, enlightened with a little bit of dharma wisdom” (As it really is, enlightened with a little bit of dharma wisdom): They are not Omniscient Wisdom (i.e. Omniscience), but Omniscience. What is “Minority of Dharma”? Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, twelve causes and conditions. They have wisdom regarding that dharma, so they tell sentient beings such a dharma!

“Good man! Thanh Van, Doc Giac don't exist, so nostalgic for others" (Hey good man! Thanh Van and Doc Giac don't really care about others): Thanh Van and Doc Giac don't care about sentient beings, only care about themselves.

“Non-existence is truly compassionate” (Not really having mercy or compassion for others): The compassion that everyone has, that is the great compassion. Thanh Van treats living beings only for their own birth and death

I don't care about living beings.

“Non-existence is truly not contemptible, non-existence is truly beneficial” (Not truly does not despise or mock others, does not truly benefit others): Bodhisattva truly does not despise, does not ridicule others, does not harm living beings. Arhats are not like that, psychologically speaking, they do not preach the true Dharma to sentient beings. Not truly cultivating others, but truly cultivating oneself. The merit from cultivating all dharmas is dedicated to oneself, not to others. There are many Dharma friends who, after reciting the sutras or praying, just dedicate it to themselves. Telling them to dedicate themselves to the dharma realm of sentient beings, they said: "Wait until I have saved myself before speaking later."

I meet a lot of people like that, [always with the mentality]: "What do I get if I dedicate it to them? I work hard reciting it, I work hard praying, dedicating it all to them?" Not being able to dedicate like that is a Hinayana mind. But they also know how to dedicate, dedicate to themselves in the future, [thinking] what is the benefit of dedicating to others? No! They also know: When they beg for alms, someone offers food to them, then they also dedicate it to others. Buddha taught like that. If you don't dedicate it, it won't work. They must also ask that person: "You offer me food, what do you wish for, what do you want to do? You say it, I will preach the Dharma to you, and dedicate it to you." That is La Han. Bodhisattva will not be like that! Bodhisattvas receive your offerings and will be able to dedicate them until you become a Buddha, just because you get a little bit is enough!

“ Non-existent u tha really recommends, non-existent u tha really desires to exclaim, non-existent u tha truly has no fanciful songs, praises beauty” (Not really helping others to improve, not really wanting to praise others, not really not admiring, praising others): Thanh Van does not do this! “Non-existence, let alone self-centeredness of body, spirit and happiness” (Not for the sake of others but not caring about your own body, making them happy): We often say, not for the sake of peace and happiness for ourselves, we only wish for sentient beings to be free from suffering. That is the great Bodhisattva who does not make false vows. There are also ten great vows of King Samantabhadra dedicated to sentient beings, vowing to suffer on behalf of all sentient beings. Like Him in prison, "I go to prison, you get out". If you are sick, "I will bear it for you, you will be healthy", great Bodhisattvas can indeed do it [like that].

There are many Dharma friends who have made that vow; Later, when you were burned by fire, you made a vow to replace someone else who was sick and that person recovered. When you get sick, you should not hold resentment. At that time, we will succeed in practicing the Bodhisattva path, and practicing the Bodhisattva path will have achievements. If not, even if you want to replace it, you're afraid you won't be able to replace it! Everyone knows Master Tuyen Hoa. The monk is from the Northeast. When he was seventeen years old, his mother passed away. He maintained filial piety at her grave for three years. At that time, the Northeast had a lot of snow and was very cold. When we were young, [in winter, it was cold] twenty or thirty degrees below zero. The monk is from Ngu Thuong district, in the northern part of Harbin, which is very cold. The monk keeps the tomb there, there are many inspirations. Therefore, the whole area of ​​Harbin, many districts, all know the Master's language and call him "The White Good Man"[14]. In 1946 and 1947, monks from the Northeast entered Buddhism. That is for “others” (other people), although it is for one's own mother, but one's own mother is also another person, for the sake of others without caring about one's own body, making others happy. That is Bodhisattva. We don't think about anything for ourselves. Whenever we have something good, we give it to sentient beings, no matter who they are. Especially my enemies, I yield to them. From then on, that person will no longer hold grudges against you. The unjust karma between you and that person will thus be destroyed. Regardless of whether that person accepts it or not, the resentment karma between you and that person has disappeared. That is called the Bodhisattva path.

“ Non-existence and others do not arise in body, speech, and mind karma” (No mistakes arise in body, speech, and mind karma towards others): Body, mouth, and mind all make others happy, make others happy. The whole body, mouth, and mind do not hurt others, do not arise, and do not make that mistake. Truly a Mahayana Bodhisattva, he has never cared about himself and always takes care of others. One's own body, speech, and mind karma may be wrong towards oneself, but towards sentient beings, one cannot make mistakes at all. In this matter, we commit a lot of mistakes, especially with those close to us. It is the easiest to commit against one's closest relatives or spouses, and even easier to commit against children: "I raised this, you are my son, you are my daughter, you don't listen to me, who do you listen to?" That is making mistakes in body karma and speech karma towards sentient beings. Hitting and cursing is even more inappropriate!

(Sutra) Phuc, good man! All sentient beings are innately cruel, harsh in their speech, truly foolish, always clever and arrogant, never stop killing, have a wrong view, are greedy for others to benefit, respectful, are proud of the world, are deeply jealous, often seek self-benefit, respectful, are proud of the world, are not attached to love, always praise themselves, disdain to destroy others, do not protect their body, speech, mind, and karma, often ridicule the necessarily evil actions, internal actions. full of poison, without compassion, without shame, without preciousness, with joy touching the mind of others, with the field of blessings, with simplicity and victory, with the self-centered dharma of renunciants, often mocking the desire to possess and provoke. Wealth has a small appearance, the judge's true character is poor, that is, contemptuously destroyed, insulted, and punished. The mind is strong, filled with confused tears, often joyfully touching the minds of monks, unconscious and absent-minded, remembering the missing body. Although the text praises the merits of the Mahayana and evokes the desire to seek it, the child's heart is eager to do all the important and evil things, and the monk is still and calm. In the Mahayana Dharma, the present self listens to the text, the teacher also listens to the text, the present self recites alone, the teacher also recites alone, the self-recommends, the mausoleum forgives the deceased. In the Mahayana dharma, respectfully and admiringly beautiful, from the Mahayana practitioner's realm, without any further study, with the ability to understand and understand, I call myself "the self of Mahayana", to encourage others, to practice self-study, to seek fame and profit, to live my own life.
(Sutra: Come, good man! There are innate beings cruel nature, rude language, vulgarity, truly stupid, conceited, smart, not giving up killing, even wrong views. When it comes to other people's gain, respect, and praise from the world, they give rise to deep jealousy, always pursuing self-benefit, respect, and praise in the world and never getting tired of praising, scorning, and belittling others, not always taking care of their own actions, speech, and thoughts all evil deeds. In the heart, there is no compassion, no shame, no shame, likes to offend, upsets others, likes to distinguish between better and worse, and when one finds faults in them, he immediately despises, scolds, scolds, and punishes them Arrogant, deluded, often fond of offending, mentally disturbed monks, not aware of their own faults, always thinking and laughing at other people's mistakes. Although they heard praising the Mahayana's merits and sought it, their hearts loved to do serious evil things, and because they deceived others, they pretended to listen to the Mahayana dharma, taught others to listen, pretended to recite it themselves, and taught others to recite it because they were self-aggrandizing, oppressing, and oppressing others, then respected and praised the Mahayana, but he himself had never studied and understood the realms of the Mahayana practices and could not understand, so he proclaimed "I am the Mahayana" and encouraged others to follow me and practice to gain fame and profit, in order to support themselves.

“Wrong view” is stupidity, ignorance, always using wrong view to replace it. “Fu thu” (Again), the Buddha continued: There are sentient beings who have a naturally rough nature, their evil nature does not change, they are very rough, they speak incoherently, and they often want to attack people. Cursing others in return, or being cursed back by others, will be unbearable. That person curses others, if others curse back, they will attack them! “If you want others to gain benefits and respect, respect them, the world will be proud, but jealousy will arise” (Seeing others gain benefits and respect, the world will praise you, giving rise to deep jealousy): This is a sign of not having wisdom. That person has a jealous heart and is also very intelligent [in a] arrogant and intelligent way. Seeing someone else achieve a little good, such as gaining a good reputation, or receiving offerings, or doing profitable business, that person will think of a way to sabotage! If they were in the same profession, they would be unjust.

“Often seeks personal gain and respect”: What that person desires is fame and gain. “The world is full of praise, never tired of praise” (For praise in the world, never tired): Regarding this matter, that person is very diligent. Even though others do not praise, that person still praises himself, praises himself, criticizes others! Regarding his own body, mouth, and mind, that person does not guard or prevent it, just keeps watching over the body, mouth, and mind of others, scolding others for speaking incorrectly, doing wrong things with their body, often correcting other people's body, mouth, and mind

otherwise, we cannot preserve or prevent our own body, mouth, and mind!

What are the things that person desires and practices? All evil deeds, all evil deeds, no good deeds. “Dark inside”: What does this word “dark” mean? Evil, chaos. That's toxic. What poison is that? It is the poison of evil deeds. Not even the slightest bit of compassion for others. Compassion is a little weaker than [compassion], which means having compassion for others. Compassion is great compassion, greater. We often imagine people like this: “Everyone has a compassionate heart”. This sutra shows that not everyone is like that! There are cruel people who are used to being cruel and have never had compassion. Not only to outsiders, but to his wife and children, it's still like that. No shame, no shame! What does he like in his heart? Causing trouble to others, always wanting to make others suffer. If something is a bit good, if he wants to do something virtuous, he will disrupt it. There are many people like that, taking other people's money to do good deeds. That person has no merit, thinking that he or she has taken advantage of it. In fact, that person is committing a crime. In Mainland China, people who [do so] are called “good insects” (worms who sully good deeds, worms who feed on good deeds), specializing in swallowing the money of monks or lay people. Such people are called “good parasites”, they are parasites, that is, parasites that give birth to good things, taking advantage of the benefits of others to create their own benefits.

There was a person who loudly boasted that he was a filial son. His mother fell ill, and he wanted to cut meat to nourish her. However, he did not cut his own meat. Another person was waiting in the bathroom. While he was urinating, he swung a knife and slashed at him. Didn't he scream loudly? Others said: "Don't cry. Cutting meat to give to your mother is the greatest filial piety. Why are you still crying?" After hearing this, how do you feel? Although it's a joke, it's true that there are people like that. As for all the fields of merit, he is picky about which ones are good and I should do them; What is not good, we should not do. Blessings have been reduced, this good root is very small, that good root is very big, big we should do, small we should not do!

When Liu Bei entrusted his orphan [to the great mandarins], he told Liu Shan[15] to remember two sentences: “The evil things are the children of the children”, which means don't see the trouble very trivial, even though it is a very small bad thing, it has no impact, you should not do it. "I don't do anything good about anything", don't do it because this good thing is very small. If you do, great merit will arise. Just like giving someone a little money, a coin, a penny, your heart is always compassionate and respectful, and you personally give it to them, the merit is immeasurable. If a king, or a minister, gives alms to the poor, or beggars, or personally comforts, no matter how much money, his merit is far greater than making offerings to countless Buddhas. Ksitigarbha Sutra teaches like that.

For a person who is a monk in my dharma, that person often likes to look for blemishes. That person did nothing else, just diligently searched for faults. Whenever he sees the mistake of a monk, that person finds a little bit, “talent to gain a small appearance” (just found a little bit), he does not test whether it is true or false, and immediately “despise, slander, criticize” (scorn, slander, scold, punish). It's a mistake, that's a great evil! Such a person does not listen to the advice of others, his mind is hard and difficult to tame. “Hate and confusion” means being cruel, cruel, and the mind is very confused. Therefore, the purpose of that person "is often happy to offend the minds of monks" (usually likes to offend and upset monks): Seeing the monks and monks in trouble, that person is very happy, his purpose is to often find the faults of monks, causing you trouble, causing you to fail to practice. That's the devil. The children of the demon king Ba Tuan were so confused that they became monks. After that, he also became a monk, wore monk's clothes, did not do Buddhist work, but was even more destructive!

There are many people of this type, who cannot become good people, so they go deep inside [Buddhism], chiseling them from the inside out. Entering Buddhism to sabotage Buddhism, destroy Buddhism, forever without thinking about your own mistakes. Always criticize and slander others, find their shortcomings. Hearing the praise of Mahayana's merits, he also knew it was a good thing. As soon as he heard people praising the merits of Mahayana, he also felt a desire to seek Mahayana, wanting to seek it. But in his heart he loves to kill, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie, he has never calmed down, he has not stopped making evil mistakes, he cannot calm himself down, he is extremely chaotic! Why? Karma makes him confused. Karma! That's called real karma. You see that those people have very heavy karma, but you cannot advise them. If you advise them, they will get angry and cause trouble for you. Therefore, Śākyamuni Buddha told King Yama: “The living beings in this Saha world are stubborn, difficult to tame, and their habits are very strong”. Doing serious evil things, never being quiet before, deceiving and deceiving others, all pretending!

“Mahayana dharma, one listens to oneself” (For Mahayana dharma, one pretends to listen and accept): With Mahayana dharma, one listens for oneself, but also teaches others to listen. "Currently reciting it alone, teaching others alone reciting it. One who recommends it to others, admires it and admires it. Respects the Mahayana dharma, respectfully praises its beauty. Self-reciting the Mahayana dharma in all realms, those who have increased their learning, are unable to understand it, they call themselves the Mahayana dharma, encouraging others" (Pretend to read and recite it yourself, teach others to recite it, in order to exalt yourself, oppress and subdue others. Respect and praise the Mahayana dharma, but you yourself respect it. with the realms of practice of the Mahayana, having never studied and not being able to understand, yet claiming "I am the Mahayana" and persuading others): Encouraging others to believe and follow him to practice and learn. You heard the first two sentences very well. The next part is not like that, there is a different intention, the intention is not correct! That person said: "I have heard it, this sutra is very good, please follow me to listen. What sutra I am reading and chanting now, will you recite it or not? I recommend and guide you, but you must listen to me." That is deceiving people.

Oppressing and oppressing others in order to subdue others. Regarding the Mahayana dharma, praising and reverent, that is a false appearance, pretending to praise and revere. Regarding the virtues and realms in the Mahayana, he has never studied them before. Even if he studies, he will not be able to do anything. Let's not talk about enlightenment! How can I understand! But that person exaggerates, "I am a student of Mahayana", advising everyone to study with me and listen to my words. In fact, that person lies in order to “seek fame and profit”, that is, for the purpose of seeking fame and profit to support themselves. That's called "living by wrong livelihood". That person impersonates the Mahayana dharma; Under that disguise, that person pursues fame and fortune. Being alone is still not enough, you still drag friends to form parties and form gangs!

(Sutra) Giving is like breaking the precepts, holding bad lawyers, violating the Thi La, mocking evil deeds. For the sake of fame and fortune, to encourage others, the spirit needs to practice and study the Vinaya Pitaka. Such as the delusional song, the deceitful sentient beings, the lower body, the upper body is difficult to attain, the retreating good beast, the Second Vehicle of Nirvana, let alone the Mahayana? General no city! When falling into an evil beast, there will be unexpected difficulties. All wise people, not willing to be close to them, have no thoughts or values, but in the great assembly, they call themselves Mahayana, like a lion's roar. For the sake of fame and fortune, fooling around and being foolish, the spirit of being selfish, working together with the party. For example, if there is a fire, the non-lion will be like a lion, if the child is like a lion. The right person has the knife and the ants, the feet of the lion. At the beginning of Minh Dich, the phase of thi Lu, Ham Cong Hoa said: "Try flying lion, the truth is impure, the true evil is evil", the race of Ha Sat, the phase plus let go. Ego theory such as Bo Dac Gia La often mocks the practice of ten evil karma, destroys all human beings and heavenly seeds, withdraws from Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment Vehicle, not to mention the Mahayana can become a dharma weapon? Stupidity, arrogance, self-proclaimed Mahayana, stalking others, cultivating benefits.
(Sutra: For example, a lawyer breaks the precepts, is evil, violates the precepts himself, and enjoys doing evil deeds. Because of fame To benefit and persuade others so that they diligently practice the Vairocana Pitaka. Such a deceitful, deceitful person will hardly be able to attain the good path of the Second Vehicle, let alone attain Mahayana, and will fall into the evil destinies, and it will be difficult for wise people to escape [that person], but that person is not ashamed, in the crowd, calling himself Mahayana, like a lion. roaring. Because of fame and fortune, he seduces and deceives foolish people, causing them to submit to him and form gangs. For example, there is a donkey, wearing a lion's skin, and then someone looks at it from afar and thinks it is a real lion. When it cries, everyone knows it is a donkey and curses: "That is not a lion, but a donkey that eats unclean food, it is really bad", all sorts of curses and scolding. Let's go together. I say that Bo Dac Gia La often likes to practice the ten evil karmas, burn all the seeds of heaven and people, and still retreats from the Thanh Van and Single Enlightenment Dharma, not to mention can he become a Mahayana dharma weapon?

“If someone breaks the precepts, an evil lawyer upholds the precepts”, a lawyer[16] is false, that person breaks the precepts, “evil observance” is the practice following evil. He upholds evil dharma and does not practice precepts. Lawyers like that violate the precepts themselves, that is, violating Thi La. “Laughing at evil actions” (Like to do evil deeds): For fame and profit, but also advising others, “spiritually need to practice the Vinaya Pitaka” means advising others to diligently practice the precepts, pretending that I am a person studying the Precepts, advising others to study the Precepts and uphold the Law, but I myself have violated the Thi La. Even so, it's still a joke, not real. "Like a false illusion to sentient beings", that is, false and untrue, deceiving sentient beings, such a person "willing to attain a lowly human body and upper body is difficult to attain", [meaning] hoping to become a lowly human being [cannot even achieve it]. Once the human body is lost, hoping to regain a lowly human body is very difficult! The ancients said: “At the gate of hell, Sangha, the East”, that is what it means. That person is neither a true monk nor a true cultivator.

Why? That person, for fame and profit, deceives and pretends. The Buddha clearly saw the end of the Dharma: During the Dharma era, many people attained enlightenment, but at the end of the Dharma, you did not see anyone attaining enlightenment. If you don't open your eyes and lie like that, you won't see them. Once you open your eyes, you'll see them. But speaking from our side, even if you see them, it's as if you don't detect them. You have to be patient and just consider that person as a holy monk. If you do so, you will gain merit, attain the merit of a saintly monk. If you consider a holy monk to be an ordinary monk, or a monk who breaks the precepts, you will not achieve anything. Even if that person is a holy monk, you still cannot achieve it. So like monk Te Dien, when you meet that monk who breaks the precepts, you can't achieve anything because you don't have that mind.

Therefore such a person must eventually fall into the evil realm. “It's difficult to escape” (It's hard to escape): Can't attain a lowly human body! Why? Having fallen into hell, when it comes time to become a human, you will have a lowly human body and your members will not be perfect. Either crazy, or the six senses are not complete. “Wise people should not be close to them” (Wise people should not be close to them): A wise person should not be close to that person, that person is not ashamed. That person in the mass “self-titled Mahayana” (claiming to be Mahayana), is like a “roaring lion”, in fact, just for fame and profit. "Seducing the foolish, the soul is submissive" (Seducing, deceiving the foolish, being close to, submitting to oneself), making others close to him, forming factions with him, he is the leader.

He himself did not practice, nor did he understand, had no wisdom, just for fame and profit, to make others close to him and depend on him, he immediately achieved his goal. The Buddha said, for example, that kind of person is like a donkey among animals. A donkey has no talent whatsoever. In the past, there was a saying that was “Kien lu chi ch” (the skill of the donkey of the Alkaline land). Qian is Guizhou province. Someone from another locality bought a donkey to take home. The tiger in Guizhou had never seen a donkey, so he was frightened by the huge animal and did not dare to harass it. After a while, the tiger saw that it was nothing special and had no skills, so it tried to harass the donkey. The tiger pulled the donkey's tail, and the donkey kicked it with its foot. Tiger saw it and said: "Your talent is only that much. Your ability is only that great." The tiger immediately ate the donkey!

The disagreement is that that person has no shame, refuses to study, thinks that he himself studies the Mahayana dharma, even explains it to others, thinks that he himself is also a lion's roar, the same lion's roar as Buddha, but that person has a flaw "for fame and profit". If it were not for fame and profit, that person would not do so. Seducing others, leading people who are no different from him, are all stupid people, even more stupid than that person. “Community equals party” (Form together into a gang): Just like in the present, forming a gang, a faction, is it any different from a donkey? He claims to be a real lion, but doesn't have the true ability of a lion. Wait until he roars. The difference between the donkey's roar and the lion's roar is too far apart! “Try to fly a lion, the visa is impure” (That is not a lion, but something that eats impure food). “Really impure” can be explained in two ways. According to Buddhist explanation, what that person did was not pure, not pure conduct. That's a disguise, a fake, an evil donkey. After everyone recognized him, they cursed him, did not agree with him, and left him!

“The ego theory such as Bo Dac Gia La often ridicules the practice of the ten evil karma paths” (I say that Bo Dac Gia La often likes to practice the ten evil karma paths): The Buddha said that that type of living beings in the past was very deeply infected. The things that person does are all things that belong to the ten evil destiniess, they like to do the ten evil destiniess of karma, their mouth likes to lie, embellish words, harsh words, double talk, in their hearts they dream of greed, anger, ignorance, their body commits killing, stealing, and prostitution. Those are the ten evil karmas. Burn all human seeds until the seeds are born in heaven. Even if humans and gods cannot do it, can there still be a sravaka or pratyekabuddha dharma? Or the Pratyekabuddha Dharma and Shravaka Dharma learned in past lives have all receded, and nothing remains. For Mahayana, that person does not become a Mahayana dharma weapon.

That person says he is Mahayana, proving he is not Mahayana! All that person has is “stupidity, arrogance”, his own disguise. Currently, regardless of the four disciples, they always think that the dharma they are learning is very wonderful, whether it is the Explicit Dharma or the Secret Dharma, but they do not really practice it at all. Seen from the phenomenon, it seems that the current practice, of course, is all Mahayana, all call themselves Mahayana. Nowadays, no matter who they are [pats their chest and declares themselves] perfect, no one says we practice Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and the Way. [People say they practice Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path] very rarely!

Currently, there is another reason: After that person became a monk, he left the teachings. Just entering the temple, being able to approach the master, especially the Zen temple, or the Pure Land temple in Mainland, even Mahayana does not acknowledge it! Actually, that's because the Patriarchs in the past said so, they all imitated it [but didn't understand the deep meaning, the intention was to advise single-mindedly, "Concentrate on practicing, don't indulge in multi-literature when you haven't achieved concentration, haven't understood the method you're cultivating" of the Patriarchs], kept repeating: "Reciting one sentence of Amitābha Buddha, vertically the utmost of the three worlds, horizontally covering the eight teachings, everything is complete. Recite one sentence. Amitābha Buddha is enough”. Bodhisattvas who have just become monks, have just come up with ideas, do not know anything, only know how to recite one sentence of Amitābha Buddha, so they are very arrogant: "I recite one sentence of Amitābha Buddha, is there any benefit compared to you studying the Avatamsaka Sutra for many years? There is no need to study the Lotus Sutra! If I recite one sentence of Amitābha Buddha, it all has it." But [they forget that] the Amitabha Sutra does not say that, nor does the Infinite Life Sutra say that. Therefore, that person does not study the Teaching, nor does he penetrate it! If one truly recites to the point of one-pointedness and undisturbed mind, Amitābha Buddha's merits are truly inconceivable, but [beginner practitioners] cannot do it!

In addition, there are many people who meditate, don't know anything, but are very arrogant and have a very hot temper. Because that person does not practice or enter Concentration, he will develop according to his personality. Without studying the teachings, due to this deficiency, that person does not understand himself, nor does he understand others, and even more so does not know what the Buddha teaches and teaches us. The Buddha reprimanded these people as “ignorant and arrogant”. Claiming to be Mahayana, thinking that he is very terrible, and even deceiving others for the purpose of accumulating wealth!

Engage in war and punishment, enter the great battle formation, map the iron effectively, and never overcome the city. Masquerading as Mahayana, dressed as a heron. Faithful, precepted, completely non-existent, not thinking about the path to endure karma, the great array of desires, fighting and punishing afflictions, creating effective results, the end is not overcome! The ego theory that the seer does not protect the three karmas, specializes in evil deeds, falsely shows the Mahayana, really the three vehicles, the stage of non-dharma, children destroy all sentient beings' courage, endure the great array of afflictions, the desire stage shows all sentient beings the eightfold holy path, the spirit enters the fearless Nirvana, the ultimate land of no-seeing! The reason why it's fake? Good man! The Mahayana practitioner, upholds the first pure precepts and rules, practices the first most wonderful virtues, is established in the first steadfast love, deep understanding, deep fear of the sufferings of the future, far away from all evil dharmas, often ridicules the practice of necessarily good dharmas, is compassionate and always benefits all sentient beings, always works for the benefit of peace and happiness, saves, rescues all sentient beings, possesses the evils and sufferings of life and death, does not care about owning peace, only seeks peace and happiness all the time. affectionate. Like the name of the Mahayana practitioner.
(Sutra: For example, someone who is arrogant, has no limbs, wants to fight, conquer, go into battle A person who lies and claims to be Mahayana is the same. He has faith in his hands and true precepts, does not consider and consider the karma that can be done, wants to fight and conquer in the great array of afflictions, and strives to establish merit, but does not succeed at all! I say that such a person does not protect the three karma, specializes in evil deeds, and is falsely called Mahayana. Indeed, he is not a dharma weapon in the three vehicles, but wants to destroy the great array of afflictions! The tenacity and courage of all sentient beings, to manifest the eight noble paths of all sentient beings, so that they can all enter the citadel of Nirvana without fear, is it possible? Why is this, good man? A person of the Mahayana is the one who practices the most sublime and sublime virtues, is fully filled with the most steadfast shame, deeply sees and deeply fears the consequences of suffering in the next life, and is far from all evil. always likes to practice all good dharmas, is always compassionate to all sentient beings, always brings benefits, peace, and salvation to all sentient beings from all kinds of suffering and the yoke of birth and death, does not care about their own peace and happiness, only seeks the peace and happiness of all sentient beings. Such a person is called a person who abides in the Mahayana.

For example, if there is a person who has neither arms nor legs, but still wants to participate in battle, wants to fight the enemy, [that is the meaning of the sentence] “inspiring war and punishing to enter the great battle”, can it be successful or not? I don't have any abilities, it's empty, and I don't have any effects. So can it be achieved? “The whole cannot overcome the success” (The whole cannot be achieved): You cannot defeat the enemy, you can only be destroyed by the enemy. It's like you don't have education or talent, and you can't even get rid of the most superficial afflictions of Views and Thoughts. How can you do things that benefit all sentient beings? That is a lie claiming to be Mahayana!

Who do Buddhist students in the present fight with? You fight with yourself, you have to fight with your own afflictions and habits. Starting first from Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, talent, beauty, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping. You cannot overcome that realm of the five desires. People curse you two times, and you get three feet high in anger. That's a tiny, tiny thing, you can't handle it, how can you benefit all sentient beings? Even putting Nga Kien in the top position, he thinks about everything for himself. So how can you put an end to birth and death? It is said to be Mahayana, yet it is not even possible to attain birth and death! You hope to get rid of afflictions and achieve a little purity, but you can't even achieve even the most gross things! Very superficial, agitated, very quick-tempered, very impulsive, always scattered all day long, if it's Mahayana, who would believe it? Everyone can't believe it!

“Trust, Precepts, complete non-existence” (Hand Faith, True Precepts, none of them are perfect): Faith in the mind is like the hand, keeping the precepts is like the feet. Then you do not have faith and do not keep the precepts pure, that is, "no arms, no legs". Without faith, without morality, everything is incomplete!

“Unable to control oneself” [meaning] because one does not know how to measure one's own strength. Consider yourself, what merit do you have? What virtue is there? Not knowing how to measure your own strength, regarding the karma that you yourself can afford to perform, learn to follow that practice, either the Shravaka Vehicle, or the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, can you do it or not? People say "smarter than a monk" (not smarter than a monk), "a person" (a person who wears a shirt made of cloth) refers to a monk. You should not see monks doing nothing! They learn something, understand it, and are extremely intelligent. Those who have knowledge and understanding will immediately understand as soon as they learn. If you have a little Concentration blessing, no matter what you learn, you will understand it very quickly. If you don't even have that bit of wisdom, you won't do anything wisely, and if you do anything casually, you'll be clumsy!

During the Qing Dynasty, Yulin National Master[17] at Niem Hoa Pagoda, that is the pagoda where I received ordination. The Master worked as Phuong Truong there. The emperor came to visit the temple, the monk kept the emperor for a meal. But the window paper in the room was torn and the wind made a buzzing sound. National monk Ngoc Lam picked up a few grains of rice from the bowl and put them on the table. The novice monk immediately walked over and held a few grains of rice and a piece of paper taped to the torn area. King Qianlong[18] sighed, that's really quite good, "smart enough to kill". National teacher Ngoc Lam then praised the emperor: “You are more powerful than the emperor”. Although it is an old story, you see that the little monk has many things that we cannot think of, he did a very good job on your behalf. That's superficial intelligence. On the other hand, if there is true wisdom, there are monks who appear stupid, stupid to the point of death, and have a very ugly and rough appearance. There are many monks with unusual appearances, you see that they are very ugly, such as Zen master Dao An[19]. During the Jin Dynasty, the monk entered the temple when he was only ten years old. His master looked down on him: "What kind of person is ugly, short, and has a pockmarked face?" Not only was he dark, one side of his face was pockmarked, he was short, the monks in the temple all looked down on him. He had no choice but to go farming and work for a long time. One day, the Master said to his teacher: "Master, you should also give me a sutra book to recite." "You want to recite sutras? Okay!" He conveniently took out a thin sutra book for the Master. Entering the garden, the monk still had to work. Roughly during a break, he picked up the sutra and read it. In the evening, when he returned, he told his teacher: "Please give me another book." “Did you see that?” The Master replied: "I have seen it, I have finished watching it all." The teacher was too lazy to tell the Master, so he took out a book three times as thick as the previous one, and the Master took it away again. The next night, when he returned, he told the teacher again: "Teacher, give me another book." The teacher was very surprised: "Why did you change again?" The monk replied: "I have finished reading!" The teacher then from the back of that sutra, randomly took any passage of scripture to ask questions. He also read it carefully; I just discovered the Master's special feature. Dharma Master Dao An is a great monk with the earliest achievements in China.

Don't judge a person by their appearance, but that person really has that ability! Not only is his faith steadfast, but his moral conduct is also pure, he has genuine talent, but he is very humble. Everyone who is truly virtuous will be very humble and will not think that they are wonderful, they cannot be like that at all. Because [he knows he is] still very far behind Buddha, even Buddha is very humble. Buddha considered all sentient beings as teachers. Everyone sees the chapter Samantabhadra Vows: “If there were no sentient beings, a Buddha would not be possible!” Therefore, if you want to repay sentient beings, you must save them. If you don't have that kind of ability, you don't even have arms or legs, do you still want to fight? You still haven't developed faith, you still don't have the mind to believe in the Three Jewels, and you don't keep the precepts. If that's the case, then why can you still say it's Mahayana? There is no small inheritance, and there is no guarantee of human inheritance!

Such people cannot protect their own body, mouth, and mind, and let their body, mouth, and mind go freely. “Loose-minded” is specializing in evil deeds, specializing in doing bad things. He himself still falsely calls himself Mahayana. Studying the Mahayana, Shravaka, Pratyekabuddha, and three vehicles are not dharma tools. That person is not someone who studies the Dharma, but is someone who sabotages others who study the Dharma. That person makes friends and gangs, can he help his friends and disciples eliminate afflictions? The afflictions of sentient beings are like a battlefield! That affliction is solid and brave, like a big front. When you want to fight there, although you don't completely fail, you still bury yourself in afflictions!

This passage contains those meanings. The Buddha spoke this sutra in the form of an example. That is, there are people who foolishly claim to be Mahayana, yet they themselves do not even end suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, nor practice the causes and effects of the world. Doing evil deeds all day long is practice. Practice is "feeling great", that is, feeling great results of suffering. Basically, that person does not practice the Second Vehicle path, the path that emerges from this world. Not only do we not practice, but our faith is also not complete. Having faith, that person will not dare to commit a crime, will always defend and protect his thoughts, will not dare to give rise to bad thoughts, will he still dare to actually do it? When you see the benefits in front of you, absolutely do not be greedy, because you know that if you are greedy, you will have to receive bad things, and you can't help it! That person does not even have a mind, neither the Noble Eightfold Path nor the Seven Bodhisattvas, hoping to enter Nirvana will not be possible, it is completely impossible! It can't be done at any time!

Truly it is a Mahayana dharma weapon, practicing pure ritual rules refers to the Bodhisattva Bhikkhu. Not only are the Bhikkhu precepts pure, but the Bodhisattva precepts are also pure. Or take the Bhikkhu precepts, two hundred and fifty precepts are all pure. Taking the Bodhisattva precepts is not easy, because the ten major precepts and the forty-eight minor precepts are Brahma Vong precepts. The Pham Vong precepts have very deep and broad requirements. The Brahma Vong precepts are observed by which Bodhisattva status? It is the Bodhisattva Dharma Ground, from Joyful Joy Ground to Dharma Cloud Ground. When saying this precept, it was not said by Śākyamuni Buddha, but by [Sambhogakaya] Lo Xa Na Buddha. That is the precept said by Sambhogakaya Buddha. When Lo Xa Na Buddha spoke this precept, he was speaking for a thousand Śākyamuni Buddhas. The great incarnation is Lo Xa Na Buddha, sitting on a lotus with a hundred thousand petals. Each throne [of each Śākyamuni Buddha] is on a lotus petal, that is, on each lotus petal [on the lotus throne of Lo Xa Na Buddha] there is a Śākyamuni Buddha. He has hundreds of millions of kingdoms, hundreds of millions of small transformations, Śākyamuni Buddha, and Lo Xa Na Buddha is a great transformation. That means [Dharmakāya's Sambhogakaya Vairocana Buddha] Vairocana Buddha said the Brahma Vong precepts to one thousand Śākyamuni Buddhas, each of the thousand Śākyamuni Buddhas was correspondingly manifested by Him (Pilotāna Buddha). That is “thousands of memories” Śākyamuni Buddha, that is, one hundred billion times hundreds of millions of Śākyamuni Buddhas. Thus, he gave the Brahma Vong precepts to one hundred billion Śākyamuni Buddhas. [Each of the] hundred billion Śākyamuni Buddhas entered his own land to teach and educate, just like Śākyamuni Buddha spoke the Brahma Vong precepts in our Jambudvipa.

Therefore, maintaining the Pham Vong precepts means being able to maintain ten major precepts and forty-eight minor precepts. See your own Dharma nature, thoughts, and Dharmakaya. Dharma nature is compatible, only if it is partially compatible can one maintain the precepts! [Bodhisattvas belonging to] the position of the Three Sages (Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications) do not dare to say "have maintained pure precepts", especially in terms of benefiting sentient beings and saving sentient beings. If wisdom and skillful means are not complete, one would not dare to say“upholding the pure precepts”. Here, when we say “reception”, it is not only pure, but also of the highest order, surpassing the usual types of receptivity. Not only the status of the Ten Faiths, but the status of the Ten Pillars, the status of the Ten Virtues, the status of the Ten Dedications, and the Dedication. Only when reaching that level can one maintain the pure precepts. Maintaining pure precepts and learning the wonderful Dharma is very difficult! Why are wonderful virtues not easy? I want to make it possible for sentient beings to attain salvation. “Completely shameful, first-rate, solid and precious” (Completely shameful, most solid): Being steadfast and precious is not easy. There are two types of purity:

- The other type is that as soon as you commit a crime, you immediately repent, as soon as you commit a crime, you immediately repent, not hiding your own shortcomings, always revealing, full of shame, always feeling that you have no wisdom, no virtue, and have not cultivated in the past. “Insight” is to see very deeply, to see things over many lifetimes. “Serious” (Deep fear) is seeing sentient beings suffering in hell, that person will not dare to do bad things.

The Law of Ritual Precepts is the law of purity. The Many Benefits of Friendship and Love is to use the wonderful dharma to liberate all sentient beings from the profound fear of suffering in the next life! Many Benefits of Friendship means always liking to practice all good dharmas, often being compassionate to all sentient beings. Compassion is equality and great compassion, there is no difference in the mind. Our minds are so different! This person is very intelligent, so he is willing to educate more. That guy is very stupid, I don't want to teach him. He's so stupid, he's taught it a hundred times, he still doesn't understand, and it's very complicated, so you get bored. In the tenth chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva asked the Buddha for guidance: "Why in this world is there such a great difference in merit and virtue from giving alms?" Buddha taught: What mind do you use to give alms? While you practice almsgiving, what is your state of mind? What attitude to use? Always greatly related to mood, behavior, and speech. Of course, when you give something to someone else, that person is happy in their heart and also [feels] saved. Sometimes you give people this or that, but the recipient is very upset because you look down on others. When begging, they still have self-respect. You must respect them very much and give things to them; After that, I had to say a few words of comfort. If you are a Buddhist, say a few more Buddhist sentences to that person, it will be even better!

Therefore, when sentient beings have suffering, you should not worry about your own happiness. The Bodhisattva vows “not to pray for peace and happiness for myself, but only to wish that sentient beings be free from suffering”. The meaning is like that. “If you only seek the peace and happiness of all sentient beings, it is like the name of a person who abides in the Mahayana” (Only seeking the peace and happiness of all sentient beings. Like that, you are called a person who abides in the Mahayana). That is truly adhering to the Mahayana, a true Bodhisattva!

What is Phap Thanh Van? What is the Thanh Van Thua Pillar? Thanh Van Thua means learning the Hinayana religion, learning Arahantship. That person has no mind of deception, no mind of deception. That person knows the consequences of good and evil karma, and his faith is very urgent. When you encounter a realm, do you know whether it is fake or not, whether your faith is true or not? That's called the U Minh bell.

Therefore, neither Sravaka nor Pratyekabuddha are instruments containing the Mahayana.

“Brain disorder of the dharma of the sages and sages, punished by the holy ca-sa” (Brain disorder of the saints in my dharma, punishment of the person wearing the red ca-sa): Reprimand the person wearing the ca-sa, to the point of defamation and chaos. 1) Although it is still possible to have a human body, it is very difficult to have a complete body. One type of [defect] is the tongue. The tongue is too short, or too long, and cannot speak. Has a mouth but cannot speak. That's a case.

dharma" (If you want to attain the supreme dharma in the three vehicles, you should skillfully observe the three vehicle dharma): If you hope to attain the Mahayana dharma, carefully observe the three vehicle dharma. “ Rejoicing in the universal enlightenment of others, attaining Buddhahood without doubt” (Happy that others have fully enlightened you, will become Buddha, certainly without doubt): People who can do so, that is the true Mahayana, can definitely become Buddha.

“Breaking the precepts, slandering, being handicapped, being arrogant, self-praising, destroying others, the name Mahayana” (Breaking the precepts, being stingy, jealous, holding on to pride, praising oneself, criticizing others, and calling it Mahayana): Not only is it not Mahayana, nor is it Hinayana, not entering Buddhism, it is even on the verge of Buddhism. Don't be stingy with the Dharma! [If] you are stingy, greedy, or jealous of the dharma, you will suffer the retribution of being tongue-tied and unable to speak!

(Sutra) The Aggregates of Knowledge, Precepts, and Places are empty, baseless, dwelling in the void, preaching the Dharma equally. Breaking the precepts, embracing evil in your mind, listening to the superior Mahayana merits, pretending to claim Mahayana for fame and profit, is like an evil donkey wearing a lion's skin, if you want to quickly attain Bodhi, practice the Ten Virtuous Karmas well, protect my Dharma, and do not destroy it!)

The Five Aggregates, the Eighteen Precepts, and the Twelve Places are all dependently arising, without self-nature. Their nature is empty. “No” means there is no form of residence, no coming, no going. Knowing that all dharmas such as the Five Aggregates and the Eighteen Precepts are non-passable, that is achieving the practice. If you can study the Three Ten Treatises of Consciousness Only, being able to clearly understand the Five Aggregates, the Eighteen Precepts, and the Twelve Bases is not an easy task! Then, what do you contemplate? Those dharmas basically do not exist. The six consciousnesses of Eye, Ear, Muscle, Tongue, Body, and Mind are illusory, like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. On the outside, the corresponding six objects, i.e. Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Dharma, are also empty and illusory like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. Because the nature is always calm, because all dharmas are illusory, they are not true. Because if there is no direction, where can emptiness depend? Nothingness depends on nothing! Speak this type of Dharma to receive sentient beings; That is the wonderful meaning of the Mahayana, causing all sentient beings to attain boundless wonderful wisdom and enlightenment, to attain Emptiness. That Emptiness is Prajna, the Emptiness that Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) used to illuminate “The Five Aggregates are empty”, the eighteen Precepts are all empty, the twelve Lands are all empty. The Emptiness of Prajna is emptiness without non-emptiness. “No non-emptiness” is Chieu.

“Breaking the precepts, the intention is filled with evil thoughts” (Breaking the precepts, the desire holds a cruel heart): Whoever violates the precepts, breaks the precepts, that person's heart is not good, definitely evil. Hearing that Mahayana merit is great, that person also deceives others, saying: "I am also Mahayana." [That is] “the false title of Mahayana” (the false title of Mahayana). The merit of Mahayana is great, everyone's mind is directed towards it, especially we like to point towards Mahayana, towards Secret, towards perfection, towards the ultimate. If we say that this dharma is not ultimate, we will not study this dharma. We want to study the ultimate dharma. Very good! Studying the Dharma thoroughly has great ambition, but [if the student] is not of good temperament, it will be related to fame and fortune!

“Like a lousy donkey, wearing a lion's skin): Same as the example mentioned in the previous section. Just a lousy donkey, wearing a lion's skin, disguised as a lion, and known to everyone! "I declare to everyone, weak desires and defects overcome Bodhi" (Now I protect all the masses, if you want to quickly achieve Bodhi victory): Now I tell everyone, if you want to attain Bodhi very quickly, practice the Ten Good Karmas well, practice the Ten Good Karmas well. The Ten Good Karmas

(Sutra) Falling into the residue of the Sutras, seeking great enlightenment, practicing the Mahayana, renouncing the Sravakas and Singles Enlightenment Vehicle, the pure hypothesis of justice. Offering offerings to countless Buddhas, eliminating evil, working hard to purify the mind. The ego encourages the advancement of sentient beings, trying to preach the One Vehicle and the Non-Second Vehicle. Kim tried to use the three vehicles of the three vehicles, had to endure the Thanh Van Vehicle, had a very troubled mind, and had many careers. The sublime Bodhi energy. Existing in ignorance and tranquility, staying in Single Enlightenment, holding on to the sublime Bodhi energy. Being able to safely abide in the sublime wisdom. Try to make fun of yourself and talk about the three vehicles. Specifically purify merit, mock liberation. The literature talks about the Mahayana falling into evil beasts, like phlegm disease and teachings. Try to increase toxicity, not eliminate disease. Like the impure atmosphere of Thanh Van Thua, Mahayana literature, the mind is confused, it easily gives rise to the View of Death, and falls into the evil realm. Try to preach the Dharma and examine the body.
Literature, the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, for the sake of the pure Buddha, who has worshiped countless Buddhas, diligently cultivated and purified the mind. To encourage those sentient beings, I only speak of the single vehicle, not the other vehicles. Now, there are people who only adhere to the Thanh Van Vehicle, with great fear in their minds. Those who are ignorant, prefer tranquility, and stay in the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, are not those who practice the highest Bodhisattva wonderful, depending on their wishes, speaking of the three vehicles. Enough pure merit, loving liberation

Heard that Mahayana, falling into evil destiniess. Like choking on phlegm, being taught to drink milk. Increasing toxicity, not eliminating disease. The Qingwen's temperament is not Mahayana. Hearing that Mahayana's mind is confused, he immediately raises the Broken View and falls into the evil destinies. When speaking the Dharma, you should contemplate the fundamentals.

“Self accumulation of residuals The scriptures preach, seek great enlightenment, practice Mahayana” (In the past I said in other scriptures: “You should seek great enlightenment, practice Mahayana”): In other sutras, I said so, advising everyone, advising all sentient beings to study Mahayana, practice the Dharma Mahayana, great enlightenment seeks to become Buddha. “Leaving the Sravakas and Single-Enlightenment Vehicles” (Abandonment of the Sravakas and Single-Enlightenment Vehicles): There is no need to study the dharma of the Sravakas and the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle. I say this dharma for the sake of pure people, “the pure person hypothesizes justice” (for the sake of pure people, I say this dharma). This sentence is intended to answer Vajrayana Bodhisattva's question.

Previously, in other Mahayana scriptures, [Buddha] once said like this: "Everyone should study Mahayana, there is no need to study Shravaka and Pratyekayana". That is because He speaks to those who are pure. Because those people have all made offerings to countless Buddhist verses, “to cut off evil, work hard to purify the mind” (to cut off evil, diligently cultivate to purify the mind), purifying the mind must be cultivated to a decent level of achievement. “I encourage the advancement of sentient beings, trying to preach one vehicle, no second vehicle” (For the sake of promoting those sentient beings, I speak of one vehicle, there is no second vehicle): The Lotus Sutra says so. "Only try the one truth, the remaining two principles are true" (Only this dharma is the only true dharma, the other two dharmas are not true) is intended to speak to those people, that is, to preach the dharma in accordance with the fundamental nature.

“The needle tries to test the three vehicles of the Three Vehicles, and has the right to abide in the Sravaka Vehicle” (Now in this mass there are enough three-vehicles, there are people who can only abide in the Sravaka Vehicle): Now I only speak completely to people in the three vehicles. The Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra covers all three vehicles. Now in this great assembly, there are people who can only abide in the Shravaka Vehicle. In his mind, he is afraid of many things. He does not have the sublime Bodhi spirit. The Pratyekabuddhas live in silence, “the sublime Bodhi spirit” (that person is not the marvelous Bodhi weapon). "If there are people who can abide in the superior wisdom, they try to mock the doctrine of the three vehicles." "Pure merit mocks liberation, literature talks about Mahayana falling into evil realms" [meaning] there are other types of people, they seek pure liberation [have no intention of saving sentient beings], hearing about Mahayana, they fall into evil destiniess.

Liberate the human world, seek to achieve the tranquility of the Second Vehicle. If I teach the Mahayana Dharma to that person, that person will not only not accept it, but will also slander it and will definitely fall into the evil realm. For example, if a person has phlegm, phlegm is an uncomfortable throat disease (pharyngitis), if he is given milk, the pharynx will become hotter and the inflammation will be more severe. It's toxic, it doesn't completely eliminate that person's illness. Drinking some celandine juice will make you feel much better. That is cutting the medicine for the right disease.

“As there is no air in the Sravakayana, the Mahayana literature, the mind is confused” (Those who belong to the Sravakayana, are not Mahayana dharmas, when they hear about Mahayana, their minds will be confused): For those who are not Mahayana dharmas, [listening to Mahayana teachings], will definitely be confused. Someone who is not a Second Vehicle dharma vehicle, if the Second Vehicle dharma is told to that person, they will not be able to enter it, because they are a Mahayana dharma vehicle. As for the Thanh Van Vehicle type of Dharma, if you tell the Mahayana Dharma to that person, after hearing it, their mind will be chaotic, and they will not even be able to achieve it. On the contrary, they will arise from the View of Death and fall into the evil realm of Emptiness. Not only is he unable to comprehend the meaning of Emptiness, but he also falls into the Evil Beast of Emptiness, falls into an evil destinies. “Try to preach the Dharma with insight into the foundation” means that when preaching the Dharma, you must be careful, you must consider the basis carefully.
