noi_dung:
V. Repentance - Prepentance DDNg

(Fifth item: Repentance)

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One preached and chanted, the assembly gathered together, countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings Enlighten the Dharma, attain enlightenment, the eight causes and effects, destroy the good roots, leave behind the evil beasts, test the sutras with literature, complete the right view, immediately arise from the seat, pay homage to the Buddha, the previous World-Honored One, deeply repent, sincerely repent, join hands, respectfully, and say to the Buddha: "World-Honored One! I am at the same level in the middle of the Sravaka Vehicle, my roots are good, my ability to mature is the Sravaka Vehicle. Later I will be enlightened by the Sravaka Vehicle. Enlightenment, enchantment without end, empty view, eight causes and effects, created by body, speech, mind, immeasurable karma, evil beasts, the previous Buddha's teachings, complete the right view, reveal repentance, not rich in emotions, vow to eliminate all evil, forever protect all evil obstacles Receiving the life, the spirit of the level of sin will surely be destroyed, in the future, there will be no wings of creation. Only the wish of the World-Honored One, whoever sacrifices the self, will be punished by the evil person., complete the vow to practice the Thanh Van inheritance
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One finished speaking that chant, in the assembly, there were countless hundreds of thousands Sentient beings who have heard the wrong Dharma, have been misled, have created empty views, rejected "there is no cause and effect", destroyed good roots, entered the evil destinies, heard this sutra, gained right view, immediately stood up from their seats, bowed at the Buddha's feet, before the World-Honored One, they were deeply ashamed, sincerely repented, clasped their hands, respectfully, said to the Buddha: "Venerable World-Honored One! We have planted good roots in the Sravaka Vehicle, but have not been able to achieve it. After meeting and hearing the Doctrine of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, we were confused and did not understand clearly, immediately arising empty knowledge and rejecting cause and effect. Because of that cause and effect, we created countless negative karma in our body, speech, and mind, and now when we hear this sutra before the World-Honored One, we are deeply ashamed and repent, not daring to hide it, and vow to eliminate it all from now on. We will never re-commit any sins in the future. We hope that the World-Honored One will have mercy on us and cause all of our sins to be destroyed. We hope that the World-Honored One will be merciful and help us in the future to receive and practice the practices of the Thanh Van Vehicle Respect, compassion, and guidance”).

Whenever the Buddha preaches the Dharma, he will eliminate the suffering of the masses attending the Dharma Assembly. Why did the Buddha say those dharmas? This is teaching the Dharma according to the fundamentals. Because in this Mahabodhi Assembly, there are sentient beings who are misguided and give birth to empty views, they have made that mistake in the past. "No cause and effect, destroys good roots" (Refutation of "no cause and effect", destroys good roots), so one goes into evil destiniess and falls in the three evil destiniess. Now “testing the sutra” (hearing this sutra), that is, hearing the Buddha speak the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, “acquiring the right view” (gaining the right view again), that is, restoring their right view. They immediately stood up from their seats, bowed at the Buddha's feet, and in front of the World-Honored One, felt deeply ashamed and repented.

This is the fifth chapter, the Repentance chapter. When we read this passage, let's consider whether we ourselves have made that mistake or not? If so, please feel free to repent. No, you may not need to rejoice. However, everyone will definitely make mistakes, more or less, and they should repent. They bowed at the Buddha's feet and repented. “Hold your palms respectfully, I pray to the Buddha” (Put your hands together, respectfully talk to the Buddha), respectfully say: “Venerable World-Honored One! I am at the same level in the middle of the Sravaka Vehicle, growing good roots” (Venerable World-Honored One! We have planted good roots in the Sravaka Vehicle): We have cultivated the path, but have not matured the roots of the Sravaka Vehicle, have not attained enlightenment, and have not achieved results. “After the recovery, I realized the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle” (Later I encountered the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle), immediately I was confused, and Emptiness arose. Once the view of Emptiness has arisen, one immediately rejects "no cause and effect" (rejects "there is no cause and effect"), not believing in good or evil retribution. Because of that cause and effect, creating “my body, speech, mind, immeasurable karma” (creating immeasurable karma in body, speech, and mind), making many mistakes. Because he did wrong, he fell into an evil destinies. Now, before the World-Honored One, "testing the sutra" (hearing this sutra) will restore the right view. “Deep in your heart, you are precious” (Giving deep shame), feeling that you have done wrong in the past, now turning to the World-Honored One to reveal repentance. “Abundance of insensitivity” (Do not dare to hide it), request the World-Honored One to prove, “pray to completely eliminate” (pray to completely eliminate) those sins of mine. When the World-Honored One finishes repenting, [those sins] will be eliminated. “Once again in the past, never to be recreated” (From now on, never to do it again): No more creating those sins, no more falling into evil views. “Protect against future sins” (Prevent all future sins): I have finished repenting; In the future, those sins will happen again, you will recognize them immediately, and you will not fall again!

“Only I pray that whoever the World-Honored One diligently accepts and accepts, all the sins of the highest order will be destroyed” (We respectfully hope that the World-Honored One will have mercy on us and cause all of our sins to be destroyed): Now we turn to the Buddha who has finished repenting, and the Buddha will bless us and cause all of our sins to be destroyed. “In the future, never to be created again” (In the next life, never to be created again): No more creating this crime! "Only I pray to the World-Honored One, whoever diligently sacrifices for us will be rewarded with evil retribution in the future" (We respectfully hope that the World-Honored One will have mercy and save us the suffering of our evil destiniess in the future): If you do not repent, in the future, you will definitely have to suffer that retribution.

“The Golden Almighty vows to undertake the first practice of practicing the Shravaka Vehicle" (Now we still wish to receive and practice the practices of the Shravaka Vehicle that we have practiced before): They are the Sravakayana energy. They said: Currently, they do not admire the Single Sense Vehicle, but still want to practice the Shravaka Dharma. “I only pray that the World-Honored One will teach you diligently” [meaning] please Buddha speak the Shravaka Dharma again for us!

(Sutra) The World-Honored One wrote: "Good ear! Good ear! All kinds of mental abilities are like precious eyes and eyes, and develop The path of repentance. The person in the Dharma is in the middle of the Dharma, the person of the two races, the name is without violation: One person, the innate nature is pure, the original person is not in violation, the person who violates the mind, reveals the person in repentance, the person in the Dharma is in the middle, the person is strong in the name, and the person is pure. U-shi, the World-Honored One, at any time, ridiculed and expediently explained the Four Noble Truths. According to the assembly, one has obtained a lower-ranked shinobi, one has obtained a middle-rank shinobi, one has obtained a top-rank shinobi, one has obtained the first dharma in the world, one has obtained the fruit of Stream Stream, one has obtained the fruit of a Once-returner, one has obtained the fruit of no return. In the middle, the eighty-four thousand celestial beings are restored, all defilements are eternally eradicated, the mind attains liberation, the good intentions are pure, one becomes an Arhat, joyfully worships the Buddha, and restores the original throne.
(Sutra: The Buddha said: “How good! How good! You can be ashamed and express it. Repent like that. In my Dharma, there are two types of people who are said to have committed no mistakes: One is the person who is pure in nature and has never committed a crime. The other is the person who has committed a crime and is ashamed and repented. Those two types of people are called brave and strong people who have achieved purity." At that time, the World-Honored One followed their wishes and told them the method of the Four Noble Truths. Among those people, there were people who attained purity. low-rank forbearance, some people attain middle-rank forbearance, some attain high-rank forbearance, some attain the highest dharma in the world, some attain the state of stream-entry, some attain the state of once-returning, some attain the state of no-return. Among them, there are eighty-four thousand buddhas who are forever free from all taints, their minds are liberated, their good intentions are pure, they become arhats, they joyfully worship the Buddha, and return to their own seats.

Buddha immediately said: “Good ear! Good ear!”, very good! “If you are ashamed and reveal your repentance, you must realize that in Buddhism: “There are two types of people, no faults in your name” (There are two types of people who are called “without committing any mistakes”), which are also pure. “One, innately diligent in nature” (One is innately diligent in nature): That person has a very good disposition to keep the precepts, diligently upholds the precepts, and does not violate them. “Second person, violating the precepts” means that once you have broken the precepts, your mind will be ashamed. “Repentance revealed” will also be pure. That type of person "is in the middle of the dharma, has a strong reputation, and attains purity" (that type of person is in my dharma, is called a brave, strong person, achieves purity), all crimes are purified and purged.

“ Ugh, the World-Honored One makes fun of him at any time” (Therefore, the World-Honored One follows their preferences): What do their minds like? “Meaning to explain the Four Noble Truths” (Meaning to explain the Four Noble Truths to them): The Four Noble Truths are Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path, including two levels of cause and effect. Practice is the worldly cause, Suffering is the worldly effect. The Way is the cause beyond the world, the Extinction is the effect beyond the world. The cause is beyond the world and the effect is beyond the world. By cultivating the Tao, one can escape. Because the Buddha said so, in that assembly, "some people attain low-quality shinobi, some people attain middle-quality shinobi, some people attain high-quality shinobi, some people attain the world's first-class dharma" (some people attain low-quality shinobi, some people attain middle-quality shinobi, some people attain high-quality shinobi, some people attain the first dharma of the world): Those are called the four states of Nirvana, Dharma, Ren, First World, and then attain the Initial Fruition. Practicing practice has obtained Noan Qi (warmth). When you first practice, there is no warmth at all, which means you have not entered the practice. Having been able to enter, either Concentration, or reciting the Mahayana, or having a feeling of joy. That is Ha Nhan.

“Trung Nhan” goes one step further. It can be said that Danh means "received". Then, reaching the First World status, which is the pinnacle in worldly dharma. Then there is the dharma that transcends the world. Leaving this world is the First Fruition. The First Fruition is a dharma beyond the world. These are all the positions of the Hinayana. “One who attains the fruit of Stream Stream” (Some people attain the fruit of Stream Stream): Taking one more step, one will achieve this position. Being a Stream-winner is the First Fruit, participating in the lineage of saints. The Hinayana is a Stream-winner, while the Mahayana is a Believer (Ten Faith position) and has joined the saint lineage. Some people attain the One-Returner, the One-Returner is the Second Fruition. The previous fruit is Tu Da Hoan, and this fruit is Tu Da Ham. There are people who attain the status of Non-Complete, that is, Ana Ham, which is the Three Fruits.

“In the middle, there are eighty-four thousand springs” (There are eighty-four thousand springs in there): In the previous section, without mentioning the quantity, [“eighty-four thousand”] here implies “a lot”. Among the great assembly present, there were also eighty-four thousand monks wearing red robes. “Eternally ending all the cankers” (Eternally free from all the cankers): No longer reincarnated in the three worlds, then attained Arahantship. “All the cankers are forever eliminated, the mind is liberated” (The cankers are forever eliminated, the mind is freed): As soon as the Thoughts or Thoughts are destroyed, the mind is liberated. "Pure good intentions, become an Arhat, joyfully worship the Buddha, restore the original throne" (Pure good intentions, become an Arhat, joyfully worship the Buddha, return to their own seats): Those sentient beings were all very happy, because they escaped the sea of ​​suffering, and also had pure repentance.

Reading the Mahayana sutras, you will surpass Noan, Danh, Nhan, The First World, [enlightenment] is better than Thanh Van Vehicle, but the Or passage is not as good as Thanh Van Vehicle! The new generation of Bodhisattva mind has just developed the Bodhi mind, and will surpass them (Sravaka Vehicle). Even though he still belongs to the status of ordinary people, he can do the things of a Bodhisattva, whether when propagating the Dharma, cultivating the Way, or benefiting sentient beings, or contemplation, the starting point [of a Bodhisattva] is not for himself, everything is for others. Even if you do it wrong, the problem is not that big! If for yourself, although you do it very right and very satisfactorily, but due to the mix of fame and profit, the problem is also very big, you will not gain any benefit at all!

(Sutra) At that time, the assembly gathered together and restored the fifty-seven hundred nadiras sentient beings, achieving enlightenment. Literature and dharma, the meaning of birth is not resolved, the eight causes and effects are empty, the good roots are destroyed, and the evil realms are gone. The text testifies to the sutra, completes the right view, immediately arises from the seat, bows to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, deeply repents, sincerely repents, joins hands, respectfully, and speaks to the Buddha: "The Venerable World-Honored One! After attaining the power of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, after realizing the teachings of the Mahayana dharma, even though one is born with ridicule, one cannot resolve it, one is ignorant and confused, one is born with no view, eight causes and effects, due to the creation of the body, speech, mind, and countless karmic conditions, after countless lifetimes, one falls into evil beasts, suffers from evil beings, and is difficult to endure. Repent, don't be sensitive, wish to destroy all the past, forever not be able to act, protect the future of all sins. Only pray that the World-Honored One will be obedient, and in the future, only the World-Honored One will not be able to create. Only the World-Honored One who is mindful will destroy the evil beasts and receive the punishment longevity”.
(Sutra: At that time, in the assembly there were again fifty-seven hundred thousand na-data beings who had once been Having heard the wrong Dharma, mistakenly giving rise to empty views, rejecting cause and effect, destroying good roots, entering evil destiniess, hearing this sutra, gaining right view, immediately rose from his seat, bowed at the Buddha's feet, before the World-Honored One, felt deep shame, sincerely repented, clasped his hands, respectfully said to the Buddha: "Venerable World-Honored One, we have planted good roots in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, but we have not been able to mature the Dharma of the Single Bodhisattva. Enlightenment Vehicle. Later, when we met and heard about the Mahayana Dharma, although we loved it, we could not understand it. We were ignorant, ignorant, and doubtful. We now had no view, denied cause and effect, and created countless negative karma in body, speech, and mind. Based on that karma, for countless lifetimes, we fell into evil destiniess and suffered all kinds of suffering and pain that were difficult to endure. When we heard this sutra before the World-Honored One, we were deeply ashamed far, express repentance, do not dare to hide it, vow to eliminate it all. From now on, never do it again, to prevent all sins in the future. We only hope that the World-Honored One will have mercy on us, so that in the future, we will never commit any more sins practice before. I hope the World-Honored One will have mercy and teach you."

This section is the Repentance section. At that time, there were so many people participating in the Dharma Assembly. In this Great Assembly, the members gathered were very complex, with countless, boundless sentient beings. First, they clearly stated that when they first started listening to the Dharma, they did not respect the Three Jewels until they heard the Dharma and then misunderstood. This misunderstanding is all considered in terms of Emptiness, here is the Evil Beast Emptiness (due to the attachment to Emptiness as being empty, not believing in cause and effect, so falling into the evil destinies). There is a person who listens to the teaching of the Diamond Sutra and [sees that the sutra says] "all is Emptiness", so that person doesn't study anything and just creates bad karma. Good karma is Empty, but bad karma is Empty, creating a lot of crimes.

In this assembly, the above section talks about the Shravaka Vehicle, here we talk about the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. In that great assembly, how many living beings were there? There were fifty-seven hundred thousand na-du-da, that is fifty-seven hundred thousand ten million living beings, they came together to listen to the Dharma, turned to the Buddha, and asked to repent. Because in the past, they heard the wrong Dharma. "Hearing the Dharma wrongly" is not at all "preaching the Dharma wrongly", but because the person [after listening to the Dharma] interpreted it incorrectly. Actually, it's not that their understanding is wrong, it's because in the past, that person didn't have that many good roots. Because they couldn't receive it, the error of No view arose. It is very difficult to destroy that view of Emptiness. If the View of Being arises, such karma is easily ended. Arising from No view, this kind of karma is not easy to end. Because when the View of Being arises, that person still believes in cause and effect and is attached to cause and effect. However, both sides are not right. Buddhist scriptures also teach that there are many sins that cannot be repented. In the previous life, we created the cause, and in this life we ​​must receive the reward. There are many erroneous ways of saying it, [like hearing] "can't repent" then argue that "you have to carry that sin forever, you will definitely fall into hell". That is a wrong view!

In the previous section, it was said that there are two types of people. One is the type of person who is naturally diligent. Basically, that person has not committed a sin. Second, the person who committed the crime is ashamed, that is, ashamed and repentant, which is also brave and courageous. The Buddha said that these two types of people are both pure. Having made a mistake when listening to the Dharma, he insisted on not repenting or being ashamed. Currently, there are many people studying Buddhism, you tell them: "You are not following that path correctly. You can use the Holy Doctrine as taught by the Buddha or as taught by the saints to compare a bit, and you will know whether it is correct or not." But they are not willing to correct their mistakes, they still think they are right, they are attached to something, they are attached to what is said in the sutra, it is not wrong. [They insisted]: “The sutra teaches ‘all dharmas are Emptiness’, that is what the Diamond Sutra teaches!” But what does No mean? They do not understand, it is also because of listening to the Dharma that they misunderstand and misunderstand Emptiness.

Take the Diamond Sutra as an example. That sutra teaches that the Second Vehicles abide in Nirvana and that the principle of Emptiness that they have attained is not ultimate. That meaning of Emptiness is also achieved by cultivating cause and effect, it does not mean there is no cause and effect. Especially in Chinese Zen Buddhism, some people who study Zen misunderstand and misunderstand "engaging in Zen to clarify the mind and see nature" as "nothing needs to be learned". Don't even believe in cause and effect, just clear your mind and see your nature! What would it be like without enlightenment? If you commit a crime, you still have to receive the same punishment! After listening to the Dharma, those people can correct their mistakes; In the past, because of hearing this Dharma, I understood its meaning. It's not wrong! “Eight without cause and effect” (Refutation of no cause and effect), destroys good roots, creates evil deeds! If you do evil, you will naturally receive evil retribution. Now in this Dharma assembly, I have heard the Buddha speak the Mahasamadhi Sutra, and now I understand clearly and immediately restore my right view.

In the past, there was right view, but later, guided by evil friends, or mistakenly believing what others said, one lost right view. How many people are like that? There were fifty-seven hundred thousand ten million such people who stood up from their seats and bowed towards the Buddha. Before the World-Honored One, they were deeply ashamed and sincerely repented. What repentance? In the past, we practiced the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle and planted good roots, but we could not mature the Pratyekabuddha Dharma weapon, nor did we attain enlightenment in the Single Enlightenment Vehicle. After that, hearing the Mahayana Dharma again, joy arose, I believed in it, sought the Mahayana, but could not understand. Not fully understanding the meaning of Mahayana, ignorance, darkness, doubt. “Ignorance” means having no wisdom, being in darkness, doubting oneself is like being in darkness. Currently, we have a lot of doubts. The biggest obstacle in studying the Dharma is doubt, not being able to believe. To study any dharma, you must have faith. Only with faith can an understanding arise, an understanding is an understanding. That is, while studying, if you want to practice a certain dharma, you must first clearly understand that dharma, the order of practice, how to apply effort and visualize!

If you clearly understand the order of practice, you will not go wrong! Just like when we want to go somewhere, you must know the way to a friend's house. If you're not familiar with people living in the South, you drive to the North. If that's the case, you won't be able to get there forever, the further you go, the farther away you will be! You must be familiar with the meaning mentioned in that dharma? Don't misunderstand! “Emptiness” in Mahayana is not the Evil Beast Emptiness, but wisdom. As you study the Heart Sutra, “Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) deeply practices Prajnaparamita many times, illuminating the Five Aggregates of Emptiness”: Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness all do not exist, nothing is good, and nothing is evil. If you do evil, that is contrary to the Dharma Nature, you will never achieve Emptiness. If you do good, you will gradually no longer be attached to good things, you will enter that Void meaning. Without explaining this, it would be “eight no cause and effect” (refutation of no cause and effect).

Due to the lack of cause and effect, that person's body, speech, and mind create ten very bad karmas, creating countless sins. Thanks to the fate of creating that karma, countless eons fall in the evil destinies, falling into the three evil destiniess. “Evil beasts” are three evil destiniess, subject to great suffering. That place of suffering is very difficult to endure, “suffering poison” is the punishments that must be endured. Now that we have heard the Buddha say so, we have regained our knowledge and enlightenment, realizing that we were wrong in the past. We have revealed and repented of the crimes we have committed. We do not dare to hide them anymore. May the World-Honored One bless us and [cause these sins] to all be eliminated. In the future, I will not do that again, I will never do it again, in order to prevent future sins and not repeat them again. The sins we have committed in the past, we only hope that the World-Honored One will have mercy on us, save us, help us, and protect us. To save the suffering and retribution of our evil destinies in the future, we still vow to "receive the first practice of practicing the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle" (receive and practice the conduct of the Single-Enlightenment Vehicle that we have practiced before), and study the dharma of cause and effect. “I only wish that the World-Honored One would diligently teach me” [meaning] now we have all forgotten the dharma of cause and effect, please Buddha teach us again!

(Sutra) The World-Honored One wrote: "Good ear! Good ear! All kinds of mental abilities are like precious eyes and eyes, and develop The path of repentance. The person in the Dharma is in the middle of the Dharma, the person of the two races, the name is without violation: One person, the innate nature is pure, the original person is not in violation, the person who violates the mind, reveals the person in repentance, the person in the Dharma is in the middle, the person is strong in the name, and the person is pure. Ugh, the World-Honored One, depending on the occasion, through expedient teachings of the dependent origination of dharmas, diligently and diligently cultivating the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle to perfection, eventually attaining the Perfect Enlightenment, achieving the Solitary Enlightenment Vehicle, attaining no regress, rejoicing and worshiping the Buddha, returning to the original seat.
(Sutra: The World-Honored One said: "How good! How good! You can be ashamed and exposed." "Repent like that. In my Dharma, there are two types of people who are said to have committed no mistakes. One is a person who is pure in nature and has not committed any transgressions. The other is one who, after having committed a crime, is ashamed and reveals himself to repent. In my Dharma, there are two types of people who are called brave and strong people who have achieved purity." At that time, the World-Honored One followed their wishes and told them the methods of dependent origination, causing them all to practice the Pratyekabuddha One after another. satisfied, they all attained the Stage of Dependent Samadhi and did not regress in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. They joyfully bowed to the Buddha and returned to their seats.

“The Blessed One wrote: - Good ear! Good ear!” (The Blessed One said: - Good! Good): You guys speak very well, have a very good heart for repentance. “You can be ashamed and reveal your repentance like that. You can feel ashamed and repent like that): Ashamed of yourself for doing such things. Repentance is making amends, correcting what you have done before. “Regret” is to never do such things again! "In the middle of the Dharma, there are two types of people, the name is free from transgressions: The one, the innate nature is pure, the origin is not transgressing. The second, the transgressor is precious, reveals repentance" (In my Dharma, there are two types of people who are said to not commit any mistakes! One is the innate pure nature, which does not commit any transgressions. The other is, having committed a crime, then be ashamed and reveal repentance): Those two types of people are called "the brave, strong, and accomplished ones." be pure". Once you repent, you are still pure.

They asked the World-Honored One to explain the dharma of cause and effect to them. This passage does not say it in detail, just a general outline. The World-Honored One "depends on each occasion", that is, based on their belief, the means to teach them the Dharma "conditions" (dependent arising dharmas). The Single Enlightenment Vehicle and the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle [the difference is that], when there is a Buddha in the world, it is called Pratyekabuddha, when there is no Buddha in the world, it is called Single Enlightenment, because they alone contemplate the birth, existence, and change of all things. all things. Why does this flower bloom? Study its charm! If we talk about twelve causes and conditions, then Ignorance depends on Actions, Actions depend on Name and Form... The dependent origination dharma that He said is the preliminary dependent origination method, while the "emptiness of dependent origination" of Mahayana is the dependent origination method according to Mahayana. Regarding that dependent origination, if you understand wrongly, it will turn into Emptiness of Ending and Extinction, rejecting "there is no cause and effect", because you do not know that Mahayana must be achieved in order. Therefore, the Buddha spoke the Dharma of Dependent Origination and taught them to practice the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle.

“Perfection” (Complete step by step) only then can one attain enlightenment. “Everyone attains the Stage of Dependent Concentration” (All attain the Stage of Dependent Concentration): Cultivating Concentration in the place of dependent origination, that person does not regress. “Happyly bowing to the Buddha, return to your seat” (Happyly bowing to the Buddha, return to your own seat).

(Sūtra) At that time, the assembly gathered together and restored the eight hundred nadirāṇa sentient beings, monks. In the past, the Buddha's Dharma was faithful, slandering Buddhism, chanting one chant in the summer. Due to the fate of seeing people, they fall into evil beasts and receive suffering from them. Dress modestly, have a comfortable and warm life, often have trouble, and cannot speak. The text testifies the sutras, completes the right view, arises from the throne, pays homage to the Buddha, pays homage to the World-Honored One, deeply gives birth to precious thoughts, sincerely repent of all evil karma, joins hands, reveres, and admires the World-Honored One. The Buddha's divine power is strong, all the words can be spoken.
(Sutra: At that time, in the assembly there were again eighty hundred thousand na-du-da sentient beings who had once In the dharma of the past, the Buddhas slandered Buddhism, even with just one recitation. Due to that cause and effect, they fell into evil destiniess and suffered retributions, and were born as a human being. They were often speechless and speechless. When they heard this sutra, they gained the right view. They immediately stood up from their seats, bowed at the feet of the Buddha, and felt deep shame before the Buddha. They sincerely repented of their evil deeds in life. Before, respectfully, clasped hands, admiring the Buddha's power, they could all speak.

These people committed greater crimes than the previous ones. “Canceling blasphemy in one chant” (Canceling even just a single chant), or slandering very little, but due to the cause of slandering, “falling to the evil beasts, receiving suffering from them” (falling into evil destiniess, suffering the karmic retributions): Although having received all the karmic retributions, when born, unable to speak, “permanently forbidden” (often with a stiff tongue): Tongue cannot speak I can't make a sound, my mouth can't speak. This type of person also participates in the Dharma assembly, hears this sutra and then “accomplishes the right view”, that is, restores the previous right knowledge and right view. “Upset the throne, bowing down to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, deep in the mind and heart, sincerely repenting all the negative karma” (Immediately stood up from the seat, bowed at the Buddha's feet, felt deep shame, sincerely repented the negative karma in the previous life): In the previous life, what negative karma did they have?

(Sutra) At the ear of the time, the Buddha of wisdom advises: “The world-honored world is well-established, the bad karma is eliminated, the metal is dealt with. middle, unable to speak? Dear people, please take the time to talk to the Buddha. In the middle, one type of action is like declaring: "Venerable World-Honored One! The ego is past and present in the Bhikkhuni Tathagata's dharma, or the language slanders the Mahayana true dharma, or the language slanders the Single Enlightened Vehicle dharma, or the language slanders the Sravakayana dharma, the lower end of the chant. The ego is bound by evil karma, for nine-ten eons of birth and death, constantly in hell, in the animal world, hungry ghosts, skandhas, non-losses, unable to speak, suffering all kinds of sufferings. Poisonous, painful, difficult to endure. Thieu kim world, conquering the body, children due to warmth, often suffering, forbidden, Buddha's divine power, method of speaking, serving memories of the past world possessing causes and conditions of evil karma.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One knew which tried meant asked: “Last life,

What evil karma have you done, now in the crowd, your mouth cannot speak? Those people all said to the Buddha together. Among them, there was a type of person who said like this: "Venerable World-Honored One! In the past, we were in the dharma of Vairocana Tathagata, either uttering words to slander the Mahayana dharma, or uttering words to slander the Pratyekayana dharma, or uttering words to slander the Sravakayana dharma, even just one chant. Due to that evil karma, we are constantly going through birth and death in ninety-one lifetimes, often in hell, being born as an animal, hungry ghost, mute, speechless, tongueless, always unable to speak, suffering from sufferings, poisons, extreme pain, difficult to bear. Starting from this life, I can regain my human body, still mute, speechless, often tongue-tied, thanks to the Buddha's divine power, I can speak, and can think and remember all the causes and evil karma in past lives")

The Buddha saw those people repenting, paying respects, knowing what karma they had created in the past. The Buddha wanted them to speak for themselves. Even though they knew clearly, they still intentionally asked. He asked: "In your past lives, what evil deeds did you do that made you unable to speak in public?" “The group of people, in turn, said to the Buddha. In the middle, one kind of person acted like a saying” (Those people all said the same thing to the Buddha. Among them, there was one type of person who said like this), not the whole at all, only quoting the words of the minority. “Venerable World-Honored One! Nhe is the same person who blasphemes the Dharma of Bhikkhu-Patri Tathagata, or speaks slandering the Mahayana Dharma” (Venerable World-Honored One! We were once in the dharma of Bhikkhu-Phat-Tathagata, uttering words that slander the main Dharma of Mahayana): Bhikkhu-Phat-Sam-Buddha is the same Bhikkhu-Shy-Buddha (Vipaśyin) in Fifty-three Buddhas are often worshiped.

During the time of Pi-Bat Thi Buddha, we blasphemed the Mahayana dharma, "or words that slandered the Pratyekayana dharma, or words that blasphemed the Sravakayana dharma" (or uttered words that blasphemed the Pratyekabuddha's dharma, or spoke that slandered the Sravakayana dharma), up to the point of blaspheming a single verse. Although there is very little defamation, the crime is still very great. Due to that sin, that is, the crime of slandering Mahayana sutras, Pratyekabuddha sutras, three-vehicle sutras, that is, slandering all three yanas, slandering the Dharma Jewels, we have gone through ninety-one lifetimes of birth and death, falling into hell since the time of Bhikkhu Buddha.

Escape from hell, either turning into an animal or turning into a hungry ghost. Because they destroy the Dharma, they cannot speak. But they repented, and because of the Buddha's blessing, they were able to speak again. This shows that the karma has been partially purified, and now one can be in this dharma assembly, blessed by the Buddha's divine power, and able to attain Sufficient Life. If you can think and remember, you must achieve Sufficient Network Information. If not, how will you know? In fact, they can participate in that dharma conference, which means their karma is lighter than ours. We can't participate yet. If we see Buddha, perhaps enlightenment will be possible. Perhaps those people are powerful beings who appear in that assembly for others to see. Therefore, the Buddha said that each sutra has many causes and conditions. Although there are people who do not make that mistake, they appear to make that mistake. This is stated to warn other sentient beings in the Dharma assembly!

(Sutra) One of a kind, works like a saying: "Venerable World-Honored One! Is the ego in the past? The Tathagata's Poetry and Qi are in the Dharma, or words that slander the Mahayana Dharma", all depend on the original conditions, as previously preached. It is of the best kind, acting like a declaration: "Venerable World-Honored One! I am eternally present in the Dharma of Bhikkhu-Fu Tathagata, or words that slander the Mahayana Dharma", all depend on the original conditions, as before. It is of the best kind, acting like a declaration: "Venerable World-Honored One! Is the ego eternal? Yet Lac Ca Ton Da Tathagata is in the middle of the dharma, or the language slanders the Mahayana correct dharma", depending on the original conditions, as previously preached. It is of the best kind, acting like a statement: "Venerable World-Honored One! Is the ego of the past intact? Yet Nacāmāmī Ni Tathagata in the Dharma, or words that slander the Mahayana Dharma", all depend on the original conditions, as previously preached.
(Sutra: There is another kind of saying like this: “Venerable World-Honored One! We were once inside The Dharma of Poetry Tathagata, or utter words that slander the Mahayana Dharma", each person depends on their own condition as has been widely said above. There is also a type of saying like this: "Venerable World-Honored One! We were formerly in the Dharma of Vairocana Tathagata, or utter words that slander the main Dharma of Mahayana", each person according to their own condition as has been widely said above. There is another type of saying like this: "Venerable World-Honored One! We were in the past in the Dharma of Yet Lac Ca Ton Da Tathagata, either utter words that slander the Mahayana dharma", each person depends on their own condition as widely said above. There is another type of saying like this: "Venerable World-Honored One! We used to live in the dharma of Yet Nac Ca Mau Ni Tathagata, or utter words that slander the Mahayana dharma", each person depends on their own condition as has been widely said above).

After that type had finished speaking, there was another type, that is, another type of person who repented and said: “Venerable World-Honored One! Is the past and present in the middle of the Tathagata's Poetry Qi Dharma” (In the past, Venerable World-Honored One, we were in the Dharma of the Tathagata's Poetry Qi): After Bhikkhu Bhikkhu Buddha is Buddha's Poetry (Śikhin). This Buddha also belongs to the last four Buddhas of the Adornment Kalpa. "The most effective type of work is like a declaration: - Venerable World-Honored One! I am the one who is past and present, Bhikkhu Pham Tathagata, or the one who slanders the Mahayana Dharma, depending on the origin, is like the pre-explanation. The one who is most worthy of the role is like the message: - The Venerable World-Honored One! NThe person who is equal to the past is the Buddha's name, Yeti Lac Ca Ton Da Tathagata's Dharma" (There is another type that says like this: - Venerable World-Honored One! We were in the past in the dharma of Viśvabhu, Tathagata, or uttered words that slandered the Mahayana dharma. Each person depends on his own destiny, as has been widely said above. There is also another type that says like this: "Venerable Lord! We were in the past in the dharma of Yeti Lac Ton Da Tathagata): This is the Exalted Buddha Sutra. (Krakucchanda), or in the Tathagata's Dharma, slandering the Mahayana Dharma. “All depend on the original conditions, as previously preached” (Everyone depends on their own conditions, as stated extensively in the previous section): The words of repentance are all similar words, so while the Buddha preached the Dharma, “The Buddha said: - Venerable The World Venerable! Nthe one who has passed away is the Dharma-dwelling Yeti Ca Mau Ni Tathagata”; This is also the Buddha Kanakamuni, “or words slandering the Mahayana Dharma” (or uttering words slandering the Mahayana Dharma), then “depending on the original conditions, as before preached” (each person depending on your own destiny as mentioned in the previous section).

(Sutra) One of a kind, it acts like a declaration: "Venerable World-Honored One! Is the past of the past? In the midst of the three Tathagata Dharmas, either words that slander the Mahayana Dharma, or words that slander the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, or words that slander the Sravaka Vehicle Dharma, the summer solstice is one chant.
(Sutra: There is another type, which says like this: “Venerable World-Honored One! We once lived in in the Dharma of Kasyapa Tathagata, or utter words that slander the Mahayana Dharma, or utter words that slander the Pratyekayana Dharma, or utter words that slander the Shravaka Vehicle Dharma, even if it's just a single verse."

Ku Luu Buddha, Kasyapa Buddha (Kāśyapa, Kasyapa), Ku Na Ham Muni Buddha, and Sakyamuni Buddha are the four Buddhas in the thousand Buddhas of the Sage Kalpa. Why do we recite the “seven Buddhas” every time we recite, because each of the seven Buddhas succeeds [in the world]. After Kasyapa Buddha is Shakyamuni Tathagata. After Śākyamuni Buddha comes Maitreya Bodhisattva. Before Kasyapa Buddha was Ku Na Ham Muni Buddha. Before Gou Na Ham Muni Buddha was Venerable Gou Luu Buddha. The distance between two Buddhas is long or short depending on the causes and conditions of sentient beings. Śākyamuni Buddha and Maitreya Buddha are fifty-six billion years apart. We feel it is very long, Maha Brahma feels it is very short!

One ​​hundred years in the human world is one day and one night in the Four Kings. Five hundred years in the Four Kings Heaven is equal to one day and night in Dao Loi Thien. A thousand years on Dao Loi Thien is equal to one day and night on Da Ma Thien. Just keep looking up to calculate, until you reach the Great Brahma, how many tens of thousands of years there are in the human world, keep increasing tenfold. We see time as very long, but the gods see it as very short, and Śākyamuni Buddha is not just a Śākyamuni Buddha! In the story about Dao Tuyen the lawyer, it is written that Dao Tuyen the lawyer was offered to a god. Every day that god offered [food to] the magician Dao Tuyen. Dharma Master Dao Tuyen then asked that god: "Now that Śākyamuni Buddha has passed away, where will he go?" The god asked back: "Which Śākyamuni Buddha do you ask?" From that god's question, we know that there are many Śākyamuni Buddhas. He asked lawyer Dao Tuyen in return: "Which Śākyamuni Buddha?" “I asked Śākyamuni Buddha in this world.” He replied: "This Śākyamuni Buddha has not yet entered nirvana. He is still preaching the Dharma in the world, but you cannot see it." From that interview, we can know: It's just because of our karma! Every Buddha is like that, because Śākyamuni Buddha is present, so they don't talk about Śākyamuni Buddha. These are all people who created evil in the previous six Buddhas. There are also people who say: "We treat the disciples of those Buddhas, whether they are Dharma weapons or not Dharma weapons, arousing contempt, insulting and disturbing them in all kinds of ways, causing them not to be at peace."

“Repentance talk: I am the same as the immeasurable monastic disciples of the Buddhas” (Someone also said: “We are to the monastic disciples of those Buddhas”): Each person's words of repentance are different, but the situation is the same, only a few sentences have changed slightly. “Either they show a dharma weapon, or a non-dharma weapon, they return to the world” (Either a dharma weapon, or not a dharma weapon, forcing them to return to the world): This type of disciple in the past was definitely powerful. This kind of penitent person, if not the king, how would he have the power to force others to return to the world? “Returning to the world, escaping from ca-sa” (Forcing to return to the world, stripping off ca-sa), up to and including taxation. The monks do not pay taxes, because they have no income and do not need to pay taxes.

Anyone who forces monks to pay taxes, taxes temples, or orders them to do forced labor will, in the future, fall into hell. You say to the tax collectors: "Okay! If you collect taxes, monks, you will fall into hell." In the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, the Buddha said so, it is called “persecution” (persecution). But for Bhikkhus who break the precepts, there can be two ways to say it: They make money, go to work, of course they have to be taxed. They do business, open shops, of course they have to pay taxes. Currently, when you come here to change your fate, you also have to pay taxes. No matter how much you earn, no matter how much you earn, you still have to pay taxes. That's called “lockdown” (taxation, forced labor). Even forcing you to do forced labor is because you don't have money and are extremely poor! Hard work, miserable work, hard work without pay. That's called “forced labor”.

“The Buddha's speech: I am the same as the immeasurable monastic disciples of the Buddhas” (There are also people who say: “We are to the monastic disciples of the immeasurable Buddhas”): “Immeasurable” refers to many Buddhist disciples in the past, regardless of whether that person is a Dharma weapon or not. It must be the same with the Dharma weapon, "arousing contempt for the heart, the seed touches the mind" (arousing the mind of contempt, all kinds of insults, confusion), does not persecute them, does not scold them, does not beat them, nor tax them, but makes them unhappy, always causing them to give rise to afflictions.

(Sutra) Fall due to the test of evil karma, suffering countless lifetimes, experiencing great suffering, suffering from poison, difficult to endure, After attaining enlightenment, he enlightened countless Buddhas, his close relatives, and made offerings to him. You will be able to enlighten and enlighten the countless Bodhisattvas, Mahasattvas, and herons who are close to you, take care of you, and make offerings to you. The most precious Buddha, the most Bodhisattva, Ma Ha Tat money, deep and precious, revealing repentance of evil karma. The one Buddha, the one Bodhisattva, Mahasattva, is able to hear and receive countless teachings, diligently protect, practice and practice countless difficult austerities. Due to the end of karmic obstacles, the spirit of the lower level can attain the peace and joy of Nirvana, and can attain the supreme merit of the Samadhi gate. The alchemist, the World-Honored One, has written and preached the sutras, conquered his deep thoughts, revealed his repentance, and has no feelings of riches. He vows to completely destroy them. Avoiding the past, forever undoing, protecting against future sins. I only wish that the World-Honored One, whoever is diligent in taking care of his life, will destroy his soul, the level of sin, and in the future, there will be no creation. I only wish that the World-Honored One, whoever is considerate in offering sacrifices to the fallen, will be punished by the evil beasts in the future. I, the alchemist, possess the divine power of the Buddha. I wish to quickly attain the peace and joy of Nirvana according to my wishes, or to attain the supreme merit of the Samadhi gate.
(Sutra: Due to that evil karma, we have gone through countless lifetimes, suffering heavy suffering and suffering. After that, I met countless Buddhas, all of whom were close to them, made offerings to them, and met countless Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, who were also close to them and made offerings to me. Before each Buddha, each Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, they were deeply ashamed and revealed their evil karma. learning countless difficult ascetic practices. Because of the residual karma that has not yet been exhausted, we have not yet been able to attain the peaceful Nirvana, and have not been able to attain the supreme merits of the samadhi gate. We are now deeply ashamed before the World-Honored One, and we repent and do not dare to hide it. From now on, we will never do it again, to prevent all future sins. cause all our sins to be destroyed. In the next life, we will never create them again. We respectfully ask the World-Honored One to have mercy on us and save us from our evil destiniess in the future. We will now rely on the Buddha's divine power to quickly attain Nirvana, or to attain the supreme merits of the Samadhi Gate.

It is precisely because in the present, "the text tests the sutra, restores the depths of the mind, reveals repentance" (hearing this sutra, deeply ashamed, revealing repentance), although I had repented before, now hearing the Buddha speak this sutra, I feel even more ashamed, revealing repentance. For the karma you have done, do not just repent once or twice, but repent countless times. From now on, "prevent future sins" (prevent all future sins), don't dare to commit them again!

(Sutra) Ushi, the World-Honored One, the Shravakas and Bodhisattvas wrote: "Good ear! Good ear!" Those who are of the same level, reveal their repentance. They have the right to be a virtuous person. One person is pure in nature, but the other person does not commit any crime. He reveals the two types of repentance. He is strong in the dharma and is a good man. He is a virtuous and pure man. He is a disciple of the Buddha The sin of trying to confuse the Buddha's disciples, the previous teachings of the Five Immaculate Conception are countless. Why do the Buddhas destroy the forbidden precepts, commit evil deeds, and by their ability to enlighten countless sentient beings, attain Nirvana, destroy the path of madness, harm all living beings, and treasure the treasures as before preached, let alone uphold the forbidden precepts and practice good dharma? Trying to destroy all sentient beings' dharma eyes, destroying the self and nine needs to suffer in attaining the true Dharma, causing great harm to all sentient beings, causing great harm to the Buddha's disciples.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One told all the Shravakas and Bodhisattvas: “Good. How good! You can be ashamed and repent like that. There are two types of people who are said to have done nothing wrong: One is a pure-hearted person who has not committed a crime. The other is a person who is ashamed and confesses. In my Dharma, he is called a strong and pure man Cockroaches mentioned in the previous section, the previous crime is only a name, not worthy of being called a crime, but this sin of deranged Buddha's disciples is countless times worse than the crime of Ngu Ngu Ngan mentioned before. Why is it that, like those who destroy the forbidden precepts and create evil things, they can still teach countless hundreds of thousands of na-du-da sentient beings the good path, the undeviating path leading to Nirvana, creating great merit for sentient beings, which is a treasure. treasure as mentioned extensively in the previous section, let alone those who keep the precepts and practice good dharmas? Because of this, if there are people who are deranged and become disciples of the Buddha, you should know that they have destroyed the nature of the Three Jewels, also known as blinding the Dharma eyes of all sentient beings, but also destroying the Dharma that we have worked hard to achieve for a long time, creating great harm for sentient beings. Therefore, the sin of derangement of the Buddha's disciples is worse The Five Infinite sins mentioned in the previous section countless times).

Although such statements are different, the meaning is exactly the same. The Buddha told everyone: “How good! How good! You (i.e. the sentient beings mentioned above) can be ashamed and reveal such repentance". There are two types of sentient beings who are called non-offenders, one type is "naturally pure, originally non-violating" (naturally pure, inherently non-violating), that is, people who maintain pure precepts. What about the second type? Even though they have committed, they can still be ashamed, can still be ashamed. repent and want to change. These two types of people are called brave and strong people in my dharma.

Repenting of sins is very difficult! In front of so many people, talking about the mistakes you made yourself is very embarrassing, right? I can't open my mouth! Showing off your merits and praising yourself is much easier said than done. Just a little bit, that person can say a lot. On the contrary, repenting for your own sins, you don't want to say anything! How to do it? In front of Buddha, Bodhisattva said, ghosts and gods will prove it to you, and dharma protectors will prove it to you. If you are too embarrassed to speak in front of everyone, you can confess in front of the Buddha statue. When we bow, why do we have to bow separately? Many people, repenting, only say those sentences, everyone is the same. Although the sentence [repentance] recited is very complete, the crimes you have committed are actually different. When you return home, face the Buddha statue, pray: "I have committed those sins." Why do people say I'm not good? We do a little good and then others sabotage it, what is the reason? Basically, in my past life, I said people were not good. Think about it, how much have you done in your mind [thinking badly of others] to the point of picking on, slandering, and despising others? Especially for monastics, or for religious friends. There are probably only a few of us who [offend against] monks, but among Upasakas or Upasikas, there are too many of these things, especially Upasakas, we must pay special attention! Among Dharma friends, we don't see each other's strengths, we only see our shortcomings. Other people's strengths were hidden, and her shortcomings were announced everywhere: "Oh my God! You see, layperson X... today took fruit from the temple!" She did not know that the fruit was given to [that layperson] by the master.

I've seen this kind of thing! After that, there were people who came crying, telling stories, and blaming others. I said: "That's what I gave her!" Don't worry, your guilt [from being exposed by her] will be eliminated like that. Don't be upset, there's nothing wrong. Because of her defamation, you committed a crime that should have sent you to hell and escaped. I'm not talking casually, that's what the Diamond Sutra teaches. Everyone reading the Diamond Sutra, let's see if it's true or not? In this way [anyone who is defamed by others] will be very happy. If you don't explain it like that, afflictions will arise in [that person's] mind. Is it [self-inflicted] afflictions? Especially when we study very diligently, we are very afraid of others saying we are not good. If someone says I'm not good, get angry right away! After that, between fellow Daoists, one thing became two things, very much involved! You don't have [those bad things], don't be afraid! No matter what that person says, that person won't harm you at all, it's useless! [Remember]: "You speak with the intention of making me suffer after hearing it. No matter how blasphemous you are, I won't listen to you at all!" Because, every Dharma friend also has these things; What should you do if you encounter it? Be ashamed! You don't have such great virtue, so you hope others won't say anything about you, that's impossible! Śākyamuni Buddha was still spoken harshly by others, there were people who insulted him, and there were people who considered surpassing him. Śākyamuni Buddha did not say anything, but the person who created that cause and effect for him fell into hell and suffered! There are people who receive retribution right in this life, "when they set up a pole, they see a shadow"!

Helping others, helping that person go one step further, that person knows that his own morality is not enough, why do people say this and that to us? Because we ourselves are not moral enough! You should be ashamed. Whenever you hear it, you must repent. If I say this life is very good, what about my previous life? What about infinite lives? The person who defames you is because in the past you spoke ill of others. Why don't you repent? Because right now you can't see it. If everyone had magical powers and knew that this was the case, they would be at peace. Because we don't know the past, we only look at the present. Looking at the present, it will not be possible to solve the problem. When studying the sutras, don't think of those sutras over and over again, just grasp a few points and you'll be fine! We always feel that no matter what time we are repenting, even the Fully Enlightened Bodhisattva is still repenting. You yourself should be skillful in praying for yourself, look outward and pray outside, you will not be able to pray! Please pray for your own mind.

I tell an old story, Zen master Phat An and Su Dongpo two people came to the temple. Su Dongpo asked Zen master Phat An: "What is Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva holding a rosary for?" Zen master Buddha An replied: "To recite." “Who do you remember?” “He chants Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!” To Dongpo said: "Is it possible that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva chants Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva?" Zen master Buddha An said: "If you don't remember yourself, then who will you remember?" That's the first thing. To Dong Pha asked again: "Do you pay your respects?" Zen master Buddha An said: "Thank you!" To Dong Pha said: "Hello who?" Zen master Buddha An said: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva bows to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!" After several rounds of questions and answers, Zen master Phat An told To Dongpo: "You have been enlightened."

Everyone, consider whether [we] are enlightened or not? Afraid that we are still not enlightened, knowing what this means? The mind of every Buddha is your mind. You just need every thought to be Avalokiteshvara, or every thought to be yourself. Don't think about your own body! Your physical body can cause sins, remember your own Dharma body. That Dharma Body includes all Buddhas, [reciting one's own Dharma Body] is reciting all Buddhas, reciting all Bodhisattvas, one means all, has this meaning! Why say so? Buddha then explained to them. Revealing that there are two types of people in repentance, in my dharma, “one who is brave and strong achieves purity” (called one who is brave, strong, and achieves purity).

If “good man! Na mentally deranged disciple of the Buddha is guilty, then the crime of the theory of Near-Non-Interrupting” (good man! Such a sin of mentally deranged disciple of the Buddha, compared to the crime of Near-Non-Interrupting mentioned in the previous section) is even more serious. more! [Because the crime of Near Vo Interruption] is only a name, not to mention a crime. That means the crime of Near Ngu Vo Tien is still not counted as a crime! But the sin of deranged disciples of the Buddha "the heron who had previously preached the Five Uninterrupted sins is immeasurably many times more" (also countless times more serious than the sin of the Five Uninterrupted Words mentioned in the previous section), is even more serious than the sin of the Five Uninterrupted Words. Therefore, falling into hell means falling into the Hell of No Cockroaches, and the time to escape is especially long.

Why is that? “If the Śūsū destroy the forbidden precepts and create evil dharmas, due to's ability to guide countless hundreds of verses of na-du-da sentient beings, the good destination of Nirvana will be reversed without madness" (Like the Śūsōs who destroy the forbidden precepts and create evil dharmas, they can still teach the good path leading to Nirvana, a path that is not crazy for countless hundreds of thousands of Śū-chi na-vu-da sentient beings). Even though that person broke the precepts and was a corrupt monk, he was still able to preach the Dharma to countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, allowing them to reach Nirvana, [showing them] the path without going crazy. Furthermore, "beings who create great merit, cherish and treasure" (make a treasure of great merit for sentient beings), means that he is a treasure as widely said in the previous section; What more if a [bhikkhu] who upholds the precepts and practices good dharma [has even greater merit]? In the previous section, regarding this situation, the Buddha said a lot. In the previous text, [the Buddha told] a monk who breaks the precepts is still a treasure trove containing precious treasures for all sentient beings, which can be used without end; What's more, those who keep the precepts well and practice good dharma! Those of you who are mentally deranged, the crime is even greater!

Why do I (Buddha) say such a great crime? He who destroys, defames, destroys, destroys the Dharma, destroys the Bhikkhu Sangha, has blinded the Dharma eyes of all sentient beings, and is also destroying the Dharma that I have achieved by diligently suffering for countless millions of eons. “Making evil beings cause great harm” (Creates great harm to sentient beings): Damages the merit and Dharma store of sentient beings. "The crime of being presumptuous and deranged as a disciple of Buddha is an immeasurable number of sins beyond the theory of the Five Uninterrupted Disciples" (Therefore, the crime of deranged mind among the Buddha's disciples is countless times greater than the crime of the Five Uninterrupted Disciples mentioned in the previous section).

(Kinh) Market, equality Precious, considerate and urgent, revealing the past repentance that creates evil karma, the compassion of the metal accepts the same level, the evil karma is gradually destroyed. In the Buddha Land, in the middle of the Sage Kalpa, Tathagata appears in this world, such as the previous Tathagata and herons are determined to reveal repentance, overcome evil karma, and protect all future sins. In the midst of the Tathagata's Good Kalpa, the Tathagata's final name is written as Lo Chi Tathagata, Fully Enlightened, Full of Wisdom and Virtue, Good Oath, Understanding of the World, Unsurpassed Man, Regulator, Teacher of Heaven and Man, Buddha, Silver Old Brahma, the ten complete names. In the same way as the previous Buddha Lo Chi, the heron is determined to reveal and repent of all evil karma, she will attain cessation, there will be no residue.
It is necessary, urgent, to reveal and repent of the evil karma created in the past. I now compassionately accept you, causing the evil karma to gradually disappear. In this Buddha land, in the Great Kalpa, there are a thousand Tathagatas appearing in the world. In front of those Tathagata, you should also sincerely repent of the evil karma, preventing all the sins in the future In this Good Life, the last Tathagata is named Lo Chi Tathagata, Fully Enlightened One, Perfect Wisdom, Perfection of Virtue, Understanding of the World, Unsurpassed Man, Regulator, Teacher of Heaven and Man, Buddha, Bodhisattva Pham, the ten names are complete. You should also sincerely reveal and repent of all evil karma until it is completely eliminated.

Shame is not enough, it must also be “high and noble”. We study the Dharma for the purpose of improving our minds, making us develop our minds, making our vows, making our repentance for our crimes always increase. Why do we have to listen to sutras? After listening to a sutra lecture, you will have a higher level of mind. If you don't listen, you won't have that mind, [that mind] won't arise easily! In the Second Bodhidharma Treatise, special attention is paid to increasing the upper conditions; But in terms of karma, it is also an increase in karma. Evil conditions increase, your karma also increases. The meaning of “high priest” is like that, the high priest must be shy, considerate, urgent.

If you can initiate repentance, you cry in pain, at least your whole body sweats profusely, even shed tears, repenting until your eyes bleed, then it is truly pure repentance. Truly recognizing crime is truly terrifying. Some people say that the suffering of hell is because the Buddha threatened us, is there really the suffering of hell? Wait until you suffer, you will know, it's too late! Suppose at that time you do not have good roots, you recite the holy name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, come quickly and save me! I am in hell." Hell immediately became nothing. Unfortunately, at that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva had long been forgotten. I couldn't think of it at all!

When we dream and see evil conditions and wake up from the dream, think about why we don't recite Buddha's name? In the dream, I was scared and my body was drenched in sweat. That's when you normally don't have any effort, and when you have to use it, you can't use it! The fuse in your house is blown, because you didn't learn [how to fix it], don't know where it is, can't find it! Even if you see it, you don't know it, you don't pay attention there, [so] you don't know, everything is like that. At first glance, it seems very simple, [but] you don't understand it, and you don't know it either. Therefore, it is necessary to be ashamed, repent well, or pray to Buddha for mercy and blessings. That is inconceivable!

For example, inviting a worker, you see, is a very simple matter. That person did it in a hurry and was done, and asked for a lot of money. You can't think: "Just need to do a few steps and ask me for so much money?" Let me tell you a story: Sun Yat-sen (Ton Van) in Shanghai, at that time, the place where he lived had a tap water system. The faucet is broken and cannot be turned off. Calling a worker to come fix it, Mr. Ton saw the worker turn it two or three times, touch it a little more and it was done, the water stopped flowing. Mr. Ton asked: "How much money?" That person said: "Twenty dong." At that time, twenty coins was quite a lot! Mr. Sun asked: "Why are you so expensive, asking for so much money?" That person replied: "Is it expensive? It's not expensive! I'll calculate it for you. I studied from elementary school to middle school, graduated from high school, I went to technical school. It took me several years to learn and understand. Isn't that worth the money?" Mr. Sun thought about it, it made sense! I just think he's expensive, I don't think how people have to learn to have that skill!

Like Ferdinand A. von Zeppelin invented the flying boat[22]. He sold all his fields and farms. Finally, when firepower was not enough, everything in the house that could be burned was thrown into the steel furnace. In the end, all six of his relatives left him, everything was gone, and he was alone! In the end, he invented the flying boat, which was called the Zeppelin. I saw that story, so I said: "You must understand, every piece of knowledge is every piece of effort, regardless of profession! Moreover, if you want to study Buddha, become a disciple of Buddha, want to attain Buddhahood, end countless lives of birth and death, can you achieve it even if you are evil and evil?" You must definitely realize that, then your shameful mind can arise! Wishing to end suffering and be happy, you see people achieving wealth easily, don't be jealous, they have their own destiny! Don't think that being an official is good. That's spending money to commit a crime! Wait until that person suffers and repent, then that person will know. Using the guise of "serving for the people", waiting until they gain power, that person does not think about the people, does not do good things for the people, but only thinks about himself!

“ Trying the Buddhaland, The Middle Sage Kalpa” (In the Great Sage Kalpa in this Buddha land): In the Human Sage Kalpa, that is, the Great Sage Kalpa, “the celestial Tathagata appears in the world” (there are a thousand Tathagata appearing in the world life): Currently four Buddhas have passed, there are still nine hundred and ninety-six Buddhas left. In the place of those Tathagatas, that is, before each of the thousand Buddhas, before each of those Buddhas, you must sincerely repent. The evil karma you have created will “protect against future sins” (prevent all future sins), because you will have to receive retribution, because of your sins, you will suffer retribution. You must be skillful in preventing it. If you repent, you won't have to suffer. You can avoid that debt of sin. "In the middle of the Tathagata in the middle of the Good Kalpa, Tathagata's final name is written Lo Chi Tathagata" (In the thousand Tathagata of this Good Kalp, the last Tathagata is named Lo Chi Tathagata): That is the Dharma Protector Vida, he finally became Buddha.

“Completely Enlightened, Perfectly Enlightened, Perfectly Virtuous, Well-Known, Understanding the World, Unsurpassed Man, Regulator, Master of Heaven and Man, Buddha, Silver Brahma”, [those are] the ten names of the Tathagata. Every Buddha has all ten names. You should treat Lo Chi Phat like you currently treat me! “Revealing repentance and evil karma” (Expressing repentance for evil karma). Only then will it be possible to “exterminate completely with no residue” (destroy everything, no leftovers), and still be able to repent of all your karma before Lo Chi Buddha. After that, it will be pure, forever no more. This is called “horoscope”. The Buddha will "tell a farewell" to that person. It is not a prediction to become a Buddha, that is something in the future. First of all, receive special notes for that person, that is [the content of] the Great Special Notes Sutra. That sutra is called Dai Ky Biet, not a promise, but intended to tell them: What must you do so that in the future you will be able to be pure.

(Sutra) Time, Sravakas, Bodhisattvas and Bodhisattvas, said to the Buddha: “However, World-Honored One! The ego is the ultimate enlightenment of the Buddha, attains the right view, abandons all wrong views, destroys evil karma without any residue, liberates all of the suffering souls of the Great Sage, always endures the Great Hell, constantly receives the most severe suffering, and has the ability to endure. The World-Honored One wrote: "Good ear! Good ear! The same level of power is like the strength of strength. The same level, through steadfast diligence and vowing force, the concentration ability to rely on Lo Chi Buddha's money, all the worldly accumulations of evil karma are completely destroyed, the concentration ability arises to increase faith, close to, make offerings to Lo Chi Tathagata, the concentration ability will permanently cut off all afflictions, become an Arhat, or the concentration ability will attain the supreme merit of Samadhi gate." At, the Shravakas visited the Bodhisattva assembly, rejoicing happy praise Buddha,

restore the position.

(Sutra: At that time, the Sravakas and Bodhisattvas at the same time said to the Buddha: “Yes, Lord World We will surely be in the ultimate Buddhahood, attain right view, abandon all wrong views, completely destroy all evil karma, and be free from all suffering. Even if we are in the Great Sagehood, constantly suffering all kinds of severe suffering, we can still endure it." The World-Honored One said: "Good! You can be so brave "Here, surely in Lo Chi Tathagata's place, all the evil karma accumulated in previous lives will be destroyed, and one will certainly develop a sense of trust and respect for the monks, be close to, and make offerings to Lo Chi Tathagata. One will certainly be able to permanently eliminate all afflictions, become Arhats, or one will certainly be able to attain supreme merit at the Samadhi Gate." At that time, the Shravakas and Bodhisattvas happily bowed to the Buddha and returned to their seats.)

Let us consider carefully, we must observe like that, we must do like that. Before Lo Chi Buddha, the last Buddha [in the Hien Kiep], repented purely. “Achieve right view, abandon wrong views, all evil karma will be completely destroyed without residue” (Achieve right view, leave wrong views, all evil karma will be eliminated, no remaining), completely destroy all evil karma, no longer exist. “No residue” means there is nothing left. "Free all sufferings" (Free all sufferings): All sufferings in the three paths, up to Kien Tu afflictions, Tran Sa can be liberated, but ignorance is still not eliminated. “The ability to endure” means being able to endure, being able to accept all dharmas that arise with immeasurable meaning. At that time, it will truly become a great dharma weapon. It is not until Lo Chi Buddha appears in the world that they can completely repent and become Buddhas.

As for the merits of each Buddha mentioned in the chapter Proclaiming the Buddha's Name of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, if we talk about each one individually, it would be very long. We bow every day, at least once a day, you must be skillful in dedicating, you must make your vows, don't miss it. Every Buddha is like that, they have the cause and condition to be called by the title Great Wisdom Tathagata[23], you can see countless millions of Buddhas giving you prophecies until you become a Buddha.

This is when we worship the last Buddha [in that sutra], which is the Great Wisdom Tathagata, we must pay attention. “Intent” means you should observe, think, contemplate, and do not miss out on the merits that are worth gaining. When you should repent of your sins, don't miss it. That is merit. Furthermore, both crimes and merits are non-existent. That practice of contemplation is Prajna Contemplation. All dharmas are dependently arisen, dependently arising from emptiness. In terms of essence or dharma nature, they do not exist. Contamination is the opposite of purity, crime is the opposite of merit. There is no merit, and no crime either. These relative dharmas do not exist at all, but you must have attained that status to be able to say that! Without reaching that level, [such empty talk] will be empty. I slapped you a few times, cursed you a few times, and you couldn't take it as a No! Yes No? Yes or no? No way! If we don't give you food for three days, you will be hungry and scream loudly; Can you stand it for a few days without drinking water? You say No, my body is all Emptiness. At that time, contemplation cannot be achieved, Emptiness cannot be achieved! If not, you will suffer immediately! We must understand this principle, immediately take this story as an example. You have committed a crime, or you have to pay the penalty now. If you don't "get vaccinated", at that time, you will definitely suffer. Why did the Great Bodhisattva come to save sentient beings? They are not infected by us, they have been "vaccinated", and have carefully defended their minds! Their mind is Emptiness, that is the True Emptiness, it is not Emptiness like ours. The Mahayana Dharma is definitive, but when you have not attained it, it will not have any effect and you cannot use it. Because you can't use it, you talk loudly!

Why couldn't Sakyamuni Buddha take control of those people, saying "Very well, you repent to me and that's enough. Your sins have been purified"? He never said anything like that. He knows you need to practice gradually, because you absolutely cannot reach that state.

Like us, even faith is not complete, we have to practice slowly. The reason I say “practice slowly” is because you are so diligent! Whenever we say "diligence in practice", [we immediately misunderstand] that we don't do anything, just worship! Who gives you food? The monk himself practices in the cave, not benefiting others, nor helping others. How can others help you? It's all mutual exchange! Although it's not an equal price exchange, it naturally has this meaning! Monks must make merit, even when eating food, they must dedicate it to others. Eating, drinking, sleeping, anytime, anywhere, you must think of others, always dedicate yourself to them. When it comes to going to the toilet, shouldn't we dedicate it? Going to the toilet is even more necessary [to do so]. When entering the bathroom, you make a vow "for all sentient beings, with greed, anger, and ignorance, to eliminate all sins and be completely pure" (pray for all sentient beings to abandon greed, anger, and ignorance, to eliminate all sins, and all be pure). When we enter there, we will abandon all our sins. We pray that all sentient beings will abandon greed, anger, and ignorance, and attain Nirvana. Even there, still not letting go. Walk, stand, lie down, sit, twenty-four hours a day, at any time make a vow, vow for all sentient beings to become Buddhas, always repent, repent of your sins!

The fourth vow in Samantabhadra's Vows says: If our sins had a form, this world could not contain it. The void is broken. Fortunately, sin has no form, it is Emptiness. Please understand this principle. Therefore, when repenting for sins, one must rely on the fourth great vow in the chapter Samantabhadra Vows to repent; If you rejoice in merit, you must rely on the fifth great vow to rejoice.

(Sutra) At the ear, the World-Honored One reported to Vajragarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva: - Good man! The Buddha's own eyes contemplate all worlds, see future worlds, test the Buddha's salvation, immeasurable beings, countless hundreds of thousands of verses of na-du-da Kshatriya-Chentala, Brahman-Chen-dala, minister-Chan-t-la, layperson-Chan-t-la, rich man-Chan-t-la, monks-Chan-t-la, Phiet-xa-Chan-t-la, Thu-datta-la Lambs and lass, weak men, weak women, with few good roots, although they attain the human body, they depend on evil friends, give rise to wrong views, create evil deeds, destroy the self and even reach the unsurpassed Dharma. The theory of non-existence of self, destruction of nature of dharma, non-creation of belief and ridicule, or the theory of evil in the Thanh Van Vehicle, corresponds to the correct dharma, slander, contempt, obscenity, concealment, and non-spirituality. Or the ego speaks evil of the Single Enlightened Vehicle corresponding to the true Dharma, slanders, despises, obfuscates, hides, and is not sacred. Or the ego speaks of evil in the Supreme Vehicle corresponding to the true dharma, defamation, contempt, obscenity, concealment, and unspiritual release.
