If you abandon anger, cultivate compassion, quickly attain enlightenment, and enjoy the holy deeds, you will be born in the pure Buddha land, stay away from evil faults, attain Bodhi, and be free from anger and anger. If you abandon wrong views, cultivate pure faith, and love the enlightenment of the three vehicles, you will also make offerings to the Buddhas, and forever be freed. evil destiniess, meeting saints and sages. Having enough Bodhisattva virtues, one attains the supreme wisdom. I say that the Ten Virtuous Karmas, or attaining Bodhi, give rise to great virtues of the Dharmas, Da-lanis, Patriarchs, and Earths. They can destroy evil destiniess and quickly attain great Bodhi.

“Weakness in abandoning desire, do not slander the holy teachings, make offerings to the ka-sa” (If you stay away from desires, do not slander the holy teachings, make offerings to people wearing the ka-sa): Transmit the ka-sa robe, propagate the three vehicles of the holy path. “When you are born in the pure Buddha land, the master's residence The unsurpassed vehicle” (Will be born in the pure Buddha land, the residence of the master. Relying on the unsurpassed vehicle): The Buddha resides in the pure Buddha land, which is the unsurpassed Mahayana. "Quickly attain the supreme wisdom, weak yet angry, one-way cultivating the mind of kindness, quick to attain the level of attainment of the holy land" (Quickly attain the supreme wisdom, even in the anger, constantly cultivating a loving mind, quickly attain the level of the mind, enjoy the practice of the saints): If you leave anger, leave greed, leave anger, practice Compassion, then only can you achieve Buddhahood. Equally maintaining (Equally maintaining) all dharmas, maintaining limitless meanings. "When reborn in the pure Buddha land, be far away from all evils, attain Bodhi in the long run, be free from anger and anger. Weakly abandon wrong views, purely cultivate pure faith, ridicule and enlighten the three vehicles, make offerings to the Buddhas. Forever escape from evil beasts, realize the sages and saints, Bodhisattva virtues, attain supreme wisdom" (Will be born in a pure Buddha land, far away from evil faults, attain Bodhi there, If you abandon evil views, cultivate pure faith, love to enlighten the three vehicles, and also make offerings to the Buddhas. Forever free from evil destiniess, meet saints and sages, possess Bodhisattva virtues, and attain supreme wisdom): Only then can you achieve Supreme Bodhi.

“If I talk about the Ten Good Karmas, one can overcome Bodhi, give birth to the Dharma Tris, Da-lani, Patience, and Earth. Test the great majesty of the wheel, defeat the evil beasts, destroy all evil obstacles, quickly attain great Bodhi” (I say the Ten Good Karmas, or enter Bodhi, one will grow) This wheel has great virtue, destroys evil destiniess, destroys evil obstacles, and quickly attains great Bodhi): This is a general statement. The Ten Virtuous Wheels are the achievements of the supreme Bodhi's cause, which can give rise to ten immeasurable dharmas, that is Da-lani. The immeasurable dharma is the Samadhi, the Da-la-ni, the samadhi. “Da-la-ni, Forbearance, Ground” is the Ten Rings, Ten Grounds. The mighty virtue of this wheel can destroy evil destiniess, destroy evil obstacles, and quickly attain great Bodhi.

Anywhere, full of great wealth, virtuous, intelligent, peaceful, happy, not having the same property as the five families. Again meeting a lovely person, subduing good dharma, full of virtue, full of virtue, true field of good knowledge, practicing and abandoning "not giving and taking", can eliminate all evil and unwholesome dharmas, can achieve all excellent good dharmas, can pray for all Mahayana dharmas, can practice all. All of the Bodhisattva's vows, gradually entering the vast ocean of wisdom, until he attains Supreme Bodhi. The Buddha's land is filled with all kinds of solemn treasures, precious trees, precious ponds, precious platforms, palaces, etc. Nothing is incomplete. All sentient beings leave the self, have nothing to receive, and are fully adorned, and the Tathagata himself has an unlimited life span, because the living beings preach the Dharma in accordance with the Buddha's foundation Enter Nirvana, the Dharma will last a long time, bringing benefit and peace to countless sentient beings. This is called the second vow of "not giving but taking" of Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

“The bases are perfect, the members are complete, depending on the place of birth, the person is rich, righteous, intelligent, peaceful, happy” (The bases are perfect, the members are complete, wherever one is born, they are full of wealth, upright, intelligent, peaceful, happy). This passage is similar to the text in the previous section. Only the middle part talks about stealing or killing differently, the other things are the same: Being born as a human again, the six senses are complete, the limbs are also complete. Wherever you are born, you will have all the wealth. Of course your family is also very rich. Born into a good family, virtuous, intelligent, very good appearance, everyone who sees him likes him, wise, clever

benefit, peace, joy.

“Non-data of the five families plus treasures” (Not sharing property with the five houses): All wealth in the world belongs to the five houses. If you don't steal, you will be the master. Not in the same house year, which house year?

1) The country confiscates, or requisitions.

2) Or thieves and robbers. They rob you, you can't guard against it, or you get stolen by thieves. Those are two houses.

3) The water submerged, the flood swept away.

4) Fire burns, those are four houses.

All property in the world belongs to those five houses. You can be peaceful and happy. [Your] property is not shared by the five families, it is only your blessing that you feel. No one can confiscate your property! Your children and grandchildren are good-natured and do not give birth to disobedient children.

“Enlightenment pleasantly, become a good dharma, have good precepts, rich in virtue, a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), a good knowledge” (Once again meet a pleasing person, subdue and achieve good dharma, full of precepts, rich in virtue, a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) to become a good knowledge): Will rely on such a person to practice, follow that person to practice, learn the way, stay away "don't give but take", keep this precept pure, no more stealing! You can cut off all unwholesome dharmas as mentioned. Even if you only keep this one precept, you can complete the other nine virtues. There is one thing to break through, the other things are also complete. “The ability to achieve all the supreme good dharmas, the ability to seek all the Mahayana Dharma, the ability to cultivate all the Bodhisattva vows, to gradually penetrate the vast ocean of wisdom, to attain the Supreme Bodhi. To reside in the Buddha land, they adorn, preserve, maintain, preserve, protect, protect the throne, are unmatched" (Can achieve all the superior good dharmas, can pray for all the Mahayana dharmas, can practice all the Bodhisattva vows Slap, gradually enter the deep and wide ocean of wisdom, until he attains Supreme Bodhi. In the Buddha land he lives, all kinds of solemn treasures, treasured trees, treasured ponds, treasured platforms, palaces, etc. are not complete): This is like the Western Pure Land world. Everyone who recites the Amitabha Sutra knows that no matter what world they are born into, they are all the same. Being born in that land is the same as being born in heaven. When you go to that Buddha land, the Buddha himself, the World-Honored One, Tathagata, has an immeasurable life span. For the sake of all sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma according to his basic nature. When you go there, you can listen to the Dharma. After the Buddha's passing, in that world, "the true Dharma is nine-dwelling, benefiting and peace- ing immeasurable sentient beings. Good man! The second wheel of Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat is known as the second wheel of eternal separation and non-attachment" (the true dharma lasts for a long time, benefits and peace of immeasurable sentient beings. Good man! That is called the second wheel of "don't give but take" of Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat).

noi_dung:
VII. Blessings Ddien Td - Pham D Tthrow

(Pseventh level: General PPlace Dfield)

(Sutra) Phuc, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva possesses ten Great Armor Wheels of Gift Giving. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat accomplished testing the wheel, developed the initial mind, must eliminate the five stages of desire, overcome all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste must necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, create a great field of blessings. It is necessary for Thanh Van and Single Enlightened Vehicle to make offerings, take care of things, and protect them. Ha class vi ten? The department gives alms foods, clothes, treasures, statues, horses, hamsters, surpluses, self-protection, sufficiency, ears, intestines, head, rot, marrow, brain, skin, bones, blood, flesh, national city, wife, child, slave, and land. Just as in the act of giving alms at the same time, regardless of one's life and life, without focusing on selfishness, seeking in the world, beyond the world, develop the mind of giving; giving; desire induces all sentient beings to experience peace and happiness, develop the mind of giving; desire eliminates all sentient beings suffering and sorrow, develop the mind to give; does not win over others, has no coarse mind, has no jealousy, has no cheating mind, and does not practice alms. If you want to give things, if you don't have much, if you don't have enough, if you want to be truly real, you don't hope to receive self-retribution, and you develop the mind of giving; you don't hope to ask for the fruition of Shravaka Vehicle, to develop the mind of giving, and you don't want to ask for the fruit of the Single Enlightened Vehicle to develop the mind of giving. The desire to give alms, the weakest, the weakest, the summer will to be truly real, the one who hopes for All Kinds of Wisdom, develops the mind to give alms.
(Sutra: Come, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva has ten Wheels of Great Gifts. If the Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves this wheel, from the beginning, all the five desires can be eliminated, far surpassing all Sravakas and Solitary Enlightened Ones, because all Sravakas and Solitary Enlightened Ones cultivate fields of great merit, all Sravakas and Solitary Enlightened Ones should make offerings, take care of, and protect. head, eyes, marrow, brain, skin, bones, blood, flesh of oneself, country, wife, children, slaves, fields, houses. When giving alms like this, one does not care about one's own life, one does not only seek happiness in the world or in the world for oneself, but only because one wants to give birth to great compassion for all sentient beings. In order to bring forth wisdom and skill in superior means, one develops the mind of giving; because he wants to bring peace to all sentient beings, he develops the mind of giving; because he wants to eliminate suffering for all sentient beings, he develops the mind of giving; does not have the mind of being superior to others, does not have the mind of being rude, vulgar, does not have the mind of jealousy, does not have the mind of being stingy, but practices almsgiving With the alms given, whether large or small, even a meal, one does not seek the fruit of the Sravaka Vehicle but develops the mind of giving, one does not seek the fruit of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle but develops the mind of giving.

After talking about the chapter Ten Good Karmas, this chapter is the chapter Phuoc Dien General. The Ten Virtuous Karmas are the seven limbs of the body and mouth (i.e. killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, double-talking, embellishing, and harsh speech), plus greed, anger, and ignorance. This is conditioned, only talking about the dharma of the Shravaka Vehicle and the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. If we take it a step further, the Ten Virtuous Karma Paths from the Human Heavenly Vehicle to the Bodhisattva Vehicle are complete and are the common dharma of the five types of practitioners. If you use the Dharma of the Ten Virtuous Karmas to manifest and save sentient beings, you will be a Bodhisattva. If they are Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, they wish to practice Suffering, Origin, Cessation, Path, and the twelve causes and conditions, and must also take the Ten Good Karmas as the basis. According to the scriptures in the previous section, after death, one is reborn in the human world and achieves great merit; That is the merit and virtue that one should receive from the Ten Virtuous Karmas. If your mind penetrates visualization, it will be Mahayana. That is the dharma common to all three vehicles. Depending on the type of base, one will be able to receive the dharma of that type.

Different merit fields; [Here], the pure field of blessings speaks according to Bodhisattva Mahasattva. Phuoc fields to sow blessings, that is, fields to sow blessings are inconceivable. Each passage [text] and each cycle has two types of appearances: One is the appearance of the world, the other is the appearance of the world. In the world, Bodhisattvas follow sentient beings to speak and practice the Bodhisattva path, causing sentient beings to accumulate fields of merit. Bodhisattva's field of blessings is Empty, that is, “field of blessings without a field of blessings”. That is the meaning of “form is formless”. If a Bodhisattva wishes to practice the Bodhisattva path, that is, the Six Virtues of the Bodhisattva path, it is to use almsgiving as the foremost [among those actions]. First of all, let's talk about Gift Giving; Next, talk about Dharma Giving. If you do not use Dharma to give alms, do not use wealth to give alms, but hope to enter the world of living beings, it will be very difficult. In order to not be swayed by the five desires and not follow sentient beings into the world, we must be equipped with a bit of equipment. Therefore, what does the word Pillar in “great armor” mean? It is Khoi who covers his head (iron helmet or thick leather helmet). “Giap” is a team wearing armor. Because, if you want to save sentient beings, co-operate with sentient beings, and manifest as sentient beings, you must take a little protection.

How to hedge? That means a little equipment to protect yourself. What to use for protection? “Armor” is imagined as being in battle, having to wear armor to avoid being injured by the enemy. If you enter the realm of sentient beings to save sentient beings, you will not be tainted by sentient beings, will not be turned around by sentient beings, but can transform sentient beings. This is referring to the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, which also means that his spiritual power is very deep. By applying this cycle, we can eliminate the suffering caused by poverty and lack of sentient beings. Without money, you will be very miserable, so you must use your resources to give alms. If the Bodhisattva achieves the Great Armor Pillar of Wealth Giving, from the moment he first develops his mind, he will be able to eliminate the five desires. This is a bit inappropriate for us! I have been a monk for more than sixty years, and at present I still cannot completely get rid of the five desires, yet those Bodhisattvas, as soon as they made their minds up, got rid of the five desires and have no attachment to the world. But they never left the world, unlike Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha. As soon as you develop your mind, you can eliminate the five desires. In the previous section, we talked a lot about the realm of the five desires. Speaking shallowly, it's easy to understand: talent, beauty, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping. The reason why we cannot be diligent or leisurely is because we are drawn and led by the five desires! When we give alms, there is always a lot of pollution mixed in! In the previous section, when talking about the Ten Good Karmas, there were many impurities mixed in, not using a pure mind to practice almsgiving. No matter what you are doing, whether it is making offerings to the Three Jewels or even providing relief in society, in every action, there are many impure thoughts mixed in. The human world is not real, you will receive a crooked result. If your mind is not pure, if you hope to achieve the true result, it will be impossible!

This passage says Bodhisattva Mahasattva used Wealth as a tool to crush the five desires. When you develop your mind, practice the Bodhisattva path, and when you are talented in giving alms, you will eliminate the five desires. Currently, he not only eliminates the five desires, but also gradually destroys the dust of ignorance. Those Dharma Bodhisattvas cut off part of their ignorance and partially realized the Dharmakaya. Therefore, they far surpass all the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, creating a huge Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) throughout all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas. All those belonging to the two vehicles of Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha should make offerings to, assist, and protect this great Bodhisattva. Why? You benefit them. Bodhisattva Mahasattva can benefit all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas. That's speaking in general. Next, tell us how to distinguish the Great Armor Pillar of Wealth Donation?

“What is ten?” (What is ten?) has the meaning of questioning, provoking, to explain in general. “The position of giving alms is food, clothes, treasures, statues, horse, far, surplus, self-attachment, self-satisfaction, ears, nose, head, rot, marrow, brain, skin, bones, blood, flesh, national city, wife, child, slave, field. Nvoid giving alms one at a time, regardless of life” (That is, giving alms All kinds of food, clothes, precious jewelry, elephants, horses, vehicles, along with hands, feet, ears, nose, head, eyes, marrow, brain, skin, bones, blood, flesh of oneself, country, wife, children, servants, fields, houses like that, without regard for one's own life): Gifts [of Bodhisattvas] are not like the way we usually give alms. Therefore, when stated in general in the previous section, it was said to be “great Bodhisattva”. He can exhaust all his strength to give alms. That act of giving includes giving food, clothes, treasures, elephants, horses, vehicles, all things outside the body. There is also His own self, down to the six senses that can be given alms. Hands, feet, ears, nose, head, eyes, marrow, brain, flesh, flesh and blood, country, wife and children, slaves, fields, houses. When you give alms like this, you don't care about your own life. Bodhisattvas do not seek peace and happiness for themselves, they only wish for sentient beings to be free from suffering. That is the Bodhisattva's original intention. Therefore, becoming a Bodhisattva is a being with a great mind. He specializes in creating benefits for all sentient beings, never thinking about himself. Shows that the Ego Clinging has also been destroyed! If Dharma Acceptance exists, it will be impossible to give to the end!

[In the following section], there is also the Dharma Offering Ten Wheels, this part talks about the world of the Ten Wheels. There is also the Ten Wheels in the world. He did not seek happiness in this world or beyond the world for himself, but he developed the intention to give alms. True human ground, true feeling and true results, can achieve Anuttara Sammyak Sambodhi. While giving alms, He did not seek worldly benefits, nor did He seek even worldly benefits. What is the appearance of that blessed field? It is the Emptiness. Therefore, in the Diamond Sutra, the Buddha said, when Bodhisattvas practice almsgiving, making offerings, and doing all good deeds, but do not gain merit. Subhuti was immediately very skeptical, why did Bodhisattva practice the Bodhisattva path without merit? The Buddha said that Bodhisattvas are not attached to that merit. If he had attachments, he would not be a Bodhisattva. Therefore, He is just not attached to that! Not caring about his own life, even giving alms like that, only for the purpose of benefiting sentient beings. The Bodhisattva's great compassion is inconceivable, and cultivating compassion is not simple and can be done!

Asanga Bodhisattva wishes to be close to Tu Thi Bodhisattva, that is, Maitreya Bodhisattva. He stayed in the mountain practicing samādhi for ten years. Wishing to become a Buddha, hoping to eliminate all suffering for sentient beings, so it is called samādhi of loving mind. After practicing for ten years, he could not achieve anything, nor see anything, it seemed hopeless, and he immediately became discouraged. He went down the mountain, halfway down the mountain, he met an old woman holding a very large iron pestle that she was grinding into a needle. He asked: "Old lady! What are you doing?" The old lady replied: "I sharpen needles." “What is the needle sharpener for?” The old lady said: "My daughter is about to get married. I'm sharpening the needle to make clothes for her as a wedding outfit." Asanga Bodhisattva smiled and said: "If you grind it into a needle, I'm afraid your daughter will die. How can you grind it into a needle?" The old woman told Him: "If you put in the effort, it will naturally come true." He suddenly became enlightened and said: "I don't have that skill, so I can't see Tu Thi Bodhisattva!" He did not go, returned to the mountain to practice for another ten years, a total of twenty years, still nothing, not even an image. As we worship, recite the Buddha's name, hope for a good dream, and pray a lot, it all belongs to the physical form. Isn't that Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat raising his mind!

Therefore, He went down the mountain a second time. This time he made up his mind to leave, but did not encounter any realms. At the foot of the mountain, next to a river, I saw a dog. The dog had an ulcer on his stomach and was moaning and in great pain. Before leaving home to study Buddhism, Mr. Vo Truoc was a physician, specializing in treating sagging diseases. Now he is faced with this situation. He practiced compassion for twenty years, intending to help him heal, but that dog was too dirty. He thought: "If this dog were human, I could still cure him." He thought about it, skipped a paragraph, and thought again: "That's wrong! I cultivated the mind of compassion in samadhi for twenty years. Cultivation of the mind of compassion is equality towards all sentient beings, why is there a mind of discrimination?" He turned back, went and came back like that, repeated several times, but could not make up his mind. Finally, he thought: "Twenty years of effort should not be wasted, we still have to help him cure it." Therefore, he closed his eyes and sucked the pus from that wound. The wound must have been suctioned with the mouth. He sucked it up, thinking it was so disgusting, he would probably vomit. When about to vomit, the taste feels wrong! A festering ulcer cannot have such a delicious, wonderful taste! When I opened my eyes, the dog was gone and Tu Thi Bodhisattva appeared. Therefore, He immediately asked: "Dear Bodhisattva! I practiced for twenty years, bowed to You every day, prayed to You, and in the end You still tested me once!" Tu Thi Bodhisattva replied: "I am also very impatient. Every day I prepare to bless you, but you do not pay any attention to me." That's because there's karma!

Therefore, we know that using great compassion to develop the mind of giving is very difficult! Without supreme wisdom, our dream of great compassion and compassion would not be able to grow! It's not that I despise you, it's the same for me! Our great compassion is extremely limited! Everyone has a compassionate mind, but in our great compassion there is love. If it is our own friend, or if it is someone we respect or like, we will have compassion. If you encounter a resentful family, or a dog as mentioned above, and cannot generate compassion, how can you give alms, not caring about your own life, offering everything you already have to others? Can't bear it! We can test this ourselves, sometimes even taking alms back!

The realms in the Mahabodhi Sutra are getting deeper and deeper, how does it teach us to practice the Bodhisattva path? When making offerings to sentient beings, we consider them to be making offerings to Buddha, and we treat sentient beings like Buddha. Because Bodhisattvas want to become Bodhisattvas, according to the Samantabhadra Vows, if there were no sentient beings, we would not be able to achieve Bodhisattvas! It is difficult to repay the kindness of living beings, because living beings make it possible for us to become Buddhas. Therefore, after the great Bodhisattva developed the mind to give alms, his purpose and aspiration was to make all sentient beings everywhere able to become Buddhas, so that all sentient beings could also give birth to the dream of great compassion. Because of such a reason, I developed the mind to give alms. At the same time, because we want to develop wisdom and skillful means, we develop the mind to give alms. Leading who? Guide all sentient beings to also develop the mind of benefiting sentient beings, and teach each other in turn. At the same time, speaking according to the Bodhisattva himself, he brings forth wisdom to benefit his own sentient beings. The Bodhisattva's method to benefit sentient beings is his wisdom of means. Having to learn that method of wisdom, we also hope to help others. If the method is not correct, not only will you not be able to help, but you will also cause yourself a lot of trouble. Many Dharma friends have had this experience: For example, when we build a temple, we hope to make some merit, build a Buddhist Institute to create merit, listen to others say this and that, there are a lot of discussions, [in the end] no temple will be built, no Buddhist Institute will be established! They have withdrawn their minds and become rebellious. I've heard so much about this, why don't I dare say anything? Not to mention the Three Jewels' fault! Even about Upasaka and Upasaya, they did not dare to speak. Don't mention the faults of the four of them. That is the basic violation of the Bodhisattva's precepts. If the blessing field is not in accordance with the form of the blessing field, when the blessing is sown, it will basically not germinate and will turn into burned sprouts and flat seeds. In the section about the Ten Virtuous Karmas and the Ten Evil Wheels, it was said very clearly. If so, you will fall into the Infinite Hell, up to the Near Infinite Hell. Blaspheming the Three Jewels is worse than falling into the Unbroken Hell!

Why have you believed in Buddha for many years, but still have not achieved anything, what is the reason? We have created too much karma of body, mouth, and mind! You don't know that you are creating karma. If you compare a little with the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, you will know that the Ten Karmas of body, mouth, and mind, the Ten Good Karmas and the Ten Evil Karmas, the Ten Evil Wheels and the Ten Virtuous Wheels are especially difficult to prevent and protect. We think it seems very easy, that is an arrogant way of thinking, not sincere! Therefore, Bodhisattvas use their superior wisdom and skillful means to practice almsgiving, allowing all sentient beings to be able to give alms in peace and happiness. When you practice almsgiving, you must develop your mind, you must make a vow, you must be full of love, compassion, joy, equanimity, and the four immeasurable minds.

At the same time, the Bodhisattva uses his gift of alms to eliminate the suffering of all sentient beings, so he develops the mind of almsgiving. When sentient beings are in suffering, you must develop the mind to give alms, give money to them, you must develop the mind to be skillful in means, develop the mind to lead them into the Dharma, guide them to attain enlightenment, and escape birth and death. You still have to let go of everything, that's just using your wealth to guide them. Therefore, Buddhism says, when saving sentient beings, first use desire to attract and gradually lead them into Buddhism. That is, first use the things they like, or the things they lack, to lure them, gradually leading them to the Buddha way and accepting them. At the same time, while Bodhisattvas develop the mind to give alms, we should not compare with others, we should not say that someone spends more money, we need to surpass him. He spent ten thousand, I had to spend twenty thousand! No matter what other people's resources are, no matter what your resources are, there is no need to compare, no need to hope to surpass others. It's okay for you to practice your religion, which means don't have the mind to win over others, don't have the mind to be rude or vulgar. “Rude, vulgar mind” means the mind is not gentle, not kind, not gentle.

While giving alms, although wealth is great, it is mixed with all kinds of thoughts that are not pure and chaste. “Great wealth”[44] is not the mind of offering. Therefore, in the Ksitigarbha Sutra, when talking about the tenth chapter, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva invited the Buddha to compare the merits and teach about the merits of giving alms to sentient beings: Why do some people enjoy one life, some people enjoy ten lives, and some people enjoy hundreds of thousands of millions of lives without end? The same wealth does not increase more, what is the reason [that causes alms-givers to enjoy different blessings]? The mind disagrees! You must use the Bodhi mind, at least don't have the mind of wanting to win over others, don't have that kind of cruel mind! There is also jealousy. Many people have that jealous mind, and there are also those who are stingy. Although giving alms, later gives rise to regret, regret, stinginess, greed, jealousy, and even regret! Practicing alms like that, no matter how much or how little the object is given, "the summer solstice is one food" (even a meal), even giving alms of the seven treasures to fill an entire three thousand great worlds in the morning, noon, and afternoon, all three times practicing alms like that, still does not achieve great merit. There are even cases where merit and virtue do not exist, especially for the Three Jewels, but also for sentient beings. Regardless of whether you give a lot or a little, you should not hope to receive retribution for yourself, or give without expecting anything in return. Chinese Confucianists also think like that (“doing kindness without asking for reward”)! When you give alms hoping to be rewarded, that means you have an intention, that is not almsgiving. Even if you give very little alms, you still hope that others will repay you, then it is no longer almsgiving! [Just think] "I do good things", then your purpose is not pure!

If you develop the mind to give, do not seek the fruit of Shravaka Vehicle, but develop the mind to give, do not expect to attain Arhatship. Developing such a mind is too limited and small. We hope to end birth and death and end the world's bad habits; After that, destroy the worldly suffering and use the cause to cultivate the Way to attain Heavenly Emptiness and Nirvana, which is not the ultimate emptiness of Nirvana. That type is Thanh Van fruit ball. Looking forward to birth and death, hoping to attain Mahaparinirvana, you develop the mind to seek Buddhahood, develop the mind to attain Bodhi. Developing that mind of giving is Bodhi mind. Therefore it is said: Do not seek the fruition of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle but develop the mind of giving. Not only do I not wish for the status of Sravaka Vehicle, but I also do not wish for the status of Socetic Vehicle. Combining the two means [not wishing] for the fruition of the Second Vehicle. Regarding the items or material things to be donated, no matter how much or how little, "the summer solstice is one food, one's birthday is to pray for All-Kind Wisdom" (even a meal, just for the sake of wishing for All-Kind Wisdom), that is, to pray to become a Buddha. After that, for good deeds, no matter how big or small, every thought wishes to achieve Omniscience, hoping to attain Buddhahood. Having such a mind is correct!

(Kinh) Thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu như thị thập chủng Tài Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Sở dĩ giả hà? Thanh Văn, Độc Giác phát tâm bố thí, vô đại từ bi, đản vị kỷ thân xả bần cùng cố, đản vị kỷ thân thoát chúng khổ cố, đản vị kỷ thân đắc an lạc cố, đản vị kỷ thân chứng Niết Bàn cố, bất năng phổ vị nhất thiết hữu tình nhi hành bố thí. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phát tâm bố thí hữu đại từ bi, phổ vị hữu tình xả bần cùng cố, phổ vị hữu tình thoát chúng khổ cố, phổ vị hữu tình đắc an lạc cố, phổ vị hữu tình chứng Niết Bàn cố, bất vị tự thân nhi hành bố thí. Dĩ thị nghĩa cố, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng, giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát tu hành Tài Thí Ba La Mật Đa thời, ư diệu ngũ dục, tâm vô nhiễm trước, tự sở nhiếp thọ nhất thiết lạc cụ, phổ năng thí dữ nhất thiết hữu tình. Y phổ nhiếp thọ chư hữu tình tâm, y tự nhẫn thọ nhất thiết khổ tâm, y diệt nhất thiết hữu tình khổ tâm, y dữ nhất thiết hữu tình lạc tâm, y dữ hữu tình đại Niết Bàn tâm, nhi hành bố thí. Dĩ thị nghĩa cố, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác đẳng, giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Thiện nam tử! Nhược ư ngũ dục, tâm vô nhiễm trước, cụ đại từ bi nhi hành bố thí, thị danh Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát dã, diệc danh nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác chân thật phước điền. Nhược bất trừ đoạn thế gian ngũ dục, vô đại từ bi nhi hành bố thí, tuy xả vô lượng vô biên thí vật, nhi do bất đắc danh vi Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát dã, diệc phi nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác chân thật phước điền. Thử thí bất mông thánh ấn sở ấn. Thị cố, ưng đoạn thế gian ngũ dục, cụ đại từ bi nhi hành bố thí. Nhược bất đoạn ư thế gian ngũ dục, vô đại từ bi, nhi hành bố thí, bất danh Bồ Tát, phi chân phước điền. Thiện nam tử! Nhiễm trước ngũ dục, hành bố thí luân, thượng bất năng diệt tự thân sở hữu thiểu phần khổ não, huống năng trừ diệt nhất thiết hữu tình vô lượng khổ não?
(Kinh: Này thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu mười thứ Tài Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân như thế, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, làm ruộng phước lớn cho khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Vì cớ sao vậy? Thanh Văn, Độc Giác phát tâm bố thí chẳng có đại từ bi, chỉ vì chính mình xả bần cùng, chỉ vì chính mình thoát các khổ, chỉ vì chính mình được an vui, chỉ vì chính mình chứng Niết Bàn, chẳng thể vì khắp hết thảy hữu tình mà hành bố thí. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phát tâm bố thí có đại từ bi, vì xả trừ bần cùng cho trọn khắp các hữu tình, vì khiến cho trọn khắp hữu tình thoát các khổ, vì khiến cho trọn khắp các hữu tình được an lạc, vì khiến cho trọn khắp các hữu tình chứng Niết Bàn, chẳng vì chính mình mà hành bố thí. Do bởi nghĩa này, vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước lớn. Hết thảy hàng Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Khi Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát tu hành Tài Thí Ba La Mật Đa, đối với các ngũ dục tốt đẹp, tâm chẳng nhiễm đắm, có thể thí trọn khắp hết thảy các vật dụng vui thích thuộc về chính mình cho hết thảy hữu tình. Nương vào cái tâm nhiếp thọ trọn khắp các hữu tình, nương theo cái tâm tự chịu đựng hết thảy các khổ, nương vào cái tâm diệt khổ cho hết thảy hữu tình, nương vào cái tâm ban vui cho hết thảy hữu tình, nương vào cái tâm ban Đại Niết Bàn cho hữu tình mà hành bố thí. Do bởi nghĩa này, hơn hẳn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước rộng lớn. Hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Này thiện nam tử! Nếu đối với ngũ dục, tâm chẳng nhiễm đắm, trọn đủ đại từ bi mà hành bố thí, thì gọi là Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, cũng gọi là ruộng phước chân thật cho hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Nếu chẳng đoạn trừ ngũ dục thế gian, chẳng có lòng đại từ bi mà hành bố thí, tuy xả vô lượng vô biên vật để thí, vẫn chẳng được gọi là Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, cũng chẳng phải là ruộng phước chân thật của Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Sự bố thí ấy chẳng được thánh ấn in vào. Vì thế, hãy nên đoạn ngũ dục thế gian, trọn đủ đại từ bi mà hành bố thí. Nếu chẳng đoạn ngũ dục thế gian, chẳng có đại từ bi mà hành bố thí, chẳng gọi là Bồ Tát, chẳng phải là ruộng phước chân thật. Này thiện nam tử! Đắm nhiễm ngũ dục, hành bố thí luân còn chẳng thể diệt chút phần khổ não vốn có của chính mình, huống hồ có thể trừ diệt vô lượng khổ não của hết thảy hữu tình ư?)

Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu mười loại Tài Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân như thế, từ lúc mới phát tâm, “nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng đoạn trừ” (hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ), vừa phát tâm liền có thể đoạn trừ. Thanh Văn, Duyên Giác Thừa chẳng làm được! Điều này cho thấy hàng Bồ Tát vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn, Duyên Giác, cho nên các Ngài có thể làm ruộng phước lớn cho Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa. Đối với bậc thiện tri thức như vậy, hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều phải nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Vì cớ sao vậy? Thanh Văn, Độc Giác phát tâm bố thí, nhưng chẳng có lòng đại từ bi, chẳng có tâm từ bi, vì họ chẳng phát Bồ Đề tâm. Từ bi thuộc về Bồ Đề tâm. Đại từ bi được nói ở đây là đại từ bi như thế nào? Chúng ta giúp đỡ, cứu tế người khác, phải giúp triệt để! Cứu một người mà chỉ cứu người ấy thoát khỏi tử nạn thì vẫn chưa tính là triệt để. Phải dùng lời Phật dạy khiến cho người ấy thành Phật thì mới là triệt để.

Having a mind of great compassion, saving all sentient beings, wishing them to become Buddhas, that is having great compassion. Just to let go of our own poverty, why do we suffer? Because in the past we did not give alms. Because of giving alms, blessings are achieved. Because he did not sow that blessing, he became poor. Everyone wants to attain Nirvana and accept birth and death, hoping to escape the three worlds, seeing the evil life and the five defilements, which are very painful, and giving rise to boredom; These are all the thoughts of the Second Vehicle. When a Bodhisattva develops Bodhi mind, the first mind is the mind of boredom, that is, the mind of renunciation. The Second Bodhidharma Commentary talks about the mind of renunciation, but [the Bodhisattva] has developed the mind of renunciation, is tired of leaving the world, but does not leave the world, why? Because all sentient beings have not yet attained salvation. Bodhisattva wants to make all sentient beings clearly understand the mind of renunciation. With the same intention, the levels of the two people (Bodhisattva and Second Vehicle) are different! The Bodhisattva, for the sake of all sentient beings, does not seek peace and happiness for himself. He hopes that all sentient beings can fully attain the mind of renunciation, not just because he only has the mind of renunciation. Because he himself clearly understood and knew that the entire world is suffering, the world is Suffering, Emptiness, Impermanence, and Non-Self, but he knew that he could not let go of the cause of saving sentient beings, he had to develop great Bodhi mind. Bodhisattva Mahasattva who develops the mind to give alms has great compassion, unlike Thanh Van. Thanh Van cannot give alms for the sake of all sentient beings. When the Bodhisattva develops the mind to give alms, he has a mind of great compassion, not only saving the bodies of others, but also wanting to save their minds, making them become Buddhas, making them develop the mind of Bodhisattva. Not only to make all sentient beings free from poverty and misery, He vows to make all sentient beings free from all suffering!

“Sufferings” (Sufferings) includes the Cessation of birth and death and the Change of birth and death. Not only because of attaining Residual Nirvana, but also because of attaining the Ultimate Nirvana without Residual, because it makes all living beings happy and peaceful. That peace is the ultimate peace. Like when we worship and recite the verse: "All sentient beings attain peace and happiness, wishing that all sentient beings are far away from suffering and suffering" (For all sentient beings to be at peace and happiness, I only wish that all sentient beings are far away from suffering and suffering). But you must pay attention to the cause: Where does that peace come from? It is necessary to develop the mind, to pay attention to the cause that makes everyone happy. How can we relieve suffering? Where does suffering come from? We must pay attention to the causes that create suffering. That is great compassion. For the sake of such sentient beings, it enables sentient beings to attain Nirvana. They practice almsgiving, not for themselves, but for all sentient beings. Thus, we bring "the merit due to giving alms for all sentient beings" to give alms to sentient beings, that is, giving alms and offering the merit [that we ourselves] have achieved to sentient beings. Therefore, when we do some work, we must dedicate it to the sentient Dharma world. Because if that is the case, then the merit will never be interrupted, because the dharma realm is complete, the dharma realm will never be destroyed.

“Due to the ultimate meaning, surpassing all Sravakas, Single Senses” (Due to that meaning, far surpasses all Sravakas, Single Enlightenments): Therefore, it surpasses all sentient beings. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat is “almost all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Ones, creating a field of great blessings” (works a field of great blessings for all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Ones), and is qualified to be a great field of blessings for them. Therefore, all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas should make offerings, serve, and protect. At the same time, when Bodhisattva Mahasattva practices the Paramita of Wealth and Giving, he will be able to reach the other shore. Paramita (Pāramitā) means “reaching the other shore” (reaching the other shore). Old Master Nang Hai explained "Yet Truth, Pārasaṃgate, Bodhi Svāhā), which means “to become a Buddha, to become a Buddha, all sentient beings will become Buddhas”. But in the past, there was a Venerable who explained that “to the other shore, to the other shore, all living beings reach the other shore”. Although the explanation is different, the meaning is the same! When Bodhisattva Mahasattva practiced almsgiving, his mind was not infatuated with the five wonderful desires, and the five wonderful desires were especially superior. Like the five wonderful desires in heaven, even the five subtle desires are inconceivable for the Bodhisattva's actions and attainments. In psychology, things like music are also the five wonderful desires. When Tu Y comes into contact, all he hears is beautiful. Sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, those five realms, and all the tools to enjoy the five pleasures can be given to all sentient beings.

“It means trying to surpass all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones” (Due to that meaning, far surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones), therefore“universally all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones create a great Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra)” (to create a large Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) to cover all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones). Speaking at a higher level, what is the cause for farming great blessings for Thanh Van and Duyen Giac? Speaking of that cause, when the Bodhisattva gives to all sentient beings, not only to the five gross desires, he is not attached; But even with regard to the five wonderful desires, He is not infected. He himself can endure all suffering, and does not cause all sentient beings to suffer. In other words, He does not cause harm to others, but wishes for all sentient beings to be free from suffering and vows to suffer on their behalf. Because it can endure all suffering, it is also possible to destroy the suffering of all sentient beings, make sentient beings not suffer, and destroy the causes that cause suffering for sentient beings. Why do they have to suffer? Because they have accumulated. “Accumulation” is the Practice of Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path, that is, the cause and effect of the world that they have accumulated. How to accumulate? The mouth speaks, the body does it, the mind thinks and accumulates like that. If bad karma accumulates, of course you will have to suffer the consequences! The mind of joy for sentient beings is the mind of joy, the mind of trust and delight, how does that happy mind arise? Rely on the Dharma taught by the Buddha, rely on the Buddha's teachings to develop your mind. Generating the mind also benefits all sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to understand that there is no birth, no death, no suffering, no joy, no self, no forgiveness. That is the great Nirvana mind, the Prajna wisdom mind. That kind of meaning, "di thi yi" (because of that meaning), far surpasses all Thanh Van and Doc Giac, and can have the power to create great fields of blessing for Thanh Van and Doc Giac.

“Nevertheless Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas of the highest level, the stage of offering, inheriting, protecting. Good man! Before the five desires of the mind are immaculate, this great compassionate person gives alms, named Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat da” (All Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas should make offerings, inherit O good man, if the mind is not attached to the five desires, is full of great compassion, and practices almsgiving, then one is called Bodhisattva Mahasattva. That is the real Bodhisattva. As for sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, or as we say crudely, wealth, beauty, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping, the mind is not infected with these things, has no desire, and is not even attached. Having enough great compassion like that to give alms, that is the true Ha Ma Ha Tat Bodhisattva, but this type of Bodhisattva usually has attended the holy land, [at least] has attained the Land of Joy (First Land).

But according to the Avatamsaka Sutra, once one reaches the First Stage of Bodhisattva, and has just developed the Bodhi mind, one can attain enlightenment. One must perfect the mind of the Ten Faiths to participate in the First Pillar. The first pillar is called Phat Tam Tru. He developed the Bodhi mind, then remained in Bodhi mind, all his actions were the cause of Bodhi. But here it is said that the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, that is, the great Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva of the Dharma Ground, can only be a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha. Even if one cannot get rid of the five worldly desires and does not practice alms with great compassion, even though one has given away boundless wealth to give alms and make all kinds of offerings, one still cannot be called a Bodhisattva or Mahasattva. One cannot be called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat because that person does not have a great Bodhisattva mind, does not have a compassionate heart, and is also unable to cultivate a field of true blessings for Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha.

Adding the words “truth” here is intentional! In the Lower volume of the Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma Sutra, it is said about “Contemplating the two fortunes”, reaching the realm of One Truth. The form of the field of blessings in the realm of One True is “the formless form”. What is the form of Bodhisattva using Bodhi mind to give alms? Formless general! When giving alms, there is Dharma Existence, Dharma Existence is not existence, there is no attachment. The Wonderful Non-Existence is True Emptiness. That is called “Zhi Quan Song Yun”. Contemplating Hue fully, only then can you reach the true field of blessings. “The alms giving is not printed on the holy seal” (That giving is not imprinted by the holy seal). “Seal” here refers to the True Seal of the Buddhas. Therefore, one should cut off the five worldly desires and have enough great compassion to practice almsgiving. If one does not cut off the five worldly desires and does not practice alms with great compassion, one cannot be called a Bodhisattva. Not only is he not a Mahasattva, but he is also not a Bodhisattva! The two words Bodhisattva are “enlightened sentient beings”, sentient beings whose minds wish to achieve the great path. That person himself is not enlightened, so how can he have the mind to enlighten sentient beings? The complete Bodhisattva is Bodhisattva (Boddhisattva). The word Bo is due to the omission of the word De, Tat is the omission of the word Doa, the complete word is Bodhi Tat Doa. Therefore, such a person is not only not called a Bodhisattva, but also is not a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra). That is speaking in the deepest sense, it is not saying "if you give alms, there will be no Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra)". Don't misinterpret!

Just as we are not great Bodhisattvas, we have given alms, nor do we have a Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra). That is to say you cannot achieve the field of blessings like Bodhisattva Mahasattva. However, you still have a Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), so why don't you have a Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) when giving alms? Giving alms can save the poor and make you rich in the next life. But when you are greedy for wealth, you always create karma, your mind is not pure. You come to the human world, have money but still do not create karma? Having accumulated blessings in the past, having status and money in this life, you create even greater negative karma. Chien-da-la king, Chien-da-la Brahmin, Chien-dala minister [as mentioned] in the previous section have this meaning. Therefore, you should not indulge in the five desires. “The superior cannot destroy the least amount of suffering inherent in oneself” (It cannot even eliminate the little bit of suffering inherent in oneself). If you do not eliminate the five desires, and because you are greedy for the five desires, you practice almsgiving, that is for a purpose. You yourself enjoy the five desires, even a little bit of your own suffering cannot be avoided. How can you eliminate the immeasurable suffering for all sentient beings? That is something that cannot happen!

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, and recited and wrote: - Accomplished talent for almsgiving, the wise are pure in mind. ridicule, abandon the five desires, and bring peace to all sentient beings. For the sake of sentient beings, there is no need for self-retribution. Even though he does a small amount of alms, his name is full of blessings. Even though he gives alms to many people, he only accepts the five desires, has non-holy seals, and stays in the Undetermined Convergence. Although he does little charity, he does not care about the five desires, and is known as Thanh Van, Doc Giac, a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) and blessings. Try to let go of the five desires, practice pure giving, bring peace to sentient beings, and become a true field of blessings.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One displayed this meaning again, then recited verses: - Succession Accumulating the gift of alms, the wise person purifies all desires and is free from the five desires, for the benefit of sentient beings, without seeking retribution. Even though he gives a little, it is called the field of true blessings, but relying on the five desires, the holy seal is not imprinted on him, although he gives a little, does not rely on the five desires, it is a field of true blessings, of Thanh Van, Soc Trang love, become a true field of blessings).

If one achieves this Bodhisattva practice of Giving Alms and Pillars, a wise person will be able to become pure. That person's beliefs and thoughts can be free from the five desires, not attached to the five desires, and can bring peace to all sentient beings. Because he wants the happiness of all sentient beings, he does not seek retribution for himself. If the mind of giving alms is pure, the objects used to give alms are also pure. Because we are mixed with so many impure things, even though we give alms and offerings, our mind is not pure, the person receiving the alms will receive very little benefit, and will not be pure. They receive alms from you, possibly creating karma. This kind of chain reaction has such a huge beneficial relationship. Therefore, when giving alms, your mind must be pure and not seek retribution for yourself. Even if you give a little alms, it is called a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra). When a Bodhisattva gives alms, he will not seek any benefit for himself, he will give all alms to sentient beings, only then can he truly create a Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for sentient beings.

“Even though he gives alms to many people, he only accepts the five desires, non-holy seals, and stays in the Undetermined Gathering” (Although he gives a lot of alms, but depends on the five desires, the holy seal is not imprinted, stays in the Undetermined Gathering): Although he gives away a lot of things, a lot of material things, the shaman even preaches the Dharma to others, but if his mind You yourself are not pure. If you preach the Dharma with impurities, the listener cannot be pure either!

In addition, when giving alms, you must contemplate the basis (consider the basis). In the previous section, we said: Don't make mistakes with Shravaka Vehicle, don't make mistakes with people of Shravaka Vehicle capacity. There is no mistake regarding the foundation, that is, the foundation and the dharma must match. If the foundation is not in accordance with the dharma, the dharma has no effect. If the Dharma is not in accordance with your fundamental ability, then it will not be effective. If he only practices the five desires to practice alms, the Buddha will not accept that. Where will you belong? Will your merit of giving alms eventually become a saint, or will you still become an ordinary person? Not certain. Because I don't know how to wish to give alms? “Undetermined Convergence” means not knowing whether you are Great or Small, has that meaning. Donating too much but only paying attention to the five desires is not enough! If one gives a little, "although he practices a small amount of giving, he does not follow the five desires" (although he gives a little, but does not rely on the five desires): Although he gives away very little material things, he does not follow the five desires, does not seek the five desires. That is the true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) achievement for Thanh Van and Doc Giac.

“Try to let go of the five desires, practice pure almsgiving, bring peace to sentient beings, and become a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra)” (You should let go of the five desires, often give pure alms, bring peace to sentient beings, and become a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra)): You give alms, make offerings to sentient beings, and become a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra). The sentient beings who receive alms from you, receive offerings from you, can also use your resources, their hearts are also pure, they can also take refuge and believe in the Three Jewels.

(Kinh) Phục thứ, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát hữu thập Pháp Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu thử luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, tốc năng hoạch đắc Nhật Đăng Quang Định, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền, nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Hà đẳng vi thập? Vị chư Như Lai sở thuyết chánh pháp, hoặc Thanh Văn Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, hoặc Độc Giác Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, hoặc dữ Đại Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, hoặc thế gian pháp, hoặc xuất thế gian pháp, hoặc hữu lậu pháp, hoặc vô lậu pháp, hoặc hữu vi pháp, hoặc vô vi pháp, hoặc bất nhị pháp. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát ư thử thập pháp thâm tín, kính trọng, nhất thiết thính văn, tùy lực sở năng, thẩm đế lãnh thọ, tư duy, quán sát, cứu cánh thông lợi, tùy kỳ sở nghi, vị tha diễn thuyết. Ư thuyết pháp thời, vô tật đố tâm, vô xan lận tâm, vô kiêu mạn tâm, vô cầu lợi tâm, vô khinh tha tâm, vô tự cử tâm, hữu cung kính tâm, hữu nhiêu ích tâm, hữu đại từ tâm, hữu đại bi tâm. Vị Thanh Văn Thừa Bổ Đặc Già La thuyết Thanh Văn pháp, bất vị bỉ thuyết Độc Giác Thừa pháp, cập Đại Thừa pháp. Vị Độc Giác Thừa Bổ Đặc Già La thuyết Độc Giác pháp, bất vị bỉ thuyết Thanh Văn Thừa pháp, cập Đại Thừa pháp. Vị ư Đại Thừa Bổ Đặc Già La thuyết Đại Thừa pháp, bất vị bỉ thuyết Thanh Văn Thừa pháp, Độc Giác Thừa pháp. Tùy chư hữu tình căn khí sở năng, vị thuyết chánh pháp. Phi căn khí giả, chung bất vị thuyết. Ư kỳ Đại Thừa chư hữu tình sở, chung bất khuyến tu Độc Giác Thừa hạnh, Thanh Văn Thừa hạnh. Ư Độc Giác Thừa chư hữu tình sở, hoặc thời khuyến bỉ tu Đại Thừa hạnh. Ư Thanh Văn Thừa chư hữu tình sở, hoặc thời khuyến tu Độc Giác Thừa hạnh, cập Đại Thừa hạnh. Ư chư Như Lai sở thuyết chánh pháp, hạ chí nhất tụng, nãi chí bán cú, thâm tín, kính trọng, chung bất hủy báng, chướng tế, ẩn một. Ư thuyết pháp sư, khởi Thế Tôn tưởng. Ư thính pháp chúng, khởi bệnh giả tưởng. Ư sở thuyết pháp, khởi lương dược tưởng, đoạn trừ ngũ dục, vô sở hy cầu, tuyên thuyết chánh pháp. Thiện nam tử! Thị danh Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thập chủng Pháp Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu thử luân, năng đoạn ngũ dục, tốc năng hoạch đắc Nhật Đăng Quang Định, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng, giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ.
(Kinh: Lại này, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát có mười Pháp Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu luân này, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, có thể mau chóng đạt được Nhật Đăng Quang Định, vượt hơn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, làm ruộng phước lớn cho trọn khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Hết thảy các Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Những gì là mười? Chính là chánh pháp do đức Như Lai đã nói, hoặc chánh pháp tương ứng Thanh Văn Thừa, hoặc chánh pháp tương ứng Độc Giác Thừa, hoặc chánh pháp tương ứng Đại Thừa, hoặc là pháp thế gian, hoặc là pháp xuất thế gian, hoặc là pháp hữu lậu, hoặc là pháp vô lậu, hoặc là pháp hữu vi, hoặc là pháp vô vi, hoặc là pháp bất nhị. Đối với mười pháp ấy, Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát tin sâu, kính trọng, hết thảy nghe nhận, tùy theo năng lực mà suy xét chắc thật, lãnh nhận, tư duy, quan sát, rốt ráo thông lợi, tùy theo lẽ đáng nên mà vì người khác diễn thuyết. Trong khi thuyết pháp, chẳng có tâm ghen tỵ, chẳng có tâm keo tham, chẳng có tâm kiêu căng, ngạo mạn, chẳng có tâm cầu lợi, chẳng có tâm khinh rẻ kẻ khác, chẳng có tâm tự đề cao, có tâm cung kính, có tâm tạo lợi ích, có tâm đại từ, có tâm đại bi. Vì Thanh Văn Thừa Bổ Đặc Già La nói pháp Thanh Văn, chẳng vì họ nói pháp Độc Giác Thừa và pháp Đại Thừa. Vì Độc Giác Thừa Bổ Đặc Già La nói Độc Giác pháp, chẳng vì họ nói pháp Thanh Văn Thừa và pháp Đại Thừa. Vì các Đại Thừa Bổ Đặc Già La nói pháp Đại Thừa, chẳng vì kẻ đó nói pháp Thanh Văn Thừa và pháp Độc Giác Thừa. Tùy theo căn khí của các hữu tình có thể tu tập mà nói chánh pháp cho họ. Đối với kẻ chẳng phải căn khí, sẽ trọn chẳng nói. Nơi các hữu tình Đại Thừa, trọn chẳng khuyên họ tu hạnh Độc Giác Thừa hay hạnh Thanh Văn Thừa. Nơi các hữu tình Độc Giác Thừa, hoặc có lúc khuyên họ tu hạnh Đại Thừa. Nơi các hữu tình Thanh Văn Thừa, hoặc là có lúc khuyên họ tu hạnh Độc Giác Thừa và hạnh Đại Thừa. Đối với chánh pháp do các đức Như Lai đã nói, dẫu chỉ một bài kệ tụng, cho đến nửa câu, đều tin sâu, kính trọng, trọn chẳng hủy báng, chướng lấp, ẩn giấu. Đối với vị thầy thuyết pháp, tưởng như đức Thế Tôn; đối với người nghe pháp, tưởng như người bệnh. Đối với pháp nói ra, tưởng như là thuốc lành, đoạn trừ ngũ dục, chẳng có mong cầu, tuyên nói chánh pháp. Này thiện nam tử! Đó gọi là mười loại Pháp Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân của Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát. Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu luân này, có thể đoạn ngũ dục, có thể mau chóng đạt được Nhật Đăng Quang Định, vượt hơn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì trọn khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước to lớn. Hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ).

Đây là Pháp Thí, câu trước nói về Tài Thí. Pháp Thí Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. “Đại giáp trụ luân” là cách nói hình dung, hình dung cái tâm thanh tịnh của Bồ Tát. Trong khi quý vị làm một việc gì đó, trước hết phải lắng lòng: Chuyện này phải nên phát tâm như thế nào? Phải phát Bồ Đề tâm. Do cái tâm Bồ Đề ấy, sẽ có thể sanh khởi trí huệ phương tiện. Khi quý vị lợi sanh, sẽ có thể quán thời gian và căn cơ để bố thí, chẳng nẩy sanh sai lầm lệch lạc, chẳng nẩy sanh lầm lộn. Nếu lúc đại Bồ Tát thành tựu luân này, tức Pháp Thí Đại Giáp Luân, sẽ giống như khi Ngài mới vừa phát tâm trong phần trước: Ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn dứt. Đoạn dứt ngũ dục, sẽ đạt được công đức, công đức gì vậy? Đắc một môn Định, tức Nhật Đăng Quang Định. Môn Định này là một môn trong một trăm lẻ tám tam-muội, thuộc loại Lăng Già Định. Nhật là “nhật quang” (ánh sáng của mặt trời), Đăng là “đăng quang” (ánh sáng của đèn), tức là hình dung vị ấy có thể phá trừ hắc ám cho chúng sanh, mà cũng phá trừ hắc ám của chính mình. Có quang minh chiếu soi, có trí huệ, đó là điều mà hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác đều chẳng có. Do vậy nói Ngài vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn và Độc Giác, cho nên có thể làm ruộng phước lớn cho Thanh Văn và Độc Giác, hết thảy Thanh Văn và Độc Giác đều phải nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. “Thừa sự” có nghĩa là đệ tử [phụng sự] đối với bậc thượng sư, hoặc đối với bậc đại thiện tri thức.

This is a general statement, followed by a distinction. However, in the chapter Phuoc Dien General, in the previous part, the Buddha gave a general overview of the ten wheels of wealth (Tai Thien Giap Giap Luan), put together. What are ten? Giving food, vehicles, elephants, horses, one's own hands, feet, are also ten types. As long as you have enough great compassion, you will be fine. Dharma giving in the present time is the same, from the moment of awakening the mind, that person attains the Sunlight and Light Concentration, superior to all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas. When that person preaches the Dharma, that is, the holy Dharma taught by the Tathagata, [if the listener's faculties] correspond to the Thanh Van Vehicle, then he speaks the Dharma of the Thanh Van Vehicle, that is, corresponding to the Thanh Van Vehicle's faculties. “Corresponding” is Yoga. Currently, when talking about “Yoga”, it means “corresponding” in Chinese. When it corresponds, it is the dharma and the corresponding basis. As soon as he hears the Dharma, he can practice. Practicing can lead to enlightenment and enter Concentration. If it doesn't correspond, that person is of the Shravaka Vehicle, and you speak of the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, the Dharma of cause and effect, or the Six Paramitas of the Mahayana, that person will not be able to grasp it, and will think that the Buddha Dharma is useless to you, so you can only tell him the Ten Good Karmas. You preach the Vajra Prajnaparamita Sutra to him, he cannot understand. If you tell that person, "Buddhism is Emptiness", from then on, that person will be born in the Cessation of Emptiness, and will not do anything! On the contrary, it also creates karma. That is “not the right root”. Without the right foundation, no benefits will be achieved. The Dharma spoken by the Tathagata will become an evil dharma for the listener. That person not only gains benefits, but also incurs the sin of blasphemy!

What about corresponding to Thanh Van Thua? In general, it is the Four Noble Truths. What is the correspondence with the Single Enlightenment Vehicle? The dharma of cause and effect, that is, the dharma of twelve causes and conditions. What about the Dharma corresponding to the Mahayana? It is the Six Degrees Dharma. This includes many things, either worldly dharma, or transcendental dharma, or dharma with asrava, or dharma with asrava. The dharma of the world is existent, the dharma beyond the world is dharma. These two things each have meaning; In each of the following paragraphs, there will be an explanation. Either it is a conditioned dharma, or an unconditioned dharma, or a non-dual dharma. The non-dual Dharma is the ultimate Dharma. If you have ever heard the Vimalakirti Sutra, [know] that it is the Dharma of Non-Duality. In general, “infected and pure are not two”. Both Mahayana and Hinayana are non-dual, as in the Vimalakirti Sutra, Manjushri Bodhisattva asked layperson Vimalakirti: "What is the method of Non-duality?" Layperson Vimalakirti replied: "Sexual action, anger, ignorance are the method of Non-duality". Lust, anger, and ignorance are Precepts, Concentration, and Hue.

In another passage, when Manjushri Bodhisattva asked Vimalakirti about the Non-Duality method, the layperson did not say a word! People talked a lot about the Non-Dual Dharma, but when asked about Him, He did not open his mouth. Manjushri Bodhisattva immediately praised: “That is the true Non-Duality Dharma!” What is the Non-Duality Dharma? Language ceases, mental conduct ceases. Unable to think, unable to use language to express. That is the Non-Duality method. If one has deep trust and respect for these ten dharmas, all listeners will listen according to their own abilities. What is your foundation? How much can you do? How much will you perceive? We consider, think carefully, observe rationally, consider the truth and then receive it in our hearts. “To receive” is to receive in the mind. Only by thinking and observing like that can we be completely clear, can we communicate! If you listen without thinking, you will forget. Forgetting it is no different than not learning or not listening! Thinking without action will lead to laziness. Thinking without doing it is nothing!

For example, if we practice the Ten Rings Sutra, we must practice the Ten Rings Dharma. If we practice the Pure Land dharma, listen to the Infinite Life Sutra, or the Amitabha Sutra, after hearing so much, you don't do it, it's useless! It's okay to beat Buddha That. Just like the old magician Dieu Canh came to Quan Am Pagoda to beat Buddha That, participating in Buddha That is enough, “doing” is doing, “doing” is practicing. But you must pay attention, reciting Buddha's name must start from the mind, and then the recitation must return to the mind. Every thought originates from the mind, every thought is directed to the mind. That is the Non-Duality method as we said. Amitābha Buddha is me, I am Amitābha Buddha, we must contemplate like that. That is also the method of Non-duality. Self and others are not two, the person reciting Buddha's name is me, the object of reciting is Amitābha Buddha. Contemplation and thought are the same Body, the same Dharmakaya. The old Dharma Master Tu Chau gave instructions on reciting the Buddha's name, combined with the ten great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva: "Reciting one sentence of Amitābha Buddha corresponds to the ten great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva". It was in 1940 that he gave such a revelation in a Buddha's room. That is the method of Non-Duality.

“Bodhisattva Mahasattva tested the ten dharmas, and developed deep respect for them” (Bodhisattva Mahasattva generated deep respect for these ten dharmas): How great is your wisdom, how many contemplations can you give rise to, how great is your concentration? How much can be received? Thinking is Concentration, observing is Hue; We must use Concentration and Hue together, then we can reach the end. If you are born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, it will be clear, the world of Ultimate Bliss is right in your mind. Amitābha Buddha is you, you can achieve that. That's called “depending on doubt”. Bodhisattva Mahasattva uses these ten dharmas to teach and transform all sentient beings; That is the dharma of making offerings, using the dharma to give alms. This is called Dharma Giving. But when preaching the Dharma, you should not have a jealous mind, you should not have a stingy mind, you should not have an arrogant mind, you cannot have the mind of seeking profit, you cannot have the mind of looking down on others. You also have to know how to meditate on the basis of teaching the Dharma. I made that mistake because I didn't know how to consider my inborn qualities, didn't have that virtue, didn't have that magical power. What do I have in mind? As long as I'm studying with everyone and you come and listen, it's predestined. If you want to listen to the Mahabodhi Sutra of the Ten Wheels, that is predestined. You come and listen, I tell you, there is no mistake! You listen to the lecture but don't like to listen, the two of us are ungrateful, you leave, I haven't made a mistake, you haven't made a mistake either! If you keep listening until the end, you may gain some benefits. For me, I don't have any merit, but for you, you really gain benefits. That means you can enter Buddhism.

Each of us Dharma friends, when propagating Buddhism, propagating it to others, facing our friends surrounding us, advising them to recite a single sentence of Amitābha Buddha, you are also speaking the Dharma. Many Dharma friends ask me: "How can I help others? How can I save others?" I replied: "You can practice the Bodhisattva path." “Can I practice the Bodhisattva path?” I said: "You can just do it like this. Do you know how to recite Buddha's name?" “I know!” I said: "Can you tell others about the benefits of reciting Buddha's name?" “It is possible!” I said: "That is the Bodhisattva way!" As for the very deep meaning, I am a professional, you are amateurs. You can do that, even stronger than me, you're not just doing it for fame or profit, isn't that right?

No matter which Dharma friend helps others, he must pay attention to the first thing: Not for fame, not for profit. Just "not for fame, not for profit" is not enough, you should also not have an arrogant mind, not be stingy, not have the mind to seek profit, not have the mind to look down on others: "You don't understand! I'd better tell you!" That is a mind of contempt. Even though you don't express it in words, it doesn't seem like you're being arrogant yourself, but saying people don't understand is being arrogant! The Bodhisattva preaches the Dharma, both are equal to good faculties and dull faculties. It will not be because these sentient beings are very foolish, if they say it once they do not understand, if they say it twice they still do not understand, if they say it ten times they still do not understand [so they despise it, let it go], but for those with good faculties they only need to say it once and they will understand [and then love and cherish it]. Seen from the Bodhisattva's perspective, both sides are equal, it won't be because this person has good faculties that it's a little better, and for those with dull faculties, they won't care, because that person is too annoying! Some Dharma friends often ask because they don't know so they ask a little more. Don't think it's too troublesome or make you feel bored. [If a mind of boredom arises], it means that there is already a mind of contempt for that person.

“No self-promotion” (No self-promotion): “Self-promotion” is praising oneself. “Praise” how? Too much right now. We don't need to give examples but [you] can still know. Always let people know your own advantages. Then everyone else is no good, only I am very good. “Self-nomination” is to despise others, to despise others in order to express oneself. That is a mistake, I'm afraid that many sentient beings commit [this mistake]! Whether unintentionally or intentionally, it is very easy to commit a crime. That is not having the heart to respect others. Respecting others will not think about yourself, which contains such meaning. You must have a mind of great benefit (to benefit others), a mind of great compassion, a mind of great compassion, with that mind, then from a heart of reverence, you will respect all sentient beings, "they are future Buddhas", often contemplate like that. Everyone knows that the Sixth Patriarch heard someone else chanting the Vajra Sutra and he was enlightened, but that person reciting the Vajra Sutra was never mentioned! Of course, that person did not realize it, but the Sixth Patriarch heard it and was enlightened, so he must understand this principle. Just because it is a person of great power, that is, talking about Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, when they practice Dharma giving, they will be virtuous and have the ability to forgive others. For people of the Shravaka Vehicle, he will absolutely not speak the Pratyekabuddha Dharma, nor will he speak the Mahayana Dharma. As for people belonging to the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, neither the Shravaka Vehicle Dharma is taught to them nor the Mahayana Dharma. For people of the Mahayana temperament, that is, for the Mahayana Bodhisattva Gia La, we will not tell them the Shravaka dharma, or the Single Enlightenment dharma. Depending on the temperament of sentient beings, they can accept and understand any Dharma, then preach the Dharma to them. The Dharma of the Three Vehicles is all true Dharma, but those who are not spiritual beings, do not have that good root, cannot comprehend it!

“Mahayana Mahayana sentient beings” (For Mahayana sentient beings): For those of Mahayana temperament, you should not advise them to practice according to the practice method of the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, nor do you advise them to practice according to the method of Shravaka Vehicle. But in the three vehicles, in the previous section, when talking about the Ten Virtuous Karmas, it was said "do not make mistakes with the Sravaka Vehicle, Gia La, do not make mistakes with the Pratyekayana, Gia La, do not make mistakes with the Mahayana, the Mahayana", the dharma of the three vehicles and the person belonging to the three vehicles absolutely cannot be confused, [must know clearly] which dharma to speak for which base! So, for what kind of living beings, what kind of dharma will be advised to practice [suitable]; The three vehicle dharma is general. As I said for three months, I could not say a few sentences that were true Dharma. The Dharma is right, but as a person I don't seem to have attained right knowledge, right view, still not completely right, sometimes even deviant and mistaken. That is something worth repenting of. But the Dharma is right, you should follow the Dharma, don't follow other people! What kind of mind do you have towards the person preaching the Dharma? How do you think about that person? If you can give rise to the mind that thinks of that person as the World-Honored One, you will be a Buddha or Bodhisattva. You are the Buddha mind. If you see someone who is greedy for fame and profit, you probably have some problems with fame and profit!

There is an old story, everyone can hear this example. When Su Dongpo and Zen master Phat An were walking together, Su Dongpo immediately asked Zen master Phat An: "How do you see me?" Zen master Phat An replied: "You are fat, have good fortune, and are also a mandarin, like a Buddha." To Dong Pha was very pleased, very satisfied, very happy. Continuing to walk for a while, To Dong Pha asked Zen master Phat An: "Why don't you ask me, what are you like?" The Master replied: "I don't need to ask you, I have nothing to ask you." He said: "You should have asked me!" The Master replied: "Okay! I ask you, what do you think I look like?" To Dong Pha said: "I see you as a pile of dog shit!" Zen Master Phat An smiled and said nothing, it was over. Returning home, To Dong Pha told his younger sister. Little Sister Su is a wise person. He boasted: "Today I won against the monk, I have never won against him before." Little sister Su immediately asked: "How did you win? Can you tell me?" He told the beginning and the end. Little Sister Su said: "You've lost for sure, you've lost completely!" "Huh! How could you lose?" "Other people's minds are Buddha's minds, seeing you is like Buddha's. But your mind is dog shit, so seeing other people is like dog shit!" Those words are very meaningful! Each person sees it differently. Why do you see different? Because you only have so much wisdom! Among us, there are still people who cannot understand the Buddhadharma from beginning to end. Why can't it be explained? I've just studied a little and I hope to penetrate Buddhism, but it's impossible! I say this because I have experienced it myself. It's been sixty-four years since I became a monk, and I still don't understand how! I often think of Lu Son in a poem by To Dong Pha: “Hanh khan becomes cold, the border becomes wind, far away, high and low dikes are different, unconsciously LuSgrateful to the true face, only the body is in the middle of the mountain” (Looking horizontally into a ridge, vertically into a peak, high, low, near, far are all different. I don't know Lu Son's true face, because the body is still in this mountain). We fall into that muddy pit, how can we perceive Buddha Dharma? Even worldly dharma is not recognized! If you can truly skillfully perceive worldly dharma, you will escape from it. If you recognize and follow the Buddha's words, believe firmly and unchangeably. I always firmly believe in what the Buddha said, without changing. The Buddha said these are the five evil defilements of the world, why are you still attached? Do you still want to find happiness in this world? There is no joy! Therefore, do not be greedy for the five desires! Good man! These are the ten types of Dharma Offerings of the Great Armor Pillar of Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, and recited and wrote: - The wise practice the Dharma, depending on the atmosphere, three theories Excessive, tasteless, redundant, terrible literature and blasphemy. Preaching the Dharma in accordance with the spirit of the body, without the spirit of the body, at all times, ridicule, promoting joy and happiness. In general, we do not recommend the Mahayana, spiritually cultivating the Second Vehicle, or we encourage the second, practicing the middle and upper vehicle. Always respect the teachings and dharma, have deep faith and never slander, and make offerings to the Dharma Master, as Buddha, the World-Honored One, thought. Encouraging literature on wonderful dharma medicine, spiritual medicine to eliminate afflictions and diseases, relaxation, nourishment, honor, and teachings of the Dharma.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One displayed this meaning again, then recited verses: - Wise people practice the Dharma, depending on the occasion, not because they are afraid of listening to the Dharma. Preaching the Dharma is worthy of the person's temperament, not because of the wrong person's desire, but encourages joy in the Mahayana, and at times advises them to follow the Second Vehicle. Always listen respectfully to the Dharma, and do not blaspheme the teachings of the Buddha brain, abandoning profit and honor, but proclaiming the Dharma).

While the Buddha was speaking the Dharma, there were often repeated chants. In the sutras, it is recorded the meaning of repeated recitation: Every time the Buddha preached the Dharma, I was afraid that people wouldn't remember it, or maybe after finishing speaking, you would miss it. Either when you heard it, you didn't hear it, or sometimes when you were away, you heard the Buddha preach the Dharma and came to find him.
