Because the Truong Hang part had already been preached, the Buddha repeated it over and over again. That's why it's called Geya (Geya, Ky Da). Also Co Khoi Tung, completely different. Ms. Khoi Tung is the Buddha who completely used the verse form to preach the Dharma. Because there is no Truong Hang text, it is called Co Khoi (Gāthā, Gia Da). Here is Tung Tung.

“A wise person practices the Dharma of Giving, speaking of the three vehicles depending on the occasion” (The wise person practices the Dharma, speaking of the three vehicles depending on the occasion): If a wise person wants to study and apply the Dharma of Giving to preach the Dharma to all living beings, when giving alms [the Dharma] to living beings, he will speak according to the living beings' temperament. Shravaka, Single-Buddha, or Mahayana Dharma. Depending on the person's ability, depending on what kind of Dharma device he is worthy of receiving, then tell him the Dharma that belongs to that vehicle. “Non-examination theory” (Not because that person speaks of a dharma belonging to another vehicle), for someone who is worthy of receiving the Shravaka Vehicle, we will not tell that person the Mahayana dharma. As for those who are worthy of receiving the Mahayana dharma, do not tell them about the Shravaka Vehicle or the Single Enlightenment Vehicle dharma. Why do that? “Terrible Van Nhi blasphemes the Dharma” (Afraid that after hearing it, they will blaspheme the Dharma): Because after hearing it, they not only do not believe it, but also slander it. Therefore, not only does it not save sentient beings, but on the contrary, it also increases the karma of sentient beings.

“Preach the Dharma according to the temperament, not without the temperament, at any time to ridicule, encourage the soul to rejoice” (The Dharma is preached according to the temperament, not for those who are not of the temperament, but encourage them according to each person's preference, making them happy): Preach the Dharma in accordance with the temperament. Being true to one's senses is also being true to one's senses. If that person doesn't have the capacity or energy of that dharma, then you can just depend on the conditions, depending on what he or she likes, then tell him or her that dharma. That person is not of Mahayana temperament, you immediately speak of the Second Vehicle Dharma, speak of Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and Path, saying that this world is all suffering. You must know Suffering, its Origin. If you speak wisely, even if they don't know, you will follow the worldly dharma and speak the worldly dharma well. It's okay to explain humanity, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and faith. It's okay to talk about the ethics of being a human being, saying "to be a human being, you have to fulfill your qualifications as a human being, and you can't be like animals." It seems that whatever kind of person he is, he preaches the Dharma like that. For those who are greedy for the five desires, you cannot follow them in talking about the five desires, but you must talk about the faults of the five desires, causing them to abandon the five desires until they are happy!

“In general, we do not recommend the Mahayana, spiritually practicing the Second Vehicle. Or sometimes recommending the second, cultivating the middle and upper vehicle” (I do not advise people of Mahayana temperament to practice the Second Vehicle. Or sometimes advise people of the other two vehicles, to practice the middle and upper vehicles): For people who are not spiritual, they are not Mahayana. Vehicle, you will not force them to practice Mahayana. If they are of Mahayana temperament, should you advise them to practice the Second Vehicle or not? That is not the breath. “Or maybe we should encourage the second one to practice the middle vehicle and the upper vehicle”, [meaning] we should not advise the Sravakayana energy to cultivate the middle vehicle (Practice Enlightenment Vehicle), or the Single Enlightenment vehicle to cultivate the upper vehicle, that is, the Mahayana. Or for the Pratyekabuddhas, we do not advise them to practice the Mahayana, nor do we advise them to practice the Shravaka Vehicle. “Or time to encourage bi”, “to bi” refers to the Thanh Van Vehicle and the Single Sense Vehicle.

“ Always respectfully listen to the Dharma, deeply believe in it and never slander it” (Usually reverently listen to the Dharma. Believe deeply, do not slander): Regardless of whether you are a Sravakayana, a Single Enlightenment, or a Mahayana dharma, you should respectfully listen to the Dharma, don't be tempted to slander it. Regarding the Dharma, you must believe deeply without doubt, there are many problems in it. For example, when we talk about the Ksitigarbha Tripitaka, is the Ksitigarbha Sutra Mahayana or Hinayana? Most people think that it is a Hinayana sutra, because it is all about hell and demons. The text also talks a lot about hell. But the masses in that Dharma assembly were told in the Dao Loi heaven, initially by the Buddha speaking to Manjushri Bodhisattva. The second chapter was addressed to the Buddha by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The third chapter is Lady Maya talking to the Buddha, each chapter is like that.

Furthermore, by hearing the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you will not be able to fall into the three realms, until you are born in another land, you will be able to reach pure lands. That is not Hinayana. Hearing the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, until the end, in chapter twelve, the Buddha advised Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara), and finally advised Void Store Bodhisattva. At the end of the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, the one who is advised is still Void Store Bodhisattva. These are Great Bodhisattvas singing praises to each other. We must definitely recognize, from many aspects, recognize the meaning in a sutra. Only then will you not listen to what others say and instead listen to what that person says, or whatever you say, listening to it is the most likely to commit a crime! Therefore, in all the sutras, Ksitigarbha Three Sutras simultaneously propagates the three vehicles. You are a human and heavenly [energy], so we can also use the Human Heavenly Vehicle to explain to you, but as long as you don't slander it, that's okay! Don't slander, listen respectfully to the Dharma, believe deeply, don't slander.

“Offering to shamanism”: Whoever preaches the Dharma, must understand the meaning of “shamanism”. If you take the Dharma as your teacher, you are a shaman. In that, there are also two groups of lay men and women. Sometimes it's called Can Su, sometimes it's called Can Tru. Close Su means “close to the Three Jewels”. That is a person who can develop a mind of reverence for the Three Jewels, has received the Three Refuges, and the Five Precepts. Can Tru is completely different. Near Abode means staying right at the Three Jewels, receiving the Eight Precepts, right in the temple. As long as what they say is dharma, they can all be magicians. A magician does not have to specialize in profit, nor does he have to preach sutras to be a magician. Whenever he stands there, tells you a few Dharma sentences, advises you to believe in Buddha, recite Buddha's name, you can also consider that person a Dharma Master. Listen to a verse and sacrifice your life. [Another person] said four sentences to him, he immediately sacrificed his life, heard a verse and became enlightened. The Venerable Sariputta met Bhikkhu Ma Thang, saw the Bhikkhu's dignified dignity, and immediately asked: "Who do you honor as your teacher?" [meaning] who is His master? Please tell me a poem first! Bhikkhu Ma Thang recited a verse, and Sariputta immediately became enlightened and led his disciples to take refuge in the Buddha. Therefore, you have the right foundation, in one word, even though you are not enlightened, others are enlightened.

While reciting the Diamond Sutra, the Sixth Patriarch came to sell firewood at the right time. Standing under someone's house, hearing someone in the house reciting the Diamond Sutra, the Patriarch heard the sentence "when the mind is born without a place to live" he immediately became enlightened. I have been reciting the Diamond Sutra for decades. I don't know how many times I have recited it. Each time I recite it, I think, "There are people who immediately become enlightened when they hear it. I have recited it that many times and still cannot be enlightened!" For what reason? Karma is deep and heavy, that is karma. Enlightenment and delusion are just reversed like that, that is, the hand is face down or face up! Therefore, if you do not achieve superior understanding or enlightenment, you should not commit sins. Listen respectfully to the Dharma, do not slander, and even more do not slander the teacher who preaches the Dharma.

In the Ten Virtuous Karmas of the previous section, we talked about respecting the Three Jewels a lot. Even with the power of wearing a piece of ka-sa, that person is still not a monk, the king wants to send that person into the deserted grave to feed the ghosts. When that person heard it, he became afraid and shaved all the hair on his head. Then, find ca-sa. Where is there? From among the torn cloths that were thrown away, he picked up a piece of red casa, still not a complete casa, and put it on him. Those demons did not dare to eat that person, so they surrounded and praised that person. There were so many Rakshasa ghosts, mothers and children, praising that person, which revealed the power of the Three Jewels. Therefore, we should not have the heart to slander the Three Jewels. Every magician is good! For those who wear a piece of ka-sa, they consider that person to be a magician, able to create a Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for sentient beings. Those demons saw that person, surrounded him, regarded him as a holy monk and respected him, considered him a holy monk of good fortune.

If we understand the principle of “all things are mind-only”, in all places, all times, the mind is Buddha. You should often contemplate like that, you can advise everyone to listen to the wonderful Dharma like that. That's the method. Just like when we have a disease, we have to take medicine. When we take the medicine, the disease goes away. What disease do we have now? There is the disease of birth and death, there is the disease of the five desires, there is greed, anger, ignorance, there are these diseases, that is why the Buddha spoke that Dharma. Fortunately, if you take that medicine, the disease will be eliminated, leaving you free of troubles. Our illness, in general, is the illness of affliction. We must let go of fame and gain, and should not preach the Dharma for the sake of fame and gain. In normal times, your mind's desire for desire is very heavy, your greed for the realm of the five desires and worldly possessions is very heavy, you should often contemplate. That is poison, you should often contemplate it. If you think like that every day, you will naturally not be greedy. You always think that desire is beneficial; In fact, it brings harm. World war is the same, what do you hope to fight for? Isn't it a fight for fame and fortune? Look at what worldly people are doing in the present and you'll know right away! Between countries, between people and people, competing for fame and benefits. Our disciples of the Three Jewels, the first thing is to let go of fame and gain, because that is not a good thing. It will drag you to hell. You often think, that's what makes us suffer, you have to be mentally prepared. After that, when you speak the Dharma to people, what you have said is the Dharma that eliminates the five desires, and does not promote the five desires at all.

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat restores the Pure Precepts to the Great Armored Wheel. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat accomplished testing the wheel, developed the initial mind, must have the five desires stage to be able to eliminate, overcome must necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste must necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment create a great field of blessings, must necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, the stage of offering, serving, protecting. Cloud Ha Tinh Gioi Dai Giap Pillar? Good man! Bodhisattva pure precepts have two types of characteristics: One, plus; two parts, no plus. Van Ha Bodhisattva Plus Pure Precepts Wheel? The lay people of the Near Affairs and the Near Residence receive the precepts, or become monks, and receive the Complete Prajnaparamita of Liberation Precepts, as shown in the precepts of the Discipline of Discipline and Liberation. The Bodhisattva name includes the pure precepts wheel, the Shravakas, and the Pratyekabuddhas. Bodhisattvas do not try to purify the wheel of precepts, they can eliminate the afflictions of all sentient beings, evil views and beasts, and have the ability to liberate the karma of birth and death. Try not to be named as the Great Armored Wheel, try not to be named as the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, be named as the Sravaka, the true Pratyekabuddha field of blessings.
(Sutra: Come, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva has the Pure Precept Great Pillar If Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat achieves this wheel, from the beginning, all five desires can be eliminated, far surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, because all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones should make offerings to, inherit, and protect the Pure Precepts of the Bodhisattva common, two is not common. What are the common pure precepts of Bodhisattvas? That is, the precepts and precepts received by lay people of Accession and Abiding, or the specific precepts of liberation and precepts received by renunciates, are called the common pure precepts of Bodhisattvas, because they are shared with the Sravaka and Pratyekayana love, or can liberate the karma of birth and death. This is not called the Great Armored Wheel, nor is it called the Bodhisattva Mahasattva, nor is it called the true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) of all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas).

The precepts observed by lay people who are Close to Sustaining and Close to Abiding are to follow the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, or to accept the Eight Precepts. Near Su is the Three Refuges, Five Precepts, and Near Tru is the Eight Precepts. “Or become a monk” (Or become a monk again), become a monk and receive the Complete Precepts. If you leave home without receiving the Complete Precepts, you will immediately receive the ten novice precepts. “Updating to receive the Complete Precepts” (And receiving the Complete Precepts): The Complete Precepts are the Prajnaparamita Vows. Completing one precept will lead to the same liberation. By upholding one precept, one is liberated in the same way. If the two hundred and fifty precepts are kept pure, they will all be liberated and attain Arahantship. "As the law of liberation separates the precepts of liberation, the name Bodhisattva adds the pure precepts" (The law of liberation like that is called the plus and net of the Bodhisattva's precepts): What does "Plus" mean here? There is a Bodhisattva like Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, who appears as a Bhikkhu. He also [maintains the precepts and postures of a Bhikkhu] together with Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha. He is both a Bodhisattva and a Bhikkhu, so he is called “Bodhisattva Bhikkhu”. That is called “combined pure precepts”, He received both the Bhikkhu precepts and the Bodhisattva precepts. The Bhikkhu precepts are also pure, the Bodhisattva precepts are also pure; This has the same characteristics as the Sravakas and Pratyekayana. Is it true that Bodhisattvas will rely on this wheel of pure precepts to be able to crush all afflictions? Cause all the afflictions and evil destiniess of sentient beings to be cut off? Possible or not? Impossible! Because Thanh Van and Doc Giac do not develop that mind. Bodhisattvas use this precept to attain the pure precept wheel, eliminating all afflictions, all evil views, and wrong knowledge and wrong views of sentient beings. Use that to free yourself from the karma of birth and death. Use these things to free yourself from the karma of birth and death. “Birth and Death” here is the ultimate, it is not the Wheel of Great Armor, it is not the Great Wheel of Pure Precepts, nor is it called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. This is something in common with Shravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, belonging to Shravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, they cannot be called Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, and cannot make a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

(Sutra) Cloud and River Bodhisattva Non-Communist Pure World Great Armored Wheel? The Bodhisattvas of all sentient beings in the ten directions, create equanimity in the mind, have no disturbance in the mind, have no resentment or hatred, protect the pure precepts, universally maintain the precepts, break the precepts, give alms, be greedy, be compassionate, resentful, diligent, entertain, lower, middle, and high-rank all sentient beings, infallibly keep the mind, infallibly think, and protect the pure precepts. Universally, the three worlds are necessarily sentient, without suffering, without anger, covering all evil deeds, and maintaining the pure precepts. Universally, the three existences of Aggregates, Precepts, and Bases, without any distinction, protect the pure precepts; pure precepts; ball y Formless precepts protect the pure precepts; bcontemplation of all beings necessarily retribution,protects Maintaining pure precepts; The Bodhisattva's name does not belong to the Pure Precepts Great Armor Pillar. Good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva became a Pure Precept Great Armored Wheel, developed his mind at the beginning, had to eliminate the five desires at all stages, and attained the name of Bodhisattva Mahasattva. Super surpasses all Sravakas and Single Enlightenment, universal taste of Sravakas and Single Enlightenment creates a great field of blessings. All sravakas and pratyekabuddhas of the 1st level make offerings, serve, and protect.
(Sutra: What is the Bodhisattva Wheel of Non-Communist Pure Precepts? That is, Bodhisattva for the sake of all sentient beings in the ten directions, raised a mind of equality, a mind without disturbance, a mind without resentment, to uphold the pure precepts, for all sentient beings to uphold the precepts, to break the precepts, to give alms, to be greedy, to be compassionate, to be angry, to be diligent, to relax, to be of low, middle, and high quality, to have no difference in mind, to have no different ideas, to uphold the pure precepts, because throughout all sentient beings in the three worlds, without anger, without hatred, and without There are evil actions that protect the pure precepts. Because they do not distinguish all the Aggregates, Places, and Realms in the three existences to maintain the pure precepts, do not rely on the Desire Realm to maintain the pure precepts, do not rely on the Formless Realm to maintain the pure precepts, do not rely on the Formless Realms to maintain the pure precepts, do not contemplate all the retributions in the existences to maintain the pure precepts, do not rely on all attainments and non-attachments to maintain the pure precepts, do not rely on actions to maintain the pure precepts. That is called the Bodhisattva's Pure Precepts, Mahasattva. If Bodhisattva Mahasattva attains this Pure Precepts, from the beginning, he will be able to eliminate all five desires, and he will be called the Bodhisattva Mahasattva; he will surpass all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, because all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas will make great merit fields. provide, serve, protect).

That is the Bodhisattva Precepts. The Bodhisattva Precepts are the “three pure precepts”, including six important precepts and twenty-eight light precepts [according to the Upasaka Precepts Sutra], or fourteen important precepts and forty-eight light precepts [according to the Brahma Net Sutra]. This is the Bodhisattva precept, not shared with the Second Vehicle, so it is called “non-combined pure precept”. Because of this wheel, we can save all sentient beings, why? They treat living beings without resentment and are equal. “If a living being harms me, I will not save that person”, that is not the case! The mind must be equal, you hurt them ten thousand times, no matter how many times you harm them, they still consider you as parents, as Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. They still respect you the same way. That is the true Bodhisattva mind. His concentration is extremely strong, not being swayed by his realm. The mind can change situations, there is no resentment. Then there will be no revenge, no suffering, no resentment, they will not take revenge. Protect the Bodhisattva's pure precepts like that. For the precepts, the one who maintains the precepts is a dharma weapon, the one who breaks the precepts is not the dharma weapon. Maintaining precepts and breaking precepts are relative dharmas. Giving alms and being greedy, refusing to give alms, compassion and resentment, extremely strong anger, diligence and laziness, [these are the opposing dharmas]. For all sentient beings of the three levels, upper, middle, and lower, there is no difference in mind. Not only does that mind not exist, but there is also no thinking, no different ideas to protect the pure precepts.

For this Purification of Precepts Great Armor and Pillar Wheel, the previous part is Plus. “Plus” means all three vehicles exist together. This part is incompatible with the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas (ie the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas do not have these dharmas at all). For all sentient beings in the three realms, there is no affliction, no anger, no anger, seeing that all sentient beings are illusory. Contemplating the nature of sentient beings is inherently empty, so the Diamond Sutra says: "When Buddhas save sentient beings, or great Bodhisattvas save sentient beings, they do not see the appearance of sentient beings, knowing that sentient beings are illusory". How can they give rise to anger and hatred? Because we don't see the logic of Mu and talk inappropriately, that's why in the relationships between people, there is a lot of resentment! At the same time, our own mind is neither pure nor ultimately pure. How do these great Bodhisattvas maintain the pure precepts? They contemplate all living beings as illusory and as transformed. For sentient beings, not the slightest affliction arises. The mind of anger is only a small part, but the mind of affliction includes so many things!

Indignation among thirteen structures. The Bodhisattva who protects and upholds the pure precepts is the one who protects like that. Towards all sentient beings in the Three Realms, no matter how they hurt me, Bodhisattvas do not harbor anger. No anger arises, of course there is no mind to harm living beings, maintaining the precepts is pure like that. When maintaining pure precepts, they separate both sides (Yes and No), displaying the meaning of the Middle Way. What is pure precepts? He does not rely on the Three Existences, that is, the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless World. As long as there is a cycle of birth and death, the Five Aggregates, the eighteen realms, the twelve realms, all dharmas have no distinction, no distinction arises. In other words, we cannot see which living beings are good, which living beings do good karma, which living beings create evil karma. When you create bad karma, you will immediately feel disgusted, angry, and resentful. For good people, the feeling mind must protect them. That is the discriminating mind, that is called "having discrimination". "Ultimately maintaining pure precepts" (Ultimately pure precepts): Precepts here are the mental precepts. The following distinctions are [talked about in detail about] the mind world. After that, he said to uphold the pure precepts, not being attached to all appearances. Yes, the pure precepts are not attached to all appearances. Next is not relying on the three realms, that is, the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, the Formless Realm, until not contemplating the retribution in all realms to protect the pure precepts. Keeping the precepts is the cause, the result achieved in the future is the retribution. Maintain pure precepts, attain Arahantship, and attain Buddhahood. They do not consider [that] at all, not because they will gain retribution in the future, or because they will gain benefits in the future, then they will maintain the pure precepts.

Furthermore, “it is not necessary to gain or gain evil or to protect the pure precepts” (not relying on all gains and disadvantages to protect the pure precepts): Upholding the precepts has merit, breaking the precepts buries the merit, and there is evil. Thus, when Bodhisattvas maintain pure precepts, how is it to maintain pure precepts? Pure mind, pure Buddha realm. All living beings are pure, all dharmas are pure, they protect the pure precepts like that. “Relying on actions to protect the pure precepts” (Not relying on actions to maintain the pure precepts), “practice” is practice, cultivating the ten signs, up to cultivating Mind-Only Consciousness, these dharmas are all considered as mind-abiding. It is not because of these things that one maintains the pure precepts. That is the Bodhisattva's Great Armored Wheel of Non-Combination of Pure Precepts. The Non-Communist Pure Precepts are not in common with the Shravakas and Pratyekabuddhas. What do they have in common with the Shravaka Vehicle and the Single Sense Vehicle? Like the Five Precepts, like the Eight Precepts, like the two hundred and fifty precepts of Bhikkhus, the Dharma Precepts of Goodness, and the Receptive Precepts, these are the Bodhisattva Plus Reception Precepts. There are places where the Bodhisattva Precepts are “not in addition” (not in common with) the Second Vehicle, that is, the Many Benefits and Sentient Precepts are not in addition to the Second Vehicle. That Bodhisattva upholds the pure precepts. In the previous section, it was said that there are two types of signs, one is the plus sign, the other is the non-plus sign. In the previous part, it talked about the common appearance, but this part is completely about the non-plus appearance.

Therefore, he can eliminate all five desires, and is called Bodhisattva Mahasattva. The great Bodhisattva among the Bodhisattvas is the enlightened sentient being, enlightening all sentient beings, making all sentient beings enlightened, and able to maintain pure precepts. Due to this kind of pure precepts, the mind is pure, not attached to worldly appearances. Therefore, He surpasses all Thanh Van and Doc Giac, so he can create a field of great blessings for Thanh Van and Doc Giac. All those who belong to the Shravaka Vehicle and the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle should make offerings to this Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, should all inherit and learn pure precepts with him. What is pure precepts?

writes: - Remains a layman, becomes a monk, liberates the precepts, possesses the Dharma of the Second Vehicle, is not known as Mahasattva. The wise person who practices the Empty Dharma, does not take refuge in the world, does not take care of all things, protects the pure precepts, separates from the Thi La prime minister, is immaculate, free from taints. (Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One displayed this meaning again, then recited verses: - Abiding The lay person follows the rules of discipline, becomes a monk and liberates the precepts, together with the Second Vehicle. He is not called a Mahasattva. A wise person practices the Dharma of Emptiness, does not rely on the worldly things, nor does he rely on the worldly beings, maintains the pure precepts, is free from attachment to Thi La, is free from defilements, is called the true field of blessings.

“Lay precepts” are the Five Precepts and the Eight Precepts. As for the six major precepts and twenty-eight minor precepts in the Bodhisattva Precepts, when you first learn the law of doubt, you will rely on form to enter formlessness, just like in the above paragraph talking about the formless dharma. That is something in common with the Second Vehicle, that is, relying on the precepts of form to receive and uphold the precepts, that is, relying on the form to receive and maintain. That is called “Two Vehicle plus data” (in common with the Two Vehicle). When combined with the Second Vehicle, one is not called a great Bodhisattva, but an ordinary Bodhisattva. Or with the initial initiation of the Bodhisattva's mind, a wise person practices the Emptiness method, that is, practices Mind Only Consciousness Contemplation, practices Emptiness Contemplation. People with wisdom then practice Khong Quan. Staying in the world, leaving the worldly appearance, not relying on the world to practice all dharmas, nor relying on beings, that is, not relying on the three realms to protect the pure precepts. Whenever you cling to appearances, you will cling to the law. Thi La is Precepts or Law. Having left, there is no attachment to appearance. Maintaining precepts without having the appearance of observing precepts; That is the mind-ground dharma door, immaculate, without defilements. All the precepts and precepts in the Second Vehicle are still tainted dharmas. Because when they talk about Purity, that Purity is spoken in opposition to Contamination. The Bhikkhu Precepts of the Second Vehicle are only intended to treat the afflictions of Views and Thoughts, and cannot be related to the physical nature. If you have wisdom, then practice the Emptiness Dharma, that is, nature.

In the previous section, Mind Only Consciousness Insight was mentioned. What is said in the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, compared with this sutra, is in close agreement with the second half. The ten great armored wheels in this passage are all the ultimate dharma of Mahayana Bodhisattva Mahasattva, all practicing Emptiness Contemplation. Contemplate that all dharmas are Emptiness, and precepts are also Emptiness. Everything is a relative dharma, and all relative dharmas have no real substance. You must maintain the precepts like that, not falling into the three worlds, until all the delusions of ignorance and the delusions of the mundane world are considered to be the delusions of existence. Because the Second Vehicle still has the suffering of Change, Change, and Birth and Death, it is still considered as an asrava, not the ultimate asrava of the Buddhas. That's just not falling into the three realms! If you can maintain the precepts like that, you will not hold on to attachments. Whenever you take something, it is an attachment. Whenever there is taking, there is bound to be letting go. Not keeping the form is also not letting go. That is the only way to make a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for the Second Vehicle.

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat restores the An Nhan Great Armor Pillar. The Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat has accomplished the test of the wheel, has the initial mind to develop the mind, must have the five desires, has the ability to eliminate the stage, overcomes the need for the Sravaka, the Single Enlightened One, the universal taste must have the Sravaka, the Single Enlightenment to create a great field of blessings, must have the Sravaka, the Single Enlightened Vehicle of the first class, to make offerings, to serve, and to protect. Van Ha An Nhan Dai Giap Tru Luan? Good man! Bodhisattva peace has two types of appearance: One person, the world. Second person, out of this world. Van Ha Bodhisattva of the world is patient? The suffering of suffering, the fate of sentient beings, the beginning of existence, the presence of form, the practice of retribution, the practice of blessed karma, the origin of patience, the origin of patience, the origin of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, the origin of existence, the existence of pleasure, the inability to resist, the power of power, the energy of sentient beings, the existence of existence, the tolerance of others, the non-benefiting of sentient beings. The name Bodhisattva of the world is patient. Such as Thi An Nhan, together with the Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas of the same level; try not to be named as the Great Armor Pillar, but not because of the Bodhisattva Mahasattva, name all the Sravakas, the true Pratyekabuddha field.
(Sutra: Come here, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Bodhisattva Mahasattva attains this wheel, from the beginning, all the five desires can be eliminated, surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightenment, because all the Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones should make offerings to, take care of, and protect the Bodhisattva There are two types of signs: One is the world, the other is beyond the world. What is the Bodhisattva's patience in the world? That is, having patience, following sentient beings, having hold, having appearances, depending on the karma to develop patience, depending on one's own Sight, Sound, Scent, Taste, Touch to develop patience, there is patience that arises, there is patience that cannot be endured, there is patience that is weak, there is patience that abandons living beings, and there is patience that leads to deception. deception, there is a kind of patience that blindly favors others, there is a patience that does not benefit sentient beings. That is called the worldly peace of the Bodhisattva. Such forbearance is shared with the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas; it is not called the Great Armored Wheel, nor is it called the Bodhisattva Mahasattva, and it is not called the true field of blessings of all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

What is An Nhan Dai Giap Tru Luan? “Good man! An Nhan has two types of appearances” (Hey good man! An Nhan has two types of appearances): Each wheel has two types of appearances, one is a worldly appearance, the other is a worldly appearance. Beyond the world is the “formless” appearance. What is worldly forbearance? The word Forbearance here cannot be understood as Forbearance, but must be understood in the sense of “admit”. Admitting what? Acknowledge the true nature, acknowledge the dharma with asrava and the dharma with asrava. “Anasrava” means “ultimate”. Existence is not ultimate. “Dependence of sentient beings” (Destiny according to sentient beings), Bodhisattva practices patience as the cause, receiving all outside sentient beings as conditions. Cause is what can arise, condition is what can help achieve. If a Bodhisattva wants to achieve the Paramita of Forbearance, he must know: There is nothing in the world that can ultimately be achieved, your Patience is still an outflow, it is an eternal patience! Because [that subject of Forbearance] contemplates all sentient beings, sentient beings act as its support. Cultivating that discipline of Forbearance, there will be attachment and form. If someone else scolds us or harms us, we immediately know that sentient beings have a deep karma and endure being insulted by that person. That is the ring of existence.

What about formless? Living beings are basically Emptiness, all dharmas are Emptiness, seeing that living beings have no self, they all come about due to conditions. What conditions exist to make this happen? Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Emptiness, Knowledge, and Consciousness are created by these seven elements. All living beings are created by the seven elements. The sutras often speak of the Four Great Elements, which are the earth realm, the water realm, the fire realm, and the wind realm. Whenever we say “four great elements”, we are talking about the four great elements of earth, water, fire, and wind. Whenever the “three worlds” are mentioned, of course they are the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm. Thus, the four great realms include the Desire Realm and the Form Realm. The Formless Realm is emptiness, so saying "earth, water, fire, wind, emptiness" includes the four great elements in it. The Formless Realm is also included in Emptiness. The Bodhisattva's patience is not to keep the form, but because he follows the world's dharma, he has the ability to keep and have the form. Depending on the consequences, you must practice, patience is the best way to practice blessings. A patient person has a very dignified appearance, a very beautiful appearance, and has the appearance of merit. If a person is angry or has a hateful mind, his appearance will be ugly. The person is beautiful and has a very dignified appearance, but whenever he gets angry, when he gets angry, his appearance will change, turning into a Rakshasa.

Therefore, one should understand that [the world's patience] has hold and form, but Bodhisattva is absolutely not like that. He depends on the world, so he looks like that. Cultivate worldly blessings, because forbearance arising from worldly blessings will depend on Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, and Touch to give birth to patience. Or you hit me, that's Contact. Contact is Suffering. You feel pain, or are scolded by others, or feel humiliated, these are all physical signs. In the face of those forms, you endure, but in the matter of ending birth and death, there is no solution. That's just depending on the world. Even if you accept birth and death, you can only attain the birth and death of the Second Vehicle. That's called Breaking Life and Death, it's not the end! That subject of Forbearance (the world of forbearance) refers to all forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and touches. That is Ngu Tran. The Five Senses come into contact with your five senses, then unpleasant things arise. If you can endure it, it is called "based on that to give birth to Forbearance". That method of Forbearance is not ultimate, it depends on following the worldly appearance to develop the mind to move forward. If you are in the form of the world and want to cut off the world and the three realms of nine existences[45], that forbearance will not end. Therefore, it is called “the ring world”.

“Incapable of patience”: If they were people in the world, they would not be able to endure (endure), but according to religious people, they would be able to endure and endure. Or someone with weak physical strength is not as good as others. If compared with others, always inferior, that person thinks that is correct, and has no mind to compete with others for victory. These are all said in the sense of “having an attachment, having a form”.

“Forbearance of sentient beings” (Forbearance of abandoning sentient beings): We see that the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas of the Second Vehicle do not save sentient beings. Not saving sentient beings is “the qi of sentient beings” (throwing away sentient beings). They practice the practice of Forbearance which is “the energy of living beings”. Or there is someone who deceives you, deceives you, deceives you, deceives you, you don't realize it's a lie, you still accept that person, blindly favor that person, make him happy, make him happy. We admit that, [that is] “forbearance for the benefit of sentient beings” (not for the sake of the benefit of sentient beings). That is called the Bodhisattva's patience with the world, it does not benefit sentient beings! Those disciplines of Forbearance are “the world of forbearance”. What kind of ring is that? It is the ring of Thanh Van and Duyen Giac. In other words, they are all dharmas belonging to the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, depending on the world. That is the ninjutsu in common with the Sravakas and the Single Sense Vehicle. That is the worldly peace and patience of Bodhisattvas. This subject of forbearance is shared with the Shravakas and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle. If you rely on that subject of Forbearance to practice, you will attain that subject of Forbearance.

(Sutra) Cloud River Bodhisattva appeared in the world An Nhan Dai Giap Giap Luan? The untainted forbearance, necessarily the sage and great dharma of light, the universal benefit of all sentient beings without tainted forbearance, the eternally bound to work in career, language, human appearance, writing, sound, and the place of peaceful practice. Cultivate patience, be able to completely cut off the three formations, three feelings, three appearances, three worlds, three existences, three virtues, three unwholesome roots, four types of bursts, four yokes, four hands, four types of body system. Practice patience and calm your mind. The famous Bodhisattva An Nhan Dai Giap Tru Luan appeared in the world. Good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva, through the An Nhan Great Armored Wheel, developed the mind at the beginning, was able to completely eliminate all five desires, attained the title of Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, surpassed all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste of Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment to create a great field of blessings. Necessary Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas of the 1st level make offerings, serve, and protect.
(Sutra: What is the birth of the Bodhisattva's An Ren Great Armor Wheel? Patience, is the light of the great dharma of all sages, is the immaculate forbearance (untainted forbearance) that benefits all sentient beings, is the forbearance that permanently eliminates all actions done, language, appearance of the person, writing, sound, practice of this practice, it is possible to cut off all the three formations, three feelings, three appearances, three worlds, three existences, three actions, three unwholesome roots, the four types. dThe four yokes, the four hands, the four types of restraint in the body, when cultivating this discipline, the mind is calm. That is called the Bodhisattva's Great Forbearance Wheel. If the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat achieves this Great Forbearance Wheel, from the beginning, all five desires can be eliminated, and he is called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, surpassing all others. Van, Soc Giac, because all Thanh Van, Soc Giac are great fields of merit, all the Thanh Van, Soc Giac Vehicles should make offerings, serve, and protect.

What is the Bodhisattva's An Nhan Great Armor Wheel in the world?

This ring is neither the Great Armor Pillar nor the ultimate peace of mind, it is called Anasrava Ring. Not only is there no “outflow” (leakage, leftovers) in the three worlds, but there is also no outflow in all Beings. “Gonorrhea” refers to the habits of ignorance and dust. This type of ring is called Dharma Ring. If you acknowledge the nature of the Dharma, it is called Anasrava Forbearance. This forbearance arises from the light of the great dharma of the sages, that is, from their wisdom. “Hien” refers to the status of the Three Sages (Ten Pillars, Ten Virtues, Ten Dedications), [Saint refers to the Ten Grounds]. This is the Bodhisattva who attains the status of sage and attains the great dharma of light and wisdom. But He absolutely does not abandon sentient beings, but benefits all sentient beings. Although it benefits sentient beings, we are not greedy and do not accept the appearance of sentient beings.

“The universal taste of benefiting all sentient beings is immaculate before patience” (Forbearance is for the benefit of all sentient beings without being attached to it): “Immaculate before patience” is due to accepting all sentient beings, not [attachment] to having the form of sentient beings, that is “selfless form, "There is no human form, there is no sentient being, there is no false life" as taught by the Diamond Sutra, there is also no self that can be patient, there is no dharma that can be patient, there is no object to be patient. There is no scene, no mind, no dharma, no self, forever ending all the work done. “The career you've done is forever ended” means not being attached. “Eternal break” does not mean doing nothing at all, but doing all things, but not being attached to all careers.

“Language, human form, writing, sound”: All the work you have done cannot be separated from language, nor can it be separated from writing, cannot be separated from the form of writing, cannot be separated from the form of language, nor can it be separated from sentient beings. The career that you can practice depends on all the conditions to achieve it. If there is no supporting fate, if the fate is destroyed, then that career will not exist either! If one can attain that practice of Patience, one will be able to cut off "three bonds, three feelings, three appearances, three worlds, three existences, three formations, three unwholesome roots, four types of bursts, four yokes, four hands, four strains of the body system. Practice forbearance at the time, the mind and mind become calm" (three bonds, three feelings, three appearances, three worlds, three formations, three formations, three unwholesome roots, four types of streams, four yokes, four hands, four types of attachments in the body. When cultivating If Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat cultivates this Great Ring of Forbearance, from the moment he first develops his mind, he will be able to get rid of the five desires.

What is “Three Life”? “Tho” here means “receive” (receive). Regardless of whether your body is in contact, or even if your thoughts are in contact, there will be three types of Painful Feeling, Pleasure Feeling, and Neither Painful nor Pleasure Feeling. Our eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are called the Six Senses. Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Dharma outside are called Luc Tran. When Can and Chen come into contact, within them there are Six Consciousnesses, i.e. Eye Consciousness, Ear Consciousness, Snake Consciousness, Body Consciousness, and Consciousness. Those three items (Can, Chen, and Consciousness) make up the Eighteen Precepts. If Can and Tran come into contact, without Consciousness, you won't know anything. When Can and Chen come into contact [without Consciousness], you don't feel anything. Because Consciousness arises with the function of discrimination, you will feel it. That feeling is Tho. Feeling is suffering, there is pleasure, there is another type of Feeling: Neither Suffering nor Pleasure, there are three types of Feeling like that. That is to say, when the Organ treats (contacts) the external environment, plus the discrimination of Consciousness, you will feel three types of Feeling. One type is the feeling of suffering (Suffering Feeling), the other type is the feeling of joy (Lof Feeling). [In addition, there is a situation where] you have no feeling at all, that is, there is no feeling of pain or pleasure at all. No suffering, no pleasure is called Sa Tho (Neither Suffering, No Pleasure).

What is “Three Commitments”? “Conclusion” is Conclusion. We are in Or karma like a tightly knotted rope or belt. Nowadays we all use leather belts. In the past, in the countryside, people used rope or fabric sewn into belts to tie. Sometimes it's very tight, especially when using Kung Fu. I'm afraid it won't be tight enough and it will come loose and slip away, so I tie it very tightly. So of course there are troubles: When removing, it is very difficult! This is like we are in affliction, hoping to remove that bondage is very difficult. What is that knotted mountain? Kien Or, [or more specifically] the eighty-eight items of History belonging to Kien Or, causing you to suffer the crime, that is Kien Or. Sometimes Body Kien and Bien Kien [in Kien Or] both take the Self as the main thing, considering this body of ours as the main thing, meaning "our own subjectivity is very strong". That is called “constantly arising Self-View” (always arising Self-View):

2) Forbidden Handicap: Forbidden Handicap (conclusion about the observance of certain forbidden precepts or taboos) is wrong view. Wrong knowledge, wrong view, wrong enlightenment. That's talking about pagans.

3) Doubt: Doubting the truth, that is, the true truth. No

For example, regarding Consciousness Only, you are skeptical. Thoughts and actions are not ethical. When we say “not reasonable” we are not speaking according to the morality as the world says. In Buddhism, “not reasonable” is speaking according to your inner self. If it does not correspond to your true heart, then it is called delusion. For example, we believe in Buddhism, but others say [we are] superstitious! I once asked some people, I said: "Please tell me, what is delusion? What is faith?" They only know how to repeat what others say. “Delusion” is ambiguous. Vaguely believing in Buddhism means being vague and confused. I said: Even though you're vague and dreamy, you still believe it? Like a person with schizophrenia, confused, not believing anything, not even knowing himself! If you are crazy, you will absolutely not believe it. Those who believe will absolutely not be fooled! Putting the two words Love and Faith together, it's impossible! Why? Skeptics will not believe. Because we have believed, believe that all dharmas are only manifested by the mind, [often said] "only the mind appears". That person did not believe and doubted. Once there is doubt, trust cannot take root. That is also a knot, which is Nghi Ket.

The Shurangama Sutra teaches us to untie the knot between Can and Tran, but that knot is very difficult to untie. Perhaps you Bodhisattvas have removed it, but I have not been able to remove it! Not being able to untie that knot is because of doubt and true faith cannot arise. What is true faith? Speaking from our side, the texts in the second half of the Sutra on Contemplating Good and Evil Karma have helped us explain the Mahayana Sutra on the Ten Wheels a lot. We have talked about this passage of scripture, believing in your true mind, believing in your True Form, believing that our bodies and the bodies of the Buddhas are identical, equal, without defects, but why can't we achieve it? It's because the Three Keys have bound you, making you unbelievable!

“Three Generals” means Pretending General, Dharma General, and Non-General. That is the Three Generals. All dharmas have these three characteristics.

1) What is Impersonation? An illusion that has a false identity has no real entity. There is only a name, but no real substance, which can be corrupted. Once damaged, that name no longer exists and can no longer represent anything. Pseudonym means you can change your name at any time. I was in prison without a name, called "prisoner number 345". Sometimes called "prisoner number 178". That means it depends on when [the warden] gives you a number. Every time your cell is adjusted, you will be given a new number. Adjust to another location, change to a new number, without letting others know where you are! If you go in there, there's no longer a name. Whenever you hear that alternate number called, you'll immediately know it's you. Not only prisoners, but also the military, up to high-ranking government officials, all use numbers as representatives. Every number has its own number, internally you will know who it is, outsiders will never know! Aren't those names pseudonyms? It's very fake, there is no real entity to be attached to. It can be given this name, or it can also be named by that name, all appearances are false appearances. As for the fake appearance, you can set a fake name corresponding to the fake appearance like that, it will change a lot!

2) The second type is French General. Dharma General is the appearance of all dharmas, as we talk about the Five Aggregates and the Eighteen Precepts, those appearances are not real!

3) The third type is the Formless General: The formless General is the one who has left the disguise. What is the appearance of the Dharma when it is separated from its impersonation? Chan Nhu. True Suchness is not real, it is just the name of the dharma! It separates from appearances. In the noun True Suchness, the noun Truth is still false, but we still don't see what True Suchness is like! What is Chan Nhu in the end? We are so far away from the true heart that we cannot meet for even a second! If you meet for one minute, you will be enlightened in one minute. Meet in one second, you will be enlightened in one second. When you hear the explanation, you believe it. When you enter, it is because you believe in a fake name, not truly gaining faith. Also, we say Desire Existence, Form Existence, Formless Existence. These things are all impersonators, they are all Generals. That is the dharma form.

“Arising form, Abiding form, Different form, Disappearing form”: Birth, existence, difference, and destruction are the Four Generals. The original form and the foreign form combined, become one, two forms become one. We are under General Headquarters. Since the day he was born, he has been a General. But while staying, it is different (changing). Strange is to say “change”, each year a change, gradually changing to death. These are the Form of Birth, the Form of Disappearance, and the Form of Destruction, which eventually disappear and are no more. This can destroy all dharmas. “Death” is the appearance of all dharmas not existing. Having been destroyed, it is said to be “no birth and death”, without death there will be no birth, without birth there will be no death. These two things are contrasting and cannot coexist. Now we are the General of Life, when we die, it will be destroyed, no more. The Extinction General, what is the Extinction General? It's no more!

“Three worlds” is easy to explain, i.e. past, present, and future.

“Three Existences”: Desire Existence, Form Existence, Formless Existence. Living beings, according to their karma, suffer retributions, leading to birth and death.

“ Tam action”, “action” means “movement movement”, something that is moving

dynamic? Body, mouth, and mind are moving. The Three Elements is about the body, mouth, and mind.

“The three unwholesome roots” are greed, anger, and ignorance. Those three things are not good, as long as there is a little [greed, anger, ignorance] they will be corrupted, they are not good roots. Those three things are contaminated with the world. Regarding the external scene, whenever you are satisfied, the situation is favorable and you immediately enjoy it. If you are not satisfied, you will be angry, you will be angry, and any trouble will come to you. That's called not having wisdom. Without wisdom, you will not understand Truth and Reason. That is the “three unwholesome roots”, the basis of all evil things.

“Four torrents” (Four torrents) i.e. the stream of desire, the stream of existence, the stream of views, and the stream of ignorance. Wealth, beauty, fame, eating, drinking, sleeping are also waterfalls. Greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, doubt are also waterfalls.

“Four yokes”: [The yoke] is not often seen. A yoke is a part placed on a vehicle, not a modern car, but a yoke mounted on a buffalo or horse cart. The part in the middle [connected to the cart] is to tie the horse, with latches on both sides, that is the yoke, which also means tying the horse tightly to the yoke so it can pull the cart. No matter how much it jumped, it couldn't escape. It was tied tightly and couldn't escape. All of us sentient beings cannot escape from samsara. “The yoke of desire is like the stream of desire” (The yoke of desire is like the waterfall of Desire), there are twenty-nine types. “Huu yoke is like the stream of Huu yoke” (Huu yoke is like the Huu waterfall), there are twenty-eight types. “The yoke ants flow together” (The yoke ants are like the waterfall of Kien Or), there are thirty-six types. “The four yoke of ignorance” (The fourth is the Abyss of Ignorance), “The four bursts of ignorance” (The fourth is the waterfall of Ignorance) have fifteen types. “Four yokes” is “four streams”, but it is divided into many things. Why is it divided so much? Because there are many things in our thoughts and actions, the Buddha spoke about them one by one. Whichever type you fit into, it will make you unable to realize your nature in that type, that's what it means!

“Four attachments” (Four attachments) is another name for afflictions. The Three Realms have eight hundred afflictions, divided into four separate categories: Attachment to Desire, Attachment to View, Attachment to Precepts, and Attachment to Ego. The Ego Clinging is all the bondage in the body, that is, the Ego Clinging arises, which also means that everything we do is to express the Self. Expressing the Self means Self-View, which is also one of the four types of emergence.

“Four types of body system” (Four types of bondage in the body) are greed and anger, attachment to precepts, attachment to reality (clinging to the essence of dharmas as real). Four types of attachments.

“Three doors of liberation” are Emptiness, Formlessness, and Wishlessness.

“The Four Complete Views” are the Four Right Efforts.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, and recited and wrote: - An endurance theory of the two species, the form of existence, the existence of nothingness. General. The appearance of the ring of existence comes first. The wise do not confess. Cultivate patience in the three elements, rely on Aggregates, Precepts, and Levels. The name has the tainted patience, not the Mahasattva form. One who destroys the Four Crazy Islands and cultivates immaculate forbearance. Tranquility and three virtues. Test your ability to be patient. Ability to calm all actions, abandon all distinctions, the mind is equal like nothingness. Test your ability to be patient. All dharmas are one and the same, Empty, Formless, and pass away. The mind has no previous place of residence. Try patience to gain great benefits.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One displayed this meaning again, then recited verses: - An There are two types of patience, the existence of form and the absence of form. The wise person who practices patience in the three actions, relying on the aggregates, precepts, and realms, is called the patience of existence, without the form of Mahasattva. Because the practice of patience is not deluded, the three aspects of patience are praiseworthy. Being calm in all formations, the mind is as equal as emptiness. The Formless is extinguished. The mind is never entangled. That ring becomes great benefit.)

“At that time, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, then recited and wrote” (At that time, the World-Honored One re-displayed that meaning, then recited verses): The Buddha repeated again the meanings contained in the above passage. “An Nhan theory of two types, one with form, one without form” [meaning] An Nhan has two types of appearances, one is form, the other is formless. “Forbearance of existence” is common to all three vehicles. “Formless Ring” is only for Bodhisattvas. “Wise people do not praise” (Wise people do not praise): People with wisdom do not praise Right Signs of Forbearance.

“Practicing patience based on the three elements, relying on the Aggregates, Precepts, and Places, is called the form of patience, not the form of Ma Ha Tat” (Practicing patience depending on the three elements, relying on the Aggregates, Precepts, Places, etc., is called patience with the form of existence, not the form of Ma Ha Tat): Relying on the body, mouth, and mind (those are the three practice), depending on the eighteen precepts and twelve realms. Practicing patience and cultivating patience like that is not the mark of Mahasattva, that is, it is not the mark of a great Bodhisattva. “The one who destroys the Four Crazy Islands” (For destroying the Four Crazy Islands): Selflessness and self-clinging are both crazy. There are no attachments. Remember that whenever there is a Self, which is not happiness, but suffering, you consider it happiness; That is [the madness] of human birth. To give an example, it's like we drink wine at a party. Drinking alcohol is because people invite and persuade each other, seeming to be very happy, drinking softly, drinking heavily. You should know that it is suffering, and it also causes the body to suffer. In the past, when I went there, there was a Dharma friend from Taiwan. He got drunk and fell under the table, breaking the front of his neck. Currently, his neck is still damaged, spending a lot of money on treatment. Originally looking for pleasure, in the end there was absolutely no pleasure!

Just like in Taiwan, there are male bartenders, there are female bartenders, women find male bartenders, men find female bartenders. Originally it was a happy thing, but they were jealous of each other, even hated each other and killed each other! Needless to say, economic loss also leads to a lot of trouble. There is also “fighting for dominance” (fighting for dominance), jealousy, a lot of suffering in that. You say, is it pleasure or pain? Originally there were no living beings, not even the Self existed, that pleasure was not pleasure. Permanence, Bliss, Ego, and Purity are the Four Virtues of the Buddhas. On the contrary, it is called the Four Crazy Islands, considering suffering as happiness, considering impermanence as permanent, considering purity as impurity. Our body is inherently impure, we still criticize this as impure, that is also impure, do you have anything clean or not? I myself do not practice Quan, because above the body there is a diaphragm (Thoracic diaphragm), below there is another diaphragm, so the bad smell [from the internal organs] does not emanate. Before we come out of our mother's womb, everything is impure, right below the birth and maturation organs[46] is dirty, right in the feces and urine, and we also have to absorb those things to be able to survive. After being born, you see this body, nine holes are constantly flowing. Due to confusion, that person often thinks [himself] is very clean, [criticizing] this thing is not clean, that thing is not clean either. That person thinks he is very good, very clean; actually, very dirty!

Suppose you say: Whenever we gather, always carry a bag of feces, a bag of urine, wrap it tightly to take away, you yourself feel very dirty. Even though no one knows, it still feels very dirty. Actually, we bring this flesh body with us, do you think it's exactly the same? It's all crazy. This life inherently has birth, must have death, it is not permanent, but we insist that it is permanent, always wanting to live for several hundred years, to live for a hundred years, to live for several decades! Advise others to do the same, have a long life! I advise everyone to practice Impermanence, always be aware that you can die at any time. There are Dharma friends who don't like to hear things like that, [grumbling] "What's the point in talking about death?" Here's what I want to remind you of, it's very good, not bad at all! If you say you die, then you die? It's not time to die, even if I say it a hundred times, you still won't die. I say die every day, I'm still alive! I've been saying for decades that I want to die. Why do you want to die? Avoid letting yourself get carried away! You always think about death, think about impermanence, what else is there in the world to be attached to? Therefore, you contemplate impermanence, practice impermanence like that, that is the meaning of not being deluded! You must admit that, “forbearance” means “admit”. If you don't acknowledge it, you will enjoy pleasure and not achieve a peaceful body. You cannot achieve the three virtues of tranquility in body, mouth, and mind! You must constantly contemplate this, you must overturn the inversions, you must be selfless, impermanent, suffering, emptiness, constantly contemplate like that. For the sake of eliminating the Four Crazy Islands, practicing immaculate forbearance, and having no attachment to all dharmas. [Or to be more specific, it would be] to have no attachment to body, speech, mind, and all dharmas. Regarding the Ten Good Karmas, [the karma of] body, mouth, and mind are all Ten Good Karmas, and there is no attachment. [The Ten Good Karmas] seems to be something worth doing, nothing worth being greedy about!

Due to patience, all the subjects of Samadhi can be achieved, eight hundred subjects of samadhi can be achieved. Why? Get rid of all distinctions. “The mind is equal like nothingness” (The mind is equal like nothingness): We consider Being and Non-Existence to be equal, we consider suffering and joy to be equal, we consider contempt and impermanence to be equal, all sentient beings, good or stupid, slow-minded, stupid and intelligent, are equal. In terms of nature, they are all equal. Why? “All dharmas are the same beast” (All dharmas are on the same path), moving towards what? No, formless, extinct. Moving toward emptiness, formlessness, and cessation. Emptiness, Formlessness, and Desirelessness are the three doors of liberation. All dharmas are Emptiness, all dharmas are formless. That appearance is a fake name, a fake appearance, the mind is not located anywhere! Your mind is not attached to anything like that, that patience is the patience of a wise person who can become a Buddha.

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva restores the Wheel of Effort Great Armor. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat accomplished testing the wheel, developed the initial mind, must eliminate the five desires at all stages, overcome all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment to create a great field of blessings. It is necessary for Thanh Van and Single Enlightened Vehicle to make offerings, take care of things, and protect them. Cloud Ha Tinh Tinh Dai Giap Truc Luan? Good man! Bodhisattva diligently possesses two types of appearance: None of the world, of the world; of the two, of the world. Van Ha Bodhisattva of the world is diligent? Bodhisattvas are diligent and courageous and need to cultivate the three types of good fortune in their career. Ha class vi tam? One person, giving blessings to one's career; two false precepts, career blessings; Tam fake, cultivate career blessings. Cultivation is the name of the three types of diligence. As for diligence, all sentient beings have their sufferings, their attachments, their retributions, their blessed karma. Famous Bodhisattva in the world who is diligent. If you diligently join the Shravakas and Single-Enlightened Vehicles of the same level, try not to be famous as the Great Armor Pillar, but if you don't try to be famous as the Bodhisattva Mahasattva, you will definitely be named Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas in the true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra).
(Sutra: Come, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva has the Great Pillar of Effort If the Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves this wheel, from the beginning, all five desires can be eliminated, surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, because all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, all the Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, should make offerings to, inherit, and protect the Wheel of Great Effort, good man! What is Bodhisattva's worldly diligence? That is, Bodhisattvas diligently, courageously, diligently practice the three worldly meritorious deeds. One is the meritorious deeds, the third is the practice of meritorious deeds. Such diligence is based on the existence of beings, relying on the merits of the world. That is called the Bodhisattva's diligence. Being diligent like that, together with the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, they will not be called the Great Armored Wheel, nor because of this, they will be called Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas, nor will they be called the field of true blessings for all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

The Bodhisattva's diligence has two types of appearances: One is worldly, the other is beyond the world. What is the mark of worldly diligence? It is the Bodhisattvas who are diligent, courageous, and diligent in cultivating the three types of things that belong to the worldly meritorious karma. Practicing the Ten Virtues and observing the Five Precepts are all blessings in the world, giving alms is also blessings in the world. So, when it comes to worldly blessings, there are three types of career signs. What are the three types of generals?

1) One is the karma of giving, that is, the karma of giving, practicing all acts of giving. The [first] form of karma is like that.

2) Second is precepts, that is, maintaining precepts. Taking the Three Refuges and Five Precepts. If you practice well, the minimum reward is to be born in heaven and forever escape the three paths. By observing the Eight Precepts, you have received the Eight Precepts. If you keep them for one day and one night, you will definitely be born in heaven. Such are the blessings and merits of the Eight Precepts. If you practice for many days, your merit will increase. If you practice it for one day and one night, you will be worthy of being born in the Dao Loi heaven. If you practice for one hundred days, you will either become Emperor Thich Thien or become a heavenly king, but you will not become a citizen of heaven because your merit is even greater. If we are not greedy for good karma, do not wish to be born in heaven, and do not seek enjoyment, we will give alms to all sentient beings, and we will be Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas. Do everything, depending on how you think. Whatever you think, you will achieve that result. Because your way of thinking is different, the results are also different. Understanding this principle, we do a little good deed, not wishing for ourselves to be happy, but only hoping for sentient beings to be free from suffering. Always think of sentient beings, your merit will be great, and your blessings will be infinite and endless. Giving alms is like that, maintaining precepts is like that, and cultivating meritorious karma is like that.

3) There are many stories about cultivating blessings, [such as] repairing bridges, building roads, praising, and rejoicing. I don't do anything, but when I see others doing it, I obey Samantabhadra's ten great vows and praise it, rejoicing, and the merit is inconceivable. I have a part in your story, I also hope to do it, depending on the merit, the merit is inconceivable! Everyone reads the chapter Samantabhadra Vows, the fifth vow is “rejoicing in merit”, you must praise and rejoice. The merit of praising and rejoicing is inconceivable. On the other hand, you slander, or think that "there is no merit, anyone can do it!" Anyone can say empty words, but that person does not act, and when he sees someone else doing it, he slanders them and minimizes their benefits. That person will be guilty. That blessing is great, but the sin [of defamation] is also very great!

Those three types of diligence, no matter how much you practice, how diligent you are, without sleep day or night, the merit and virtue you gain is only existent! This is an outflow of [merit], because there is leakage, there is attachment, due to relying on retributions, due to relying on blessings, it is called the Bodhisattva's worldly diligence. Such diligence will be in common with the Sravakas and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, not the Great Armored Wheel. Nor is it possible to be called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat because of that; but also cannot cultivate true merit fields for Shravaka and Pratyekayana.

What is the Bodhisattva's Great Wheel of Armor? What is the Bodhisattva's Great Armor Pillar of Effort? They are Bodhisattvas who are brave, diligent, and have an egalitarian nature towards all sentient beings. It's very difficult for us to do, because our minds discriminate very heavily, no one can avoid it! Male appearance, female appearance, elderly appearance, child appearance; Such respect cannot be given to children! I didn't say this, but everyone can probably feel it! We monastics and cultivators have a very serious attachment to appearances. We cannot approach women, nor can women approach men, and bhikshunis cannot approach bhikshus. Is [attachment to] such appearances equal or not? As in the Avatamsaka Sutra, National Master Thanh Luong asked himself: “The body does not touch the stupa of the lay people, the body of the nuns does not touch the dust, the body does not touch the dharma precepts of the sutras” (The body does not touch the bed of the lay people, the feet do not step on the dust of the bhiksuni, the sitting does not turn the back to the place where there are Dharma sutras), that is, if there are sutras behind the place where he sits, then absolutely do not sit. Before now, she had never entered a Bhikkhunī monastery. At that time, I joked with other Dharma friends: "National Master Thanh Luong has violated the precepts." He asked: "What precept? What precept does such a virtuous person violate?" I said: "Don't interact with bhikshunis." He said: “People did not ask Him.” I said: "Even if you asked, you wouldn't come. You wouldn't enter a bhikkhunī's monastery, right? Your feet wouldn't step on a bhikkhunī's dust! If lay people want to make offerings to you, your body wouldn't touch the lay people's bed. You can't lie down on a lay person's bed. Also 'mouth doesn't taste food past Noon' (the mouth doesn't taste food past Noon). It's past Noon, and the tea isn't even there." drink!”

What is Tri Ngo? If you really practice Ngo, the water will be colored and you will not be able to drink it; That's called "tri Ngo". If you receive the Eight Precepts, you must pay attention to the precept "don't eat past noon", you can't eat it casually! The reason why there are precepts like the Five Precepts and the Eight Precepts, if I have time, I will tell you so everyone can clearly understand what it is all about! Drinking a cup of cow's milk, let's say it's not eating past Noon. I have told many people that drinking milk is not okay; If the water has any color, it's a no-go! As for breakfast, regardless of whether it is morning or not, it must be the time when the clear form appears. What is “The appearance of a clear figure”? It's already light and when you see the lines on your palm, you can eat this and that. As we currently rely on external manifestations, it is not yet dawn, [but having already eaten breakfast] will not work! The Buddha's precepts have certain limits. Precept means “stop”, not inequality! As the National Master Thanh Luong perfected it, in one mote there are realms of water as many as the mote. You see that he criticized and commented on the Avatamsaka Sutra very tolerantly, but his requirements for himself were extremely strict!

Bodhisattvas who are brave and diligent, all sentient beings, have an equanimous mind, eliminating all afflictions and sufferings. Such as being diligent, necessarily the sages should be honored. Vof impure, non-attachment, non-attachment. Pmust be diligent, leisurely, giving alms, xan greedy, precept-breaking, compassionate, resentful, lower, middle, and superior of all sentient beings, infallible in mind, infallible in thoughts, brave, diligent.Pof the three realms of all sentient beings, equal, non-dual, career-creator, speech, thought, base of practitioners, non-devoted baseto stand before, strong, diligent. Pof the three aggregates of Aggregates, Precepts, Bases, without distinction, strong, diligent. strong diligence. Bconsistency in all beings necessarily retribution brave diligence. Bany y necessarily encountering evil and inadvisable bravery diligence. Ball y practice bravery and diligence. Ball y y the three types of blessing karma bravery and diligence. Bodhisattva named Diligence Great Armor Pillar.
(Sutra: What is the birth of the Bodhisattva Wheel of Diligence? That is, the Bodhisattvas Courageous, diligent, towards sentient beings, His mind is equal, eliminating all afflictions, karma, and suffering. With such diligence, all sages and sages praise him. He does not hold back, does not rely on anything, because throughout all sentient beings, whether they are diligent, lazy, generous, greedy, precept-obsessed, compassionate, and resentful, in the upper, middle, and lower levels, their minds are not different. They are brave and strong in their thoughts. Because all sentient beings in the three realms are equal, they do not rely on all the Aggregates, Precepts, and Realms in the three worlds, but do not rely on the Desire Realm, but do not rely on the Form Realm, but do not rely on the Formless Realm, but do not rely on all the results Not relying on all attainments and non-gains, but courageously striving. Not depending on the three types of worldly merits, but courageously striving for all three types of meritorious deeds. That is called the Bodhisattva's Great Effort.

“Dear sentient beings, have an equal mind” (Equality of mind towards sentient beings) can eliminate all suffering and afflictions; that is diligence. What is equality? From your mind, this equality belongs to Reason, not equality in all things. In Things, there can be no equality. There can never be equality! Someone argued with me, saying that "Things must also be equal". I say: Absolutely there can be no equality! For example, we cannot eat in the living room. From today, the order is to go to the street to eat, each person three bowls. People "go out" (people in the monastery go out to work and farm) and work hard there. For a thirty-year-old young man, three cups is not enough, he needs five cups. But you can't, you can only eat three bowls. Old people, after eating, don't move! Or they stay at home, sit there all day, force them to go there and eat three bowls, even if they strangle them to death they still can't eat! No way! That is inequality, is only three cups per person equal? That kind of equality is an attachment. What is considered equal? Your stomach is equal. You can eat a lot, so you eat a lot. That's called equality. It's impossible to say, "Someone else can carry a hundred kilos, another person can carry two hundred kilos", forcing [everyone] equally to carry two hundred kilos. Many people can't do it! What does equality mean? We want to say "to be equal, everyone must have equal wealth, there can be no rich people", so we flatten everyone, confiscate your property, then divide it equally. I said: "Buddhism doesn't talk about equality that way!" “What do you say?” I said: "If you create your own karma, you will suffer it yourself. In the past, that person created that karma; in this life, he will encounter hardship. The rich person enjoys it because he created [merit karma] in the past. That is called equality. Equality in the aspect of creating karma."

equal okay! What kind of equality is that? I said: "Currently, everything is unequal." That person said: "What kind of inequality?" I said: "I'm locked up. You're outside, so free. What kind of equality is that? Inequality, how can it be equal!" “You broke the law!” I replied: "I broke the law. Who decided that law?" Equality, when Buddhism talks about equality, it means according to Ly, the Dharmakaya is equal, all are equal. No mistake! They are all equal, but you have not yet practiced the Dharmakaya, but the Buddhas have! The Great Bodhisattva has practiced, but has not yet been able to become a Buddha. He must be like me, unable to do it [due to not having enough strength]! That is your wish. You hope to level things evenly: You fall into hell, but you're still afraid that no one else will go to hell! Impossible! There are resentful people, they are very miserable, so they resent others. When they see others rich, they become jealous. We often see sentient beings resenting anything, we can visualize it from Reason. How can these resentments be said to be equal? Regarding sentient beings of the three levels: lower, middle, and upper, "no difference in mind, no difference in thought, strong diligence. All sentient beings in the three realms are necessarily equal and incomparable" (no difference in mind, no difference in thoughts, no difference in diligence.
