Because all sentient beings in the three worlds are equal, not two). According to Ly, it is to eliminate afflictions and suffering for sentient beings. When Bodhisattvas develop Bodhi mind, they are equal towards living beings and eliminate their afflictions. Such diligence is great diligence. No asrava, no attachment, inherently no asrava. The Dharmakaya has never had asrava, nor has hell!

When teaching the Ksitigarbha Sutra, I often tell people "there is no hell", but people don't believe it! There is a Dharma friend who often tells me: "I am constantly thinking. In this whole life I have not practiced anything. In the future, I am afraid that I will fall into hell. Do you have any method to help me?" "I have no method! You will definitely fall into hell." That person complained: "The teacher said the same thing!" I replied: - Yes! You always think like that. I never said that. You don't think about anything else all day long, you only think about falling into hell. Even if Buddhas appear in this world, there's no way to save you! The Buddha wants you to think about Buddha Dharma, but you don't think about it, just think about hell. Buddhist scriptures talk about a lot of issues, you don't think about it, why do you think about hell? Why do you think about hungry ghosts? Or think about the three diagrams? In front of the three disciples, you should say that you have no part, then you will have no part in the three disciples! Whatever you think in your mind, you will move towards it. Why do we always think about the Pure Land? Thinking about the world of Ultimate Bliss, without two thoughts, I have made up my mind, don't doubt it. When I die, I will definitely be reborn in the Pure Land. You will be born there.

“Language, thinking, the base of the actions, have no prior base” (For language, thinking, and the reliance of the actions, do not be attached): Regardless of everything you have done, all the thoughts in your mind, all the things you have done through your body, speech, and mind, do not be tied. bound, not liberated, but also not attached. Freedom from bondage is liberation, liberation is freedom from bondage. Not being attached means not being attached to either side. Don't be attached to either side, this principle is very deep, and there is nothing that is diligent, nor is there anything that is not diligent! What is diligence? What is not diligent? Actually, according to Ly, both sides are impossible, but currently we cannot say that! Because right now we're entertaining. Laziness is the opposite of diligence. Diligence is also the opposite of laziness. Courageous diligence, fulfilling all three meritorious karmas in the world is courage and diligence, called the Bodhisattva Wheel of Great Effort. The "Three Blessed Karmas" are Blessings, Sins, and Inactivity.

(Sutra) Good man! If the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat is diligently diligent in the Great Armor and Pillars, he must develop his mind at the beginning and must completely eliminate the five desires, attain the title of Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, and surpass all the Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones. The universal position of Sravakas, Single Enlightened Ones, great merit fields, Sravakas, and Single Enlightened Vehicles of the same level makes offerings, ministers, and guardians.
(Sutra: Dear good man! If Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves Great Effort in the Wheel of Effort This, from the beginning of the mind, all five desires can be eliminated, called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones. Because throughout all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Vehicles should make offerings to, minister to, and protect.
.

Good man! If Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves the Great Armor Pillar of Effort, from the beginning, all five desires can be eliminated. As soon as you develop your mind, you eliminate the five desires. That is the great Bodhisattva. Bodhisattva Mahasattva is a sentient being with great enlightenment like that. Therefore, his diligence far surpasses that of Thanh Van and Doc Giac, and can create a huge field of blessings for all Thanh Van and Soc Giac. All Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas should be close to him, make offerings to him, take care of him, and learn from him how to practice this great wheel of diligence?

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One revealed the meaning, and recited and wrote: - The six bases of infection before, pfoolishly and diligently, the wise are destroyed. The destiny of sentient beings is to be diligent, to possess effluents, to possess attachments, not to be a true field of blessing, not to be known as Mahasattva. A wise person needs to be diligent, separate from all things first, have a mind with no attachments, and a true name filled with blessings. Untainted by name and form, separate from the Aggregates, Precepts, and Bases, they take refuge. The title of Ma Ha Tat. Practice like water and moon, practice diligently to save the day. Testing the eternal cycle of energy, sentient beings are afflicted with afflictions.
immersed in the six senses, drifting foolishly through the five falls, even though they are diligent and diligent, wise people are discouraged. Because of their diligence and attachments, the field of blessings is not real, and they are not called Mahasattvas. A wise person who is diligent and free from all attachments, with a mind without attachment, is a true field of blessings, free from the Aggregates, Worlds, and Realms. All sentient beings take refuge, and are called Mahasattvas. Slap. Wandering in the world, like the shadow of the moon in the water. Cultivate diligently, this cycle is forever broken, afflictions bind living beings.

“Five streams” (five streams) i.e. eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, [plus] mind, forming six senses imbued with the senses of Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, and Dharma. That is drifting in the five desires, drifting in birth and death, it can also be said drifting in the six paths. Even though you are brave and diligent, you still cannot attain fruition, you cannot reach the end. “Fake wisdom is destructive” (Wise people are fed up and criticize): Wise people will not do that. “The fate of sentient beings to be diligent, to have anasrava and to have grasping, is not a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), not named Ma Ha Tat” (The fate of living beings to be diligent, to have anasrava and to hold on to it, is not a true field of blessings, not called a Mahasattva): If one holds on, there is renunciation, that is, an asrava is, one cannot reach anasrava. That type of person cannot make a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for sentient beings, even less can he make a Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra) for Bodhisattva, Pacceka [and Sravaka], so he is not called a great Bodhisattva. “The wise person needs to be diligent, free from all attachments, the mind has no reference, the name is a true field of blessings” (The wise person is diligent, far from all attachments, the mind does not point anywhere, then it is called the true field of blessings): In the mind, it does not rely on all appearances, does not hold on to anything, does not cling to all dharmas. In my mind, I don't point to anything, what does it point to? What is y pointing without y pointing? That is Dharmakaya. Dharmakaya is without support.

“Untainted by name and form, separated from the Aggregates, Precepts, and Realms, the one they take refuge in is called Ma Ha Tat” (Untainted by name and form, separate from the Aggregates, Precepts, Grounds, etc. As a place of refuge for the masses, he is called Ma Ha Tat): Absent from all dharmas, not accepts all dharmas, then accepts immeasurable meanings, that is, maintains immeasurable meanings, becomes a refuge for sentient beings, a place where sentient beings turn to rely on, and is also a great Bodhisattva who helps them escape the ocean of suffering. "Practice the world like the water and moon, cultivate diligently to save the end, test the wheel of energy forever, afflicting sentient beings" (Walk in the world like the moon in the water, practice with utmost diligence. This wheel can permanently cut off the afflictions and bonds of sentient beings): Bodhisattvas do all things in the world, like the moon silhouetted in water, empty, non-existent. All dharmas are like illusions, dreams, bubbles, and shadows. Practicing diligently like that, that Bodhisattva is truly diligent, will forever end the cycle of birth and death, and eliminate the afflictions that bind living beings.

(Sutra) Second recovery, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat restores the Tinh Lu Great Giap Abiding Wheel. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat accomplished testing the wheel, developed the initial mind, must eliminate the five desires at all stages, overcome all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment to create a great field of blessings. It is necessary for Thanh Van and Single Enlightened Vehicle to make offerings, take care of things, and protect them. Van Ha Tinh Lu Dai Giap Tru Luan? Good man! Bodhisattva Tinh Lu possesses two types of appearances: Nthe one, the world; the two, the world time. Van Ha Bodhisattva in the world of Tinh Lu? The Bodhisattvas practice Tinh Su before the Aggregates, practice before the Precepts practice Tinh Su, practice before the Dhyanas practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Desire Realms practice Tinh Su, practice before the Formless Realms practice Tinh Su, practice before the Three Laws and Practice Tinh Su, practice before the Three Liberations practice Tinh Su, practice before the Four Pillars of Mindfulness, practice before the Four Right Paramitas practice Jing Lu, practice before the Four Divine Succulents practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Five Roots practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Five Forces practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Seven Levels of Enlightenment practice practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Eight Noble Paths practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Earth Realm practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Water Realm practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Fire Realm practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Air Realm practice Tinh Lu, practice before the Space Realm practice Tinh Lu, practice Before the Realm of Consciousness, practice the Static Lu, before the Blissful Feeling, practice the Static Lu, before the Suffering, practice the Static Lu, before the Realm of Non-Suffering, Neither Pleasure, practice the Static Lu, before the Boundless Emptiness, practice the Static Lu, before the Boundless Consciousness, practice the Static Lu, before the Land of Nothingness, practice the Static Lu, before the Realm of Non-Perception, Non-Perception, practice the Static Lu, before the test of existence, practice the Static Lu, Before others practice Tinh Lu, with small thoughts practice Tinh Lu, with great thoughts practice Tinh Lu, before immeasurable thoughts practice Tinh Lu. Like Thi Tinh Lu, possessing gonorrhea, possessing hands, possessing the robes first, named Bodhisattva of the world Tinh Lu. Such as Thi Tinh Lu, together with Thanh Van and Single Enlightened Vehicles, try not to be famous as the Great Armor Pillar, but don't try to be famous as Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, mentioned necessarily Thanh Van, True Single Enlightenment Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra).
(Sutra: Come here, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Sattva also has the Great Self-Enlightenment Wheel. If the Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves this wheel, from the beginning, all five desires can be eliminated, surpassing all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Ones, because all the Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Ones should make offerings to, inherit, and protect the Bodhisattva's Static Power two types of appearances, one is worldly, the other is beyond the world. What is the Bodhisattva's worldly Tranquility? That is, Bodhisattvas rely on the Aggregates to practice Tranquility, rely on the Precepts to practice Tranquility, rely on the Sense Realms to practice Tranquility, rely on the Formless Realm to practice Tranquility, rely on the Three Laws to practice Tranquility, rely on rely on the Three Liberations to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Four Pillars of Mindfulness to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Four Right Paradigms to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Four Divine Sustains to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Five Senses to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Five Strengths to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Seven Enlightened Factors to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Eight Noble Paths to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Earth to practice Tinh Lu, rely on enter the Water world to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Fire world to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Wind world to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Space world to practice Tinh Lu, rely on the Consciousness world to practice Tinh Lu, rely on Blissful Feeling to practice Tinh Lu, rely on Suffering to practice Tinh Lu, rely on No Suffering, Never Pleasure to practice Tinh Lu, rely on Boundless Emptiness to practice Tinh Lu, rely on Consciousness The Boundless Place to practice Tinh Lu, relying on the Land of Nothingness to practice Tinh Lu, relying on the Place of Non-Perception, Non-Perception to practice Tinh Lu, relying on this life to practice Tinh Lu, relying on other lives to practice Tinh Lu, relying on small thoughts to practice Tinh Lu, relying on great thoughts to practice Tinh Lu, relying on immeasurable thoughts to practice Tinh Lu is the Bodhisattva's worldly Tranquility. Such Tranquility is in common with the Shravakas and Single-Enlightened Vehicles. It is not called the Great Wheel of Armor, nor is it called Bodhisattva-Mahasattva because of these things, nor is it called the true field of blessings of all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

“Serve the good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat restores the Static Lu Great Armor Pillar” (Come on, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat has the Static Lu Great Armor Pillar): That is Concentration. Tinh Lu is cultivating thinking, also samadhi. “Samādhi” (Samādhi) is translated as Tinh Lu, also translated as Concentration, and also translated as Thinking Practice. If Bodhisattva Mahasattva accomplishes this cycle, he will be able to eliminate the five desires as soon as he awakens his mind. "Superior to all Sravakas, Single-Enlightened Ones, universally superior to all Sravakas, Single-Enlightened Ones, creating great fields of merit" (Far beyond all Sravakas, Single-Enlightened Ones, because throughout all Sravakas, Single-Enlightened Ones are great fields of merit): All Sravakas, Single-Enlightened Ones should make offerings to, serve and protect Him. Here it is repeated.

“Van Ha Tinh Lu Great Giap Abiding Wheel? Good man! Bodhisattva Tinh Lu has two types of appearances: One, worldly, two beyond the world. Van Ha Bodhisattva of the world, Tinh Lu?” (What is the Great Armored Wheel of Static Lu? Good man! The Bodhisattva's Jing Lu has two types of appearances: One is worldly, the other is beyond the world. What is the Bodhisattva's worldly Jing Lu?) Bodhisattvas rely on the Aggregates to practice Tinh Lu, rely on Form to practice Tinh Lu, rely on Feeling to practice Tinh Lu. Tinh Lu means quiet observation. We give an example, depending on Form, Form Is Samadhi, Mind Is Samadhi, Nhat Hanh Samadhi. As for Form, all visible things have form. So Tinh Lu is thinking. In the previous section, we said: All dharmas are impermanent, contemplate all dharmas as selfless and empty! This Tinh Lu Mon is the Tinh Lu of Nhi Thua. You attain Concentration in the human world, the Nine Concentrations, based on this world to practice Concentration, you must practice first [the worldly Concentration subjects]. Just like we said about the method of contemplation of So Tic, you can rely on it, that is also Tinh Lu. The Quan Thuc Quan still belongs to the Tinh Lu of the world. That is the first step of worldly Tranquility, which can make your mind calm. First of all, be quiet and then start contemplation. Relying on Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness to reflect a little, you will be able to be calm. Contemplation is Hue, it can be calm and still. That is Dinh.

As we are in the Desire Realm of the three worlds, relying on the Desire Realm, relying on the Form Realm, or relying on the Formless Realm. Rely on the Three Laws of Doubt to practice Tranquility, rely on the Three Liberations to practice Tranquility, rely on the Four Pillars of Mindfulness to practice Tranquility, rely on the Four Right Paradigms to practice Tranquility, rely on the Four Spiritual Supplies to practice Tranquility, rely on the Five Roots to practice Tranquility, rely on the Five Strengths to practice Tranquility, rely on the Seven Factors of Enlightenment and the Noble Eightfold Path to practice Tranquility.

“In front of the Earth world practice Tinh Lu, in front of the Water world practice Tinh Lu, in front of Fire world practice Tinh Lu, in front of the Wind world practice Tinh Lu, in front of the Air world practice Tinh Lu” (Relying on the Earth world to practice Tinh Lu, relying on the Water world to practice Tinh Lu, relying on the Fire realm to practice Tinh Lu, relying on the Wind realm to practice Tinh Lu, relying on the Space realm to practice Tinh Lu): This needs to be said a little. “Emptiness” is inherently nothing, how can it be reciting Tinh Lu! When people meditate, rely on Emptiness to practice which method of Stillness? “No” is a display of dharma, a visual way of speaking. Only by relying on Emptiness can one abide in all dharmas. Because of Emptiness, we can build houses. Because of Emptiness, the Nam Thiem Bo Chau can be contained. Nam Thiem Bo Chau is in the air. Below Nam Thiem Bo Chau is a water wheel. People probably think there is a water wheel underneath the ground, but that's not true. The entire earth is in the air, the water wheel is also in the air. In the past, Buddhist scriptures said that, but some people were skeptical and didn't believe it. Now the satellite has risen into the sky. Seen from satellite, the earth is always blue. Outside the earth is the water wheel. The water wheel surrounds the earth. At first, when we heard that principle, we [wondered] If the earth is in water, why doesn't it sink? Under the water there is still wind, the wind maintains that cycle. The entire world sea of ​​Hua Tang has a great wind wheel underneath to maintain it. There are twenty types of air wheels, each air wheel maintains an air wheel [above it, each air wheel] has a name [detailed in the World Flower Store chapter of the Avatamsaka Sutra]. It must be Buddha's wisdom to be able to know, but our wisdom cannot! I'll talk a little about Tinh Lu in general.

If you know it's No, why are you still pursuing it? You are calm, needless to say, compatible with Truth. Using that Emptiness, you can reach the Land of Boundless Emptiness. When you practice Mind-Only Contemplation, you attain the Land of Boundless Consciousness and the Land of Boundless Emptiness. Rely on these dharmas to practice, rely on Consciousness to practice Boundless Consciousness, rely on Pleasure to practice Tranquility, rely on Suffering to practice Tranquility. You think all suffering is impermanent, what is the nature of suffering? No! If you often think like that, the effect will be there, but you don't think often. Suffering really comes, if you temporarily meditate a little, of course you can reduce some of the pain. You practice Contemplation, use Emptiness or Non-Self, you say, who will be attached to pain? Or it's okay if you think about one side in your mind. By shifting the goal, you can greatly reduce your suffering. Or if the time is too long, to practice that suffering, we must rely on the practice of Contemplation. These ways of practicing Tinh Lu are all worldly Meditation. That is a small thought, not a big thought. That is called “relying on small thoughts to practice Tinh Lu”. Relying on great thoughts, relying on immeasurable thoughts, will not be easy! Practicing stillness, if considered according to worldly dharma, great thoughts are the same, but small thoughts are also the same, with a base (something to rely on), a previous base (something to cling to), and an attachment to appearances, then it is all called Worldly Concentration. Relying on worldly Meditation to practice, what is formlessness? What is the world? Cultivating True Emptiness Absolute General Contemplation, establishing all generals. Practicing Emptiness Contemplation, cultivating False Contemplation, all dharmas are false, all dharmas are Emptiness, that is ultimate emptiness. Although it belongs to the Bodhisattva status, it is not ultimate. You must practice Middle Way, Middle Way is the most ultimate.

The Avatamsaka Sutra explains Madhyamaka differently. “Contemplation of absolute emptiness”, “Contemplation of unhindered reason”, “Contemplation of unobstructed events” As I just said, Emptiness and Being are two sides combined, Emptiness is Reason, Being is Reality. The two sides of Reason and Truth combine to form one Body. Reason is Truth, Truth is Reason. Facts and Reason combine, that teaching is called Chung Giao. In the Middle Way, the Truth is the Truth, the Reason is the Truth, the Reason is unhindered, called the Unobstructed Contemplation of Reason. But in the end, there is Chau Nhan Ham Dung Quan, which means arbitrarily taking one dharma, no dharma is not a dharma realm. It is already the dharma realm, immeasurable and boundless in all dharmas, all belonging to the dharma realm. Each dharma is a dharma realm, which is called “endless overlap”. The Avatamsaka Sutra established the Three Contemplations like that. The Four Teachings establish three Contemplation disciplines: Emptiness, Falsehood, and Middle Way, while the Three Luan Sects[47] only establish one Madhyamaka school. Different sects say things differently, but the things to raise contemplation are the same. When practicing Tinh Lu, relying on the written word, relying on this order, that is called “Zen enlightenment”. That is True Form Zen, not the deep-clothed Formless Zen of Zen Buddhism. Master Than Tu in the North follows the physical form and diligently progresses step by step. Master Huineng in the South taught the Zen of Formlessness, called Absolute Emptiness, without attachment or attachment. Both types can be cultivated gradually.

For such a kind of great education, when you want to study, if you want to fully explain all the famous signs, we can't explain it clearly every day! You have to work hard and study at the same time. If you study the Four Meditations and Eight Concentrations for a long time, wait until we finish talking and start teaching again from the Book of Insights. Now that we are starting to practice, [the Dharmas of Tinh Lu just mentioned above] are not the dharmas we should practice! The Quan Tuc Quan book is simple and clear. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches us the book of contemplation, according to which to practice, you can also enter into it. Counting numbers but don't even know? Counting numbers is not counting one, two, three, four, five, six, but counting your breath: The appearance of exhalation, the appearance of inhalation. From coarse to subtle. Once dead, there is no more breath; Already Just, already Determined! It seemed like there was no breathing, the breathing stopped, there was no exhaling, nor inhaling. That's called Dinh. If you use your finger [place it under the nose of someone who has entered Samadhi] to check, [you will see that the person] is not breathing out. Take that person away and bury him alive. If you do that, he won't even know if he has entered Samadhi. It is said: If that person does not breathe out, there is absolutely no breath. If no one touches it, even for a great kalpa, that person will not die. When that person has entered Samadhi, his body will not be damaged. This is unthinkable. If you use fire to burn it, of course that person's body will be damaged. If thrown into the sea, it will definitely swell with water. That's talking about cultivating Concentration. These Concentration subjects are not of Bodhisattva Mahasattva. The Concentration subjects mentioned above are all [Concentration subjects] in common with the Second Vehicle.

(Sutra) Van Ha Bodhisattva appeared in the world of Tranquility Lu? The Bodhisattvas are far removed from the Aggregates to practice the Stillness, far from the Precepts to practice the Stillness, far away from the Places to practice the Stillness, far away from the Desire World to practice the Stillness, far away from the Form Realm to practice the Stillness, far away from the Formless Realm to practice the Stillness, far away from the Three Laws and Practices to practice the Stillness, far away from the Three Liberations to practice the Stillness, far away from the Four Pillars of Mindfulness to practice the Stillness, far away from the Four Noble Truths practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Four Divine Sustains practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Five Senses practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Five Powers practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Seven Levels of Enlightenment practice practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Noble Eightfold Path to practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Earth world practice Tinh Lu, far away from the Water world practice Tinh Lu, far away from the world of Fire practice Tinh Lu, far away from the world of Wind practice Tinh Lu, far away from the world of Space to practice Tinh Lu, far away far away from the world of consciousness to practice stillness, far away from the realm of pleasure to practice quietness, far away from suffering from pain to practice peace of mind, far away from the realm of neither suffering nor pleasure to practice stillness, far away from the realm of boundless emptiness to practice peace of mind, far away from the realm of boundless consciousness to practice peace of mind, far away from the world of non-existence to practice peace of mind, far away from the realm of neither perception nor non-perception to practice peace of mind, far away from the world to practice peace of mind, far away Far from others practice Tinh Lu, far from small thoughts practice Tinh Lu, far away from great thoughts practice Tinh Lu, far away from immeasurable thoughts practice Tinh Lu. Like Thi Tinh Lu, who is able to develop sages and saints with great light, without outflows, without grasping, and without precepts. Tnamed Bodhisattva in the world of Tinh Lu, the Great Armor of the Wheel. Good man! The Bodhisattva Mahasattva became a Static Lu Great Armored Wheel, developed his mind at the beginning, had to eliminate the five desires at the stage, attained the name of Wild Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, transcended all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment created a great field of blessings, necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment of the 1st level to make offerings, take care of, and protect.
The Aggregates practice the Static Lu, separate from the Precepts practice the Static Lu, separate from the Bases practice the Static Lu, separate from the Desire Realm practice the Static Lu, separate from the Form Realm practice the Static Lu, separate from the Formless Realms practice the Static Lu, separate from the Three Laws and Practices practice the Static Lu, separate from the Three Liberations practice the Static Lu, separate from the Four Pillars of Mindfulness practice the Static Lu, separate from the Four Right Paradigms practice the Static Lu Lu, away from the Four Noble Truths practice Tinh Lu, away from the Five Senses practice Tinh Lu, away from the Five Powers practice Tinh Lu, away from the Seven Levels of Enlightenment practice practice Tinh Lu, away from the Eight Noble Paths practice Tinh Lu, away from the Earth realm practice Tinh Lu, away from the Water world practice Tinh Lu, away from the Fire world practice Tinh Lu, away from the Air world practice Tinh Lu, away from the Space world practice Tinh Lu practice Tinh Lu, away from the Consciousness world practice Tinh Lu, away from Pleasure Feeling practice Tinh Lu, away from Suffering Feeling practice Tinh Lu, away from Non-Suffering, Non-Pleasure practice practice Tinh Lu, away from Boundless Emptiness practice Tinh Lu, away from Boundless Consciousness practice Tinh Lu, away from Non-Existence practice Tinh Lu, away from Non-Perception, Non-Perception practice Tinh Lu, staying away from this life, practicing Tinh Lu, staying away from other lives, practicing Tinh Lu, staying away from small thoughts, practicing Tinh Lu, staying away from countless thoughts, practicing Tinh Lu. Such a great light of sainthood, no attachment, no reliance is called Tinh Lu, the great wheel of Bodhisattva Ha Tat who achieves this Great Armored Wheel of Static Power, from the beginning of his mind, all the five desires can be eliminated. He is called the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, far superior to all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Vehicles, because throughout all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Vehicles, they work great fields of merit, all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Vehicles should make offerings, serve, and protect).

We talk about practicing Tranquility with Mind-Only Consciousness, without looking at the text. All written words are separate from the form of written words. Even if you look at the text, you won't be able to grasp it. Why? You must leave all appearances and all dharmas to practice Thought. That is Khong Quan. At first, the Empty Contemplation of the Mahayana and the Second Vehicle had differences. The Second Vehicle also achieved Emptiness and entered Nirvana in tranquility. They also attained Nirvana, which is also immortal and immortal. They think that it is Emptiness, but cannot save sentient beings. From Emptiness, Existence cannot emerge, from Emptiness enter the Unreal, from the Emptiness enter Emptiness. They do not understand this principle; Therefore, [Second Vehicle Meditation] is called worldly Meditation. The Second Vehicle of the world relies on the world to practice. The Great Bodhisattva does not rely on the world to practice, but relies on the path of “the ability to emit the vast light of sages and saints” (can radiate the vast light of sages). Everything that has thoughts, appearances, and attachments is not the realm of a Bodhisattva. The Great Bodhisattva who practices the Great Giap Abiding Wheel of Tinh Lu and emerges from the world, is still not cultivating the Void Contemplation world. Emptiness is the ultimate form of emptiness. The Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma is also said by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. [In that sutra], Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teaches the practice of Contemplation, one is Mind-Only Consciousness Contemplation, two is Contemplation of Truth as it really is, entering the Realm of Real Generals. On one side is Quan and Mat; On the one hand, there is Concentration and on the other hand, there is Only. [Or in other words] Xa Ma Tha (Śamatha, Contemplation) and Vai Ba Xa Na (Vipaśyanā, Contemplation). Bodhisattva practices Vaibhava Monastery. Contemplation and Hue are two aspects that combine to practice. Only Concentration, without Hue, belongs to Thanh Van. The Second Vehicle must be applied together by Samadhi and Contemplation. If one can achieve this Great Armor Pillar, from the moment one first develops the mind, the five desires can be eliminated. Thus, it is called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat.

(Sutra) At the time of the ear, the World-Honored One clearly shows the meaning, and recites and recites: - The renunciation is important, cultivating possession Concentrate, seek to cut off afflictions, not true wisdom and false appearance. Contemplation of the spirit of possession, seeking liberation and cultivating Concentration, first trying the shore, does not benefit sentient beings. For the benefit of sentient beings, cultivating concentration and equanimity is important, eliminating all afflictions, revealing true wisdom and false appearance. By relaxing all sentient beings, cultivating non-attachment before Concentration, forever cutting off all sentient beings' love, becoming a great wisdom person. The person who resolves all misfortunes, attains the spirit of fearlessness, practices Tathagata Samadhi, and is known as Mahasattva.
(Sutra: At that time, the World-Honored One displayed this meaning again, then recited verses: - Because Letting go of burdens, cultivating Concentration to gain possession, praying for oneself to eliminate afflictions, not the form of true wisdom. Relying on the world to contemplate, praying for liberation, cultivating Concentration, clinging to the characteristics of both sides, not benefiting sentient beings, cultivating Concentration, letting go of all afflictions, is the form of true wisdom, cultivating Concentration without clinging to love, is called a great wisdom person. called Ma Ha Tat).

What kind of burden is that? Discharge yourself! Just because you can escape, you are in the Second Vehicle. The Concentrations mentioned earlier are all practices of the Second Vehicle. Bodhisattva is the opposite! In the above passage, it is absolutely not said that the Bodhisattva specializes in cultivating any dharma. His dedicated practice is completely contrary to the Second Vehicle, which is the practice of a Bodhisattva. Bodhisattvas practicing Emptiness Contemplation are non-emptiness. Where is real not shown? We must save sentient beings, so that all sentient beings can understand clearly that "this world is suffering", even "this world is neither suffering nor pleasure". Hang Nhi Thua, or Tieu Thua, is completely different! Because, in order to let go of their own burden, they feel that the burden is too heavy and wish to get rid of it, so they practice to attain Concentration, what is it? Da Nirvana is quiet. That is the tranquil Nirvana of the Second Vehicle. Forever get rid of your own afflictions, get rid of Kien Tu Or. That is not a wise person, not the characteristic of a truly wise person! Wise people do not practice like that. "Relying on the worldly energy to have the object of contemplation, seeking liberation and cultivating Concentration, clinging to this shore and that shore, does not benefit sentient beings" (Relying on the worldly energy to have the object of contemplation, seeking liberation but cultivating Concentration, accepting this shore and the other shore, does not benefit sentient beings): That is also not the practice of a Mahayana Bodhisattva.

That method of contemplation is not true wisdom, so what does it rely on? He refers to worldly enlightenment. That method of contemplation is true contemplation, to practice Concentration for the sake of liberation. That is to say according to the Second Vehicle: "I want to be free from afflictions, so I practice Concentration like that." There is no wisdom, no benefit to sentient beings. Wisdom is not great because it clings to this shore and that shore. We come from this shore, want to reach the other shore. Isn't the Six Paramitas reaching the other shore? That's a figurative way of speaking, using [the other shore] as an example. There is neither this shore nor the other shore! If you wish for liberation, then practice Concentration, grasp, and accept "I am at the edge of birth and death, I want to reach Nirvana". That is not the benefit of sentient beings, nor is it Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat.

“For the benefit of sentient beings, practice Concentration, let go with great courage” (For the benefit of sentient beings, practice Concentration to remove the burden): I am for the benefit of sentient beings, so that all sentient beings can achieve benefits. Practicing like that means cultivating Concentration to relieve the burden on sentient beings. Cultivation of Concentration aims to eliminate all afflictions of sentient beings. That is the characteristic of a truly wise person. A great Bodhisattva, Ma Ha Tat, for the benefit of sentient beings, practices Non-Imitation Before Concentration, forever cutting off the love in all realms (love), then he is called a person of great wisdom. It's not just for yourself, it's the same for cultivating Concentration, even cultivating a few movements, it's the same for all the Diligence. This Dharma is about not relying on anything, not being attached to anything. Regarding the method of cultivating Concentration, it is absolutely not the case that "you can cultivate Concentration by sitting, but you cannot cultivate Concentration by standing". “Na Gia is always in Concentration” (Buddha is always in Concentration). Walking, standing, sitting, lying down, in the four postures, you can practice Concentration. When sitting and cultivating Concentration, there are two types of obstacles: One is distraction. Whenever I'm quiet, old stories from eighty years ago come to mind. Their silhouettes appear, their endless thoughts make them unable to sit still, causing them to get angry. Angry with whom? Get angry with yourself. At that time, [kept thinking, if only] I shouldn't have done that, until now I was at a loss. You regret. Whenever chaos occurs, [after clearing up chaos], once you have achieved concentration, you will fall into drowsiness again. Sometimes, Dinh falls asleep for an hour or two. When you wake up, you still don't know, you see that a while has passed!

We meditate quietly in the Zen Hall. Within a large incense stick (in the time it takes to burn one incense stick), there are people who are very determined, while others are extremely disturbed in their hearts. The more [that person] looks around, the more they can't stand it! That incense stick is so rough, so long, it burns for at least two and a half hours. You look at the incense burner: "The incense is still intact, not burned at all!" It really doesn't decrease. Some people simply don't look at it, just ignore it, then enter Concentration, [in fact], they fall asleep! Two or three hours passed, waiting to hear the tapping (reminding the crowd to give up Zen), that person woke up, [the Zen session] had passed, and did not know what to do. There are times when our meditation practice goes well and our feet don't hurt. However, sitting in Zen well is [actually] the worst, because the person sleeps for two or three hours straight. You see that person's appearance as if he is entering Samadhi, in fact, he is soundly sleeping. This must be achieved through practice. Looking from the outside, it won't be obvious. That person was sleeping, feeling very comfortable. The peace of mind when entering Samadhi and sleeping is the same. Achieving peace, you don't think about anything, you really let go of everything, stay in that peace. That's not opening up wisdom, you need to be diligent and courageous.

If for the sake of increasing living beings, cultivating this method of Concentration, without relying on, without attachment, forever eliminating the loves in Beings of the three worlds, not for oneself, but for the benefit of sentient beings, allowing sentient beings to enter Concentration without relying on, without attachments, we can forever cut off all attachments (bondage due to love). That is a person with wisdom, "one who liberates all blessings, lives in a fearless city, practices Tathagata, and is known as Mahasattva" (because he removes the bonds of the Bodhisattvas in the three worlds, makes [sentient beings] stay in the citadel without fear, but cultivates the discipline of Tranquility and tranquility, then [that person] is called Ma Ha Tat). Because it causes all sentient beings to be freed from all hindrances and bondages, and live in the citadel without fear, that is, the citadel of no birth and no death. Practicing Zhi, cultivating Concentration like that, means Pure Dharma Concentration. That is the great Bodhisattva. If everyone reads books about Meditation, they will know these things. Now we only recognize nouns. That is not the Dharma we will practice. Wait until we have finished teaching [this sutra, everyone] skillfully practice the Dharma of the Book of Contemplation as mentioned by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and at the same time skillfully recite the Buddha's name. People who truly recite Buddha's name and practice the Book of Contemplation will be exactly the same as cultivating Stillness.

(Kinh) Phục thứ, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phục hữu Bát Nhã Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu thử luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Vân hà Bát Nhã Đại Giáp Trụ Luân? Thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Bát Nhã hữu nhị chủng tướng: Nhất giả, thế gian; nhị giả, xuất thế gian. Vân hà Bồ Tát thế gian Bát Nhã? Vị chư Bồ Tát duy y độc, tụng, thư tả, thính văn, vị tha diễn thuyết tam thừa chánh pháp, dục cầu trừ diệt nhất thiết chúng sanh vô minh hắc ám, dục cầu phát khởi nhất thiết chúng sanh đại huệ quang minh, vị ư Như Lai sở thuyết chủng chủng dữ Thanh Văn Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, tinh cần độc tụng, thính văn, thư tả, vị tha diễn thuyết, khuyến chánh tu hành. Hoặc ư Như Lai sở thuyết chủng chủng dữ Độc Giác Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, tinh cần độc tụng, thính văn, thư tả, vị tha diễn thuyết, khuyến chánh tu hành. Hoặc ư Như Lai sở thuyết chủng chủng dữ Vô Thượng Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, tinh cần độc tụng, thính văn, thư tả, vị tha diễn thuyết, khuyến chánh tu hành. Bất cầu hiền thánh vô lậu đạo chi, bất cầu thánh đạo, bất cầu thánh đạo sở nhiếp giải thoát, bất hành tịch tĩnh chân thật Bát Nhã, thường hành hữu kiến, hữu tướng Bát Nhã. Như thị Bát Nhã, hữu thủ, hữu trước, thị danh Bồ Tát thế gian Bát Nhã. Như thị Bát Nhã, cộng chư Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng, thử bất danh vi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, diệc bất do thử danh vi Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát dã, cập danh nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác chân thật phước điền. Vân hà Bồ Tát xuất thế Bát Nhã? Vị chư Bồ Tát tinh cần tu tập Bồ Đề đạo thời, tùy lực độc tụng, thính văn, thư tả, vị tha diễn thuyết tam thừa chánh pháp, nhi ư kỳ trung, y vô sở đắc phương tiện nhi trụ, vô sở hành động, vô sở tư duy, vô hữu căn bản, dĩ như hư không tâm, phổ tịch diệt tâm, vô tăng giảm huệ, vô thủ trước tâm, vô sanh diệt tâm, vô thoái chuyển tâm, pháp bình đẳng tâm, Chân Như tâm, thật tế tâm, pháp giới tâm, vô ngã tâm, vô phân biệt tâm, tịch diệt an nhẫn ly phân biệt tâm, thiện xảo an trụ vô thành hoại địa, thiện xảo an trụ vô trụ vô trước thắng diệu huệ địa. Như thị Bát Nhã, vô thủ, vô trước, thị danh Bồ Tát xuất thế Bát Nhã Đại Giáp Trụ Luân.
(Kinh: Lại này, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát lại có Bát Nhã Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu luân này, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước to lớn. Hết thảy hàng Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Thế nào là Đại Giáp Trụ Luân của Bát Nhã? Này thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Bát Nhã có hai loại tướng: Một là thế gian, hai là xuất thế gian. Thế nào là Bát Nhã thế gian của Bồ Tát? Tức là các Bồ Tát chỉ nương vào đọc, tụng, biên chép, lắng nghe, vì người khác diễn thuyết chánh pháp tam thừa, muốn cầu trừ diệt vô minh hắc ám cho hết thảy chúng sanh, muốn cầu phát khởi quang minh đại huệ cho hết thảy chúng sanh, tức là đối với các thứ chánh pháp tương ứng với Thanh Văn Thừa do đức Như Lai đã nói, bèn siêng ròng đọc tụng, lắng nghe, biên chép, vì người khác diễn nói, khuyên họ tu hành chánh đáng. Hoặc là đối với các thứ chánh pháp tương ứng với Độc Giác Thừa do đức Như Lai đã nói, bèn siêng ròng đọc tụng, lắng nghe, biên chép, vì người khác diễn nói, khuyên họ tu hành chánh đáng. Hoặc là đối với các thứ chánh pháp tương ứng với Vô Thượng Thừa do đức Như Lai đã nói, bèn siêng ròng đọc tụng, lắng nghe, biên chép, vì người khác diễn nói, khuyên họ tu hành chánh đáng. Chẳng cầu vô lậu đạo chi của hiền thánh, chẳng cầu thánh đạo, chẳng cầu sự giải thoát được nhiếp thọ bởi thánh đạo, chẳng hành Bát Nhã chân thật tịch tĩnh, thường hành Bát Nhã có kiến, có tướng. Bát Nhã như thế nếu chấp giữ là có, thì gọi là Bát Nhã thế gian của Bồ Tát. Bát Nhã như thế cùng chung với các Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa. Đó chẳng gọi là Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, cũng chẳng do đó mà gọi là Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, cũng chẳng gọi là ruộng phước chân thật của hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Thế nào là Bát Nhã xuất thế của Bồ Tát? Chính là khi các Bồ Tát siêng ròng tu tập Bồ Đề đạo, tùy sức mà đọc tụng, lắng nghe, biên chép, vì người khác diễn thuyết tam thừa chánh pháp, nhưng ở trong ấy, bèn trụ vào phương tiện “không có gì để đạt được”, không có hành động, chẳng có tư duy, chẳng có căn bản, dùng cái tâm như hư không, cái tâm tịch diệt trọn khắp, cái tâm trí huệ chẳng tăng giảm, không chấp giữ, tâm chẳng sanh diệt, tâm chẳng thoái chuyển, tâm pháp bình đẳng, tâm Chân Như, tâm thật tế, tâm pháp giới, tâm vô ngã, tâm chẳng phân biệt, tâm tịch diệt an nhẫn lìa phân biệt, tâm thiện xảo an trụ địa vị chẳng thành hoại, thiện xảo an trụ địa vị trí huệ mầu nhiệm thù thắng vô trụ, không chấp trước. Bát Nhã như thế chẳng giữ lấy, chẳng chấp trước, gọi là Bát Nhã Đại Giáp Trụ Luân xuất thế của Bồ Tát).

Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu trí huệ Bát Nhã Đại Giáp Trụ Luân này, từ khi Ngài mới phát tâm, đã có thể đoạn tuyệt ngũ dục. Đấy là nói bậc Thập Trụ Bồ Tát phát tâm, hoàn toàn chẳng phải là nói về Sơ Tín. Như chúng ta cũng phát tâm, nhưng chẳng thể đoạn ngũ dục. Hàng Sơ Trụ Bồ Tát trong địa vị Thập Trụ vừa phát Bồ Đề tâm, ngũ dục đều đoạn trừ, họ có thể nhanh chóng đoạn dứt. Lại còn vừa phát tâm, đã vượt xa Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vượt xa A La Hán, hơn hẳn hàng Nhị Thừa. Do vậy, Ngài có thể làm ruộng phước to lớn cho hết thảy Thanh Văn và Độc Giác. Vì thế, hết thảy Thanh Văn và Độc Giác Thừa đều phải nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thân cận, thủ hộ Ngài. Đấy là điều tương thông, văn tự giống như trong các đoạn trước.

What is the Prajnaparamita Pillar? Bodhisattva's Prajna wisdom has

two types of appearances: One is worldly, the other is beyond the world, that is, one is worldly Prajna, the other is worldly Prajna. The world of Prajna is in common with Thanh Van and Doc Giac, the world of Prajna is not in common with Thanh Van and Doc Giac. After the Bodhisattva achieves this wheel, what will he rely on when preaching the Dharma to all sentient beings? Bodhisattvas will read, chant, write down, and listen. When Bodhisattvas practiced in past lives, they also relied on reading, reciting, writing, and listening. Listening is Van Tu, that is, after listening, then thinking, thinking and then being able to practice. Reading, reciting and writing notes is a way of practicing spiritual practice, different from sitting still and meditating. One way is to enter from form, enter gradually. On the one hand, it is from the Body that one enters and attains sudden enlightenment. We know that Master Hui Neng did not read or recite, nor did he write down notes. He was also illiterate, [yet] he suddenly attained enlightenment. Our constitution is not like His. If he had that kind of capacity, and were to tell him the dharma of the Second Vehicle of the Sravakas, telling him to read, recite, and listen, it would be wrong! In the previous section, we said “do not make mistakes regarding the three vehicles”, if you do so (preaching the Dharma without the right foundation) it will be a mistake. If for people with “progressive” (gradual progress) faculties, we only talk about the dharma of sudden enlightenment and [teach them] to study the clear mind and realize the nature, then at this time, for that kind of faculties, it will not be appropriate.

Why did the Bodhisattva do that? He practices for the sake of living beings. Reading, reciting, copying, and listening are all aimed at expounding the Dharma of the three vehicles. Here, add the word Right, [implying that what they did was] aimed at eliminating the darkness of ignorance of sentient beings. The ignorance and afflictions of sentient beings must rely on this method to rescue, and we must hope to eliminate the darkness in the minds of sentient beings. Only by relying on the dharma can we eliminate darkness, not by relying on lamplight, sunlight, or moonlight [to eliminate darkness]. These types of light (lamplight, or sun and moon light) cannot eliminate their darkness. They can eliminate darkness in phenomena. If they want to eliminate the darkness in their psychology, they must study the Dharma, practice the Dharma, causing them to give birth to their own inherent light and great wisdom. For this reason, Bodhisattvas must meditate on the body. Contemplating the foundation means considering what kind of faculty [the subject being preached] has in order to tell that person the appropriate dharma belonging to that vehicle.

Next, [the main sutra lists] various dharmas. If the Dharma corresponds to the Shravaka Vehicle, then speak to people of the Sravaka Vehicle, make them listen to the Dharma and study it diligently, “listen, write and describe” (listen, write down), and advise them to practice. After [the subject] has heard the Dharma, he will advise them to practice. “Speak altruistically, encourage righteous practice” (Speak for others, advise righteous practice), do not practice following an evil destinies. Our purpose of listening to the Dharma is to fear that our practice is not righteous. If it's not true kung fu and if you use it wrongly, [for example] learning Qigong can easily lead to a dead end. If you are guided in a bad way, because your practice is not good, it will lead to many diseases. Therefore, regarding this dharma, the correct dharma must also be said like that; Then you have to be diligent, don't relax. “Need” (diligent) is not lazy! In terms of the meaning of reciting, reciting is reading according to the scriptures, reciting is reciting by heart. Reading scriptures mostly depends on reading the scriptures. A set of Lotus Sutras, considering our intelligence, cannot memorize it. We cannot memorize the Avatamsaka Sutra; Even we cannot memorize the Maha Prajna Sutra! Part of it, like the Heart Sutra, we can memorize. If you know it by heart, [you can read it without the scriptures], then it is Chanting. Reading according to the scriptures, or copying them yourself, you can do this, but advising others to practice properly is not possible!

Practicing contemplation is not effective, as Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) teaches you to practice, opening up our Prajna wisdom. That wisdom gives birth to great wisdom and light, only then can you see "The Five Aggregates are Emptiness". If not, how can we see that the Five Aggregates are all Emptiness? Are we still grinding on the five desires? Not understanding the fifty types of Skandhas, you are basically in the demon world, still thinking you know how to practice very well, you are wrong! Why must we regularly read the scriptures? Use scriptures to compare. Sutras are like the surface of a mirror. We have dark spots on our faces, we can't see them ourselves, you will know as soon as you look in the mirror. Therefore, advise them to practice properly. If you feel that your practice is not correct, compare it with the scriptures and see what the Buddha taught? Let's compare! According to the Dharma taught by the Tathagata, if one has the basis of the Sravaka Vehicle, speak the A Ham Sutra, or explain the Cau Xa to that person, that is, the correct Dharma corresponds to the Sravaka. If he is a Pratyekabuddha, tell him the dharma of cause and effect, the twelve causes and conditions. The thirty-seven teachings, i.e. the Four Right Efforts, the Four Fulfilling Minds, the Five Faculties, the Five Powers, the Seven Factors of Enlightenment, and the Eightfold Path, are common to all three vehicles. You can [explain] deeply, but you can also explain shallowly. Thus, Thanh Van, Doc Giac, “listen to hear, write, speak altruistically, encourage righteous practice” (listen, write down, perform for others, advise them to practice righteously).

“Or does the Tathagata preach that the evil species of the Supreme Vehicle corresponds to the true dharma” (Or for the Dharma corresponding to the Supreme Vehicle as said by the Tathagata): If you meet sentient beings seeking the Supreme Vehicle, then advise them to practice properly, saying the true dharma corresponds to the Supreme Vehicle, such as the Prajnaparamita Sutra, the Flower Sutra. Serenity, Lotus Sutra, clear mind to see nature. Especially the Lotus Sutra, which enlightens them to enter Buddha's knowledge and tells them Buddha's knowledge. The Second Vehicle cannot be trusted! Let's immediately take the friends in the present to say, I have met a few people, they do not object. You preach the Lotus Sutra, and they also listen to it a little. You preach the Avatamsaka Sutra, they also listen. This is sowing good roots! They do not have the basis of the Second Vehicle, they cannot attain sainthood, they just sow good roots, but they can hear the name of the sutra, can listen, it is all because they have planted good roots from countless eons until now! Otherwise, they won't be able to listen, they will sit down and then get up and leave!

When I preached the Avatamsaka Sutra at Nanputuo Temple in Xiamen, preaching for more than half a year, some people listened a little and then left, unable to listen from beginning to end. Students can't, they can't even listen, because they are students at the Buddhist Academy and must listen to lectures. They are not that foundation; If it is not that root, then it is considered sowing good roots. In their future lives, they will gradually achieve that foundation, that is, sowing the cause. But being able to sow this cause is because there is enough cause and condition. Like this passage says, if we want to truly attain true Prajna, that is, we are now teaching the second half of the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, teaching about true Prajna, then what we have just said is only the appearance of Prajna. Prajna Prajna with the Existing Form is completely different from the Prajnaless Form Prajna. The Form of Existence is “existence of existence, existence first” (there is holding on to it, there is attachment to it), while No Form has no existence.

They diligently read and recite the Mahayana, listened, and wrote down notes like that, which means that their "correct practice" (rightful practice) is not the same as the practice in the previous sections, and do not seek the outflow-free wisdom of the Second Vehicle. “Not seeking the holy path” refers to the [holy path] of the Two Vehicles. Without seeking, without attaining, without seeking the liberation mentioned in the holy path [Second Vehicle], without practicing the true practice of Nirvana. On the contrary, for true tranquility and Prajna, they do not practice, so the things they practice are all Prajna with visible forms. For that type of Prajna, some take it, some give it up, that is having an attachment to appearances. Practicing like that means that Prajna is not true Prajna, that is, it does not practice true Prajna. “Practice” is seeing, the dharma practiced is Prajna. That Prajna has taking and letting go; That is not the true ultimate Prajna of the Bodhisattva. What is that? It is the Bodhisattva's world of Prajna. Therefore, regarding the distinctions and discriminations in the essential dharma of the three vehicles, doesn't the Buddha say no difference and equality? That is equality, [corresponding to] the dharma they should receive. How much they can accept, you will tell them. They cannot accept what you [teach] beyond their ability, [they will not accept it at all]. That is inequality!

This has the same meaning as the eating example I mentioned in the previous section. We assign that person to eat three bowls. People can eat five bowls, but it will not be enough. People can only eat one bowl, forcing them to eat three bowls, they can't stand it! That's inequality! What kind of foundation is that person, what dharma can he hear, what dharma can he write down? You act for him, advise him to practice properly, not to make mistakes. Someone who is not of very deep energy, does not wish to become a Buddha, does not wish to reach ultimate enlightenment, you cannot teach a very deep dharma to that person! That person can listen to the Dharma, can also listen, can also write down, but that person's purpose is different. Their practice of liberation is also different, their practice always depends on physical form, conditioned things, and attachments!

Like the Bodhisattva precepts and the bhikkhu precepts, the bhikkhu precepts and the novice precepts, the novice precepts and the eight precepts, the eight precepts and the five precepts, are all different. Because that person's mind is only that big. That is the form of Prajna. That Prajnaparamita can still take it, give it up, accept "this is impure karma, I can't do it". That is called “attachment”. Bodhisattvas are without prior (no attachment), are truly equal. Speaking of Thanh Van and Pratyekabuddha's attachments, it is not that they are attached to the five worldly desires, but what attachments are they? They are attached to the dharma. [For them], if the Self no longer exists, it means one has succeeded in cultivating. Ego Clinging has been cut off, but Dharma Clinging is still not cut off. Although that person has wisdom, it is only half of it, which is called the Bodhisattva's world of Prajna. Bodhisattvas must fulfill two types of Prajna. This type of Prajna (worldly Prajna) is in common with Shravaka and Single Enlightenment. They also rely on this type of Prajna to study and attain it in the same way. Although the Bodhisattva also relied on that Dharma to learn, after learning it, he benefited sentient beings, not for himself to enjoy, but for others to enjoy. This type of Prajna cannot be called “The Wheel of Great Armor”, because it does not have the power of that wheel, it cannot be called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, it cannot be considered a great Bodhisattva, it cannot be called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, nor can it be a field of true blessings for Shravakas and Bodhisattvas

Slap. That is the Bodhisattva's world of Prajna.

Prajna has two types of appearances: One is the world, the other is beyond the world. Out of the Bodhisattva Prajna world, “Bodhisattvas diligently practice the Bodhi path” (that is, when Bodhisattvas diligently practice the Bodhi path), raises a different premise: He practices the Bodhi path, while cultivating the cause, has relied on the Bodhi path to practice, and in the real world attains Bodhi. “Depending on the power of poison, chanting, hearing, writing and writing” (Depending on the strength of reading, listening, writing), depending on the strength of that person, that is, depending on the strength of wisdom. If you have great wisdom, you will be able to study that dharma. After you have finished studying, you can immediately benefit sentient beings and demonstrate the three vehicles of the Dharma to sentient beings.

“In the middle period, he possesses no means of abiding, no actions, no thoughts, no fundamental existence, like the mind is empty, universal cessation of the mind, no increase or decrease in wisdom, no grasping before the mind, no birth and destruction of the mind, no turning back of the mind, dharma of equality of mind, True Such mind, Truly Subtle mind, dharma world mind, no self mind, no distinction of mind, cessation of mind with patience, separation of mind" (But in there, depending on means, nothing can be achieved to abide, there is no action, no thinking, no basis, using a mind like space, the mind is completely extinguished, wisdom does not increase or decrease, the mind does not grasp, the mind does not arise or die, the mind does not regress, the mind is equal, the mind is likeness, the mind is True, the mind is real, the mind is dharma, the mind is not self, the mind does not differentiate, the mind is extinguished with patience. separation). There are twelve consciousnesses in total. Bodhisattva attains the Basic Wisdom, depending on the Basic Wisdom, the Later Knowledge arises. Bodhisattvas must have skillful means, from the Basic Wisdom, the Second Vehicle only attains half, they do not have skillful means, because they cannot save sentient beings, [so] they do not give birth to skillful means.

What is skillful means? Bodhisattva saves sentient beings but does not see the sentient beings' forms. Sentient beings should use whatever ability they need to attain salvation, so they manifest that ability. To those living beings who should give alms a little money or a little Dharma, the Bodhisattva should give alms to that person a little money or Dharma. Therefore, it is not possible for that person to maintain the precepts, for him to receive the precepts, for him to practice Great Forbearance, Prajna, and Prajna. That person cannot do it, because he does not have such great strength. Even though we do everything, we don't have any attachments, "nothing to do" means "no attachments". Saving sentient beings without seeing the appearance of sentient beings, nor does it indicate that "I myself can save sentient beings", nor do I have sentient beings to be saved, without attachment. That is called “three wheels of emptiness”.

The following minds are all intended to visualize the realm of saving birth: What mind do you use. On the contrary, it would be to rely on the wisdom of Truth and Prajna. We "do nothing", which means we also do not save sentient beings. All sentient beings are "thoughtless" (have nothing to think about), that is the meaning of Emptiness, attaining nirvana, that is the meaning of Emptiness. Are all our thoughts non-existent? Our thoughts are all illusory, not real! The Bodhisattva's true thinking is not thinking, but it is not without thinking. The meaning in Mahayana is like that. Saying "has no basis" means saying that the person has nothing to rely on, no attachment to anything. That's basically it. Think about it, when the Buddhas attained enlightenment, they absolutely did not say to rely on the Dharmakaya to practice all the actions to achieve the Sambhogakaya, to rely on the Sambhogakaya to achieve the Transformation Body. Absolutely don't say that! He is manifest wisdom. Why? His mind is like nothingness, of no use. What effect does nothingness have? Nothingness has no effect.

“Universal cessation of mind”: Makes all sentient beings able to achieve tranquility, without disturbance! For Hue, mortals do not decrease, holy places do not increase. Prajna Wisdom does not decrease in mortals, [because, every sentient being] is inherently full of Prajna wisdom, fully equipped with the Dharmakaya and virtues of the Buddhas. Once you have attained sainthood and ultimately become a Buddha, you cannot increase your monkhood. Fellow monks! When we teach the Heart Sutra, you all know that “no increase, no decrease” is because mortals do not decrease, holy places do not increase. This kind of wisdom mind does not hold back, is not attached to, and is not attached to all dharmas. That person not only has no attachment to the Self, but also has no attachment to all dharmas. That is to have reached an inconceivably mysterious realm, a wonderful land of wisdom. Contemplate that all dharmas are non-born and non-destructive. We contemplate that all dharmas have birth, death, increase, and decrease, so we cannot enter. When we help others, we cannot help completely, we can only sow good roots, we cannot solve the problem, we cannot make that person get rid of their afflictions, and we cannot make that person attain Bodhi. Because the Bodhisattva's mind is like space, there is no eternal decline. This is referring to the Bodhisattva of the Dang Ground Bodhisattva, the great Bodhisattva who has attained Prajnaparamita and will never regress. The Eight Grounds, that is, the Immovable Ground, will not regress.

“The Dharma is equal in mind”: All dharmas are equal, immaculate, impure, without increase, without decrease, without birth, without death. That is the dharma of mind equality! That mind is real, the True Mind. We say Truly Subtle Ground, that noun is intended to describe the Dharmakaya, but “truly subtle mind”, “dharma realm mind”, “egoless mind”, with respect to egoless mind, there is one more distinction: The Second Vehicle also achieves egolessness, but it is Small Egolessness. Selflessness also means that there are no scenes that belong to us. The mind can transform all scenes, the mind can transform all dharmas. All dharmas are selfless, have no discriminating mind, are not tainted, pure, big, small, long, short, square, or round. Quietly extinguished, calm and unmoved, neither coming nor going, so there is no discriminating mind. “Skillful abiding in a state without becoming or ruin” (Skillful abiding in a state that neither becomes nor perishes): Very skillful expedients with equal success and destruction. “Equality” as just mentioned means that in terms of achievement and destruction, that person sees both things as equal.

As long as there is that kind of distinction, when it comes to something that has been achieved, there will be no way to destroy it. That is having a discriminatory mind, not being able to see equality! If we see equality, is there any need to destroy it? Equality is not destructive. All dharmas are established, it is said "In the world, all dharma positions, the appearance of the world permanently abides", that is, each dharma will be in its proper place, that appearance will permanently abide. All dharmas do not destroy their original position, that is the permanent worldly appearance. The meaning of “permanent” is not at all the meaning of flowers blooming forever. “Permanently abiding” here means continuing without end, continuously and permanently abiding! Therefore, the Vajra Sutra says "no appearance of self, no appearance of human beings, no appearance of living beings, no appearance of life", "life of existence" is continuous without ceasing, life span is continuous without end, it is not at all that we will live for ten thousand billion years, that is not the meaning. We from one life to the next forever circulate in the three worlds without stopping. That's what it means. “The skillful abiding in the sublime wisdom position without abiding in it” (Abiding in the sublime, mysterious position of wisdom, without abiding, without attachment), that is true Prajna. What shape does Bat Nha have? “Without beginning, without prior. Tname the worldly Bodhisattva Prajnaparamita Prajnaparamita Wheel” (Not holding on to, not being attached to. That is called the Bodhisattva Prajnaparamita Prajnaparamita Wheel emerging into the world). If the Bodhisattva had accomplished this wheel, from the moment he first developed his mind, this wheel would have been able to destroy everything. Every passage of scripture says the same. The ten armored pillars are all like that.

(Sutra) Good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva became a Prajna Great Armored Wheel, developed the mind at the beginning, had to eliminate all five desires at the stage, attained the name Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, surpassed all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment to create a great Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra). Excess equality giai consent

to offer, to serve, to protect.

(Sutra: Good man! If Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves Prajnaparamita This Wheel, from the beginning of the mind, all five desires can be eliminated, called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, far surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, because throughout all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones should make offerings to, serve, and protect.

As soon as he develops his mind, he can eliminate the five desires. Or, “all five desires can be eliminated at all stages” (all five desires can be eliminated), that is a great Bodhisattva, called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat. As soon as the Great Bodhisattva awakens his mind, he immediately "surpasses all Sravakas and Single Enlightenment" (far surpasses all Sravakas and Single Enlightenment). This story must be said in a moral way for you to understand! Because he has perfected the mind of the Ten Faiths, what realm is the mind of the Ten Faiths? It is the wish of the heart, that is, the wish to save all sentient beings to become Buddhas. He not only made that vow, but also acted on it. Therefore, he developed Bodhi mind and saved all sentient beings. According to the Avatamsaka Sutra, the mind of the Ten Faiths is very profound. Ordinary people develop their mind, the most basic thought is that every thought never retreats, every thought never leaves the Three Jewels. Realizing that the previous thought is evil, immediately stop it and eliminate the next thought, not allowing it to arise. That is Faith. Bodhisattva believers, who truly develop faith, can we observe whether we are like that or not? If so, then it belongs to the Faith position. One mind, two minds, three minds, four minds, four wisdom minds, if you have a wish, have a mind to protect the dharma, reach the Seventh Faith and protect the dharma. What is dharma protector? If someone slanders the Three Jewels, we can sacrifice our own lives to protect the Three Jewels. Hearing the defamation of the Three Jewels, we use our own bodies and lives to protect the Dharma and Buddha. Can we do that or not? That is the Seventh Faith. Eighth is Dedication of the Mind, dedication to all sentient beings. Whatever we do, we dedicate it to sentient beings. Like that until reaching the Development of Mind Pillar, that is, participating in the position of First Pillar; Having perfected the ten faiths, he participated in the Development of the Mind Abode. As soon as you develop your mind, you can develop your great mind. You can work as a field of blessings for all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Ones. You can also be a refuge for all Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Ones, advising them to develop Mahayana minds. That is the Prajnaparamita Bodhisattva.

(Kinh) Phục thứ, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phục hữu Thiện Xảo Phương Tiện Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu thử luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền, nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Vân hà danh vi Thiện Xảo Phương Tiện Đại Giáp Trụ Luân? Thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát thiện xảo phương tiện, hữu nhị chủng tướng: Nhất giả, thế gian; nhị giả, xuất thế gian. Vân hà danh vi Bồ Tát thế gian thiện xảo phương tiện? Vị chư Bồ Tát hoặc vị tự lợi, hoặc vị tha lợi, hoặc vị câu lợi, thường hoài bỉ thử, thị hiện chủng chủng công xảo kỹ thuật, vị tự cập tha đắc thành thục cố, thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn, hoặc chư Bồ Tát, hoặc chư Độc Giác, hoặc chư Thanh Văn, hoặc mẫu, hoặc phụ, hoặc chư bệnh giả, hoặc chư luy liệt vô y hỗ giả. Nhược kiến ách nạn, lâm bị hại giả, chủng chủng cần khổ phương tiện cứu tế, dĩ Tứ Nhiếp Sự thành thục hữu tình. Thị chư Bồ Tát tự trụ Đại Thừa, ư chư Thanh Văn, cập Độc Giác Thừa, phi Đại Thừa khí, nhược chư Thanh Văn, cập Độc Giác Thừa, căn vị thục giả, vị thuyết vi diệu thậm thâm pháp giáo, linh kỳ tu học, hoặc khuyến cần tu chư thánh Tĩnh Lự, hoặc vị khai thị Tối Thắng Nghĩa Đế, khuyến linh tu hành, siêu Tứ Điên Đảo, giác ngộ tứ chủng vô đọa pháp tánh, hoặc linh thú nhập Tứ Vô Ngại Giải, hoặc phục nãi chí khuyến linh an trụ Tứ Niệm Trụ, Tứ Chánh Đoạn, Tứ Thần Túc, Ngũ Căn, Ngũ Lực, Thất Đẳng Giác Chi, Bát Thánh Đạo Chi, hữu dư, vô dư đạo, cập đạo quả, thú nhập xảo trí, linh kỳ thành thục. Nhược chư hữu tình tham cầu danh xưng, lợi dưỡng, phú quý, chư căn tháo nhiễu, thiện căn vị thục, khuyến linh độc tụng chư A Cấp Ma, cập Tỳ Nại Da, A Tỳ Đạt Ma. Hoặc khuyến độc tụng trừ Phật sở thuyết thuận giải thoát luận, linh kỳ thành thục. Nhược chư hữu tình bất nhạo bố thí, khuyến linh huệ xả chủng chủng trân tài, linh kỳ thành thục. Nhược chư hữu tình bạo ác bất nhân, khuyến linh tu học tứ chủng phạm trụ. Nhược chư hữu tình tâm đa phẫn khuể, khuyến linh tu nhẫn. Nhược chư hữu tình tâm đa giải đãi, khuyến tu tinh tấn. Nhược chư hữu tình tâm đa tán loạn, khuyến tu Tĩnh Lự. Nhược chư hữu tình cụ túc ác huệ, vị thuyết chánh pháp, vị dĩ ký thuyết, giáo giới, phương tiện, linh kỳ thành thục. Nhược chư hữu tình bất kính Tam Bảo, cụ Vô Y Hạnh, khuyến thọ Tam Quy, linh kính Tam Bảo, hoặc khuyến thọ học Cận Sự luật nghi, hoặc khuyến thọ học Cận Trụ luật nghi, linh kỳ thành thục. Hoặc khuyến tu tập chủng chủng công xảo kỹ thuật nghiệp xứ, linh kỳ thành thục. Như thị đẳng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát chủng chủng thế gian xảo phương tiện trí, quá Căng-già sa Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, dĩ thị nhất thiết thư luận, công xảo, kỹ thuật nghiệp xứ, gia hạnh, tinh tấn, xảo phương tiện trí, tồi phục nhất thiết ngoại đạo dị học. Như thị danh vi Bồ Tát thế gian thiện xảo phương tiện. Thử xảo phương tiện, cộng chư Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng, diệc tác nhất thiết Phật pháp y nhân, diệc thị thiện xảo chư hành y xứ, diệc thị thiện xảo nhậm vận vô tư, diệt thoái đọa pháp.
(Kinh: Lại này, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát lại có Thiện Xảo Phương Tiện Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu luân này, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, vượt hơn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước lớn. Hết thảy các Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Thế nào là Thiện Xảo Phương Tiện Đại Giáp Trụ Luân? Này thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát thiện xảo phương tiện có hai loại tướng: Một là thế gian, hai là xuất thế gian. Thế nào là thế gian thiện xảo phương tiện của Bồ Tát? Tức là các Bồ Tát hoặc vì tự lợi, hoặc vì lợi ích cho người khác, hoặc vì hai bên cùng có lợi, thường nghĩ đến đôi bên, thị hiện các thứ kỹ thuật hay khéo, vì để cho mình lẫn người được thành thục mà thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn, hoặc các vị Bồ Tát, hoặc các Độc Giác, hoặc các Thanh Văn, hoặc mẹ, hoặc cha, hoặc những người bệnh, hoặc những kẻ yếu đuối, không nơi nương cậy, Nếu thấy kẻ bị hại vì các thứ ách nạn, bèn siêng khổ dùng các phương tiện cứu giúp, dùng Tứ Nhiếp Sự để thành thục hữu tình. Các vị Bồ Tát ấy tự trụ Đại Thừa, đối với các Thanh Văn, và Độc Giác Thừa chẳng phải là căn khí Đại Thừa, nếu các Thanh Văn và Độc Giác Thừa căn cơ chưa chín muồi, sẽ vì họ nói pháp vi diệu rất sâu để dạy họ tu học. Hoặc khuyên siêng tu các thánh Tĩnh Lự, hoặc vì họ khai thị Tối Thắng Nghĩa Đế, khuyên họ tu hành vượt khỏi Tứ Điên Đảo, giác ngộ bốn loại vô đọa pháp tánh, hoặc dạy họ tiến nhập Tứ Vô Ngại Giải, hoặc lại còn cho đến khuyên họ an trụ trong Tứ Niệm Trụ, Tứ Chánh Đoạn, Tứ Thần Túc, Ngũ Căn, Ngũ Lực, Thất Đẳng Giác Chi, Bát Thánh Đạo Chi, đạo hữu dư, vô dư, và đạo quả, tiến nhập trí khéo, khiến cho họ thành thục. Nếu các hữu tình tham cầu tiếng tăm, lợi dưỡng, phú quý, các căn xáo động, nhiễu loạn, sẽ khuyên họ đọc tụng các kinh A Cấp Ma, Tỳ Nại Da, và A Tỳ Đạt Ma. Hoặc khuyên đọc tụng các bộ luận thuận theo giải thoát luận chẳng do đức Phật nói, khiến cho họ thành thục. Nếu các hữu tình chẳng thích bố thí, khuyên họ thí xả rộng rãi các thứ tài vật quý báu, khiến cho họ thành thục. Nếu các hữu tình bạo ác, bất nhân, khuyên họ tu học bốn thứ Phạm Trụ. Nếu các hữu tình tâm lắm sân khuể, khuyên họ tu nhẫn. Nếu các hữu tình tâm lắm giải đãi, khuyên tu tinh tấn. Nếu các hữu tình tâm lắm tán loạn, khuyên tu Tĩnh Lự. Nếu các hữu tình trọn đủ ác huệ, sẽ vì họ nói chánh pháp, tức là dùng phương tiện như ký thuyết (thuyết pháp đúng với căn cơ và ước nguyện của họ) và giáo giới (răn dạy) để thành thục họ. Nếu các hữu tình chẳng kính Tam Bảo, trọn đủ Vô Y Hạnh, bèn khuyên họ thọ Tam Quy, khiến cho họ kính trọng Tam Bảo, hoặc khuyên thọ học Cận Sự luật nghi, hoặc khuyên thọ học Cận Trụ luật nghi, khiến cho họ thành thục. Hoặc khuyên tu tập các thứ nghiệp xứ kỹ thuật hay khéo, khiến cho họ thành thục. Các thứ trí xảo phương tiện thế gian của các vị Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát nhiều hơn cát sông Hằng như thế, dùng hết thảy các thứ trí phương tiện nghiệp xứ, sách vở, luận thuyết, kỹ thuật hay khéo, gia hạnh, tinh tấn ấy để dẹp tan dị học của hết thảy ngoại đạo. Như thế thì gọi là phương tiện thiện xảo thế gian của Bồ Tát. Phương tiện hay khéo ấy chung với các Thanh Văn và Độc Giác Thừa, và cũng là cái nhân để hết thảy Phật pháp nương vào, và cũng là chỗ nương tựa của các hạnh thiện xảo, và cũng là pháp thiện xảo tùy ý không suy nghĩ, diệt trừ thoái đọa).

Chỉ có trí Bát Nhã thì chưa được, còn phải có thiện xảo phương tiện. Đấy là nói đến Ngũ Minh Bồ Tát. [Một loại trong] Ngũ Minh[48] của Bồ Tát là Công Xảo Minh; chẩn bệnh có phải là phạm giới hay không? Bồ Tát chẳng phải như vậy, Ngài có Y Phương Minh, có trí huệ, phương tiện thiện xảo, trí huệ không chấp trước, có minh, có đại trí huệ để làm các việc ấy. Khi thành tựu thiện xảo phương tiện luân, vừa phát tâm, ngũ dục đều bị đoạn trừ, sẽ vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, lại còn có thể làm ruộng phước lớn cho Thanh Văn và Độc Giác. Hai chữ “thị hiện” cho thấy chẳng phải là thật sự có, mà là thị hiện. Phương tiện thiện xảo cần đến kỹ thuật hay khéo. Sự hay khéo ấy là để thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn, hoặc cúng dường chư Phật, Bồ Tát, hoặc cúng dường Độc Giác, hoặc cúng dường Thanh Văn, hoặc cha mẹ của chính mình. “Hoặc chư bệnh giả, hoặc chư luy liệt, vô y hỗ giả. Nhược kiến ách nạn lâm bị hại giả, chủng chủng cần khổ, phương tiện cứu tế” (Hoặc là đối với người bệnh, hoặc kẻ suy yếu không nơi nương tựa. Nếu thấy người bị hại vì ách nạn, bèn dùng đủ mọi phương tiện để siêng khổ cứu giúp). Đấy là phương tiện thiện xảo. Do vậy, dùng Tứ Nhiếp Pháp để thành thục hữu tình, Bồ Tát hiện đủ loại thân. Thứ nhất là bố thí, bố thí đến mức độ nào? Phải là nội thí, ngoại thí, trong lẫn ngoài đều thí. Các thứ tiền tài bình thường đều chẳng tính! Ngay cả vợ con đều có thể bố thí, huống hồ nhà cửa, cho đến ruộng vườn, đều có thể bố thí. Đấy là “ngoại thí”. “Nội thí” là mắt, tai, mũi, lưỡi, thân, và ý của chính mình đều có thể bố thí, bố thí cho chúng sanh. Đó gọi là Bố Thí.

“Colleague”: Appears to do the same things as them, or they are civil servants, you are also civil servants. They work there, you also work there, so you can reach them. That is “the manifestation of Co-worker Photography”. Giving Alms and Collaborating to do things that benefit all sentient beings is called Beneficial Action. As for Ai Ngu, it means you cannot speak harshly or harshly towards anyone. Everyone you meet is greeted with Love. That's called the Four Methods of Photography. Only a great Bodhisattva must fully implement the Four Dharmas. Manjushri Bodhisattva, anything appears, goats, buffaloes, horses... all appear. Everyone who looks at the Green Inductions of the great Bodhisattvas, [will see] them manifesting [all kinds of] different living beings. That is the Bodhisattva.

“Self-abiding in the Mahayana”: This is not the case that whenever we see any sentient being, we accept that person to abide in the Mahayana. No way! We have Dharma friends who are determined to only propagate the Avatamsaka Sutra, not to speak of the Three Vehicles Dharma. They came to listen, it was the foundation that came to me, but I wasn't looking for the foundation. If living beings ask me, I will tell them. If you don't ask me, I won't say; Whether they understand or not is their business, it has nothing to do with me. Currently, our Dharma propagation situation is like that! But the situation of Bodhisattva preaching the Dharma is not like that. The Bodhisattva himself abides in the Mahayana.
