As for the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas [who] do not have the Mahayana temperament, it is impossible to tell them the profound and wonderful Dharma, or to teach them how to practice! For those who are not of Mahayana energy, their energy is not yet ripe, or their Sravakayana and Single Enlightenment energy is ripe, we can only tell them the dharma belonging to the Sravaka Vehicle or the Single Enlightenment Vehicle. But when the Mahayana energy is not yet ripe, when they have not yet entered the Mahayana, you tell that person a very profound and wonderful Dharma, and teaching that person to practice is wrong.

How does the Bodhisattva use skillful means? They are not of Mahayana temperament. If you want to convert them into Mahayana, you must guide them slowly, it is not possible to ripen them immediately! As for the base of the Single Enlightened Vehicle, or the base of the Shravaka Vehicle, [but actually the Mahayana energy] is not yet ripe, they [really] are not Sravakas, nor are they single-enlightened, you should slowly advise them, tell them the very profound and wonderful dharma, teach them to practice, or advise them to diligently practice the saints of Static Lu. All First Qua saints are considered saints. In the Hinayana, the First Fruit is considered a saint, while in the Mahayana, even the Four Fruits are not considered a saint. Make them practice Concentration, practice samadhi, up to the Nine Concentrations, because they reveal the Noble Truth of the Supreme Meaning, gradually revealing the Noble Truth of the Supreme Noble Truth. How many types of Tot Thang Nghia Emperor are there? The Four Noble Truths are considered the Supreme Noble Truths. Regarding worldly dharma, advise them to practice and overcome the four types of insanity.

The Four Crazy Islands: Permanence, Bliss, Self, Purity are the Four Virtues of Buddha; But sentient beings are crazy, considering impermanence as permanent, accepting non-self as self, accepting non-pleasure as happiness, accepting impurity as pure. Suffering, emptiness, impermanence like that! Those four things (impermanence, pleasurelessness, selflessness, impurity) make them crazy. We must advise them to overcome these four types of insanity, escape ordinary people, and reach the realm of saints.

how many types? There are four types of Bodhisattva's conduct, the first is to reach the other shore, to reach the other shore, to achieve divine conduct, to mature the conduct of sentient beings[49], that is, the four paths in the Bodhisattva's conduct, to achieve the benefit of sentient beings, making them enter the four non-falling natures.

In addition, there are the Four Limitless Solutions. The Four Unobstructed Solutions are unobstructed dharma, unobstructed meaning, unobstructed words, and unobstructed eloquence. A person who has unhindered eloquence means that he or she is knowledgeable about all dharmas. “Unobstructed” means there is nothing unknown. The Bodhisattva's skillful means towards worldly dharma are the same. Therefore, at first the Buddha said that shooting arrows, skillful professions, regardless of the types of Skillful Crafts in the world, all skillful professions [when the Buddha was still a Crown Prince, or when practicing Bodhisattva conduct] could be done, and they were far superior to living beings, they were all the best!

The Four Foundations of Mindfulness, the Four Right Efforts, the Four Divine Powers, the Five Faculties, the Five Strengths, the Seven Limbs, the Eightfold Path, we have talked a lot about these famous generals! “Residual, non-residual path result”: Residual, Non-residual are Residual Nirvana and Non-Residual Nirvana. “Education” is also very much. The first fruition is also the path and fruition, up to the path of Bodhisattva, the ultimate Buddhahood. But Bodhi used wisdom and skillful means to make them all mature. Whatever kind of capacity they have, they will mature that kind of fruit [of the capacity], gradually encouraging them, but there must be skillful means to receive sentient beings.

“If sentient beings desire fame, gain, wealth, wealth, their roots are free from interference, good roots are mature” (If sentient beings desire fame, gain, wealth, their roots are turbulent, disturbed, their good roots are not yet ripe): In the previous section, it talks about those whose good roots are ripe, but here are those who are good. The base is not yet ripe, it is also advised that they "singlely recite the Agamas" (read and recite the Agama sutras), that is, the Agama Sutra, "reciting Vinaya" is the Vinaya Pitaka, Abhidharma is the Abhidharma Pitaka, advise them to read and recite the Abhidharma Tripitaka. Or advise them to "single-recite the Buddha's doctrine of liberation, attain spiritual maturity", that means what do you advise them to recite? Worldly dharmas follow the theory of liberation spoken by the Buddha. In addition to what the Buddha taught, worldly dharmas, although not Buddhist, can still be learned by them, making them proficient in skillful professions.

Tho Tam Quy is taking refuge in the Dharma, not taking refuge in pagan books. So that Bodhisattva said, for things not said by the Buddha, we just need to follow the liberation theory of our [Buddhism], that theory has a meaning that does not contradict liberation, and can also achieve liberation [can be learned]. Just like there are many things in the world, for example, Taoism is also a practice that, socially speaking, does not cause problems for others. [Confucianism has an aphorism] "If you don't want anything, don't do it to others" (what you don't want yourself to do to others), is it any different from our Buddhist compassion? Don't impose things on others that you don't want. That's called "according to liberation", but it's not what the Buddha said. There are many stories like this, making them mature will be helpful for them to mature in cultivating the Way. This means advising them. They study Buddhism but cannot believe it, so they use worldly dharma to advise them. This Bodhisattva is not a monastic Bodhisattva, a monastic Bodhisattva cannot do that. “Bodhisattva” includes the four disciples, up to and including all sentient beings. Great Bodhisattvas appear in many ghost paths. In the eighth chapter of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, [it is said] The Demon King wished to become a Buddha, and the Buddha immediately gave him a prediction. He is a demon, going down that road. There are many cases of such manifestations.

For those who do not like giving alms, advise them to give alms. “Encourage the spirit to give alms” (Advise them to give alms generously, or advise them to give alms to create favors): You must be generous, you must give favors to sentient beings. This is different from the way the Buddha spoke. Buddhist disciples give alms without expecting anything in return. But when you tell people today to let go, they will have wishes. Do good things, advise them "doing good will bring you the most happiness". That is also the way to liberation. In this way, it will be possible to make them generous in giving alms of all kinds of gold, silver, and wealth, making them gradually mature. “If sentient beings are cruel and inhumane” (If sentient beings are cruel and inhumane): Those who are cruel and unmerciful, those who have no compassion at all, are like a king who carries out a brutal policy, completing all cruel and inhumane things. For such people, I advise them to study “four types of Brahma Pillars” (four types of Brahma Pillars). What are the Four Brahma Pillars? The Four Brahma Pillars refer to four types of pure conduct, which four types are they? Loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and renunciation are also the Four Immeasurable Minds. As long as we cultivate compassion, violence will not arise. Cultivate compassion to counteract violence.

“If sentient beings have a lot of anger and resentment in their minds” (If sentient beings have a lot of resentment and anger in their minds): People who easily get angry, advise them to practice patience. “If sentient beings are too lazy” (If sentient beings are too lazy), we must advise them to practice diligently. If we advise them like that, will they be diligent or not? Therefore, a great Bodhisattva must have skillful means. They don't speak bluntly like we do. Seeing the person entertaining him, he immediately said straight to his face: "You must be diligent, you must practice, recite Buddha's name a lot to benefit!" [If you say it like that], those people will ignore you and glare at you. You must have skillful means. Why is it necessary to be skillful? If you are not skillful, you will not be able to accept them. Currently, there are people who, seeing someone who has just believed in Buddha, advise that person to become a monk: "I accept you, only if you become a monk can you be diligent!" How? Those who have become monks are not very diligent! Having become a monk, that person thought he had achieved something, so he relaxed. In the previous section, we said: “You can wear the robe, the robe is blessed by the Buddha”. It's not that speaking personally, it's not that as we saw in the previous section, if you apply kasa you will immediately attain salvation. Qualified? Still in the same hell! People respect that robe, because the robe represents the Buddha, represents the Dharma, and represents the Sangha. You have misinterpreted it! Advise others to practice diligently and follow the right path. If you have skillful means and guide people, they will naturally be diligent. Waiting until the person's energy is ripe, he or she will become a monk and will be able to attain enlightenment.

Currently, you convert many people to become monks. Not only do they not attain enlightenment, but on the contrary, they miss the mark and commit crimes. Because after they became monks, they did not practice to become a monk, which is a sin! Originally pure and permanent, it suddenly became completely different! You must know your fundamentals. For those who are lazy, advising them to be diligent is right. If you are not diligent, what is wrong? You do half! If you don't concentrate on doing it, nothing will work out. What's more, practice Buddhism? Slowly advise that person like that. It's not just mere words that can move that person, you also have to take the lead and carry it out! Bodhisattva saves sentient beings, sentient beings also help him. If you take refuge with me, follow me and worship, everyone can relax once, not come and bow: "I'm very tired today, please rest for a day." Until now, I have not dared to ask for leave. Every day I don't bow, others don't bow either. If I don't bow for one day, if I don't bow for several days, everyone won't bow. It's like that in New York and Tam Phien (San Francisco), but I rarely don't bow. I establish that practice myself and must be diligent.

Sometimes our mind is very chaotic and chaotic, so we must practice Concentration. How is Tu Dinh? Wait until we finish teaching and we will talk about Soc Tic Quan. If you practice from the beginning, you will be able to enter. Don't look at me, [someone is probably wondering]: "Counting your breath in and out, what merit is there?" That merit can be very great, because when you attain Concentration, reciting Buddha's name in Concentration, it is inconceivable. Not scattered, not dull, not disturbed, you recite with one mind. Isn't it true that we wish to meditate to the point of being single-minded and undisturbed? It's not enough to recite a hundred thousand sentences, but if you recite a hundred thousand, a thousand ten thousand sentences, you won't be born in the Pure Land. How should you recite? Single-minded and undisturbed. For those who are scattered, you must advise them to practice Tinh Lu.

“If sentient beings are full of evil wisdom” (If sentient beings are full of evil wisdom): “Evil wisdom” is wrong knowledge, wrong views, that person always has disagreements with others, there is a gap. If someone else says East, that person must definitely say West, in disagreement with you. If you are a person with wrong knowledge and wrong views, how should you deal with it? "Speaking the Dharma", you must bring the teachings of the Buddha, the great wise men, and the great masters, and use means to guide that person and make him mature. “If sentient beings do not respect the Three Jewels” (If sentient beings do not respect the Three Jewels): In the previous section, we talked about Vo Y Hanh. Non-Year means being without reliance; A person who does not wear clothes is someone who disrespects the Three Jewels. We advise that person to receive the Three Refuges, to take refuge in the Three Jewels, to make him or her respect the Three Jewels, or to advise him or her to study the Near-Studying Discipline, which is the Five Precepts, or the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts, and to advise him or her to study the Near-Stand and Discipline, which is also the Eight Precepts. The Eight Precepts should have been nine precepts. We often think that the Eight Precepts have only eight precepts. According to Journey to the West, Pigsy followed Tang Monk to request sutras, which are the eight precepts. In fact, in addition to the eight precepts, there is also a Trai, which means "don't eat after noon". “Trai” means “term”. So [strictly speaking] it should be nine. Why is the Bat Quan called Quan (closed)? Closing evil destiniess. If you receive such a day, the Eight Precepts will close the evil destiniess.

I see a lot of people receiving the Eight Precepts, many of them are very strict, they don't drink it past noon. The water is colored and the Buddha decreed that you cannot drink it. Not only can't we drink cow's milk or soy milk, but even tea and fruit juice aren't water? Impossible! Can only drink water. But there is destiny in there. If we take the precepts, we must first learn to create conditions, we must always find the means. For example, if we cannot support ourselves and our body is weak, if we have received the precept "don't eat after noon", but if we get sick, we will immediately open the relationship, and after noon we can drink juices.

“Or recommend cultivating the skillful technical karma, making them mature” (Or recommend cultivating the skillful technical karma, making them mature): Jobs that require high technology, or construction, but all techniques can [be done]. That is called the world of Bodhisattva's Skill and Wisdom. Skillful Wisdom is the Bodhisattva's means of wisdom. There are as many Bodhisattvas with skillful means and wisdom in the world as the sands of the Ganges River. Great Bodhisattvas are able to perform and increase these karma with skillful writing, discourse, craft, and skill due to their skillful and expedient wisdom. What pagans know, we all know. Great Bodhisattvas not only know, but also surpass them so they can admire you. They know how to do something, you know how to do it. Whatever you can do is top notch and they will follow you. A great Bodhisattva must have that kind of wisdom and skillful means to be able to subdue all heretics. That is called the Bodhisattva's worldly skillful means.

This skillful means is in common with the Sravakas, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. Thanh Van and Single Sense Vehicle can all learn, can do, and can do the same. That is called making the cause of relying on all Buddha Dharma, relying on the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha to sow that cause. All skillful means are his place of practice, his place of reliance, and also the method of skillful, thoughtless discretion to eliminate degradation. This is not easy! The Dharma of not thinking, forever eliminating degeneration, the Dharma of not regressing is skillful means. “Rich fortune” (at will) is natural, seeing all dharmas arising and passing away. He can, from within all dharmas, lead back to the Essence of Dharma nature, from within birth and death, lead others back to no birth and death. Only by reaching "no birth and death" can one not regress. Things that are unacceptable [to worldly skill in means] will be mentioned below.

(Sutra) Good man! Bodhisattvas who do not rely on wise masters or good friends, practice the worldly skillful means, Bodhisattvas foolishly rely on the worldly skillful means, turn to evil beasts, are not able to abide in the world according to the wisdom of skillful means, and are not necessarily true in the Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), unable to skillfully perceive the differences in the actions of sentient beings. Because of the skillful means and stupid means, the Shravakas, attaining the Single Enlightened Vehicle, non-Mahayana energy, attaining the Mahayana-rooted practitioner, proclaim the Mahayana, spiritual practice. The Mahayana dharma practitioner has sentient beings, preaching the Thanh Van, the Single Enlightened Vehicle, the spiritual practice of the Thanh Van, the Single Enlightened Vehicle inheriting the conduct. The Single Enlightened One possesses the sentient dharma vehicle, teaches the Sravaka Vehicle, and practices the Sravaka Vehicle in a miraculous period of time. The Sravakayana teaches the sentient dharma, preaches the dharma of birth and death, the spirit of love first, and does not preach the dharma of birth and death. Huu Uu is skillful in foolish means, weakening sentient beings to mock and kill living beings. He preaches about the attachment to wrong views. He preaches the profound teachings of the Mahayana, without declaring the flow of life and death, death and rebirth, suffering and retribution for all beings. He hates the Buddha and abandons all evil dharmas. Huu Uu is skillful in means, foolish and weak, and makes sentient beings mock the practice of pure precepts and spiritual practice of almsgiving. All sentient beings ridicule the practice of peace and patience, encourage renunciation and peace of mind, and cultivate pure precepts. We discourage sentient beings from cultivating diligently, encouraging renunciation to be diligent, spiritually cultivating peace and patience. We encourage sentient beings to mock the practice of Tinh Lu, encourage them to renounce Tinh Lu, and practice spiritually diligently. All sentient beings mock the practice of Prajna, encourage renunciation of Prajna, and spiritual practice of Tinh Lu. Like a Bodhisattva, ignorant of the worldly skillful means, unable to truly benefit sentient beings, harming sentient beings through evil knowledge. Try the skillful means you possess, own the attachments, like the reputation of the worldly Bodhisattva skillful means. Just like in the world with skillful means, together with the Sravakas and Single-Enlightened Vehicles, try not to be named as the Great Armor Pillar, but without testing, be famous as the Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, mentioned necessarily Sravakas, the true Single-Enlightenment Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra).
(Sutra: Again, good man! If Bodhisattvas do not rely on masters, do not rely on good friends In order to practice worldly skillful means, those Bodhisattvas, due to their ignorance of worldly skillful means, tend towards evil destiniess, unable to abide in the wisdom of worldly skillful means, nor are they all true fields of blessings, unable to skillfully know the different faculties and actions of sentient beings. not yet ripe, but preach the Mahayana, causing them to practice. Again, because sentient beings belong to the Mahayana dharma, preach the dharma of the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, teach them to practice the practices of the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, because the sentient beings belonging to the dharma vehicle of the Single Enlightenment say the Sravaka Vehicle, cause them to practice the dharma of the Sravaka Vehicle, because the sentient beings belonging to the Sravaka Vehicle preach the dharma of birth and death, it is not because they preach the dharma of being bored with birth and death cunning, if sentient beings like to kill living beings, in general, even to the point of being attached to wrong views, then because they preach Mahayana very deeply, not because they preach the flow of birth and death, death here, birth there, suffering, causing them to be bored, afraid, and abandon evil deeds. Again, due to ignorance in skillful means, until if sentient beings like to practice pure precepts, then teach them to practice almsgiving, then advise them to give up peace If sentient beings like to practice diligence, teach them to practice patience. If sentient beings like to practice Patience, teach them to practice diligence. If sentient beings like to practice Prajna, then advise them to practice Prajna. Such Bodhisattvas are ignorant of worldly skillful means and cannot truly benefit sentient beings, and do evil to sentient beings That depends on what is achieved and attached to, then it is called the worldly skillful means of the Bodhisattva. Such worldly skillful means are shared with the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas; it is not called the Great Armored Wheel, nor is it called the Bodhisattva Mahasattva, nor is it called the true field of blessings of the Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas).

In skillful means, we can change the world's dharma depending on the world's dharma. You obey the world's dharma, but are turned around by the world's dharma. That is not a great Bodhisattva. For this wisdom of skillful means, you must be someone who truly understands. Being called “one who understands”, there is no Dharma that is not known in the Sutras, Laws, and Treatises, and no Dharma that is not understood. Truly knowledgeable, with regard to their ability, they will know how to accept and accept the teachings, then they can enter the Buddha way. This story is like the Bodhisattva first using desire to entice them, causing them to gradually enter the Buddhist path. Not only that, but you can also use the five desires to lure them. The world is greedy for wealth and greed for beauty, these two things are common diseases of all living beings. The Bodhisattva immediately appears to satisfy you, and shows the impermanence of birth and death. You have already been greedy, but if you don't have it anymore, you will immediately wake up [the world is impermanent]. It is in this way that the great Bodhisattva has this skillful means!

As everyone is very familiar with Zen master Dao Te (Te Dien). He was crazy and crazy, using wine to save lives, using madness to save lives. He pretended to be naive and foolish to save others. Why do people revere Him so? He knows the truth and can also solve all your difficulties. If you do not have wisdom and skillful means, you will not be able to solve the suffering of sentient beings. Your knowledge of skillful means is immediately reduced to stupidity! That is not wisdom, but ignorance of skillful means, not wisdom of skillful means. That is heading towards the evil destinies, not towards the good path, not being able to abide in the wisdom of skillful means beyond the world, not being able to follow the wisdom of skillful means! As mentioned in the previous section, you can talk about the dharma, but you must follow the Tathagata, so that you can be like the Tathagata has taught, and you can achieve liberation. If you go against those things, you will not be in accordance with the dharma nature and will not be able to achieve it! You cannot be a truly wise person, nor can you cultivate a true Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), nor can you have skillful means. You don't have that wisdom and don't know that living beings have different natures. You don't know all the different signs in their behavior. How will you save them? There is no way to save them! That is called “skillful means of stupidity” (foolishness in skillful means); that is, stupidity in ignorance! That is not the Mahayana energy, right

Even Thanh Van and Doc Giac cannot achieve it!

Because of ignorance regarding skillful means, regarding the fundamentals of the three vehicles, you preach the Dharma in a crazy way. People are of Sravaka nature, and you talk to them about worldly love affairs, without saying "know suffering and cessation", and without telling them the Dharma to stop birth and death. As for the basis of the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, he does not tell them the dharma of cause and effect, but instead arrogantly tells them the Mahayana dharma. As for the Mahayana energy, he told them the Dharma of Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha, the dharma of birth and death, Suffering, Origin, Cessation, and the Path. That's impossible! That's called being crazy, it's also called being ignorant of skillful means, which is not skillful means!

“If sentient beings mock the act of killing, spreading the word that they are attached to wrong views” (If sentient beings like to kill, in general, even to the point of clinging to wrong views): These are killing, stealing, prostitution, lying, drinking alcohol. If we talk about the Five Precepts, those sentient beings can understand; Those are the five worldly desires. In front of the five desires, you should tell them the dharma to end desires, the dharma to end birth and death, such as how the five desires harm people? How bad is it for you? Those dharmas are correct for their basic abilities, [but] you tell them the Mahayana dharma too deeply, and do not declare the dharma of the transition of birth and death to them! "Death here, birth there, retribution is suffering" (Death here, rebirth there, retributions are painful): You say these things, they [hearing] may get bored and scared. [Rather than saying] "the dharmas you rely on are all Emptiness" is exactly in line with their preferences. They say "inherently empty", they are more eager to violate and cling to the realm of the five desires. That is not the wisdom of skillful means, that is called ignorance of skillful means, not wisdom. Regarding those sentient beings who like to kill, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie, you must tell them that [because of these things] they will fall into hell, and must leave those evil things. That's only right. But you speak the Mahayana Dharma to them, saying "No meaning" without meaning, it's completely wrong!

Until in the Six Dharmas, ten thousand virtues, they naturally like to keep the precepts, but you say alms. They naturally like to practice patience, but you tell them to practice pure precepts. That is preaching the Dharma without the right foundation. If sentient beings like to practice diligently, advise them to let go of their diligence to cultivate patience. People are practicing very diligently. You advise them to let go and practice patience. That is “dharma when said is illegal, illegal when said is dharma!” If sentient beings like to practice Tranquility and wish to practice Concentration, [you arrogantly] advise them to let go of Concentration and tell them to practice diligently. If sentient beings like to practice Prajna, advise them to abandon Prajna and tell them to practice Tinh Lu. They want to cultivate wisdom, you force them to study Concentration, both ways fail. “Such a foolish Bodhisattva” means that the Bodhisattva is quite foolish, not a Bodhisattva, with regard to worldly skillful means, “unable to truly benefit sentient beings” (unable to truly benefit sentient beings). The Bodhisattva's skillful means aim to benefit sentient beings. As long as you are crazy like that, sentient beings will not gain benefits. That is not the good knowledge of sentient beings, but the evil knowledge of sentient beings. “Try skillful means based on possession, possess attachment” (That skillful means depends on possession, has attachment): [If you think] by relying on this skillful means, because of practicing this skillful means, you will be able to attain enlightenment, that is, you are attached to this skillful means. "Such is the Bodhisattva's skillful means in the world" (Such is called the Bodhisattva's skillful means in the world): Isn't that the skillful means beyond the world! Whenever there is gain, there is loss; have, there will be something that cannot be. That is a relative dharma. Therefore, it is a mistake, not to call it the Great Armor Pillar, "unable to test the name of Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat" (also not called Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat for that reason). That is not Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat.

(Kinh) “Vân hà danh vi Bồ Tát xuất thế thiện xảo phương tiện? Vị chư Bồ Tát đản vị lợi tha, bất vị tự lợi, thị hiện chủng chủng công xảo kỹ thuật, vị thành thục tha thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn, hoặc chư Bồ Tát, hoặc chư Độc Giác, hoặc chư Thanh Văn, hoặc mẫu, hoặc phụ, hoặc chư bệnh giả, hoặc chư luy liệt vô y hỗ giả. Nhược kiến ách nạn, lâm bị hại giả, chủng chủng cần khổ phương tiện cứu tế, dĩ Tứ Nhiếp Sự thành thục hữu tình, tùy kỳ ý nhạo, tùy kỳ căn khí, vị chư hữu tình tuyên thuyết chánh pháp. Hựu năng tiệm thứ khuyến chư Thanh Văn tu Độc Giác Thừa, khuyến chư Độc Giác tu tập Đại Thừa. Nhược ư Thanh Văn cập Độc Giác Thừa căn vị thục giả, vị thuyết yếm ly sanh tử khổ pháp, linh kỳ tu học, yếm ly sanh tử, hân cầu Niết Bàn. Nhược chư hữu tình nhạo hành sát sanh, quảng thuyết nãi chí nhạo trước tà kiến, tùy kỳ căn tánh, hoặc vị tuyên thuyết sanh tử lưu chuyển, tử thử, sanh bỉ, chúng khổ quả báo, linh kỳ yếm bố, ly chư ác pháp. Hoặc vị tuyên thuyết dữ Thanh Văn Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, hoặc vị tuyên thuyết dữ Độc Giác Thừa tương ứng chánh pháp, hoặc vị tuyên thuyết Vô Thượng Thừa trung thiển cận chi pháp, linh tiệm tu học. Nhược chư hữu tình dĩ nhạo bố thí, vị thuyết thắng thượng thọ trì tịnh giới, linh kỳ tu học, quảng thuyết nãi chí nhược chư hữu tình dĩ nhạo Tĩnh Lự, vị thuyết thắng thượng vô lậu thánh đạo sở nhiếp Bát Nhã linh kỳ tu học. Thử xảo phương tiện y vô sở đắc, vô sở chấp trước. Như thị danh vi Bồ Tát xuất thế Thiện Xảo Phương Tiện Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Thiện nam tử! Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu như thị Thiện Xảo Phương Tiện Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, đắc danh Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát dã, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền, nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ”. Nhĩ thời, Thế Tôn dục trùng hiển thử nghĩa, nhi thuyết tụng viết: “Sở tu huệ hữu nhị: Thế gian, xuất thế gian. Thủ trước danh thế gian. Vô thủ trước, xuất thế. Tu thiện xảo phương tiện, y nhị chủng sai biệt, hữu sở đắc thế gian, vô sở đắc xuất thế. Nhược duy thuyết Nhất Thừa, thị danh ác thuyết pháp, bất năng tự thành thục, diệc bất năng độ tha. Nhất hướng ác chúng sanh, vị thuyết tam thừa giáo. Thị tắc vi ngu si, bất danh Ma Ha Tát. Hữu kham thú tam thừa, hân cầu văn chánh pháp, vị thuyết nhạo sanh tử, phi vi trí giả tướng. Chuyên ý đế tư duy, tùy căn dục giáo hóa, thử thiện xảo phương tiện, trí giả sở xưng dự. Chúng sanh tuy hữu ác, nhi kham nhập tam thừa, tùy căn khí giáo đạo, linh giải thoát chúng ác”.
(Kinh: Thế nào gọi là phương tiện thiện xảo xuất thế của Bồ Tát? Tức là các Bồ Tát chỉ vì lợi ích người khác, chẳng vì tự lợi, thị hiện các thứ kỹ thuật hay khéo, vì thành thục người khác mà thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn, hoặc các Bồ Tát, hoặc các Độc Giác, hoặc các Thanh Văn, hoặc mẹ, hoặc cha, hoặc những người bệnh, hoặc những kẻ suy yếu không nơi nương cậy, hoặc thấy người bị hại bởi các ách nạn, sẽ dùng các phương tiện siêng khổ để cứu giúp. Dùng Tứ Nhiếp Sự thành thục hữu tình, tùy theo lòng yêu thích, tùy theo căn khí của họ, vì các hữu tình tuyên thuyết chánh pháp. Lại có thể lần lượt khuyên các Thanh Văn tu Độc Giác Thừa, khuyên các Độc Giác tu tập Đại Thừa. Nếu đối với Thanh Văn và Độc Giác Thừa căn khí chưa chín muồi, vì họ nói pháp chán lìa sanh tử, khiến họ tu học, chán lìa sanh tử, vui cầu Niết Bàn. Nếu các hữu tình thích hành sát sanh, nói rộng là cho đến đối với kẻ thích chấp trước tà kiến, sẽ tùy theo căn tánh, hoặc vì họ tuyên thuyết sanh tử lưu chuyển, chết đây, sanh kia, các thứ quả báo khổ sở, khiến cho họ chán sợ, lìa các ác pháp. Hoặc vì họ tuyên thuyết chánh pháp tương ứng với Thanh Văn Thừa, hoặc vì họ tuyên thuyết chánh pháp tương ứng với Độc Giác Thừa, hoặc vì họ tuyên thuyết các pháp thiển cận trong Vô Thượng Thừa để họ dần dần tu học. Nếu các hữu tình đã thích bố thí, vì họ nói thọ trì tịnh giới thù thắng bậc thượng, khiến cho họ tu học. Nói rộng là cho đến nếu các hữu tình đã thích Tĩnh Lự, bèn vì họ nói thánh đạo vô lậu thắng thượng bao gồm Bát Nhã, khiến cho họ tu học. Phương tiện hay khéo ấy chẳng nương vào “có đạt được”, chẳng chấp trước gì. Như thế thì gọi là phương tiện thiện xảo Đại Giáp Trụ Luân xuất thế của Bồ Tát. Này thiện nam tử! Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu phương tiện thiện xảo Đại Giáp Trụ Luân như thế, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, được gọi là Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, vượt hẳn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước lớn. Hết thảy các Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Lúc bấy giờ, đức Thế Tôn muốn hiển thị lại nghĩa này, bèn nói kệ tụng rằng: “Tu huệ có hai thứ, thế gian, xuất thế gian. Chấp giữ gọi thế gian; chẳng chấp giữ: Xuất thế. Tu phương tiện thiện xảo, nương hai thứ sai khác. Hữu sở đắc: Thế gian. Vô sở đắc: Xuất thế. Nếu chỉ nói Nhất Thừa, gọi là ác thuyết pháp, chẳng thể tự thành thục, cũng chẳng thể độ người. Chúng sanh chuyên làm ác, bèn giảng pháp tam thừa. Đó là kẻ ngu si, chẳng gọi Ma Ha Tát. Có kẻ kham tam thừa, ưa cầu nghe chánh pháp, nói pháp thích sanh tử, chẳng phải là bậc trí. Chuyên tâm, tư duy kỹ, tùy căn, dục giáo hóa. Phương tiện thiện xảo ấy, bậc trí đều khen ngợi. Chúng sanh tuy có ác, nhưng kham nhập ba thừa, theo căn khí chỉ dạy, khiến giải thoát các ác”).

Phần trước đã nói về hai tầng quan hệ: Vì tự lợi và lợi tha (lợi ích người khác). Ở đây, chẳng phải vậy. Đây là phương tiện thiện xảo xuất thế gian của Bồ Tát, chuyên vì lợi ích người khác, chẳng vì tự lợi. Ngài cũng “thị hiện chủng chủng công xảo kỹ thuật, vị thành thục tha, thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn” (thị hiện các thứ kỹ thuật hay khéo, vì thành thục người khác, mà thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật Thế Tôn). Như vậy thì các vị đại Bồ Tát ấy hoàn toàn vì lợi ích người khác, chẳng vì tự lợi, thị hiện các thứ kỹ thuật hay khéo, nhằm mục đích thừa sự, cúng dường chư Phật. Chẳng hạn như, chúng tôi thấy các lạt-ma ở Lạp Tát (Lhasa), bọn họ dùng bơ và tản-ba (tsampa, bột lúa mạch rang) có thể làm rất nhiều hoa, có thể tạo thành đàn tràng để tu đạo. Họ cũng chẳng có danh, chẳng có lợi chi cả. Đàn tràng được kiến lập tại đó, ai cũng chẳng biết là do vị lạt-ma nào làm! Chẳng có ghi tên, mà cũng chẳng đạt được tài lợi gì, thứ gì cũng đều chẳng có, làm việc cho tự viện. Làm việc mà chẳng được trả công. Nghề khéo kiểu này hoàn toàn vì lợi ích người khác, cúng dường chư Phật, mà cũng chẳng phải là lợi ích con người, đều là cúng dường chư Phật.

Whenever there are misfortunes, this great Bodhisattva immediately shows all kinds of diligent means to save them, and approaches them, allowing them to change. But you must have wisdom. You don't have wisdom, how can you do it! Like the story of Mr. Te Cong saving the dog meat seller. That guy sells dog meat and kills dogs every day. Towards his mother, he was extremely unfilial, often scolding her and hitting her. One day, when he was about to kill a female dog, he didn't know what he had forgotten. He had to go out and come back, but no matter how he tried, he couldn't find the dog scalpel. He couldn't find it inside or outside, so he cursed and forced his mother to look for it too. His mother also went looking, but couldn't find him. Finally found it, he saw a puppy lying face down right in front of him, so he kicked the puppy and ran away. Below the puppy is a knife. The puppy used its body to hide the knife. At that time, he was still butchering that bitch. However, in his heart he was very ashamed and said: "I want to kill his mother. That puppy hid the knife and used his life to cover it. I am a human being, so unfilial to my mother!" He immediately bowed his head, repented to his mother, and said: "Mom! After selling dog meat today, I will no longer do this business and find another job. From now on, I will respect you properly!"

He deserved to suffer the retribution of “fifty thunderstorms”. The so-called “five thunders” retribution means death in the five elements of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. When he pushed the cart out and wanted to defecate, he stopped the dog meat cart on the side of the road. To defecate, he had to find a hidden place. He ran to a place where there was a dirt wall where no one could see him so he could squat down to defecate. He went out and kept an eye on the dog meat cart. Te Cong had supernatural powers and knew he was about to be crushed to death by the [collapsed wall]. Because of a single thought of filial piety, his crime disappeared; Te Cong walked over and pushed the cart away. He was impatient: "This is the last [sale], I have some capital. He pushed my car away, what should I do?" He stopped defecating, tightened his pants, and chased after him: "Master! I'm offering you dog meat, stop. That's my capital." He kept shouting, Te Cong stopped the car. He said: "Master! Thank you." But as soon as he ran after him, the earth wall where he had just squatted collapsed. He was so scared that he broke out in a cold sweat and said, "Master! I have to thank you! I'll give you half of this dog meat." He said: "I don't need your dog meat, I just help you sell it." Te Cong immediately sold it for him, and passersby bought it. Te Cong said: "Today we sell at three times the price." “Can it be sold at three times the price?” Te Cong said: "Don't worry! I can sell it!" As soon as Te Cong chanted the spell, people passing by that place all bought it. They smelled the fragrant dog meat smell, so they immediately bought it and immediately sold out the dog meat cart. The proceeds are a lot, three times more than the capital. He said: "Master! How can I thank you?" The monk said: "You don't need to thank me. A thought of filial piety arose, this morning you repented to your mother. It was due to your filial piety."

If you do not have that skill, you will not be able to save the person, causing him to be crushed to death by a collapsing wall. Isn't being crushed to death a result of going to hell? We can't even wait for him to repent, his killing karma is so heavy! Bodhisattvas have the ability to save sentient beings. This skillful means is not the skillful means that we have. Our skillfulness [truly speaking] is not skillful, it is simply for self-benefit, not for the benefit of others. We must understand this principle. Don't use excuses to help other Dharma friends, what kind of heart do you have? If it is truly purely for the benefit of others, without the slightest bit of self-interest, then that is a Bodhisattva who has truly developed his mind.

We learn like that, in every thing you do, you must definitely contemplate your own mind, where does that mind arise from? You leave behind greed, anger, ignorance, and craving, which is very important! Bodhisattvas do foolish things, “all species need suffering means, to save all sentient beings” (all kinds of diligent means, help all sentient beings), using the Four Dharma to mature sentient beings. The Four Dharmas are giving alms, cooperating, benefiting, loving speech, following the wishes of living beings, not following your mind: Whatever you want in your heart, then hope to do it like that! Now the Bodhisattva benefits sentient beings. Bodhisattva, think about what you should do, everyone must listen to me; That is completely wrong! When preaching the Dharma, it depends on what they like, then tell them that. Because of that dharma, they can attain enlightenment, because they can gradually advise those in the Shravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle, advise them to return to the Small Enlightenment Vehicle towards the Great Vehicle, advise those in the Single Enlightenment Vehicle to practice the Mahayana, and advise the Sravaka Vehicle to advance higher to practice the Single Enlightenment Vehicle. If they have the power of Thanh Van Vehicle, it will make them practice and study, be weary of birth and death, wish for Nirvana, pray for no birth and no death.

“If sentient beings mock the act of killing, openly talk about mocking in front of wrong views” (If sentient beings like to kill, in general, even to the point of liking wrong views): Killing, stealing, sex, lying, these are the four basics. “Depending on their nature” (Depending on their nature), because they preach the flow of life and death. “Death here, rebirth there): The suffering consequences cause them to give rise to a feeling of fear, to feel bored and separate from those evil things. You then declare to them all the Dharma that corresponds to the Shravaka Vehicle, or the Dharma that corresponds to the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle. With the foundation of the Mahayana, "or because they preach the middle and short-sighted dharma of the Supreme Vehicle" (or because they proclaim the short-sighted dharmas in the Supreme Vehicle), cannot immediately enter the Mahayana! From the beginning, we must start from the shallow, close dharma, to the dharma equivalent to the middle level, and finally talk about the Supreme Vehicle dharma.

Everyone, when reading the three chapters of the Avatamsaka Sutra, you can feel that everyone can do the Pure Hanh chapter: Seeing something, then thinking about something, that is called “generating the mind”. Pham Hanh is to enter pure Void. Pham Hanh is pure conduct, everything done is pure. Everything does not exist, even the Ten Powers of Buddha do not exist. That is No, really No. But it is still not enough, the Samantabhadra Vows are endless, from Nothingness comes Existence. Existence is Existence, Existence is non-existence, that is, Emptiness. True Emptiness is not Empty. Emptiness is Dharma Existence. Samantabhadra Hanh's practice turns over and over again like that, meaning there are stages. If you read the Avatamsaka Sutra, it is best to choose those three chapters, then you will have them all. Tu Thien Tai first develops his mind, starting from the position of Ten Faiths, until reaching the level of Enlightenment. Having completed the consultation, until the stage of Buddhahood, it was still not enough, so he returned to Manjushri Bodhisattva. Maitreya Bodhisattva told him to return to visit Manjushri Bodhisattva. He returned to Manjushri Bodhisattva, using Faith as the basis, “Faith is the source of the path, mother of merit, nourishes all good roots”. Once grown and nurtured, return to your own mind. Manjushri Bodhisattva told Thien Tai to return to pay his respects to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again, only then can he finally achieve the inconceivable Dharmakaya Buddha. That is also Sambhogakaya Buddha. Only then can we be called a Bodhisattva with all the skillful means. That skillful means has no attachments. Speaking the Dharma is short-sighted; After that, gradually make them practice. If living beings like giving alms, just giving alms is not enough, we must also maintain precepts and practice patience. Patience is not enough, you must practice Meditation. Step by step, make them practice the Six Paramitas, make them realize, just non-attainment (nothing to achieve), no attachments. The Bodhisattva's extraordinary skillful means are like that; That is the real Great Armor Pillar.

If you practice skillful means, you also rely on two types of differences. Whenever there is something to be attained (possession), it is the world; without attainment is to emerge from this world. For the world that has nothing to gain, it will be possible to go beyond the world. "If you only talk about the One Vehicle, it is called an evil teaching, unable to mature yourself, unable to save others" (If you only talk about the One Vehicle, it is called an evil teaching, unable to mature yourself, and unable to save others): Do not talk about the three vehicle dharma, only talk about the One Vehicle dharma of the Mahayana. Preaching the Dharma like that is bad Dharma teaching, not good Dharma teaching, neither can one oneself become mature, nor can one save others. “One-minded towards evil sentient beings, one preaches the three-vehicle teachings” (Towards sentient beings who consistently do evil, because they speak the three-vehicle dharma): Those who do not have good roots, do all evil. If you tell them the Three Vehicles Dharma, don't tell them the shallow, close Dharma of taking refuge, and don't teach them to practice the Ten Virtuous Dharmas, how can they enter into it? That's called stupidity.

“A person who is interested in the three vehicles, is happy to seek the teachings of the Dharma, a person who mocks birth and death, is not wise and fakes appearance” (There are people who are interested in entering the three vehicles, who like to listen to the Dharma, [yet] because they talk about [dharmas] like birth and death, they are not wise): That person is able, “kham” is possible, that is, able to achieve, enter the Hinayana, Middle Vehicle, Mahayana, enjoy it very much, happily seek to hear the true Dharma. You tell them the dharma of birth and death, because they say they like birth and death. Talking about the dharma of birth and death [is talking about the dharma practiced to] be born in heaven, become a human, and sow good roots. That is the dharma of birth and death, the ten good dharmas of introduction. That is not a wise person, because [the sermon] is not of the right nature. “Concentrate on thinking, depending on the base to educate” (Be dedicated to thinking carefully, following their base and desires to educate): Bodhisattvas do not save sentient beings like that arbitrarily, they must think carefully, think logically. If you don't know their background, you can listen to what they say. You talk to them, they will express, they will tell you what capacity they have. So when you talk to living beings, although each person doesn't have their wishes and thoughts written on their faces, it is true that from their faces they let you know, what they want to do, they also have wishes that you can recognize. This matter must be carefully observed, must be skillfully thought about, and be taught according to their base and desires. That is truly skillful, worthy of praise from wise people!

“Even though they are evil, they cannot enter the three vehicles” (Even though they have evil, they can enter the three vehicles): Those beings do evil, like in the story I just told, that guy killed the dog, that is, he did evil and was not filial to his mother. But in the past, he had good roots, now his good roots are ripe, he can put down the scalpel, he can raise a single thought of kindness. His good roots have grown and become a good person. As for those who do good throughout their lives, until they are about to die, their evil nature does not change. Those evil deeds in the past life are very serious, [creating] causes and conditions that hinder the path. You can use such skillful means to observe the basic abilities of living beings. Although in their past lives they were evil, in the present, they can attain the three vehicles. You must teach and accept that person, making him or her free from evil. Saying “put down the scalpel and become a Buddha right there” has the same meaning. Don't do bad things because of that person, don't accept them, don't speak good dharma to them. That is also a mistake, not skillful wisdom, not observing that their [good roots] are ripe now!

(Kinh) “Phục thứ, thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phục hữu Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu thử luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền, nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Vân hà Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân? Thiện nam tử! Từ hữu nhị chủng: Vị pháp duyên từ, hữu tình duyên từ. Pháp duyên từ giả, danh vi đại từ, danh đại giáp trụ. Hữu tình duyên từ, bất danh đại từ, phi đại giáp trụ. Sở dĩ giả hà? Hữu tình duyên từ, cộng chư Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng. Thanh Văn, Độc Giác vị tự lợi lạc, bất vị hữu tình, tinh cần tu tập hữu tình duyên từ. Thanh Văn, Độc Giác vị tự tịch tĩnh, vị tự Niết Bàn, vị diệt tự Hoặc, vị diệt tự kết, bất vị hữu tình tinh cần tu tập hữu tình duyên từ. Thị cố, thử từ bất danh đại từ, phi đại giáp trụ. Kỳ pháp duyên từ, bất cộng Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng, duy chư Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát chúng sở năng tu hành. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phổ vị lợi lạc nhất thiết hữu tình, tinh cần tu tập thử pháp duyên từ. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phổ vị nhất thiết hữu tình tịch tĩnh, cập đắc Niết Bàn, diệt phiền não kết, tinh cần tu tập thử pháp duyên từ. Thị cố, thử từ danh vi đại từ, thị đại giáp trụ. Hựu chư Bồ Tát tu pháp duyên từ, bất y chư Uẩn, bất y chư Xứ, bất y chư Giới, bất y Niệm Trụ, nãi chí bất y Đạo Chi, bất y Dục Giới, bất y Sắc Giới, bất y Vô Sắc Giới, bất y thử thế, bất y tha thế, bất y thử ngạn, bất y bỉ ngạn, bất y đắc, bất y bất đắc. Như thị Bồ Tát tu pháp duyên từ, siêu chư Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa địa, thị danh Bồ Tát pháp duyên Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Thiện nam tử! Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành thử Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, đắc danh Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát dã, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng, giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ”. Nhĩ thời, Thế Tôn trùng hiển thử nghĩa, nhi thuyết tụng viết: - Thanh Văn cập Độc Giác, tu hữu tình duyên từ, tâm đới thập tam quá, duy cầu tự lợi lạc. Bồ Tát đại danh xưng, phổ vị chư hữu tình, tu bất cộng đại từ, tâm ly thập tam quá. Tâm trừ thập tam cấu, vị thú Đại Bồ Đề, tu pháp duyên đại từ, thành phước điền phi viễn. An trụ thập tam lực, xuất quá chư hữu tình, do như sư tử vương, siêu thắng chư cầm thú. Hàng phục thập tam oán, ly đoạn thường biên chấp, tâm vô hữu nhiễm trược, tốc chứng Đại Bồ Đề.
(Kinh: “Lại này thiện nam tử! Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát lại có Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân. Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu luân này, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, vượt xa hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước lớn. Hết thảy các Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ. Thế nào là Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân? Này thiện nam tử! Từ có hai loại, tức là pháp duyên từ và hữu tình duyên từ. Pháp duyên từ được gọi là đại từ, là đại giáp trụ. Hữu tình duyên từ chẳng gọi là đại từ, chẳng phải là đại giáp trụ. Vì cớ sao vậy? Hữu tình duyên từ cùng chung với hàng Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa. Thanh Văn, Độc Giác vì lợi lạc cho chính mình, chẳng vì hữu tình mà siêng ròng tu tập hữu tình duyên từ. Thanh Văn, Độc Giác vì sự tịch tĩnh của chính mình, vì Niết Bàn của chính mình, vì diệt Hoặc của chính mình, vì diệt kết phược của chính mình, chẳng vì hữu tình mà siêng ròng tu tập hữu tình duyên từ. Vì thế, lòng Từ ấy chẳng gọi là đại từ, chẳng phải là đại giáp trụ. Pháp duyên từ chẳng cùng chung với hàng Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa, chỉ có các vị Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát là có thể tu hành. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát vì lợi lạc trọn khắp hết thảy hữu tình mà siêng ròng tu tập pháp duyên từ này. Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát vì làm cho trọn khắp hết thảy hữu tình đạt được tịch tĩnh và đắc Niết Bàn, diệt phiền não kết, mà siêng ròng tu tập môn pháp duyên từ này. Vì thế, lòng Từ này được gọi là đại từ, là đại giáp trụ. Lại nữa, các Bồ Tát tu pháp duyên từ, chẳng nương theo các Uẩn, chẳng nương theo các Xứ, chẳng nương theo các Giới, chẳng nương theo Niệm Trụ, cho đến chẳng nương theo Đạo Chi, chẳng nương theo Dục Giới, chẳng nương theo Sắc Giới, chẳng nương theo Vô Sắc Giới, chẳng nương theo đời này, chẳng nương theo đời khác, chẳng nương theo bờ này, chẳng nương theo bờ kia, chẳng nương theo đắc, chẳng nương theo bất đắc. Bồ Tát tu pháp duyên từ như thế, vượt hẳn các địa vị Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa; được gọi là pháp duyên Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân của Bồ Tát. Này thiện nam tử! Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân này, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, được gọi là Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, vượt hẳn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước to lớn, hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ”. Lúc bấy giờ, đức Thế Tôn hiển thị lại nghĩa ấy, bèn nói kệ tụng rằng: - Thanh Văn và Độc Giác, tu hữu tình duyên từ, tâm mang mười ba lỗi, chỉ cầu lợi lạc riêng. Bồ Tát thanh danh lớn, vì khắp các hữu tình, tu bất cộng đại từ, tâm lìa mười ba lỗi. Tâm trừ mười ba cấu, tiến nhập Đại Bồ Đề, tu pháp duyên đại từ, thành phước điền chẳng xa. An trụ mười ba lực, vượt khỏi các hữu tình, ví như sư tử chúa, vượt xa các cầm thú. Hàng phục mười ba oán, lìa đoạn, thường, biên chấp. Tâm chẳng có nhiễm trược, mau chứng Đại Bồ Đề).

Đại Từ Đại Giáp Trụ Luân là gì? Giống như trong phần trước, Từ cũng có hai loại: Pháp duyên từ, và hữu tình duyên từ. Một đằng là xét theo người, một đằng là xét theo pháp. Xét theo pháp để nói, Từ là đại từ, là đại giáp trụ. Nếu nói theo tình, thì chẳng gọi là đại từ, chẳng phải là đại giáp trụ. Vì sao phải nói như vậy? “Sở dĩ giả hà?” (Vì cớ sao vậy?): [Câu này] mang ý nghĩa gạn hỏi. Tiếp đó liền nói: “Hữu tình duyên từ” là “chư Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng”, [nghĩa là lòng Từ] tương đương với họ. Vì sao? Do Thanh Văn Thừa và Độc Giác Thừa vì lợi lạc chính mình, chẳng phải vì hữu tình. Họ tinh tấn tu tập, chẳng phải là duyên theo hết thảy hữu tình mà tu tâm đại từ bi. Họ vì tịch tĩnh, vì Niết Bàn của chính mình, vì diệt trừ Hoặc nghiệp và đoạn trừ Kết Sử của chính mình. Kết Sử Hoặc rất khó đoạn! Kết Sử khiến cho quý vị phiền não, khiến cho quý vị đọa lạc, vì cái nghiệp đã kết thành, sẽ chẳng thể giải thoát được! Thanh Văn, Duyên Giác Thừa chỉ mong diệt Kết Sử của chính mình, chẳng phải vì hữu tình mà siêng ròng tu tập. Họ là hữu tình duyên từ. Chúng tôi lại nói đơn giản, Thanh Văn, Duyên Giác Thừa chẳng dẹp khổ cho chúng sanh. Ngay như tôn giả Mục Kiền Liên vì cứu mẹ mới đến địa ngục đưa cơm cho mẹ. Ngài trọn chẳng phát đại tâm đưa cơm cho hết thảy chúng sanh trong địa ngục. Tâm lượng của Ngài quá nhỏ, chỉ vì chính mình, chẳng có tâm đại từ bi. Thanh Văn Thừa chẳng thể đại từ, đại bi, chẳng thể vì hết thảy hữu tình mà siêng ròng tu tập. Lòng từ ái của họ là tình kiến hữu ái. Ái là vô minh, lòng Từ kiểu ấy “bất danh đại từ” (chẳng gọi là đại từ).

What is the shape of “Dharma of dependent origin”? “Not in common with the Sravakas and the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, only the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas have the ability to practice” (Not in common with the Sravakas and the Pratyekabuddhas, only the Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas can practice): This is the practice of the great Bodhisattva. How do they practice? They practice diligently for the benefit of all sentient beings, diligently practice for the benefit of all sentient beings, not for themselves. That is called Dharma of Dependent Compassion. He is dependent on Dharmakaya, the word Dharma [in Dharma Dependent Compassion] can also be understood as Dharmakaya, because it has the same Essence with Dharmakaya. We and sentient beings are the same, because we have the same Body, we must save them. You yourself are included in it. That is the Dharma of Dependent Compassion. Never thinking about himself, wanting to benefit sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to attain tranquility, attain ultimate Concentration, achieve Nirvana, eliminate all problems and afflictions for sentient beings, and untie the knots for sentient beings. As it is said in the Shurangama Sutra, “unleashing the six ends, transcending the three emptiness” (untie the six knots, go beyond the three emptiness). The Six Links are the Six Roots, that is, the afflictions caused by the Six Roots corresponding to the Luc Tran are all removed, and you reach the realm of True Emptiness. The realm of True Emptiness includes the Two Vehicle Emptiness, the Bodhisattva Emptiness, the Ultimate Emptiness, and the All Winged Emptiness. You reach that ultimate state, eliminating afflictions for sentient beings, diligently practicing this Dharma of Dependent Compassion. That is called great kindness, eliminating all suffering for sentient beings.

The three realms belong to birth and death. “Try it” is this life, “alternately” is the future life. The great compassion of that Bodhisattva, whether in the future or the present, is equal in the three lifetimes, in the three realms, all dharmas are equal, there is neither this shore nor the other shore. If one shore is birth and death, the other shore is Nirvana. Because of liking Nirvana, one can end birth and death and escape the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death. Having that kind of intention is not big. After all dharmas have been destroyed, only then can all dharmas be established. Only when all dharmas no longer exist can there be non-emptiness. If we are now non-empty, it will be an attachment. After it was gone, he returned and saved sentient beings again. Saving sentient beings without seeing their physical appearance. You think this is very simple, but we can't move! If we can transfer it, it would be great, we would all become Buddhas, that's how it is! Very simple at first glance! Affliction and Bodhi, birth and death and Nirvana, the ancients imagined, affliction is the palm of the hand, Bodhi is the back of the hand, just a hand, nothing else! If you understand, you will attain enlightenment. If you don't understand clearly, you will be misled. When will we understand clearly? It depends on each person's practice. There is success, there is failure, if there is success, there is definitely failure. Do not rely on that to start a mind of great compassion. Dharma of Dependent Compassion is equality. Therefore, we should not rely on that to arouse our compassion. That is called Dharma of Dependent Compassion.

“At that time, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, then recited and wrote it” (At that time, the World-Honored One re-displayed this meaning, then recited the verse), we read this verse once. “The Sravaka attains the Solitary Enlightenment, cultivating the condition of love and compassion, the mind is bound by thirteen excesses” (The Sravaka and the Doctrine of the Enlightenment, cultivating the existence of the condition of love and compassion, the mind carries thirteen errors): If one cultivates the condition of love and compassion, there will be thirteen mistakes, because they only seek benefit for themselves, seek benefit for themselves. “Bodhisattva's great name, universal for all sentient beings, cultivating without adding pronouns” (Bodhisattva with great fame, for all sentient beings, cultivating without pronouns): [That kindness] is not in common with Shravaka, Pratyekabuddha. “The mind is separated from thirteen mistakes” (The mind is separated from thirteen mistakes): There are no thirteen mistakes! “Mind minus the thirteen attachments, enjoy great Bodhi, practice the dharma of great loving-kindness, attain a far-reaching field of blessings” (Mind subtract the thirteen attachments, enter great Bodhi, practice the dharma of great loving-kindness, attain a field of great blessings not far): You will definitely become an ultimate field of blessings, attaining Buddhahood is not far away, but “thirteen attachments” are very difficult to eliminate. “An abiding in the thirteen powers, surpasses all sentient beings, like a lion king, surpasses all animals” (An abiding in thirteen powers, surpasses all sentient beings, like a lion king, surpasses all animals). Like the lion king, the lion is the king of beasts. “Quit the thirteen resentments, abandon the attachment to permanent and boundary” (Quit the thirteen resentments, abandon the attachment to cessation and eternity): Thirteen resentments are born from the views of the Eternal and Permanent attachments. Thus "the mind has no impurities, quickly attains great Bodhi" (the mind is free from defilements, impurities, quickly attains great Bodhi): Second Vehicle Shravakas and Pratyekabuddhas who cultivate compassion are conditioned by compassion, can escape the "thirteen errors". Thirteen errors are mentioned in volume ninety-nine of the Yogācāra Master Diaśāstra, which says fifteen errors. From those fifteen errors, we can piece together one or two things [to understand the thirteen errors]. First, we read fifteen errors at a time.

“The first falsehood, the fourth falsehood is too much” (One is the four levels of mistakes), “the second falsehood, the strength of Zen is too much” (the second is the mistake while practicing Zen, using too much force), “the third falsehood, the dharma fund is too lacking in joy” (the third is the mistake of lacking, not using too much force) full of joy), "the four falsehoods, too many false foundations" (fourth is the mistake of being bound by others), "fifth falsehoods, untrue belief, unbelief" (fifth is causing people who do not have true faith to contradict and disbelieve), "six falsehoods, true true believers' spiritual variation too much" (sixth is the mistake that causes people with true faith to change differently), the two things five and six can be combined into one, that is, is to make people with righteous faith unable to increase their faith, on the contrary, it causes their faith to decline. That's a mistake. When you do a career, your compassion is inherently good, but others make fun of you, and there are even fellow believers who blame you. You originally came from compassion, but others think you have other goals. That was a mistake. “Too much wealth, too many careers” (Error due to having too much wealth, too many careers): Too much wealth, you will commit a crime. Too much career, can't do it. “Too much previous infection” (The mistake of immersing oneself in infection), “Too much brain damage” (the mistake of disturbing others), “Too much disease arising” (the mistake of causing illness), these are things we cannot avoid. No one wants to get sick, but you get sick. Why do we get sick? The disease comes from the mouth, eating too much! It's okay to eat less. There are many types of this disease. "Too far away from a good destination" (Errors due to obstacles to entering the good path): Sometimes we feel as if Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are right in front of our eyes. Sometimes in our minds we apply corresponding effort, we feel as if Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are very close to us, great joy arises in our minds. Sometimes when you put in the effort, ten or eight years of effort, it seems like you are infinitely far away from Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. The same goes for reciting sutras, reciting mantras, it seems like Buddhas and Bodhisattvas don't bless them, the more they recite, the more confused they become. These are mistakes that hinder you from entering the good path.

There is a mistake that is to arrogantly protect someone who should not be protected. This principle is just fear that everyone has, and must avoid suspicion. Those who should be protected will be protected, those who should not be protected will not be protected. We give an example: Buddha saves all sentient beings, Bodhisattva saves all sentient beings. That being comes from evil intentions, you say, should we protect him, or should we not protect him? He gives rise to evil thoughts and does not seek the Dharma. If you have supernatural powers, you can know. Without supernatural powers, how can you know? That person is duplicitous, either wanting to test you, or wanting to confuse you. If you do something to benefit sentient beings, how should you do it? For example, there are sentient beings who ask: "Old shaman, how do you practice? What sutras do you recite?" What does this have to do with him? What's the use of knowing those things? That magician will probably have doubts: "What are you asking me for? Do you want to test my practice?" But should we protect that person or not? Depends on whether you have wisdom or not? If you have wisdom, you won't protect him. You will explain to him a little bit: "This has nothing to do with you! I practice, but you don't see success in practice. I practice, you don't see effectiveness, and it doesn't mean that [you see me practice any method] you should practice! There are things that are 'through', 'through' in the sense of 'common, universal', [that is, the dharmas that] I practice, you can also practice, [that is] But there are some methods that I practice that you cannot practice." It's okay to explain clearly to that person. With these mistakes, if you want to benefit sentient beings, you will commit many shortcomings. Don't be obedient but do it for that person. You should be obedient but you are arrogant and do not obey; those are all mistakes. Should be respectful but not reverent; You should not be respectful, but you are arrogant and respectful. That is also not accurate.

As for the “thirteen faults”, in the Yogācāraṇāṇāṇa, it says “fifteen types of faults”, [such as] should be a treasure but not a treasure; is not worthy to be a treasury, but to be a treasury. You should practice, but you don't practice. It is not worth studying, but studying instead. There may be no need to explain these two types. Those are thirteen errors. Therefore, if you make those mistakes, you will not be able to achieve great compassion. What should great compassion be like? For all sentient beings, do not abandon or do not have those mistakes. In other words, if you have those thirteen things, you are cultivating predestined love. What will those mistakes produce? Because you seek your own benefit, you only think of your own benefit, not the benefit of others. Bodhisattva is the opposite. Bodhisattva has great reputation, he benefits all sentient beings. He practiced no plus pronouns. “Non-plus” is not in common with Shravaka and Pratyekabuddha (ie Sravaka and Pratyekabuddha cannot have those qualities), but in common with all those who develop Bodhi mind. Thus, cultivating this method (Dai Tu Dai Giap Giap Luan), there will be no such mistakes, "the mind minus the thirteen components" (the mind minus the thirteen components). As for “thirteen structures”, in the Buddhist Dictionary there are “fourteen structures”, I put fourteen structures together, it will be “thirteen structures”. [According to the Buddhist Dictionary], the fourteen structures are the Four Consequences, the Four Places, and the Six Foundations of Wealth[50], combined into fourteen sections.

What is Quarterfinals? It is the End of History. We often read [sutras mentioning] Conclusion. Those kinds of problems, if you can't solve them, will cause you to commit crimes. What types are these? These are killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying in the Five Precepts, which are the Four Conclusions. Those four types are basic. Until you become a Buddha, you will completely cut off ignorance. Ignorance is ignorance, [becoming a Buddha] puts an end to ignorance. There is also desire (desire), khui (anger), father (fear), and delusion. In all realms, desire arises. In all realms, anger and anger arise, anger arises. Khue means harm, also “indignation” (disgust, anger), resentment. There is also terror (panic, fear), that is stupidity. If he were not a foolish person, he would not have desires and would know all dharmas such as dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. That person does not arouse desire, [because he clearly knows] that it is an illusory realm, a deception. If there is love, there will be suffering. Without love, there will be no suffering, and there will be no love. If it is said to be indifferent to humans, then it seems that that person is a cold-blooded animal and is indifferent. Is that right? That's not right! Cold-blooded animals also have feelings, cold-blooded animals are not without feelings at all. Like fish, which is a cold-blooded animal, living in the sea, it has feelings, for the children it gives birth to, it protects, that is, it has feelings!

“Unconscious” means “to all dharmas, there is no attachment”. Some people think that once we Buddhists believe in Buddhism, we will be heartless and no longer need emotions. Wife, husband, father, mother don't need anything. That is a wrong criticism, Buddha is not heartless. People who study Buddhism are not heartless, but are especially affectionate. Not only towards one person, [that is] not towards parents, wife and children, but sentient beings, without feelings towards others. That's not true! To all sentient beings, that person is sentient. “Many emotions are the Buddha mind” (Many emotions are the Buddha mind), that person will save all sentient beings. But the word Love is explained differently. That person has wisdom, has no attachments, and does not give rise to attachment. That way there will be no defects!

There is also contamination, which means people who like to drink alcohol will make a lot of mistakes! Why did the Buddha include the precept of drinking alcohol in the Five Precepts? In India, this kind of thing has arisen: Because of drinking alcohol, committing sexual immorality. Because of anger and fear of being denounced by that person, he killed someone and ran away. Run away, because you don't have money, so you steal and lie. Because of drinking alcohol, all “murder, crime, sexual misconduct, and lies” are committed. In the Buddhist world, there are many stories like this. Therefore, the reason why drinking alcohol is included in the Five Precepts is very important! Especially for Bodhisattvas, the precept against alcohol is also fundamental. Bodhisattva cannot sell alcohol. The sin of selling alcohol is worse than the sin of drinking alcohol. You seduce so many people, it's equivalent to selling poison, that's how it is. But national law does not punish, on the contrary, it encourages the sale of alcohol. Why cheer? Tax collection and alcohol tax are huge! On the other hand are indulgent and indulgent joys. This story is divided into two types: Infatuation is like brothels and entertainment places. A place of entertainment is a place of promiscuity. For those fourteen structures, I combined them into thirteen structures. Furthermore, combined with evil speech, it will lead you to do many bad things and make mistakes. There is also falling, that is, if you relax, you will definitely fall. When you relax, think that you will definitely fall into hell. That's how the Long A Ham Sutra teaches.

“Thirteen resentments” means “eleven types of anger”, plus two more things, it will be thirteen resentments. Strong negative karma, what is strong? When angry, anger is strong. When you can't control your anger, anger arises, and you don't care about anything; Even the loss of a family, the loss of a country and the dissolution of a family are all possible. If the anger is very strong, or the brain is disturbed, or someone else stirs up troubles, or holds resentment, the person who has resentment towards me, I hope to take revenge on that person, up to "thirteen resentments" for this body. “Appearance” is in resentment and evil appears, that is “appearance”. “Toxic” is using poison to harm others. “Uninterrupted” is anger that cannot be interrupted and continues without stopping!

8) Eighth is Concentration Power, which is the power of Samadhi, which is cultivating Xa Ma Tha (Sham). Because of cultivating Xa Ma Tha, strength is born.

9) Ninth is Hue Power. Hue Force is due to cultivating wisdom, the achievement of Hui Quan gives birth to strength.

10) Tenth is Da Van Luc. Due to the multi-literacy of Dharma, due to regularity

when you hear, wisdom will arise. If you don't listen, how can you understand clearly? If you don't listen, you won't understand clearly. Must be multicultural! By listening to the Dharma, the true Dharma will be born, and there will be a kind of power that will bless you. Because that power blesses you, you will feel Buddha right before your eyes. Whenever you relax, Buddha is no more, that power is gone, that power is very far away! I think every Dharma friend has this feeling: While you quiet your mind, either reciting ten thousand times, reciting one hundred thousand times, the feeling of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is truly right before your eyes. Or chant Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha is right in front of your eyes. Whenever you relax, that strength is no longer there! Sometimes very far, sometimes very close, that is your own strength.

12) Twelfth is Mindfulness. We start thinking all day long, we must have the correct thoughts. Whenever you start thinking, it's all for the benefit of others, not for your own peace and happiness. That recitation is reciting the Buddha, reciting the Dharma, reciting the Sangha; That's all mindfulness. It includes right contemplation, “intelligent powers” that is, supernatural powers, achieving mindfulness. Right contemplation of Luc Thong, three powers.

(Sutra) Phuc, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva restores the Wheel of Great Compassion, Great Armor. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat accomplished testing the wheel, developed the initial mind, must eliminate the five desires at all stages, overcome all Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment, universal taste necessarily Thanh Van, Single Enlightenment to create a great field of blessings. Necessarily the Thanh Van, the Single Enlightened Vehicle, the level of offerings, support, and protection. The reason why it's fake? It is necessary for Thanh Van and Single Enlightened Vehicle to attain the benefit and joy of the body, the child to practice compassion, and the universal taste for all sentient beings to benefit and practice great compassion. Bodhisattva Mahasattva is selfless and benefits his body, and tries to practice compassion, and all sentient beings have the benefit and joy, and tries to practice great compassion. In the past, the Bodhisattva achieved the Great Compassion and Great Armor Pillar, surpassing all the Sravakas and Single Enlightenment, universally attaining the Sravaka and Single Enlightenment to create a great field of blessings. Necessary Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas of the 1st level make offerings, serve, and protect.
(Sutra: Come here, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha Sattva also has the Great Compassion and Great Armor Wheel. If Bodhisattva Mahasattva achieves this wheel, from the beginning, all the five desires can be eliminated, far surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, because all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones should practice their hearts Compassion, not wanting to practice great compassion for the benefit of all sentient beings. The Bodhisattva does not practice compassion for the benefit of himself, but only wants to practice great compassion for the benefit of all sentient beings. Therefore, the Bodhisattva who achieves the Great Compassion of the Wheel of Compassion, surpasses all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, for the sake of all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, he should make offerings to all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones. guardian).

The Second Vehicle cultivates compassion for its own benefit, only for its own benefit to practice compassion like that. Therefore, compassion is not complete. We often say “have mercy on others”, or practice great compassion for things or people. We do not want to practice great compassion for the benefit of all sentient beings. Just for the sake of peace and happiness, not for the sake of sentient beings to be free from suffering, then it will not be able to fully benefit all sentient beings. Practicing great compassion like that, when that person practices the Dharma, there will be two different types of differences in the mind. Therefore, when we do something, we must use it wisely. Manjushri Bodhisattva teaches us to use our mind skillfully, depending on how you contemplate? It's the same story, you use one coin to offer alms, [yet] the merit is boundless and limitless; Others use ten thousand dong to give alms and offerings, the merit is tiny! What's the reason? Disagree with your mind! Must be clever

use your mind, depending on how you see it, how do you do it?

Every thing has two types of appearances: If you do it right, the merit is immeasurable; If you do the opposite, the harm is boundless! We often think that murder and arson are crimes, but sometimes the Bodhisattva wants to benefit the majority of living beings. He cannot stop the person who harms living beings. He can kill that person or burn him to death. Just for the benefit of many sentient beings, Bodhisattvas are not afraid of suffering. To that living being, the Bodhisattva still owes his life; Later, we still have to convert him. Regardless of whether it is favorable or unfavorable, the Bodhisattva has great compassion, because his starting point is great compassion, so he is great compassion. As long as you don't seek peace and happiness for yourself, it will cause sentient beings to leave suffering; The Bodhisattva who achieved Great Compassion, Great Armor and Pillars like that, immediately surpassed all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, and for all Sravakas and Single Enlightened Ones, he created fields of great blessings for them. They can pray for blessings from the Bodhisattva.

(Kinh) “Thị Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát phổ vị nhiêu ích chư hữu tình cố, hành Tứ Nhiếp Sự nhi thành thục chi, vị do đại bi phổ vị lợi lạc chư hữu tình cố, hành Bố Thí Nhiếp, năng xả nhất thiết trân bảo tài vật, cầm thú, bộc sử, quốc thành, thê tử, nãi chí thân mạng, vô sở lận tích. Hành vô sở đắc vi phương tiện cố, bất kiến nhất thiết sở hóa hữu tình, bất kiến thí giả, bất kiến thọ giả, bất kiến thí vật, bất kiến thí hạnh, bất kiến thí hạnh sở đắc quả báo, nãi chí bất kiến vô sở đắc hạnh. Như thị đại bi, phổ vị lợi lạc chư hữu tình cố, hành Ái Ngữ Nhiếp, hành Lợi Hành Nhiếp, hành Đồng Sự Nhiếp, tùy kỳ sở ưng, như thượng quảng thuyết, nãi chí bất kiến vô sở đắc hành. Thị Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thường dĩ tối thắng năng điều phục tâm, năng tịch tĩnh tâm, vô số lượng tâm, bất hành nhất thiết Uẩn, Xứ, Giới tâm, sở sanh vô động, vô trụ, Đại Bi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, thành thục nhất thiết sở hóa hữu tình, tâm vô yếm quyện. Như thị danh vi Bồ Tát Đại Bi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, bất cộng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Thiện nam tử! Nhược Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành thử Đại Bi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân, tùng sơ phát tâm, nhất thiết ngũ dục giai năng trừ đoạn, đắc danh Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát dã, siêu thắng nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, phổ vị nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác tác đại phước điền. Nhất thiết Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đẳng giai ưng cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ”. Nhĩ thời, Thế Tôn trùng hiển thử nghĩa, nhi thuyết tụng viết: “Thậm thâm vi diệu pháp, sở thành chi đại bi, nan trắc loại hư không, vô sắc, vô an trụ. Bồ Tát đại tinh tấn, cụ đỗ-đa công đức, thắng trí thành đại bi, dũng kiện siêu chư thế. Vô y hỗ hữu tình, sanh tử khổ uế phược, đại bi thủy mộc dục, linh giải thoát chúng khổ. Bồ Tát hành đại bi, năng kiệt sanh tử hải, phi chư Thanh Văn chúng, cập Độc Giác sở hành. Chúng sanh tham, khuể, si, mê mậu đọa ác thú, trạc dĩ đại bi thủy, thoát khổ đắc tiêu nhiên”.
(Kinh: “Vị Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát ấy vì lợi ích trọn khắp các hữu tình mà hành Tứ Nhiếp Sự để thành thục họ, tức là do đại bi lợi lạc trọn khắp các hữu tình, nên hành Bố Thí Nhiếp, có thể xả hết thảy tài vật quý báu, cầm thú, tôi tớ, quốc thành, thê tử, vợ con, cho đến thân mạng chẳng hề tiếc nuối. Do hành “không có gì đạt được” để làm phương tiện, chẳng thấy hết thảy hữu tình được hóa độ, chẳng thấy người thí, chẳng thấy người nhận, chẳng thấy vật được thí, chẳng thấy hạnh bố thí, chẳng thấy quả báo đạt được do bố thí, cho đến chẳng thấy hạnh “không có gì để đạt được”.
