Đại bi như thế vì lợi lạc trọn khắp các hữu tình mà hành Ái Ngữ Nhiếp, hành Lợi Hành Nhiếp, hành Đồng Sự Nhiếp, tùy theo lẽ đáng nên, như trong phần trước đã rộng nói, cho đến chẳng thấy hạnh “không có gì để đạt được”. Vị Bồ Tát ấy thường dùng cái tâm có thể điều phục tối thắng, tâm có thể tịch tĩnh, tâm chẳng có số lượng, tâm chẳng hành hết thảy Uẩn, Xứ, Giới, sanh ra Đại Bi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân chẳng động, chẳng trụ, thành thục hết thảy hữu tình được hóa độ mà tâm chẳng chán mệt. Như thế gọi là Đại Bi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân của Bồ Tát, chẳng cùng chung với hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác. Này thiện nam tử! Nếu Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát thành tựu Đại Bi Đại Giáp Trụ Luân này, từ sơ phát tâm, hết thảy ngũ dục đều có thể đoạn trừ, được gọi là Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, vượt hẳn hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, vì khắp hết thảy Thanh Văn, Độc Giác làm ruộng phước to lớn. Hết thảy hàng Thanh Văn, Độc Giác Thừa đều nên cúng dường, thừa sự, thủ hộ”. Lúc bấy giờ, đức Thế Tôn hiển thị lại nghĩa này, bèn nói kệ tụng rằng: - Pháp vi diệu rất sâu, thành tựu lòng đại bi, khó lường dường hư không, vô sắc, chẳng an trụ. Bồ Tát đại tinh tấn, trọn công đức đầu-đà, thắng trí thành đại bi, mạnh mẽ vượt thế gian. Hữu tình không nương tựa, sanh tử khổ dơ, trói. Nước đại bi tắm gội, khiến giải thoát các khổ. Bồ Tát hành đại bi, cạn khô biển sanh tử. Các Thanh Văn, Độc Giác, chẳng thể hành hạnh này. Chúng sanh tham, giận, si, mê lầm đọa nẻo ác, nước đại bi gột rửa, thoát khổ, được an nhiên).

Bồ Tát vì lợi ích các hữu tình, bèn hành Tứ Nhiếp Pháp, khiến cho các chúng sanh và các hữu tình đã thành thục đều được thành tựu, lìa khổ, được vui. “Vị do đại bi phổ vị lợi lạc chư hữu tình cố, hành Bố Thí Nhiếp” (Tức là do đại bi lợi lạc trọn khắp các hữu tình mà hành Bố Thí Nhiếp): Bố thí là xả vật chất, hoặc là nội thí, ngoại thí, hoặc xả thân thể, vì làm cho những người khác được lợi ích. Có thể xả các vật chất gì? Hết thảy “trân bảo, tài vật, cầm thú, bộc sử” (vật quý, tài vật, chim thú, tôi tớ): “Cầm thú” [ở đây] là nói tới những con vật quý vị yêu thích, như vẹt, bát ca (nhồng), đều là những con vật được ưa thích nhất. Đó là hàng tại gia Bồ Tát. Cầm thú, người hầu, đầy tớ, cho đến quốc gia, quốc thành, vợ con của chính mình đều có thể xả. Thậm chí tự thân “vô sở lận tích” (chẳng hề keo tiếc), chẳng tiếc rẻ. “Tiếc rẻ” nghĩa là không xả được. Đối với bất cứ sự vật nào nơi bản thân hay ngoài thân, cho đến tất cả hết thảy, Ngài đều có thể xả; nhưng khi xả, Ngài chẳng cầu quả. Do vậy, chẳng có người nhận, chẳng có kẻ thí, cho đến chẳng thấy quả báo đạt được do bố thí. Ta xả như vậy, trong tương lai sẽ đạt được quả báo gì? Chẳng có quả báo, chẳng chấp trước quả báo, chẳng tham cầu quả báo, xả như thế đó. Ở đây, có một vấn đề: Thời đức Phật thuyết pháp, vợ con thuộc quyền sở hữu của chính mình, giống như một phần tài sản. Nhưng hiện thời, chú trọng bình đẳng, cô ta có tự do, có quyền lợi của chính mình, ta xả cô ta cho ai? Chẳng thể được! Hiện thời chẳng thể được! Vợ muốn thí xả chồng, cũng chẳng thể. Quý vị nói: “Tôi đem chồng thí xả cho ông để dùng anh ta làm nô lệ”. Chồng sẽ chẳng nghe lời quý vị. Đấy là nói theo tình hình xã hội trong quá khứ.

He releases his own body or property, it is a part of himself, he can release it at any time. Currently, when I leave my country, my wife, someone asks: "I am the king, I intend to leave." You wish to let go, do your ministers agree or not? If you let go, the government won't agree. Currently, the President says: "I give up!" You give up the position of President, the two houses of the General Assembly (the Senate and the House of Representatives) have not yet passed it, you cannot let go! This issue is looked at from another perspective, speaking from the inside. When the Bodhisattva practiced the Dharma, in his mind he thought like this: "Whatever my mind craves, I have no greed or love for anything. Everything can be let go, and I don't regret anything!" That is called skillful means; But when we let go, we absolutely do not see ourselves as someone who can let go, nor do we see anyone receiving alms. As long as there are still items given by me, as long as there is still [the idea] "I practice almsgiving because of practicing great compassion, practicing the Bodhisattva path. After I have given, what retribution will I achieve in the future"; If you consider and worry about those things, you will not become a great compassionate Bodhisattva.

To cause great compassion like that, “for the universal benefit of sentient beings, practice Ai Ngu Nhiep” (for the benefit of all sentient beings, practice Ai Ngu Nhiep). Everyone knows that Ai Ngu is to speak pleasant words, not to say words that make others sad. There is a Chinese aphorism: “Speaking kindly according to one's feelings”, which means saying good things according to people's feelings, will make people happy. “Evil words are evil”, meaning you say bad words to others, people hear and then hate you, don't want to contact you, and rarely talk to you. You must pay attention to this, you must make others happy, but you should also not go against the wishes of the Three Jewels. Speaking loving words must contain a mind of renunciation. For example, when talking about the relationship between the two sexes, you say nice things that make them happy: "I can help you find a girlfriend, I can help you find a boyfriend." Saying that is not okay, at that moment, you have violated the precepts. Therefore, in the sexual world there are many problems [you must pay close attention to]. If you explain each precept, you will [find yourself] unintentionally breaking many rules. It's just that [what was committed] is not fundamental! Why do we have to study the precepts for five years after becoming a monk? Because if you don't study, you won't know and will violate the precepts at will.

There is also the matter of benefiting others through Collaboration and Benefit, doing useful things for others, accepting others like that. You help people work, of course they are happy. You don't ask for compensation, you help others without expecting anything, everyone is happy. But you do it as you please, it's also because of your great compassion, either when other people's actions are inconvenient, you support them, or when they carry a heavy load and can't carry it, you help them a little. These things are called Loi Hanh, we must do things that benefit others.

“Depending on one's wishes, as the above widely preached, there is no way to attain happiness. The Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, always supreme, is able to tame the mind, is able to calm the mind, countless minds, not necessarily acting on the Aggregates, Bases, Precepts, mind, all born motionless and baseless, Great Compassion, Great Armor Pillar. Wheel" (According to what should be, as mentioned extensively in the above section, until there is no virtue to achieve anything. That Bodhisattva Ma Ha often uses the mind that is supreme, can be controlled, the mind can be calm, the mind has no quantity, the mind does not act on all the Aggregates, Places, and Precepts, arising without movement and without standing Great Compassion Great Armor Pillars): That is what he contemplates. Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat can control his own mind, not relying on Sight, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, not in all forms of the realm to give birth to the mind. What kind of mind is that? “No prior mind” (The mind has no attachments), “unmoved mind”, “ability to calm the mind” (the mind can be calm). “No quantity” means no calculation or measurement. Without practicing all the Five Aggregates, the twelve Regions, and the eighteen Precepts, nothing exists! All Forms, Feelings, Thoughts, Actions, Consciousness, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, including Eye Consciousness, Ear Consciousness, Snake Consciousness, Tongue Consciousness, Body Consciousness, and Consciousness. Those are called the eighteen precepts. Everyone, think about it, if you leave those things out, what else is there? Nothing is there. What is born? That is the Great Compassion Great Armor Pillar. That is "should not dwell anywhere to give birth to a mind" (should not dwell anywhere to give birth to a mind). Great compassion is born like that. The Diamond Sutra teaches: “Never dwelling on Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma gives birth to the mind, if you rely on no place to give birth to the mind” (Do not rely on Form, Sound, Scent, Taste, Touch, Dharma to give birth to the mind, you should not abide in any place to give birth to the mind). What is that mind called? Carefree! “The Taoist is heartless” is the ultimate achievement.

“At that time, the World-Honored One repeatedly revealed the meaning, and recited and wrote: - Even profound and wonderful Dharma, attaining great compassion” (At that time, the World-Honored One re-displayed this meaning, then recited verses: “The Dharma is very profound and wonderful, achieving great compassion”). What is “Very profound and wonderful Dharma”? It is the wheel of great compassion, it is a very profound and wonderful dharma. What is reaching a very deep realm? There is no one who gives alms, there is no object to be given, there is no one to receive alms, there is no dharma to perform almsgiving, all is Emptiness. That Emptiness is the Truth. In the Sutra of Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, the True Form is Truth, it is Emptiness like that, but isn't it empty, can we not do it? Bodhisattvas often practice great compassion and giving like that, but it is always Emptiness like that. “Difficult like the void” (Difficult to fathom like the void): This principle, if only used by speculation, will be unfathomable! Who can fathom the edge of nothingness? Measuring emptiness, [will realize] there is no way to measure. “No form, no abiding”: There is no form or form that can be attained, nor to abiding in that place. Without land, without form, how can you fathom it? That is the Bodhisattva's great diligence.

“Complete merit of Dau-da” (Complete merit of Dau Da): All the worldly defilements have been eliminated, that merit “superior wisdom becomes great compassion” (superior wisdom becomes great compassion): Use superior wisdom to achieve great compassion. “Courage beyond all worlds” (Strong beyond all worlds): That Luan is very powerful. Why? No! Courage is also Mu. The things just mentioned above are all Emptiness, Emptiness without hindering Being. Therefore, Bodhisattvas have Wonderful Being to give birth to great compassion, that great compassion is inconceivable. “Unsupporting sentient beings” means sentient beings have no refuge, no one to take care of them, Bodhisattva will take care of them. Staying in “this birth and death suffering and impurity” (this birth and death suffering, impurity and bondage), suffering the suffering of birth and death, impurity and impurity, being bound by all karma. Bodhisattvas can use the water of great compassion to bathe, cleanse, and liberate all sufferings.

“A Bodhisattva who practices great compassion can exhaust the sea of birth and death, and is free from the Sravakas, reaching the sole enlightenment place” (Bodhisattva who practices great compassion dries up the ocean of birth and death, Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas, cannot practice this Dharma): The Bodhisattva's great compassion can cause all living beings to dry up the ocean. In life and death, Thanh Van and Doc Giac cannot do this. “Beings are greedy, angry, and ignorant” means greed, anger, and ignorance [of sentient beings]. “Delusion and falling into the evil realm” (Due to delusion and falling into the evil destinies): Falling into the three evil realms. "The water of great compassion, escape from suffering and attain enlightenment" means that by using the water of great compassion to wash like that, you will be pure. That is the wheel of great compassion.

(Sutra) Phuc Thu, good man! Bodhisattva Mahasattva has the power to lead and transform the immeasurable and limitless space of the great assembly, from the unobstructed, to completely explain the Buddha Dharma, all the samāsamās, all the dharanis, solidly Great Forbearance, Great Armor and Pillars. The Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat has accomplished the test of the wheel, with the initial development of the mind, the five stages of desire have the ability to eliminate, transcending all the Sravakas, the Single Enlightened Ones, the universal taste, all the Sravakas, the Single Enlightened Ones, creating a great field of blessings, the Sravakas, the Single Enlightened Vehicles of the first level, making offerings, serving, and protecting.
(Sutra: Come here, good man! Bodhisattva Ma Ha The Bodhisattva also has the solid Wheel of Great Forbearance, the Great Armor, which can lead to boundless and boundless Words and Unobstructed Understandings of all Buddha Dharma, all kinds of samadhi, and vast dharanis throughout space. If a Bodhisattva achieves this wheel, from the beginning of his mind, all the five desires can be eliminated, surpassing all Sravakas and Single Enlightenment, because throughout all Sravakas and Single Enlightenment, he becomes a great Field of Merit (puṇyakṣetra), all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas. All Single Enlightened Ones should make offerings, take care of things, and protect them.)

This is the image of Dai Nhan Dai Giap Truc Luan, but before that there were so many more meanings, those meanings are very deep, here only the nouns are mentioned. That is all about the practice of Bodhisattvas from the Ten Grounds and above. They can use this type of Great Forbearance to create [those dharmas] throughout space. Nothingness is infinite, endless, immeasurable, limitless, vast, full of everything. The depths of space and the entire dharma realm are your tools to become Buddhas. “Extensive assembly” (Complete with all great things), complete with what? The cause becomes Buddha. You must definitely acknowledge this principle. Admitting that it is forbearance is not talking about forbearance! Tolerance here is “approval, recognition”. All words, language, and writing are just spoken words. In words, including the Word of Unrestrained Explanation, it means "capable of praising all Buddha Dharma". For all Buddha Dharma, there are no obstacles, giving birth to unsurpassed wonderful wisdom. Only then can it be acknowledged. Dwelling in the samadhi are all the Jīdhis, all the samādhis, “the dharanis” are the Total Recipients, “the sum of all dharmas, reciting immeasurable meanings”. This kind of achievement of Great Forbearance, Great Armor Pillar, compared to the Great Armor Pillar of all Thanh Van and Doc Giac, is superior to them, they don't know it, and they don't seek it either.

So as soon as Thanh Van and Doc Giac hear that the Buddhist path is so long, fear and regression will arise in their minds. They see that saving sentient beings is so miserable! They see living beings as real, see all dharmas as truly existing, contemplate themselves as selfless, becoming empty, but they cannot know that living beings and themselves are the same, everything is empty. Therefore, there is no great compassion, nor is there great patience. Therefore, as soon as the Bodhisattva develops his mind, he can go far beyond the Shravakas. Pratyekabuddha, can create a field of great blessings for all Sravakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

(Kinh) Vân hà Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát năng dẫn biến mãn hư không, vô lượng, vô biên quảng đại chúng cụ, Từ Vô Ngại Giải, nhất thiết Phật pháp, chư tam-ma-địa, chư đà-la-ni kiên cố Đại Nhẫn Đại Giáp Trụ Luân? Vị chư Bồ Tát ư nhất thiết pháp, thẩm đế chiếu sát, như minh nguyệt quang biến mãn hư không. Kỳ tâm bình đẳng, vô y, vô tướng, vô trụ, vô nhiễm, phổ ư nhất thiết tam-ma-địa môn, đà-la-ni môn, tâm vô hành động. Ư chư nhãn sắc, nhãn thức, nhãn xúc, ly ý nhiễm trước, tâm vô hành động. Ư nhãn xúc duyên, sanh nội tam thọ, hoặc lạc, hoặc khổ, hoặc phi khổ lạc, tâm thường tịch định, vô sở thủ trước. Ư chư nhĩ thanh, nhĩ thức, nhĩ xúc, ư chư tỵ hương, tỵ thức, tỵ xúc, ư chư thiệt vị, thiệt thức, thiệt xúc, ư chư thân xúc, thân thức, thân xúc, ư chư ý pháp, ý thức, ý xúc, quảng thuyết diệc nhĩ. Phổ ư nhất thiết tâm ý thức trung, tâm thường tịch định, vô sở thủ trước. Ư tâm ý thức sở sanh tam thọ, hoặc lạc, hoặc khổ, hoặc phi khổ lạc, tâm thường tịch định, vô sở thủ trước. Phổ ư tam thế chư Uẩn, Giới, Xứ, nhất thiết phẩm loại, giai vô thủ trước, tâm vô hành động. Phổ ư nhất thiết tam giới, tam hạnh, tam xúc, tam thọ, tam căn, tam thừa, Tam Luật Nghi, Tam Giải Thoát, nhất thiết phẩm loại, kỳ tâm tịch tĩnh, vô trụ, vô tướng, vô sở thủ trước, bình đẳng nhi trụ. Phổ ư nhất thiết bố thí, tịnh giới, an nhẫn, tinh tấn, Tĩnh Lự, Bát Nhã Ba La Mật Đa, tâm vô hành động, tịch tĩnh nhi trụ. Như thị phổ ư Tứ Niệm Trụ, Tứ Chánh Đoạn, Tứ Thần Túc, Ngũ Căn, Ngũ Lực, Thất Đẳng Giác Chi, Bát Thánh Đạo Chi, tâm vô hành động, tịch tĩnh nhi trụ. Phổ ư nhất thiết Cửu Thứ Đệ Định, tâm vô hành động, tịch tĩnh nhi trụ. Hựu ư tam hạnh vô chướng pháp trí đạo chi, đạo thể sở dẫn tác dụng, giai vô thủ trước, tâm vô hành động. Ư A Lại Da, phi A Lại Da, hữu thủ, vô thủ, hữu lậu, vô lậu, thử ngạn, bỉ ngạn, tiểu đại vô lượng, tác dữ bất tác, thiện, ác, vô ký, chư phẩm loại trung, tâm vô hành động, tịch tĩnh nhi trụ. Phổ ư nhất thiết đại từ, đại bi, thiện xảo phương tiện thành thục hữu tình, nãi chí Thập Địa, tam bất hộ, tứ vô sở úy, nãi chí thập bát bất cộng Phật pháp, nhất thiết phẩm loại, giai vô thủ trước, tâm vô hành động, tịch tĩnh nhi trụ.
(Kinh: Thế nào là Đại Nhẫn Đại Giáp Trụ Luân kiên cố có thể dẫn khởi vô lượng vô biên trọn đủ các thứ Từ Vô Ngại Giải đối với hết thảy Phật pháp, các tam-ma-địa, các đà-la-ni rộng lớn trọn khắp hư không? Tức là các Bồ Tát đối với hết thảy các pháp, suy xét, chiếu soi kỹ càng, như quang minh của vầng trăng sáng trọn khắp hư không. Tâm Ngài bình đẳng, chẳng nương tựa, vô tướng, vô trụ, vô nhiễm, trọn khắp hết thảy các tam-ma-địa môn và đà-la-ni môn, tâm chẳng hành động. Đối với các sắc thấy bởi mắt, nhãn thức, nhãn xúc, lìa ý đắm nhiễm, tâm chẳng hành động. Đối với nhãn xúc duyên sanh ba thứ cảm thọ bên trong, hoặc lạc, hoặc khổ, hoặc chẳng khổ lạc, tâm thường tịch định, chẳng chấp giữ gì. Đối với các tiếng nghe bởi tai, nhĩ thức, nhĩ xúc, đối với các thứ mùi ngửi bởi mũi, tỵ thức, tỵ xúc, đối với các vị nếm bởi lưỡi, thiệt thức, thiệt xúc, đối với các sự đụng chạm nơi thân, thân thức, thân xúc, đối với các pháp tiếp nhận bởi ý, ý thức, ý xúc, nói rộng thì cũng đều như thế. Trong khắp hết thảy tâm, ý, thức, tâm thường tịch định, chẳng chấp giữ gì. Đối với ba thứ cảm thọ sanh bởi tâm, ý, thức, hoặc lạc, hoặc khổ, hoặc chẳng khổ lạc, tâm thường tịch định, chẳng chấp giữ gì. Đối với khắp hết thảy các phẩm loại thuộc các Uẩn, Giới, Xứ trong ba đời, đều chẳng chấp giữ, tâm chẳng hành động. Đối với trọn khắp hết thảy tam giới, tam hạnh, tam xúc, tam thọ, tam căn, tam thừa, Tam Luật Nghi, Tam Giải Thoát, hết thảy phẩm loại, tâm Bồ Tát tịch tĩnh, vô trụ, vô tướng, chẳng chấp giữ gì, bình đẳng mà trụ. Đối với trọn khắp hết thảy bố thí, tịnh giới, an nhẫn, tinh tấn, Tĩnh Lự, Bát Nhã Ba La Mật Đa, tâm chẳng hành động, tịch tĩnh mà trụ. Đối với trọn khắp Tứ Niệm Trụ, Tứ Chánh Đoạn, Tứ Thần Túc, Ngũ Căn, Ngũ Lực, Thất Đẳng Giác Chi, Bát Thánh Đạo Chi như thế, tâm chẳng hành động, tịch tĩnh mà trụ. Đối với trọn khắp hết thảy Cửu Thứ Đệ Định, tâm chẳng hành động, tịch tĩnh mà trụ. Lại đối với tác dụng dẫn khởi bởi tam hạnh, trí chẳng chướng ngại pháp, Đạo Chi, và đạo thể, đều chẳng chấp giữ, tâm chẳng hành động. Đối với A Lại Da, chẳng phải A Lại Da, có lấy, chẳng lấy, hữu lậu, vô lậu, bờ này, bờ kia, nhỏ, lớn, vô lượng, làm và chẳng làm, thiện, ác, chẳng thiện chẳng ác, trong các phẩm loại, tâm chẳng hành động, tịch tĩnh mà trụ. Đối với trọn khắp hết thảy phương tiện đại từ, đại bi, thiện xảo thành thục hữu tình, cho đến Thập Địa, ba thứ chẳng hộ trì, bốn điều chẳng sợ hãi, cho đến mười tám pháp bất cộng trong Phật pháp, hết thảy phẩm loại đều chẳng chấp giữ, tâm chẳng hành động, tịch tĩnh mà trụ).

“Vị chư Bồ Tát ư nhất thiết pháp, thẩm đế chiếu sát” (Tức là các vị Bồ Tát đối với hết thảy các pháp bèn suy xét, chiếu soi): Suy xét, thẩm định dựa trên đế lý chân thật, quán chiếu một phen. “Sát” là xem xét. “Chiếu” là trí huệ chiếu soi. Trí huệ đã chiếu xong, phải tư duy, thẩm sát (thẩm định, suy xét) chân thật. Chiêm Sát là sau khi quý vị “bói toán” xong, phải thẩm định, tư duy chân thật, suy xét xem [kết quả chiêm sát] có ăn khớp hay không. Chiêm Sát Luân nói như thế đó. “Ăn khớp” tức là có tương ứng hay không? Thẩm định kỹ càng, suy xét như thế thì sẽ thành tựu Đại Giáp Trụ Luân.

Observe and consider what shape it will really look like? Like the light of the radiant moon, like the full moon of August, when the sky is cloudless, filling all of space. The light of the moon is equal, not saying "I shine here, I don't shine there". There is no such distinction! Like the light of a lamp, does it discriminate? Does it only reflect me, you, and not others? It doesn't think that way. He has expanded his wisdom, like a lamp. This is to use an example to show the principle of the Dharma, the Bodhisattva's mind is equality. “Unsupported” (without reliance), what does one rely on to be born? No! After being born, what will it look like? No!

“Without clothes, without form” where does it reside? Is there a country or not? No! “Unattached” means “no attachment”. All are not attached. If everything has no attachments then it is immaculate. We see light, such as sunlight, people wearing sunglasses. Whatever color sunglasses you wear, you will see that color outside. Light has no color, but comes from our own discriminating mind. Why do you differentiate? The eye facing the scene, the eye is the Base; Then, in front of external form, there will arise a discriminating consciousness. That's called the eighteen precepts, that's not called dharani; Please understand this meaning. The mind is equal, has no dependence, has no form, does not dwell, is not contaminated, pervades all samadhis and dharanis, the mind does not act. Abiding in a state of tranquility, that is Suchness. Nhu Nhu means “immobile”. Therefore, we recite ten names of the Buddha, one of which is Tathagata. As if immovable, Lai is for the benefit of sentient beings. Benefiting sentient beings does not touch His essence at all, nor does it have the appearance of benefiting sentient beings. That is Such, coming is Such, going is also Such. Going and coming are both Suchness, there is no appearance of coming or going. That's the meaning.

Next, to elaborate, “the eyes of form, the eyes of consciousness, the eyes of contact” [meaning] with respect to Form, our eyeballs must definitely face Form. Form is the form of the external realm. Eye Consciousness is discrimination, Touch is contact. Every apartment is like that. When in contact, Consciousness makes absolutely no distinction. To give an example, there are times when our eyes are facing objects, when we are awake and not paying attention, that is also when our mind is focused on one scene. Reciting the Buddha's name is to make you concentrate on one scene. When other realms appear, you don't have any feelings, no thoughts arise, that is, you focus on that scene.

If our mind, speaking in worldly language, would be “highly focused”; While your thoughts are highly concentrated, focused, people will see you sitting there with eyes wide open, people will come into your house, you still won't see them. Entering the house and walking around, to the place where you took things and left, you still didn't see them, because you were paying attention, looked but didn't see, looked but didn't see, that's the meaning. When we concentrate on one scene, it causes us to recite to the point where our mind is not disturbed, that is, to the point where all the worldly scenes cannot be disturbed. If you focus on one scene, you will focus on it and become attached to that scene. The eyes are like that, but so are the ears, nose, tongue, and body.

The next part of the text repeats: The mind is not passive, but whenever the eyes come into contact with external conditions, it will give birth to Feelings (feelings), including Internal Feelings, External Feelings, and Cau Thos (both internal and external feelings), three types of feelings. When feeling, either suffering, or pleasure, or neither pain nor pleasure, these are three types [of feeling]. Feelings upon contact are those three types. Why? His mind is often calm, He is in Concentration. There is no such idea, there is no distinction, neither good nor accepted, nor bad. He is neither good nor bad. Good or bad depends on our discriminating mind. “For the sounds heard by the ear, the ear consciousness, the ear contact, for the smell smelled by the nose, the nose consciousness, the nose contact), the nose smells fragrant, rotten, until the tongue, “the taste, the tongue consciousness, the tongue contact” (the taste tasted by the tongue, the tongue consciousness, the tongue contact), until “the body contacts, body consciousness, body contact, all dharmas of mind, consciousness, mind contact, heron ears" (for the touching of the body, body consciousness, body contact. For the dharmas felt by mind, consciousness, mind contact, broadly speaking, it is the same). That being said, they are grouped into eighteen categories. In the Great Wisdom Treatise, each type is mentioned, all are overlapping. Why such overlap? Hope you pay attention! The first time, you don't hear clearly, the second time you don't hear clearly, the third time, six senses, six consciousnesses, six sense objects, eighteen precepts, say it eighteen times, you will remember clearly, that's the meaning! Coordinate with the six senses. Having finished speaking, take the six senses and coordinate them [with each sense]. Having finished speaking, again bring the six consciousnesses together [with the senses and objects]. The eighteen precepts are said eighteen times. After that, I tell you the twelve Places again, eyes enter into Form, ears enter into Sound... Say it again!

You clearly understand the meaning! Thus, because you reach non-discrimination, it makes you enter samadhi, makes you carefully consider entering samadhi. After you have considered and attained dharani, the first step is discrimination. After distinguishing, one reaches non-discrimination, not accepting, not holding on to those realms. “Without clinging to anything. U the conscious mind gives birth to three feelings, either pleasure, pain, or non-suffering pleasure” (No attachment to anything. For the three types of feelings born from mind, mind, consciousness, either pleasure, or pain, or no pain or pleasure): The mind is always calm, not subject to rotating scenes, but the mind can change scenes. He talked about Concentration, that still cannot be changed. The Shurangama Sutra can still be transformed, meaning that all appearances of the external realm can be transformed into one's own mind. There is no dharma that is not born of the mind. Even the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind, form, sound, smell, touch, dharma, up to Eye Consciousness, Ear Consciousness, Snake Consciousness... [are all] just one thought like that. That is, our present thought, no matter how busy the external world is, all kinds of thoughts arise inside, all of which are just one thing, the mind.

“The mind is always calm, with no pre-attachment, universal in the three worlds of Aggregates, Precepts, and Places, of all types, with no pre-attachment” (The mind is always calm, not clinging to anything, with respect to all the qualities of the Aggregates, Worlds, and Places in the three lifetimes, there is no attachment): Not only is the present life, but neither the past nor the future holds. Not keeping the tainted dharma, nor keeping the pure dharma, all the stories of Buddha and Bodhisattva's teachings in India are basically non-existent, not kept, and not grasped. Because whenever there is purity, there will be impurity; if there is good, there will definitely be its counterpart which is bad. Wherever there is big, there will definitely be small. There is long and there is short. Big, small, long, short, square, round, it's all like that. All dharmas are like that. “Universally, the three realms, the three conducts, the three emotions, the three feelings, the three senses, the three vehicles, the Three Disciplines, the Three Liberations, the three qualities, the mind is at peace” (For all the qualities in the three realms, the three conducts, the three contacts, the three feelings, the three senses, the three vehicles, the Three Rules of Doubt, the Three Liberations, the mind is calm): Understand clearly and clearly, do not give rise to discrimination, do not give rise to attachments, are not confused. stuff. If you're in a deep sleep and don't know anything, that's a different story. Understand clearly, have no attachments, nothing is good, nothing is bad, nothing is the holy path, nothing is the ordinary path, nothing is the six paths, the mind has no attachments, does not dwell in formlessness.

“Without holding on to anything, standing on equality” (Standing on nothing, holding on to equality): Equality. What is equality? Because of the egalitarian mind, then give alms, maintain precepts, be patient, be diligent, practice Concentration, Prajna, practice Tinh Lu; That is Paramita Meditation. That is Luc Do's ten thousand virtues. As for those things, all of them do not move, they remain calm and still. As for the Four Pillars of Mindfulness, the Four Right Paradigms, the Four Divine Supplies, the Five Faculties, the Five Strengths, the Seven Factors of Enlightenment, and the Eight Noble Paths, the mind does not act, remains calm and remains. That is, both good and evil are lost, mind and conduct are destroyed, until the Ninefold Determination. "The mind does not act, it is calm and abides. Huu The three actions, the unobstructed dharma wisdom, the path factor, the path body that leads the effect, the stage has no preoccupation" (The mind does not act, it is calm but stays. As for the effects that arise from the knowledge of the unobstructed dharma on the three actions, the path factor, the path body, there is no attachment): Not only to the tainted dharma, but also to the pure dharma, there is no attachment in the mind.

“ U A Lai Da, non-A Lai Da, with-hand, without-hand” (As for the Store of Consciousness, it is not the Store of Consciousness, it holds, it does not hold), they do not exist. “Being asrava, no asrava, testing the bank, the other bank, small, great, immeasurable, doing no evil, doing no harm, good, evil, indeterminate” (Being asrava, no asrava, this shore, that shore, small, big, immeasurable, doing and not doing, good, evil, neither good nor evil): Those are the three natures. "In the middle grades, the mind is inactive, the mind is calm and still, it abides with universal kindness and great compassion, and is skillful in means to mature sentient beings" (Among the grades, the mind is inactive and calm but abides. Using all the skillful means, great compassion, and great compassion to mature sentient beings): Being calm but remaining, is not like the Second Vehicle, once entering Nirvana, it will be motionless. He will give rise to the skillful means of great love and compassion to mature sentient beings. In the previous section, we talked about contaminated dharma and pure dharma; [To those dharmas], He has no attachment. If you don't have attachments, is it an act of great kindness and compassion? Unlike the Second Vehicle, His mind is always in Concentration. When Buddhas and Bodhisattvas benefit sentient beings, we know that Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) appears in many bodies in this world, there is no place where Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva does not appear. [But] before now, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has never come, never came to this world. His essence is still in the world of Ultimate Bliss, unmoving in its original nature but pervading all places, benefiting sentient beings. Although it benefits all sentient beings, it does not change the original nature. Śākyamuni Buddha had never been to [Sa Ba world], the god [who served as a donor to offer food every day] answered [Mr. Dao Tuyen] like that!

But we see it, think it's true! Suppose our feelings are like this: When we gather, the people we like and the people we love are often together, always in high spirits. Whenever you are separated, or separated for a short time, or separated for a long time, or die, you cry bitterly. If you remember everything in your mind all day long, you will be attached to everything, you will not be able to be liberated, you will not know that all dharmas are like that. Therefore, we must practice Contemplation a lot. All the actions, nothing entered the mind, matured sentient beings like that, becoming the Bodhisattva of the Ten Grounds. The "Three Unprotected" is the Buddha who does not need to protect his body, mouth, and mind, because he does not have the slightest evil! “All kinds of qualities, the stage has no grasping, the mind does not act, calm and still abides” (All the qualities are not accepted, the mind does not act, calm and still abides). That is the Bodhisattva's Ring of Rings.

(Sutra) Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, due to the trial of rotation, has eternal energy, that is, he can eliminate the past three lifetimes, and is eternally destroyed. necessarily distinguish, can permanently separate from necessarily Dharma General. Retaining the power of abiding can lead to the eyes of the empty space, the samamas, the dharanis, the Skillful Convenience of the Great Armor Wheel. The Bodhisattva abides like the eternal wheel, necessarily leading to the end of evil and unwholesome karma in the past, countless evil beings, beings, animals, death and birth, all karma, the ability to be eliminated, the spirit to be exhausted without residue, and to receive no retribution.
(Sutra: Bodhisattva Mahasattva because this wheel can forever eliminate the mistakes of the three kind of feeling, can forever destroy all distinctions, can forever be separated from all dharma. LWho can abide in the Wheel of Skill and Convenience, the Great Armor Pillar, can give rise to all emptiness eyes, samadhis, and dharanis After all, the evil destiniess are not leisurely, the realms, paths, and karma of birth and death that originate from the past can all be completely eliminated, there will be no residue left, and there will be no retribution.)

This Ring of Rings "has the eternal ability to eliminate the three feelings beyond seven" (can permanently eliminate all kinds of mistakes in the three types of feelings): Painful Feeling, Pleasure Feeling, Neither Suffering nor Pleasure Feeling do not exist; That kind of mistake will never happen. In the previous section, we talked about “thirteen mistakes” that are more numerous than this type of mistake. [Due to cultivating this Ring of Patience], they all become calm, can be forever extinguished, and all discriminatory thoughts do not arise. “Ability to permanently separate from all dharma appearances” (Ability to permanently separate from all dharma appearances): What we arise are all dharma appearances, they are all nouns. Nouns basically do not exist, nouns are pseudo-names that are created. How do we say Five Aggregates, No Liberation Gate, “Emptiness”? “No Form”: “No Form” has no form. Vo Tac basically doesn't do anything, what other form does it have? Therefore, it is called the Three Liberation Gate. No Wishing means not having any wish, not asking for anything. “Pray” is a request. Nowadays we "don't ask for anything" and you can't do it. We still hope and pray to follow this holy scene and destroy that evil scene, but we know: To reach the ultimate point, we must have no wishes and no desires.

“Abiding in the function of abiding, it is possible to guide all the emptiness eyes, samamas, dharanis Skillful Means Great Armor Pillar” (Again, being able to abide in the Skillful Means Great Armor Pillar can give rise to all emptiness eyes, the samadhi, dharanis): This Great Armor Pillar is to abide in skillful means, benefiting sentient beings. Regarding the noun “empty eye”, what else does empty space have? Does nothingness still have eyes? Do you still have eyes? This is a visual way of speaking, using the visualization method to describe. The idea is that all the samāma-grounds, all the dharanis, up to the skillful means, will enable all sentient beings to achieve. If "Bodhisattva abides in such a wheel" (Bodhisattva abides in such a wheel), do we need to repent for all the unwholesome evil karma that originated from the past? Must repent like that. All evil and unwholesome karma in the past that have not yet been purified have now been completely purified. “Infinite” means that when you practice, your body cannot relax. “Unlimited” means to suffer endlessly. When practicing, there is no time to practice! Now, after believing in Buddha, everyone feels that time is not enough. Why is it not enough? Because worldly dharmas take up a lot of your time, because your mind is always busy with those things. If you can't let it go, of course there won't be enough time. Interested in having fun, going out all day and night. You can play mahjong for days or nights without feeling tired. When traveling, they can visit everywhere. That is, we are crazy, worthy of being called “crazy beings”, but when the evil destinies comes, everything is gone! Next, [the scriptures] talk about evil dharma, speaking in terms of the world, all of these things are completely gone. What retributions do you still have to endure? Retribution is non-existent, empty, without cause, without effect. At that time, I practiced this Contemplation method, but this Contemplation method came from "cause and effect". Therefore, when studying the Sutra on Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma, the first half of the book talks about contemplation of the wheel of life, the second half of the book says completely different things. Two concepts, two feelings, absolutely different. This sutra is the same, the first part talks about ten evil wheels and ten good wheels; Currently talking about the ten chakras of the Bodhisattva. That is the Bodhisattva who ultimately becomes a Buddha.

(Sutra) Good man! For example, if the world's fire disaster arises, the five days appear, the world will necessarily have small ponds, big ponds, small rivers, big rivers, small seas, great oceans, and the water level will dry up and be destroyed without any residue. Such a Bodhisattva has the ability to guide and pervade the emptiness, immeasurable and boundless, and the vast masses of people are able to understand the boundless wisdom of the Buddha Dharma, all the samāma-grounds, all the dharanis, and solidify the wheel of great forbearance and great armor. The energy of abiding by the ability to guide the eye of the empty space, the samama-grounds, the dharanis, the Skillful Means of Great Armor, the Wheel, necessarily leads to the eradication of evil, unwholesome karma, infinite evil beasts, beings, animals, death and birth, all karmas, the stage of destruction, the soul ends without residue, and receives no retribution. Good man! For example, at the beginning of the world's water disaster, the three thousand great thousand worlds, the small worlds, the four great continents, the eighty thousand small continents, the Dieu Cao mountain king, and the mountain ranks, the stages of the foggy water are completely extinguished, and the spirit has no residue. Such a Bodhisattva has the ability to guide and pervade the emptiness, immeasurable, boundless and vast masses of people, From the Unobstructed Understanding, all Buddha Dharma, the samāma-grounds, the dharanis, solidify the Wheel of Great Forbearance, Great Armor. The energy of abiding by the ability to guide the eye of the empty space, the samāṇas, the dharanis, the Skillful Means of Convenience, the Great Armor Pillar, necessarily leads to the eradication of evil and unwholesome karma in the past, the infinite evil beasts, the beings, the beasts, the karma of death and birth, the stage of destruction, the soul ends without residue, and receives no retribution.
(Sutra: Come here, good man! Like the world on fire The disaster is about to rise, the five suns appear together, all the small ponds, large ponds, small rivers, large rivers, small seas, large seas in the world, the water will dry up, completely extinguished, there will be no more left. In the same way, the Bodhisattva who achieves Great Forbearance, the Great Armor of the Solid Wheel, can give rise to boundless, boundless, all kinds of vast and boundless Understandings for all Buddha Dharma, samadhis, and dharanis throughout space. Also, being able to abide in the skillful means of the Great Armor Pillar, can give rise to all the emptiness eyes, samadhis, dharanis, all unwholesome evil karma, evil destiniess that are not at ease, all realms, paths, and karma of birth and death that have arisen from the past can all be completely eliminated, without remaining, without receiving retribution. Again, good man! world, when water disasters arise, in this three thousand great thousand worlds, the small worlds, each of the four great continents, eighty thousand small continents, Lord Dieu Cao's mountain, and the mountains are all crushed and destroyed by ash water, with no residue left. In the same way, the Bodhisattva achieves the solid Great Ring of Great Forbearance, able to give rise to limitless, boundless, complete and vast Infinite Understandings of the Buddha Dharma, the samadhis, the complete dharanis. throughout the void. You can also abide in the Great Armored Wheel of Skillful Means, can give rise to all the empty eyes, the samadhis, the dharanis, all the unwholesome evil karmas that have not yet been exhausted, the evil destiniess that are not leisurely, the realms, the paths, the birth and death karmas that originate from the past, can all be completely eliminated, without remaining, without receiving retribution).

For example, in this world, when it is not yet time for the world to end, if a fire breaks out, this world will begin to be destroyed. When the five suns rise together, five suns appear in the sky. At that time, “small river, big river, small sea, big sea” (small river, big river, small sea, big sea). The ocean is the ocean. “The water phase is dry” (The water is all dry), dry, completely destroyed, not even a single drop of water remains. Buddha pointed out: When this world is destroyed, five suns appear, so all small ponds, large ponds, all places with water in the world will dry up. When the Bodhisattva achieves Great Forbearance, the Great Armor Pillar has all kinds of Unobstructed Words as vast as space. He can also cause all the evil and unwholesome karma in the past that have not yet completely disappeared from sentient beings, or the karmic obstacles "death here, birth there, death there, birth here" can all be eliminated, and still not receive retribution, just like when the five suns appeared, the world was destroyed, not even a drop of water was left! We say that Mount Tu Di and the seven ranges of Kim Son [surrounding Tu Di] are incredibly solid, but when faced with water disasters, even gold is ruined. Do you believe it or not? That's karma, soaking in water for a long time will naturally rot. Fire disasters are the same, as soon as the fire burns, it will no longer exist. When the three disasters occur, when the wind blows, [everything] will return to nothingness. All established things are in emptiness. On the void is the water wheel, on the water wheel the so-called earth is maintained. Everyone who reads the World Accomplishment chapter in the Avatamsaka Sutra, [will see] how the world is achieved? In the void.

Currently, science has proven; nebula in the air forming a sphere. After that, that sphere gradually had people living like that, and then it was destroyed again. Destructive then becomes again, becomes then perishes again, perishes then becomes again, infinitely, endlessly, continuously and endlessly like that. The first great disaster is a fire, that fire burns everything into butter (lava), and as soon as the water is submerged, it immediately turns to mush. Once it's mushy, it's very much like soft butter. As soon as the wind blows, it's thrown into the air, everything is gone!

For example, when a water disaster occurs in the world, the three thousand worlds, the small worlds, the four great continents [in each of those worlds], eighty thousand small continents, the mountain lord Dieu Cao, that is, Mount Tu Di, and the mountains are all absorbed by the water and destroyed, soaked and rotten by the water. We see that the rock is hard, but the rock is constantly soaked by water and will gradually wear away, so we don't see it. Water drops [down the terrace] from the terrace roof, the water is very soft, when it rains, [the terrace roof] drips a few drops. If water drips for a long time, there will be a few small gaps under the porch steps. Drops of water falling from soft terraces can wear down hard tiles. That's called “soft grinding hard”. Don't get angry, being soft is much more beneficial than being tough. Think about this principle, it can be explained!

(Sutra) Good man! For example, darkness permeates the void, the light of day appears, and the power of eradication occurs. Such an accomplished Bodhisattva has the ability to lead and transform the boundless, boundless space of the vast assembly, from the Unrestrained Understanding, all Buddha Dharma, the Samamas, the Dharanis, solidly Great Forbearance, Great Armor, and Pillars. The ability to abide in the universe can lead to the eyes of the empty space, the samāṇas, the dharanis, the Skillful Means and Means of the Great Armor Pillar, to generate boundless emptiness and sun wisdom, the ability to eternally eliminate the darkness of the Four Islands of ignorance, to necessarily lead the past to the end of evil, unwholesome karma, the infinite evil beasts, the beings, the beasts, the karma of death and birth, the ability to destroy, the soul to have no residue, to receive no retribution. Due to trying, the Buddha Dharma, monks and monks develop freedom, always without turning back, not surrendering to the evil forces of action, often attaining the view of all Buddhas, including Bodhisattvas, Shravaka disciples, not leaving the Dharma, not being close to them, and making offerings to the Sangha. With all the merits, the mind is always without aversion, the desire for Bodhi is always uninterrupted. Huu often never abandons the thought of reciting the Buddha's name, his long-suffering dreams remain, and the heron disappears temporarily.
(Sutra: Come here, good man! For example, darkness is everywhere In the void, when the sun rises brightly, all [darkness] is eliminated. In the same way, the Bodhisattva who achieves the Great Ring of Great Patience is solid and can give rise to all kinds of boundless and vast Enlightenment from all Buddhadharmas, samadhis, and dharanis throughout the entire space. The wheel can lead to all the empty eyes, samadhis, and dharanis, to give rise to the boundless sun of wisdom in the sky, to forever eliminate the four delusions of ignorance and darkness within oneself, to all unwholesome evil karmas that have arisen from the past that have not yet been eliminated, to evil destiniess that are not leisurely, to realms, to paths, to birth and death karma, all of which can be completely eliminated, with no remaining, no fruit. Like that, it is very easy to fall into decline; Why will it decline? Because that person hopes to gain something; At that time, because we did not achieve it [so we were disappointed and depressed]. If that person has no inherent possession, will never have a mind of regress, and does not expect to achieve anything, then what we do is right. That person's thoughts do not have a depraved mind. If discrimination arises, thinking there is something to gain but does not achieve it, that person will regress.

I sometimes think, having been a monk for more than sixty years, during that time I encountered some obstacles, but what have I achieved in Buddhism? Achieved nothing! “ At that time, the World-Honored One repeatedly demonstrated the meaning, and recited: - Desire becomes all dharma objects, necessarily eliminating afflictions, constantly entering the Emptiness, all things are unproblematic" (At that time, the World-Honored One re-displayed that meaning, then spoke verses and chanted: - If you want to become all dharma objects, destroy all afflictions, often enter the Emptiness, everything is not difficult to do): Show all the signs. Even though it displays all appearances, it destroys all appearances and shows the True Emptiness. What is that? It is the Perfect Contemplation of True Emptiness in the Avatamsaka Sutra, the True Contemplation of Thien Thai Four Teachings; Emptiness, Falsehood, and Neutrality are cultivating True Emptiness Contemplation. “For the sake of breaking the bonds of existence” (Because of cutting off the bondages in the realms of existence), the three realms all have bondage. Thus, one often “needs to practice the Dang Tri” (diligently practice the Dang Tri), often diligently cultivates that samadhi, all dharmas are equal. Reciting all meanings, reciting a single thought of your own mind, your mind is always equal. “Merit, Corresponding Concentration” (Corresponding Merit and Concentration): If you attain this type of Concentration, this type of merit compared to the Concentration you achieve, the two sides correspond, there can be no mistake! Merit is Concentration, Concentration is merit, but there is no merit, nothing is Concentration. “Surely attaining wisdom that is difficult to imagine” (Surely attaining wisdom that is difficult to imagine), that is to say, achieving merit. Having attained concentration, one can still attain wisdom, attaining inconceivable wisdom. “Inconceivable” (Hard to think) is inconceivable. If you want to practice Tranquility, practice Concentration, a thousand times, leave Form. Tinh Lu is Formless, without all forms, practicing Tinh Lu leaves all forms.

This is called “Destroying Concentration of True Emptiness”, cultivating the Absolute Cessation of Concentration, the form of emptiness is absolute, all forms are no longer there. At that time, in Concentration, the supreme wisdom of reciting the Buddha's name arises, destroying all evil, using True Emptiness Contemplation to destroy all conditioned dharmas. Existence is the same, and Non-existence is the same. Existence is the equivalent of non-existence, which is not true emptiness at all. Use Void Contemplation to destroy that Existence and Nothingness. That Existence and Non-existence is, on the one hand, the permanent dharma, and on the other, the cessation of dharma. Existence is permanent law, Non-existence is cessation. True Emptiness is not like that, True Emptiness can give birth to Miraculous Existence. Dieu Huu is not Phi Huu, Phi Huu is True Emptiness. True Emptiness is non-empty, that is, Wonderful Existence, which is also the attainment of all signs of merit. What does the Buddha's merits look like? Dieu Huu non-existence!

“If you practice Chan Emptiness Contemplation well, you need to practice all good dharmas, make offerings to all Buddhas, and quickly attain Buddhahood” (If you practice Chan Emptiness Contemplation diligently, diligently practice all good dharmas, make offerings to all Buddhas, you will quickly attain Buddhahood): If you practice Chan Emptiness Absolutely Perfect Contemplation, you can diligently practice all good dharmas, and not dwell in Emptiness at all. That Emptiness is not non-existent. [If you understand Emptiness as nothing], that is not correct. Only if you can skillfully practice Chan Emptiness Contemplation will you be able to diligently practice good dharmas; That's called cultivating the Four Contemplations of True Perfection, relying on the principle of Emptiness to give rise to all things. That's the principle of unobstructed things. The dharmas practiced are called "good dharmas". Use this to make offerings to Buddha, use the dharma to make offerings to all Buddhas, and achieve Buddhahood very quickly. For the sake of friends and sentient beings, eliminate afflictions. Only then will you have great power and be able to reflect on the sentient beings related to you, causing diseases and afflictions to be eliminated and to save them.

“ Quickly abide in the pure Buddha land” (Quickly abide in the pure Buddha land): To be born in the pure Buddha land, where one can “achieve great Bodhi”, all living beings are like the Buddha, seeing all living beings are Buddhas. “Pervasive Buddhaland” (Complete in the Buddhaland): All sentient beings in that pure Buddhaland become Buddhas. Thus "the stage of seeking the Buddha Vehicle, separating from the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment" (all progress towards seeking the Buddha Vehicle, leaving the Sravaka Vehicle and the Single Enlightenment Vehicle), leaving the position of the Second Vehicle and seeking to become a Buddha. Wait until I finish talking about the Chuc Luy chapter, I will come back and talk a little about cultivating the Book of Contemplation, counting as we reach perfection.

Phục hữu vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh, văn Phật sở thuyết, giai đắc tối thượng A La Hán quả. Phục hữu vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh, văn Phật sở thuyết, tâm cầu xuất ly tam giới lao ngục, y Phật xuất gia, thú nhập chánh pháp.
