Do thử chánh kiến, trừ diệt nhất thiết vãng ác thú nhân, phiền não ác nghiệp, tăng trưởng nhất thiết hướng thiện thú nhân, chánh nguyện thiện nghiệp. Phục hữu vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh, văn Phật sở thuyết, giai thọ Tam Quy, an trụ Cận Sự, Cận Trụ tịnh giới, nhạo cúng dường Phật, nhạo thính văn pháp, nhạo phụng sự Tăng, trú dạ tinh cần, tằng vô giải phế. Phục hữu vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh, văn Phật sở thuyết, viễn ly nhất thiết tà thú, tà quy, ác ý, ác nghiệp, ư Phật pháp trung, đắc quyết định tín, khí xả gia pháp, thanh tịnh xuất gia.
(Kinh: Khi đức Phật nói đại pháp môn như thế, trong chúng hội có các vị Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát nhiều như cát sông Hằng, trong quá khứ đã tu tập Niệm Phật tư duy từ lâu, nay nghe đức Thế Tôn nói về phương tiện Niệm Phật Tu Quán, đều đắc Niệm Phật tam-ma-địa môn. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe pháp ấy rồi, đều đắc Nhất Thiết Định Mạng Hoa Man Đà-la-ni môn. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, đều đắc hết thảy Thủ Lăng Già Ma Điện Quang Y Chỉ Đà-la-ni môn. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, đều đắc Nhất Thiết Pháp Tự Tại Chuyển Quang Minh Y Chỉ Thuận Nhẫn. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh, nghe đức Phật nói, xa lìa trần cấu, sanh pháp nhãn thanh tịnh trong các pháp, đắc quả Dự Lưu. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, đắc quả Nhất Lai. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh, nghe đức Phật nói, đắc quả Bất Hoàn. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, đều đắc tối thượng A La Hán quả. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, tâm cầu thoát lìa lao ngục tam giới, nương theo đức Phật xuất gia, tiến nhập chánh pháp. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, cho đến hết thọ mạng, an trụ trong Thập Thiện Nghiệp Đạo, nương theo Thanh Văn Thừa, phát tâm bất thoái. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, cho đến hết thọ mạng, an trụ trong Thập Thiện Nghiệp Đạo, nương theo Độc Giác Thừa, phát tâm bất thoái. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, cho đến hết thọ mạng, an trụ trong Thập Thiện Nghiệp Đạo, nương theo Đại Thừa, phát tâm A Nậu Đa La Tam Miệu Tam Bồ Đề, chẳng còn thoái chuyển. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, đắc chánh kiến thế gian. Do chánh kiến ấy, diệt trừ hết thảy các cái nhân, phiền não, và ác nghiệp tiến đến đường ác, tăng trưởng hết thảy cái nhân, chánh nguyện, và thiện nghiệp hướng vào đường lành. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật dạy, đều thọ Tam Quy, an trụ tịnh giới Cận Sự và Cận Trụ, thích cúng dường Phật, thích nghe pháp, thích phụng sự Tăng, ngày đêm siêng ròng, chưa từng lười nhác, bỏ phế. Lại có vô lượng vô biên chúng sanh nghe đức Phật nói, xa lìa hết thảy đường tà, quy y tà, ác ý, ác nghiệp. Trong Phật pháp, đạt được niềm tin quyết định, vứt bỏ pháp thế tục, thanh tịnh xuất gia).

Đây là phẩm cuối cùng của kinh Đại Tập Thập Luân, pháp hội tới đây đã viên mãn. Sau khi nghe pháp, những ai đạt được lợi ích? Cũng như thâu được hiệu quả gì? Điều thứ nhất, có bao nhiêu vị Bồ Tát trong đại chúng? Có các vị đại Bồ Tát nhiều như cát sông Hằng. Trong quá khứ, các Ngài đã học pháp môn Niệm Phật tư duy, Niệm Phật ở đây không nhất định là niệm A Di Đà Phật. Chữ Phật trong Niệm Phật ở đây là nói phổ quát. Phàm là [nói tới] Niệm Phật tức là nói theo ý nghĩa “hết thảy chư Phật”. Tu Niệm Phật Quán, dùng phương tiện tu Quán để xưng danh hiệu Phật, quán tưởng tượng Phật. Đấy là điều họ đã học trong quá khứ, ở trong pháp hội Đại Tập này, nghe giảng cách tư duy và quán tưởng Niệm Phật, họ đạt được lợi ích, nhập tam-ma-địa, đắc Niệm Phật tam-muội. Trong ấy, có khi là niệm Hóa Thân Phật, có khi là niệm Báo Thân Phật, có khi là niệm Pháp Thân Phật, tùy thuộc sức quán tưởng của chính mình mạnh hay yếu mà đạt được pháp môn cũng khác nhau. Đấy là nói về Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, họ đắc Niệm Phật tam-muội, nhập Niệm Phật tam-muội.

“To serve limitless and boundless sentient beings, the text shows the dharma, one will attain the All-Determining Life of the Flower Man Dà-la-ni-mon” (There are also boundless sentient beings who, after hearing this dharma, will all attain the All-Determining Life of the Flower Man Da-la-ni-mon): This is the name of the discipline. Dinh. All-Determining Life Flower Man Da-la-ni Mon is the name of another samadhi subject.

“To serve limitless and limitless sentient beings according to the Buddha's teachings, one will absolutely attain the Shurangama Demonic Power of Light and Medicine Da-lani Mon" (There are also boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha's teachings and attain all of the Shurangama Demonic Power of Light and Medicine Da-lani Mon): This Concentration is called [Prime] Mausoleum of the Demon Palace of Light Y Chi Da-la-ni.

“For the immeasurable and boundless sentient beings of the Buddha's teachings, one will attain the Complete Dharma of Freedom in Transforming Light and Clearness, Only with Patience and Patience” (Furthermore, there are boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha's teachings and all will attain the Omnipotent Dharma of Freedom in Transforming with Light and Clearness, with Patience and Patience): Only with Continuity and Forbearance is still Concentration. “Y is just patience” is the y refers to that Concentration, Just Concentration.

“There are boundless sentient beings according to Buddha's teachings, far removed from the world, in the midst of all dharmas, born of pure dharma eyes” (There are also limitless and boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha's words, separate from the worldly structure, and give birth to pure dharma eyes towards all dharmas): “Born pure dharma "eye" is the eye that achieves the pure dharma, that is, it has right knowledge, right view, without wrong knowledge or wrong views, it is also the end of false views. By listening to the Buddha's words, he attained Stream-Winning. The fruit of Stream Stream is the fruit of Sotapanna, which is the First Fruit.

“There are boundless sentient beings according to Buddha's teachings” (There are also boundless sentient beings who heard the Buddha speak): After that, they achieved the fruit of Once-returner. The result of Nhat Lai is Tu Da Ham, which means there is one more birth in the three realms of the human world; That's called Nhat Lai Fruit.

“To serve boundless sentient beings according to Buddha's teachings, attain the fruit of Non-returning” (There are also boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha's words and attain the fruit of non-returning): The fruit of non-returning is the fruit of Ana Ham, the third fruit.

“By serving boundless sentient beings according to Buddha's teachings, attain the ultimate Arhatship” (In addition, there are boundless sentient beings who hear the Buddha's words and attain the ultimate Arhatship), immediately attaining the Four Arahantships. In this Dharma assembly, the Buddha preached equality. This shows: Different fundamentals [even though listening to the same dharma], still achieve different results. Some people attain the First Fruits, some people attain the Four Fruits. There are sentient beings who hear the Buddha speak and can then abide in the mind of renunciation. What kind of divorce is that? Leaving the three worlds. When that person hears the Buddha preach the Dharma, his mind feels that this world is extremely impure, and a mind of boredom arises and he escapes from the prison of the three worlds, which also means becoming a monk. “To leave home and enter the Dharma” [means] following the Buddha to become a monk and enter the Dharma.

“Serve the boundless sentient beings of the Buddha's teachings, and forever abide in the Ten Good Karmas" (There are also boundless sentient beings who hear the Buddha's words, until the end of their lifespan, and abide in the Ten Good Karmas): From the time they hear the Dharma in the present until the end of their lifespan, that is, they have died, in time. During that time, that person never went against the Ten Virtuous Karmas. There are people who rely on the Shravaka Vehicle, develop Bodhi mind, know Suffering, cut off the Origins, admire Cessation, and practice the Way. Some people listen to the Single Sense Vehicle, practice the twelve causes and conditions, and study the dharma of cause and effect. There are boundless and limitless sentient beings "Buddha's teachings say, to abide in the Ten Good Karmas for the rest of their life" (listening to the Buddha's words, for the rest of their life, to abide in the Ten Good Karmas): "To abide in the Ten Good Karmas" means practicing the Ten Good Karmas. Practicing the Ten Virtues can be born in the human and celestial vehicle. There are also people who, after listening to the Dharma, rely on the Mahayana and develop the mind of Anuttara, Sammyak, and Bodhi, and never regress. Faith is steadfast, after listening to the Dharma, abide in the Mahayana, and develop the mind to become Buddha.

“There are boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha's teachings and attain the right view of the world” (There are also boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha and attain the right view of the world): That right view is not the worldly view, but the right view of the world. Right view is to distinguish between wrong and wrong, to distinguish between what is good and what is evil, what is correct, what is right knowledge and right view, and what is wrong knowledge and wrong view. If that person attains the right view, he will be able to eliminate all cause and effect and evil karma leading to evil destiniess. Eliminate the causes of afflictions and evil karma, you will not feel the results of suffering, you will not feel the negative effects of afflictions and evil karma, and all the causes will grow towards the good path. “Right vow of good karma”: That person's vow is to vow to practice good karma, not create evil karma.

“For the boundless sentient beings who read the Buddha's teachings, take the Three Refuges” (There are also boundless sentient beings who hear the Buddha's words and all receive the Three Refuges), that is, take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha. “Abiding in the pure precepts of Near Sus, Near Abiding” (Abiding in the pure precepts of Near Sustaining and Near Abiding): [The rules of] Near Sustaining, Near Abiding are the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts. The Pure Precepts are the Eight Precepts. “Laughing at making offerings to Buddha, mocking listening to Dharma texts” (Like making offerings to Buddha, liking listening to Dharma): Listening to sermons. “Serving the Sangha” [must be understood in a broad sense] is to love making offerings to the Three Jewels, following the Buddha to listen to the Dharma, following the Sangha to listen to the Dharma, being diligent day and night, not slacking off, “not letting go of the Sangha” (never relaxing or abandoning): After listening to the Dharma, achieving the effect of diligence.

“To serve limitless and boundless sentient beings, according to the Buddha's text, completely abandon evil beasts, evil refuges, evil intentions, evil karma” (There are also boundless sentient beings who listen to the Buddha's words, stay away from all evil destiniess, take refuge in evil thoughts, evil intentions, evil karma): Do not give rise to evil thoughts, do no more evil karma. “Being faithful to the Buddha Dharma, gaining decisive faith” (Achieving pure faith in the Buddha Dharma): Faith does not retreat. “Let go of the dharma, become pure as a monk” (Let go of the dharma at home, become a pure monk): “Renunciation” here does not mean attaining enlightenment, once you become a monk you still have to practice. In this dharma assembly, that is, the Great Assembly of the Ten Wheels, the Buddha spoke of several types of Ten Wheels, one is the Ten Wheels of the king, based on the world's dharma to represent the Buddha's Ten Wheels. And also talking about Existence and Non-existence. Non-existence means not having the Three Jewels to rely on; Therefore, if you create bad karma, you will receive retribution, you don't know which way to go! To wear is to rely on the Three Jewels, to not to wear is to refer to the Ten Evil Wheels. Huu Y refers to the Ten Virtuous Wheels. Finally, we talk about the Ten Wheels of the Bodhisattva. This sutra is called the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra. After everyone listens to the Dharma, they will gain different benefits. Even if one listens to the Dharma in the same place, the listener receives it differently, each person has different causes and conditions. Just like now, we have been preaching for more than two months, because it is not a daily preaching, but intermittent, we can listen to the entire sutra, not many people, all of which are interrupted.

What is the reason? Destiny is different. It's not like you want to interrupt at all. [When the cause and effect is ripe], even if you don't interrupt, you will be interrupted. Even if you want to be interrupted, you won't be interrupted! When the time comes [to meet the predestined conditions to listen to the sutra], you will come [to listen to the sutra lecture], everyone has their own predestined conditions! But we should understand that each person has their own karma, don't admire others and then yourself become depraved, and don't see another person have good karma and admire that person, it's not necessary! Each person creates their own cause, resulting in a separate result. That's what it means. Some people who listen to this sutra can attain unsurpassed samadhi. Some people, after listening to the sutra, accept the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts. Taking the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts is just sowing good roots. Quite a few Dharma friends have only recently received the Three Refuges, but without even listening to the sutras, they still receive the Three Refuges. That is a different cause and effect. All dharmas that are born of causes and conditions are not real!

After speaking this sutra, the Buddha advised, whom to entrust? Advise and entrust yourself to Void Tang. “Tang” means “to contain”. What does it contain? Nowhere! “No” then what else is there? “No” means there is no. “No” means hoping that we all clear away our afflictions, habits, and karma. Thanks to that name, we can explain. If all impurities, impurities, and filth are removed, only purity will remain. Purity is the merit of Dharmakaya. Now that we have heard, what benefits do people gain by studying together? In everyone's heart there is something to gain. Since the time the shaman Huyen Trang translated this sutra into Chinese, until now, no one has explained it. This is the first time we are teaching, there may be mistakes. If there is any mistake, please repent. We study this sutra together, it is still very difficult, everyone must develop their heart to be able to reach perfection. Today

now it is considered completed.

This sutra evokes us and tells us that in practice we must definitely abandon the Ten Evils and practice the Ten Virtues; At the very least, we should have that faith. Then, in daily life, do not show a fierce face to others, always have a smiling, happy face towards others. If others are very troubled, they will see that our attitude is very good, and the fire of their afflictions will subside. Suppose you get angry towards that person, including towards your own children and friends. People today, towards their own parents, often have the same expression towards their parents as the young monk towards the old monk, always so dissatisfied. That expression is like someone has a lot of money but doesn't give it to them, both sides can't talk! In Buddhism, [if you behave like that], you have broken the precepts. What precept is that? Everyone knows? Anger! The mind always creates an impure impression on others. Mouth uttering evil words and making false statements, these all belong to the Ten Evil Karmas. Because there is anger in the mind, the external appearance will naturally not be pleasing to the eye. That's of course! At that time, when discussing with others, the discussion is rarely successful!

Having studied the Mahabodhi Sutra of the Ten Wheels, realizing what the evil wheel is, what the good wheel is, in daily life, [karmas] in the body and mouth account for all seven things, consciousness only accounts for three. That is good or evil right in your mind. After we listen, we should achieve good things as mentioned in the previous section. We cannot achieve the Ten Wheels of the Buddha and the Ten Wheels of the Great Bodhisattva, at least we receive the Three Refuges. We must have refuge, rely on the blessings of the Three Jewels, so that we do not create the Ten Evil Karmas, try our best to practice the Ten Good Karmas, preserve our human body, meet the Buddha, listen to the Dharma, often meet good knowledge, listen to the Dharma and practice the Way.

(Kinh) Nhĩ thời, Thế Tôn cáo Hư Không Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát ngôn: “Thiện nam tử! Ngô kim trì thử Địa Tạng Thập Luân Đại Ký pháp môn, phó chúc nhữ thủ. Nhữ đương thọ trì, quảng linh lưu bố. Nhược chư chúng sanh ư thử pháp môn, hữu năng độc tụng, tư duy kỳ nghĩa, vị tha giải thuyết, trụ chánh hạnh giả, nhữ đương vị bỉ thủ hộ thập pháp, linh ư trường dạ, lợi ích an lạc. Hà đẳng vi thập? Nhất giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ nhất thiết tài vị, linh vô tổn phạp. Nhị giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ nhất thiết oán địch, linh bất xâm hại. Tam giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, linh xả nhất thiết tà kiến, tà quy, thập ác nghiệp đạo. Tứ giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, linh miễn nhất thiết thân ngữ trích phạt. Ngũ giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, giá đoạn nhất thiết báng hủy, khinh lộng. Lục giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, linh ư nhất thiết quỹ phạm, Thi La, giai đắc vô phạm. Thất giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, linh tất trừ diệt nhất thiết phi nhân, Tứ Đại quai phản, phi thời lão bệnh. Bát giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, bất tao nhất thiết phi thời, phi lý, tai hoạnh, yểu một. Cửu giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, mạng dục chung thời, đắc kiến nhất thiết chư Phật sắc tượng. Thập giả, vị bỉ thủ hộ, linh kỳ chung hậu, vãng sanh thiện thú, lợi ích an lạc. Thiện nam tử! Nhược chư hữu tình ư thử pháp môn, hữu năng độc tụng, tư duy kỳ nghĩa, vị tha giải thuyết, trụ chánh hạnh giả, nhữ đương vị bỉ cần gia thủ hộ như thị thập pháp, linh ư trường dạ, lợi ích an lạc”. Thời, Hư Không Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát bạch Phật ngôn: “Dụy nhiên, Thế Tôn! Ngã đương thọ trì như thị pháp môn, quảng linh lưu bố. Nhược chư hữu tình ư thử pháp môn, hữu năng độc tụng, tư duy kỳ nghĩa, vị tha giải thuyết, trụ chánh hạnh giả, ngã đương vị bỉ, thủ hộ thập pháp, linh ư trường dạ, lợi ích, an lạc”. Thời, Bạc Già Phạm thuyết thị kinh dĩ, ư chúng hội trung, Hư Không Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Địa Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Kim Cang Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Hảo Nghi Vấn Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Thiên Tạng Đại Phạm đẳng, cập chư thiên long, Dược Xoa, Kiện Đạt Phược, A Tố Lạc, Yết Lộ Đồ, Khẩn Nại Lạc, Mạc Hô Lạc Già, nhân phi nhân đẳng, nhất thiết đại chúng, văn Phật sở thuyết, giai đại hoan hỷ, tín thọ, phụng hành.
(Kinh: Lúc bấy giờ, đức Thế Tôn bảo Hư Không Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát rằng: “Này thiện nam tử! Ta nay đem pháp môn Địa Tạng Thập Luân Đại Ký này phó chúc vào tay ông. Ông hãy nên thọ trì, lưu truyền rộng rãi. Nếu các chúng sanh đối với pháp môn này mà có thể đọc tụng, tư duy ý nghĩa, vì người khác giải nói, trụ trong chánh hạnh, ông hãy nên vì người đó thủ hộ mười pháp, khiến cho người đó lợi ích, an lạc trong đêm dài. Những gì là mười? Một là vì người ấy thủ hộ hết thảy của cải, địa vị, chẳng để cho hao tổn, thiếu thốn. Hai là vì người ấy thủ hộ chẳng để cho hết thảy oán địch xâm hại. Ba là vì người ấy thủ hộ, khiến cho bỏ hết thảy tà kiến, tà quy, thập ác nghiệp đạo. Bốn là vì người ấy thủ hộ, khiến cho tránh khỏi hết thảy sự trừng phạt nơi thân và lời nói. Năm là vì người ấy thủ hộ, ngăn che, đoạn trừ hết thảy báng hủy, khinh mạn, trào lộng. Sáu là vì người ấy thủ hộ, khiến cho hết thảy khuôn phép và Thi La đều chẳng trái phạm. Bảy là vì người ấy thủ hộ, khiến cho các thứ già bệnh trái thời do phi nhân hay Tứ Đại chẳng điều hòa gây ra đều bị trừ diệt. Tám là vì người ấy thủ hộ, chẳng gặp hết thảy các tai nạn bất ngờ trái thời, phi lý, và chết yểu. Chín là vì người ấy thủ hộ, khiến cho khi mạng sắp hết, được thấy hình tướng của hết thảy chư Phật. Mười là vì người ấy thủ hộ, khiến cho sau khi mạng chung, được sanh về đường lành, lợi ích an lạc. Này thiện nam tử! Nếu các hữu tình đối với pháp môn này, có thể đọc tụng, tư duy ý nghĩa, vì người khác giải nói, trụ trong chánh hạnh, ông hãy nên vì người ấy càng thêm siêng năng thủ hộ mười pháp như thế, khiến cho được lợi ích an lạc trong đêm dài”. Khi đó, Hư Không Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát bạch với đức Phật rằng: “Kính vâng đức Thế Tôn! Con sẽ thọ trì pháp môn như thế này, lưu truyền rộng rãi. Nếu các hữu tình đối với pháp môn này, có thể đọc, tụng, tư duy ý nghĩa, vì người khác giải nói, trụ trong chánh hạnh, con sẽ vì người ấy thủ hộ mười pháp, khiến cho được lợi ích và an lạc trong đêm dài”. Khi đó, đức Bạc Già Phạm nói kinh này xong, trong chúng hội, Hư Không Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Địa Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Kim Cang Tạng Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Hảo Nghi Vấn Bồ Tát Ma Ha Tát, Thiên Tạng Đại Phạm v.v… và các trời, rồng, Dược Xoa, Kiện Đạt Phược, A Tố Lạc, Yết Lộ Đồ, Khẩn Nại Lạc, Mạc Hô Lạc Già, nhân phi nhân v.v… hết thảy đại chúng nghe lời đức Phật dạy, đều hoan hỷ to lớn, tin nhận, vâng làm).

“Thiện nam tử! Ngô kim trì thử Địa Tạng Thập Luân Đại Ký pháp môn, phó chúc nhữ thủ” ( Này thiện nam tử! Ta nay đem pháp môn Địa Tạng Thập Luân Đại Ký phó chúc vào tay ông): Ta nay dặn dò, giao phó ông một chuyện: “Chúc” là căn dặn, phó thác; “lụy” làm phiền ông, giao cho ông gánh vác. Gánh vác điều gì? Ông hãy “quảng linh lưu bố” (lưu truyền rộng rãi) bộ kinh này, khiến cho hết thảy chúng sanh đều có thể đạt được lợi ích nơi pháp môn này. Phải làm như thế nào thì mới được lợi lạc? Đức Phật chẳng yêu cầu rất cao. Nếu yêu cầu cao, đức Phật biết chúng sanh thời Mạt Pháp chẳng làm được! Đọc tụng là được rồi. Có thể đọc, xem, nghe, đồng thời phải tư duy các đạo lý được nói trong bộ kinh này. Không chỉ tự mình hiểu rõ, mà sau đấy còn phải giải nói cho người khác, khiến cho hành vi của họ đoan chánh. Quý vị đồng thời phải tu Huệ, tu Định, hoàn toàn chẳng phải tu Thập Thiện Nghiệp là đủ rồi. Đó là pháp dành cho nhân thiên, còn phải tu Định. Muốn thành thánh nhân thì phải tu Giới, Định, Huệ.

Suppose no one can recite or think about this morality, then Void Store Bodhisattva must be responsible for protecting them. What guardian is that? The Buddha spoke ten dharmas to help Void Store Bodhisattva protect people who can read, chant, and think about the principles in this sutra, allowing them to be peaceful and happy in the long night, and able to reach a good place. The main benefit is the good place. What nice place is that? Make that person happy all night long. Long night equals darkness. Throughout this life, you will always be in darkness. That is to say, the world of Sa Ba is like darkness, there is no light, it seems to be forever in darkness. Allowing them to reach a good place, to be peaceful, to be bright, to gain benefits, which means there is no trouble, in general, there is joy and happiness.

What is ten? “One, the one who protects all wealth, position, and spirit without harm” (One is to protect all wealth and status, so that there is no harm or lack): If there is a person who reads and recites this sutra, thinks about the morality in this sutra, you should protect that person, so that he or she does not suffer loss of property. Buddha knew that living beings are greedy for wealth and consider money as the most important thing. [Therefore] the first thing is to protect their money so that there is no loss. On the other hand, when that person has income and gain, he will not suffer any loss. If money is not achieved, how can one achieve it? [The above sutra] contains this meaning. Money is lost because it belongs to the five families, that is, the country confiscates it, thieves steal it, and it is burned by fire. In this way, being robbed by enemies, burned by fire, robbed by others, or confiscated by the king, or submerged by water, these things can still be prevented. Because in many past lives, you were in debt to others, they came to collect your debt, [being born as] unfilial descendants and destroyed your inheritance. Many emperors and high-ranking mandarins have spent all their assets within three generations. If you have merit, you will do well and will be able to preserve it for a long time!

Everyone reads the stories in Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Touching Luc, where it is written that when unfilial descendants rob [parents, grandparents] of their property, it turns into [property] of their descendants. After that, not being respectful towards them is still disobedience. That is to collect debt, to take revenge. An old couple had eight children, none of whom were filial. After that, they invited Ksitigarbha's statue, worshiped Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and burned incense and worshiped him all day from morning to night. If you don't worship, it will be better. As soon as you worship, all eight children will die one after another. At Tet, the old couple complained to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, grumbling: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! When we were not worshiping You, no matter how unruly they were, there were still people who were annoying. Now they are all dead, and when Tet comes, only the two of us will be left!" After praying, at dusk on the thirteenth day, the gods descended to the world. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva of course has supernatural powers, so he immediately told both of them in a dream: "Tomorrow morning, when you come to the river, you can see those eight children." The old man had a dream and woke up in the morning. Before the old man could speak, the old woman said: "Yesterday I had a dream and saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in a dream, saying: This morning we can go to the river to see our eight children." The old man said: "I also dreamed like that. Okay, we two have to go and see." The two of them went to the riverbank to look and saw in the water eight children appearing one after another, all of them were unjust families in the past. The reason the two of them became rich was by harming others, or robbing, or using tricks to exploit other people's property. As soon as they saw it, they were stunned. After returning, he did not dare to hold grudges and instead asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to repent. In the evening, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva again dreamed and taught: "I give you my child. Your lifespan will be very long, because you two are my dharma protectors, my benefactors, I will bless you." The two woke up and thought: "Is this possible? This old woman is so old, how can she still give birth? That is something that cannot happen in the human world!" But after the dream, the old woman immediately became pregnant, and at an old age gave birth to a child. The two of them lived to be ninety-some years old, nearly a hundred years old, and had their child take care of them until death. In Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Premonitions, there is that story.

“Second, the one who protects is bound to resent the enemy, and his spirit cannot be harmed” (Secondly, because he protects, all enemies and enemies are not harmed): This is very difficult! The enemy is reincarnated as a descendant, transformed into your own child. The more you love it, the more it harms you, that's how it is. Since you cannot solve this problem, how to solve it? You advise him to believe in Buddha and worship him every day. The more disobedient it is, the better you are to it. Moreover, you still have to repent, I am very sorry for him, he came to collect debt, I cannot accept it. That's how you resolve it. If your child is also very good, it's not that you owe him, but he owes you, that's very good. But the Buddha advised Void Store Bodhisattva: If someone reads and chants the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, watches the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, learns the meaning of the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, the first thing is to protect that person's wealth. The second thing is to protect, not to let enemies harm that person. The third thing is to preserve it, so that the person does not have wrong views, takes refuge in wrong ways, and takes refuge in the ten evil destiniess. You must protect and not let that person fall into the ten evil destiniess. If that person has wrong views or takes wrong refuge, he will fall into the ten evil realms and into the Five Infinite Hells. Therefore, before that person develops an attack, we must focus on protecting it first, so that the person does not fall into it.

“Four, the protector, the soul is completely immune to body and language punishment” (Four is the protector that helps the person avoid all punishment in the body and speech): Either the body is punished, or someone else uses words to punish the person, or uses all kinds of tools to punish the person's body. You must guard carefully, do not let that person suffer punishment

penalty.

“The fifth person, the guardian, must stop all slander and contempt” (Fifth is because he protects, prevents and eliminates all slander, contempt, and ridicule): Those are two aspects. On the one hand, others do not slander, despise, ridicule that person, or make fun of that person. Second, that person himself does not commit that mistake, does not slander others, does not slander the Three Jewels, does not slander the honor of others. Those are two aspects. The Buddha advised Void Store Bodhisattva that he must protect him so that he does not commit any mistakes, nor suffer this type of retribution.

“Six is the guardian, the guardian, the holy one is bound to violate, the Thi La, the one who is not violating” (Six is the guardian of that person so that all the rules and the Thi La do not violate): If that person is a monk, or a disciple of the four groups, the Three Refuges, the Five Precepts, the Eight Precepts, the novices, the Saṅgha Di-Ni precepts, Bhikkhu precepts, Bhikkhu-ni precepts, all the rules and regulations, Thi La is the precepts, “the treasury” is the rules. Regardless of rules or precepts, they are not violated.

“The Seven, the protector, the spirit must completely eliminate all non-humans, the four great evils, the untimely old age and illness” (Seven because he protects, makes all the untimely old and sick things caused by non-humans and the Four Elements unharmonious): Protects him so that he is not harmed by non-humans, that is, ghosts [brain damage]. The evil spirits cause the person's Four Elements to become out of harmony. “Anti” is not normal, not worthy of becoming old and poor. You should not be sick but be sick. “Non-time” means the time of life has not yet ended, that is called “death” (sudden death). Originally, it was possible to grow up normally, but due to illness, it means being harmed by non-human beings. Especially young children are very susceptible to epilepsy. That is the evil spirit that harms the spirit and reduces its lifespan. Aging and illness "untimely" means that it is not yet time to get old and you are already old, and it is not time to get sick and you are already sick. That person is only forty years old, but his back is bent and his legs can't even walk, all of which are related to bad timing and brain damage. The Buddha instructed Void Store Bodhisattva to protect them, making them safe, healthy, and auspicious.

“The eight, the protector is not necessarily untimely, unjustly calamity, premature” (Eight is the protector so that the person does not encounter all the unfortunate disasters and premature death at the wrong time, unreasonable): This story is said very clearly. Things that are not ethical, that is, natural disasters, the simplest being car accidents. When we stopped in Hong Kong, within just two days, we saw an accident. They worked on the top, there was a path at the bottom, and they built planks [for the masons to stand on]. Something above fell, causing the board to kick out, hitting the skull of the person [walking] below. If that person walks a little slower, he won't be hit; if he walks a little faster, he will pass. That person is neither fast nor slow, just clever! Every car accident is like that. These are all tragic accidents and unjustified premature deaths. The Medicine Sutra says nine types of death (death in a wrong way) because of this meaning. The Buddha advised Void Store Bodhisattva: Whoever reads the Ten Rings Sutra, you must protect that person, so that person does not encounter this type of accident!

“The nine, the protector, at the end of his life, will be able to see all the Buddhas' forms” (Ninth is because he protects them, so that when he dies, he can see the appearances of all the Buddhas): This is very difficult, absolutely not everyone who dies can see the Buddha images. [When you are about to die], if you hear someone advise you to recite Buddha's name, this is very unlikely to happen. Especially in the present, it is even more impossible. If you are sick, you will be taken to the hospital. Especially expatriates living in America. Brought to the hospital, the hospital does not allow religious rituals, can you advise that person to recite Buddha's name? Give that person a Buddha recitation device, the hospital will say you are disturbing others, take it away, and basically won't allow you [to use it]. You can't bring the patient home. If you put it in there, you can't take it out. How to do this? You must tell everything clearly in advance: Just when you are sick, do not take yourself to the hospital! Encountering that situation, you expect to see a Buddha statue, but you don't see it. We can recite the Great Collection of Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, Void Store Bodhisattva will protect us. Not only do you see the Buddha statue, but there are also people who come to help you chant, come in front of you to recite the Buddha's name, see the image of Ksitigarbha, see the Buddha image, see the image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Whenever you see it, your mind will arise and your karma will disappear. Therefore, the Buddha instructed Void Store Bodhisattva to protect the reader and recite the Ten Rings Sutra, making it possible for that person to see the images of the Buddhas at the time of death.

“The ten, the protector, the ultimate spirit, is reborn in a good destination, with benefits and peace” (The ten is because he protects, so that after death, he will be born in a good path, with benefits and peace): This is very difficult! Therefore, the Buddha advised Void Store Bodhisattva. Everyone who reads the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra, like everyone [present in the sutra lecture assembly, or reading this lecture, or just reading this sutra] has this status. Anyone who has heard the Ten Rings Sutra, even if they have not heard the whole thing, just one sentence, still counts. A sentence, a verse mentioned in this sutra, “one sentence” is a sentence, the most urgent sentence is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If you hear four sentences, the more you hear the better, you will definitely be born in a good path, not falling into the three evil destiniess, bringing you benefits and peace.

“ Good man! Nmay all sentient beings try the dharma method, have the ability to chant alone, think with strange meanings, altruistic explanations, and maintain righteous conduct” (Hey good man! If there are sentient beings who can read this dharma method, reciting, pondering the meaning, explaining for others, staying in right conduct): “Right conduct” is the Ten Good Karmas mentioned in the previous section. Can abide in the Ten Good Karmas. “Those who are diligent in protecting these ten dharmas” (You should be more diligent in protecting these ten dharmas for that person): The Buddha advised those ten dharmas again; You have to pay attention, you have to protect it, you shouldn't be lacking. “Long-lasting souls, peaceful benefits” (Make them benefit and peaceful in the long night): Permanently gain benefits. “Time, Void Store Bodhisattva said to the Buddha: - Of course, World-Honored One!” [meaning] that's right, World-Honored One, I listen to your advice. “I am currently receiving and maintaining the dharma door, spreading it widely” (I will receive and maintain the dharma method like that, spreading it widely): Sentient beings must hear this dharma method in order to have a relationship with Him. If anyone does not listen to this Dharma, nor read it, nor recite it, He will not be able to protect that person. How to do this? You yourself should receive and maintain this method, widely spread this method, so that all sentient beings can know this method.

If sentient beings with this method can “single chant, think about the meaning” (read, chant, think about the meaning), “altruistically explain, abide in righteous conduct” (for others to explain, abide in righteous conduct), I will definitely protect those ten dharmas for that person, “spirit long-lasting benefits and peace" (brings benefits and peace in the long night).

“ At, Silver Age Pham preached sutras, to the gathered assembly, Void Store Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, Vajra Store Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, Good Questioning Bodhisattva Ma Ha Tat, Thien Store Bodhisattva Maha Brahma class” (At After Bodhisattva Pham finished speaking this sutra, in the assembly, Void Store Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Vajra Treasury Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Good Questioning Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Heavenly Store Bodhisattva Mahasattva, etc.) These are the people who requested the Dharma in the Ten Chakra Sutra, up to “heaven, dragon, Yak Xo, Kien Dat Phuoc, A To Lac, Yet Lo Do, Khan Nai Lac, Mac Ho Lac Gia, human and non-human beings, all the masses have written the Buddha's teachings, they are greatly delighted, believe in, and follow" (heaven, dragon, Yak Xo, Gandharva, Asura, Ca Lau La, Khan Na La, Ma Hau La Gia, non-human beings, etc., all the masses hear the Buddha's words with great joy, believe, accept, and follow): The Great Collection of Ten Chakras is completed here. satisfied.

Now we talk again about a means called Import-Export-Contemplation. The Buddha showed us a method called Entry, Exit, and Contemplation. Entering and Exiting is contemplation of breathing in and out, paying attention to your breathing, exhaling and inhaling. Contemplation is paying attention, [Sho Tic Contemplation is] paying attention to the breath going in and out. What does “Import and export” mean? It is the practice of “retaining past thoughts” (holding the idea of ​​coming and going). "The idea of ​​coming" is entering (inhaling), "the thought of going" is breathing out. Inhaling is Entry, exhaling is Exit. By cultivating past and present thoughts, you can reach the Forbearance of Dependent Consent, the Forbearance of Formless Forbearance, the Dependent of Formless Forbearance, and the three doors of liberation can be attained. In other words, liberation is possible! How to chant? Observe how the breath goes in and out? There are six types of sequences, exhaling one breath, inhaling one breath is called “respiration”. Between those two inhales and exhales, count as one. If you count like that, from one to ten; Every time you breathe in and out, count [a number]. Then exhale and inhale again, counting as one exhalation and inhalation, counting to ten. Then, count from the beginning again, again one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. After counting, count again from the beginning, count [from ten a second time], count again [from the beginning from one to ten a third time, and so on].

That is the practice of concentration, you should try it. Every time you count, you get the numbers wrong. We all say "reciting the Buddha's name focusing on one scene", yet with every thought, false thoughts arise. You count your breath in and out, that is, you breathe in from your mind. If you're careless, you'll count wrongly. Regarding the number ten, currently, you always count unsuccessfully, follow your breathing, follow your exhalation and inhalation to count. When you are concentrated, the breath in and out is extremely subtle, you cannot feel it. This method of contemplation is different, this method of contemplation is thinking and illumination. Once illuminated, the thoughts will follow the breath, turning into purity, no more. While cultivating Concentration, there are all kinds of phenomena. Contemplating the five impure karma, you will give rise to a mind of disenchantment, contemplating your own body as impure, contemplation of the external realm as also impure. “Transition” is returning to purity. First, let's talk about Books. For So, everyone reading the scriptures, there are two types of Intent. [Contemplation is looking for things in their gross appearance], “Tu” is investigating [in their subtle appearance], that is, raising false thoughts. What do we use to stop false thoughts? Based on the pattern of breathing in and out. Exhale is Ho, Ho is escape. To inhale is to inhale. When inhaling, see its appearance, pay attention to it. When you pay attention, [you will notice] the breath is very rough. When you first sit down, the breath in and out is very rough, you can feel it, you can also see the breath out like that. Following the pattern of the breath, you will gradually be able to let go. What discharge? Let go of those thoughts, there will be no more thoughts (searching, considering the gross and subtle appearances of things). “Fu” means “to leave”, to be able to leave false thoughts.

“The skillful hand in entering and exiting is the form” (Skillfully holding the form of the in and out breath): It is called “good hand” (skillful in holding) meaning “not holding on”. “Good hand” means neither taking nor giving up. As for the Book of Contemplation, the four teachings or the five teachings all teach about the Book of Contemplation.

For the Book of Insights, the four teachings or five teachings all refer to the Book of Insights. Counting the breath in and out is called So Ti, which means “import and exit” (breath in and out). In general, those six subjects are called Book of Insights. It is just the destruction of the form of “importing, entering, and exiting”, and it is no more. That person can eliminate the signs of appearing in and out of consciousness. Once destroyed, it is Concentration, one can abide in the superior samadhi, [that is, the samadhi] is very superior. As long as that person stays in Concentration, he will be extremely happy, leaving the appearance of birth and death. Concentration is called the Land of Separation from Birth and Joy, [implying] "to leave birth and death, feeling great joy in the mind". When you observe, you will know that you can feel that the breath in and out has ceased, there is no breath in or out. This kind of practice cannot be achieved in a day or two. While you practice, with normal faculties, people with good virtuous roots can gradually enter Samadhi in almost a hundred days. When entering Samadhi, the Book immediately disappears. At that time, you can contemplate the scene yourself. The mind that contemplates and the scene that is contemplated, the mind and the scene are just one. Having contemplated this, contemplated that, looked at the scriptures, only then can the mind be calm, mind and scene are no different. To move is to go one step further. Transfer means Complete.

“Ability to release the Aggregates of Hands” (Able to use the means to release the Aggregates of Hands): The Five Aggregates of Hands: Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma are the six sense objects. Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind are the six senses. [Cand and Chen] hold the Five Aggregates of Form, Feeling, Perception, Action, and Consciousness. That consciousness distinguishes all external appearances, which is called the Five Aggregates of Hand. Meanwhile, that person can skillfully expel the Five Aggregates. “Let go” is not the ultimate renunciation! Ultimate renunciation is like Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara)'s vision of the Five Aggregates as Emptiness, he has gradually reached the meaning of Emptiness. At that time, you can become a saint, enter the holy land, and achieve achievements. That achievement has not yet eliminated afflictions, it has only subdued them. Wait until you are calm and then you can end your afflictions and end the End of History. Until the end of Views or Obstacles, that person will realize the First Fruition, and gradually get rid of Thoughts and Ordains. After reading a few chapters, you will immediately realize the First Fruition, and gradually you will end the Fourth Ordinance. After reading a few chapters, I realized a few chapters. If all thoughts and feelings are completely cut off, you will attain Arhatship. Again, cut off the habit of afflictions, depending on your practice. That is called practicing Entering and Exiting Contemplation, and you will be able to freely contemplate the Five Aggregates of Hands, i.e. Form, Feeling, Thought, Actions, and Consciousness.

Next, talk about how to contemplate the Five Aggregates. Where does the breath come in and out? Rely on the Aggregate of Form. The form of the body is form, it is the Body of Form. For such an in-and-out breath, that person “creates” the in-and-out breath, the in-and-out breath is the creation. What artifact? Only by breathing in and out can you breathe. Only by breathing can you maintain your body! That in and out breath, in and out, then in and out again, you will feel and receive. If you only exhale and don't inhale, you won't be comfortable. You will feel that receiving, “tho” means “receiving”, which belongs to the Aggregate of Feeling. For the breath going in and out, back and forth, you keep its appearance, the appearance of exhalation, the appearance of inhalation, contemplating the appearance of exhalation and inhalation, this belongs to Thought. Perception Thu Uan can clearly perceive the appearances created by the exhalation and inhalation. Willow attains, knowing is the Aggregate of Consciousness. Because of the five Aggregates of Grasping, i.e. Form, Feeling, Thought, Action, and Consciousness, you practice the practice of Record, Dependence, Contemplation, Contemplation, Transformation, and Purity, allowing you to enter Concentration, being able to stop the three karmas of body, mouth, and mind. Depending on the power of contemplation, you can reach the goal. What is the goal? Enter Concentration, step by step penetrating Ignorance, Desire, Attachment, practice step by step, gradually achieving perfection.

In this sutra, the Book of Insights is said very simply. In the Luc Dieu Mon of the Tieu Chi Quan series of great master Tri Gia, it is divided into many departments. Luc Dieu Mon includes six types; Here, we only talk about one of them, because the Six Noble Gates are the basis for cultivating Concentration. Regardless of whether Thanh Van, Doc Giac, or Bodhisattva, Six Wonderful Gates are all paths that must be traversed. When cultivating the path, you must definitely go through it, Śākyamuni Buddha was also like that. At first, Śākyamuni Buddha practiced Prajnaparamita, relying on these six types of Lottery, Dependence, Samadhi, Contemplation, Perfection, Purity, all virtues were developed from here. When demons attain enlightenment, the Buddha shows us a rule for good practice, what is it? Samadhi of Form, Samadhi of Mind, [meaning] all forms are calm, have attained concentration, and the mind also ceases. At that time, one will reach the Samadhi of One Mind, which is also the Samadhi of Buddha Recitation. In the previous section, I followed the scriptures to preach. My way of reciting is to use the Buddha's name method to practice the Book of Contemplation, absolutely no need for the Book (counting numbers). The meaning of So is "a breath in and out". I divide the exhale into two parts, exhale is A, inhale is Di, exhale is Da, inhale is Buddha. Moving like that, turn the rhymes one by one, “Amitābha Buddha, Amitābha Buddha”, following the breath in and out, moving like that.

I use this method to practice Concentration. After that, I changed to reciting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the same thing. I don't use numbers, nor do I count from one to ten. Everyone else's practice method depends on your choice. Book, Sui, and Chi all have the same meaning, and are also the same six types. Six types of Dharma Books, i.e. methods of counting numbers. The Book of Contemplation is the second dharma in the Six Wonderful Doors, called the Six Wonderful Doors (six mysterious doors that give birth to each other in turn). I read those nouns to you a little bit.

The second type is the Sixth Order that gives birth to the Six Wonderful Doors, [that is] in order, giving birth to Book, Dependence, Silence, Contemplation, Perfection, and Pureness. Hoan in Luc Dieu Mon has the same meaning as Zhuan, according to the order of birth. Thus, after having the Book, Sui will be born. Having Sui can give birth to Chi. Having attained Samadhi, Contemplation can be born. From Only, Contemplation is born, from Contemplation, Perfection is born. From Hoan comes Tinh. The sixth thing is Purity, which is the Six Noble Gates arising in order. Every Zen practice you practice has the Six Noble Gates.

Third, Luc Dieu Mon is convenient; Fourth, Luc Dieu Mon depending on treatment; Thursday, Tuong Nhiep Luc Dieu Mon; Friday, Thong Beet Luc Dieu Mon; Saturday, Completely Zhuan Luc Dieu Mon; Eighth, Contemplating the Six Wonderful Minds; Ninth, Vien Quan Luc Dieu Mon, these subjects are very deep. Currently, I rely on the Mahayana Sutra of the Ten Wheels to cite the Six Wonderful Doors. Second Life is a staircase for you to progress step by step in your desire to enter the Buddha path. If you are in the Desire Realm and want to practice Concentration, it will be very difficult. How to do it? Please rely on those six types to be able to achieve Concentration for yourself.

The first subject is to practice the Book, which means counting numbers, counting ten numbers. Exhale, inhale, count one, exhale, inhale, count two, exhale, inhale, count three, [up to ten] and then return [counting from one] like that.

The second thing is the Number Proof, which means you prove the number you just counted. There are two types of numbers: One is practice, the other is realization. After realizing it, he transferred and entered Sui. After realizing, that way of counting numbers stops, there is no more counting, that is Dependence. Practicing the Book aims to regulate your breathing, from the very coarse to the very subtle. We gradually adjust like that, but you should not rush. When counting numbers, you must take your time, follow your breath naturally, without needing any intention. Whenever Intention, Concentration will be very difficult to arise, that is not natural. How to regulate breathing? Not fast, not slow, not rough, not slippery, you must practice to a level of peace, slowly like that, from one to ten, counting like that.

The reason we can focus is based on counting numbers. If you can meditate on the mind, that is, use Amitābha Buddha's name to capture the mind. You recite the Buddha's name and recite it to the point of following the breath in and out, moving forever, the breath is no longer there, you still feel the Buddha's effect following you to move (that is Dependency). So you have Concentration. But the Sui Dharma depends on each person's practice. First of all, you must know the number, from one to ten, to control the mind, not letting it wander quickly or slowly, so that the mind can be controlled, not running around, never thinking about anything else. If the mind thinks about something, [don't pay attention to it], just let it go. If you want to think about something, there will be no time, there will never be any gaps to interfere, making it impossible for confusing ideas and thoughts to arise!

For Digital Certificate, what is considered "certification"? You realize that the mind naturally follows that way of counting ten times, there is no more confusion, it naturally follows the correct order and is attained. From one to ten, you don't need to think, you don't need to use your mind to count, you don't need to use any effort to urge. At first, if you don't pay a little attention, you will immediately get confused and count wrongly. Until you become proficient in counting, from one to ten without confusion, you can count like that at will, without having to waste any effort, gradually the external conditions will fall away. The mind stays, the condition of reciting is completely stopped, meaning "the condition of relying on the breath [to count numbers]" [has ended], that is, the thing of depending on the breath to reciting is no longer there. After that “condition of mindfulness” (relying on the breath to recite) is no longer there, you will feel that the breath is as if it exists or is not. Saying “there is no breath”, it still seems like there is subtle breath. Say "yes", there is no more breath. Without breath, that means in terms of effort, there is no more breath. By that time, my mind no longer had the thought of counting numbers anymore.

throw away the number. That's called Depends.

The second type is Cultivation and must be Certified. To practice means to abandon that method of counting numbers. Your mind naturally moves with your breath in and out, your mind doesn't run around, there's no need to count anymore. Counting is to prevent the mind [from wandering]. The scattered mind is no longer wandering around, there is no need to be on guard, follow the thoughts to follow the breath in and out. But the breath in and out is very small, the breath is like a thread, like the breath of a person about to die. But your mind is completely free of external objects and follows the breath. The subtle breath operates according to its conditions, that is called Dependence. “Depending” means following the breath as a condition. The breath is extremely subtle, causing the practitioner to stay in mindfulness, until the end is Attainment, the mind is calm, no longer chaotic. That is Sui Tru, the mind is determined, no longer confused. At that time, you feel the breath whether it is long or short, clearly, distinctly, until you realize that the breath is not only coming out from the nose, not only at the tip of the nose, but every pore on the body seems to exude subtle breath, they are also inhaling and exhaling, that is called Variable. The change is that the whole body is exhaling and inhaling. Therefore, your subtle minds depend on each other at will and are interconnected with each other. The person exhales, not necessarily the breath exhaled from the nose, the breath from the nose is no longer recognizable, it can be exhaled everywhere. Meanwhile, the practitioner abandons Sui, no longer pays attention to the breath, has entered Concentration, the breath is no longer there, that is Only.

What is the practice of Chan? One is Cultivation, the other is Certificate. When practicing meditation, all predestined thoughts become Concentration. Concentration is Concentration (Concentration due to cessation). You have stopped [false thoughts], you can feel the breath [very subtle]. In Concentration, the breath in and out is present. In every pore, with every in and out breath, all [pores] have exhalation and inhalation. Pores are clear; Otherwise, how can you sweat? Pores that sweat are clear. Sometimes you don't breathe out, but your pores breathe. Having stopped, don't think about Numbers (counting numbers), don't think about Sui, purify your mind to practice.

What about Certificates? At that time, neither the body nor the mind were known. Mind and body are as one, nothing more, have entered Concentration. But this type of Concentration has not yet entered Emptiness, still belongs to the form of existence. This Concentration must be transformed into formlessness. When you realize, you cannot see the internal or external appearance, the Concentration method is to keep the mind immobile at will. People who practice like this have entered samadhi, their mind gives rise to a feeling of joy and tranquility, but there is no Wisdom, only Concentration. We say “Zhi Quan doubles the operation, Dharma meditation doubles the practice”. If there is only Concentration, it will not work. That person (the person who practices this Dharma method of Book of Contemplation) generates wisdom light to meditate. Contemplation is wisdom illumination. Without the means of Hue, one cannot destroy birth and death. Even though you have achieved Concentration, Concentration still cannot break through birth and death, you still have to flow, that is, you cannot practice successfully, what should you do? Still have to rely on Fake, still have to destroy life and death.

“Creating mindfulness, practicing the Dharma phase of fake meditation belongs to causes and conditions” (Think like this: The Zen discipline currently being practiced all belongs to causes and conditions). That Mon Dharma comes from cultivating the Book and Depends like that. Practicing to that level is the dharma of cause and effect, belonging to the dharma of the Five Aggregates, belonging to the dharma of the eighteen realms, due to harmony. Contemplation is the generation of thoughts. Having started thinking, that means starting up contemplation to remember. This story is false and not true, what are we planning to do now? Now I don't see, I don't recognize, I don't think, I don't initiate enlightenment. We must contemplate, we must reflect. Whenever you start a thought, just start thinking like that, don't be attached to that mind, don't be attached to that Concentration, don't enjoy that happiness and then start to contemplate and discriminate. That's Quan.

Only Contemplation gives rise to Contemplation. What about Tu Quan? From within that Concentration, he used the Hue mental factor to distinguish, observe the subtle breath in and out, observe it like wind in the air. As the Buddha said, there are thirty-six objects in our body, all of which do not really exist, are illusory and not real. That is practicing Emptiness Contemplation, not Emptiness Contemplation. The Emptiness Contemplation then [explains] that the main essence is Emptiness, but here [is the Contemplation of Emptiness], that means analyzing the Emptiness, dividing the Emptiness. The mind is impermanent, does not exist in every moment, and does not have a Self, even the body, feelings, and mind dhammas all have no self-nature. So, where does our Concentration rely? How do we decide? Where do you rely? Tu Quan means observing at any time. Observing in Concentration like that is called Thinking Practice. Contemplation and Hue are in balance, we often say “Only Contemplation two movements”, which has this meaning. Use this to contemplate the breath, recognize the breath going in and out, every pore in the entire body and mind, all pores are breathing in and out. This requires you to open your wisdom, clear your mind, and contemplate thirty-six objects clearly for yourself. At that time, you feel disgusted with this body. Visualize each breathing pore as the insect's cloaca, its breathing hole. That shop is where they hide, both inside and outside are impure, from the inside out, there is nothing clean. At that time, compassion and joy arise in the mind. Compassion (Sadness) because my own body [is so impure], happy because I can also progress and break the Four Crazy Islands. As for the impure body, thoroughly realizing that it is truly impure, the mind that loves and regrets the body will be cut off. That's called Evidence.

Ultimately attain contemplation, in the mind, follow the realm being contemplated, letting go of the realm of Concentration. That contemplation still belongs to Concentration. It is still not contemplation while walking, but while sitting still, concentration turns into contemplation. That is Dinh Hue dual destiny. At that time, contemplation uses discrimination, analysis method, and recognizes that thought is circulating. If your thoughts are still circulating, they are not true. You should let go of Quan and Tu Hoan.

Speaking of Complete means letting go of Contemplation and practice of Transformation. One is Cultivation, the other is Certification. Cultivation is observation: A thought arises in our mind, then we contemplate that thought arising from the mind. When the mind is born, dharma is born. That's what we analyze, it's still not the fundamental condition, it's not the essence of the Dharmakaya, we have to use Reflection to contemplate the mind. Contemplate the present mind, where does that mind arise from? Gradually realize that mind is born from Contemplation, or is it not born from Contemplation? If the mind is not born from Contemplation, then who is contemplating? Where does that mind ultimately arise from? A thought arises in the mind, then that mind disappears. This thought arises, that thought passes away, that is contemplating the birth and death of the mind. Contemplate that this mind arises because that mind disappears. Contemplating like that, if from the mind also gives birth to the mind, from cessation also gives birth to the mind, that is, the birth of two minds, that is the birth and death of the mind. Contemplating just one thing takes a lot of effort, yet there are four sentences in total, that is, “birth, death, not being born, not going away”. After finishing the contemplation, then we know that our mind is inherently unborn. If it is unborn, there is no existence. Unborn is non-existence, non-existence is emptiness. Since it is Emptiness, what else do we have to contemplate the mind? If it is not, then even the mind of contemplation (the mind of contemplation) does not exist. The ability to contemplate the mind does not exist, so how can we contemplate the scene? Our mind confronts the scene, the mind already does not exist, so does the scene still exist? Both the scene and the mind are lost.

I often tell my friends that repentance must be recited like that, thought like that. Such repentance is the purest. “The mind is gone, the scene is still, two sentences are empty, the name and name are true repentance” (The mind is gone, the scene is quiet, both sides are empty. That is called true repentance). The mind doesn't exist, the scene doesn't exist, do you have any sins that you can repent of? Sin does not exist, contemplate like that. If you practice Khong Quan successfully then there will be nothing. Therefore, we say that suffering, suffering, or suffering in body and mind, sadness and afflictions, are all due to your false thoughts. If you can meditate, when you meditate, you feel very miserable. Let's take that suffering out [observe], what is it that makes us suffer, is that really good? Is it really good? As soon as you meditate, it's no longer there, it's all gone! For example, a couple quarrels and wants to divorce; At that time, I felt very miserable. Once you contemplate, [you will realize] that your partner (wife or husband) is not you, you are not that person, you can't even find it yourself, what can you say about others! What relationship does that person have with us? If it is emptiness, then all suffering will no longer exist. That's fate. Dharmas that arise from causes and conditions are false. If it's fake, it's not real. If it is not true, what afflictions arise in us? Suffering is affliction, then your afflictions will end. That is the method to eliminate afflictions.

The mind is gone, both the scene and the wisdom are gone. That's Transfer. What is moved will be moved like that. If you leave the scene, leave the mind, you also leave the mind that contemplates and the scene being contemplated. There is no wisdom or scene. If you meditate for a long time, the scene will not exist, nor will the wisdom exist. It is not through effort that the mind of wisdom expands and arises, and you yourself give birth to great wisdom. That wisdom is illumination, this requires cultivating Purity. Having cultivated purity, one must again attain purity. To be pure is to be pure. When you practice Purity, you know that all forms are inherently pure, your body and mind are inherently pure. All dharmas are inherently unpolluted, due to their inherently pure nature. Regarding all delusions and discriminations, you should not discriminate, pure is not pure, contaminated is not infected. Contamination and purity do not exist, they are both scenes. The external environment is empty, false thoughts are delusions. Delusional thoughts no longer exist, nor do defilements exist. That is, from the moment of cessation of discrimination, then there was structure, until now, everything does not exist, it is all Emptiness. Emptiness is truly pure, practice like that.

That's just the order in Luc Dieu Mon. According to the order of birth, there are causes, conditions, and mutual birth. But that is only the content of a part of Luc Dieu Mon of Tieu Chi Quan. If you want to truly practice Contemplation, study Chi Contemplation, you still have to practice Ma Ha Chi Contemplation. The Avatamsaka Sutra teaches about Samādhi which is very magical and very difficult to enter. Just starting out is cultivating True Emptiness Absolute General Contemplation, which means that all generals do not exist. The form inside the mind, the form outside the mind, the form of all Buddhas, all dharmas, all dharma treasures, whatever form there is, it is all illusory, the ultimate emptiness! Cultivating and achieving Absolute Emptiness gives birth to the Contemplation of Unobstructed Reasons. Reason pervades Things, Things are Reason. Because Reason pervades Everything, Truth is Reason, so Reason is unobstructed. Reason is unobstructed, but Su is also unobstructed. Therefore, it is possible to “turn the great wheel of dharma in a single particle”, which has that meaning. One mote is Ly, all things are contained in Ly. Reason is Truth, Truth is Reason, Reason is unobstructed!

Going one step further is the Contemplation of the Unobstructed Matter. Without using the Law to complete everything, the Truth itself is unobstructed in everything, so it reaches the realm of Hoa Tang. We cannot practice that type of Contemplation because our mental strength is not enough. Even if we kowtow and meditate, we cannot meditate. If we kowtow, you think that "the nature of the ceremony and the nature of the ceremony are not passed away" (the nature of the person bowing and the person receiving the ceremony is not dead): I am the one who can pay homage, and the Buddha is the one to whom I pay homage. The Nature and Body of me and Buddha are both Emptiness and tranquility. Just as we say “citta samadhi”, even if we cannot attain the Samadhi of Mind, even the Samadhi of Form cannot be attained. Once attained, one will attain the President of the Mind, and then one will reach the Samadhi of the One Mind. To say that reciting the Buddha's name achieves one mind without confusion is still not a sentence. Reciting the Buddha's name, reciting until one mind is not disturbed, within seven days you can have one mind undisturbed, seventy days, one hundred days, you can also achieve one mind undisturbed. Based on this to practice, that is, from observing the breath in and out. If you don't contemplate the breath going in and out, meditate on the four words Amitābha Buddha to change your mind, which means you don't pray to return to purity at all, just pray that you can stop being still!

For one day, if even in your dreams, you are Amitābha Buddha. Amitābha Buddha does not create thoughts, but naturally moves thoughts. Even if you die, you will not be reborn in the Pure Land? Affirmation will be born. Because your mind has merged with the world of Ultimate Bliss, with Amitābha Buddha "body and land are not two". The world of Ultimate Bliss is Amitābha Buddha, it is the body and the water realm that are not two. Amitābha Buddha is the world of Ultimate Bliss. If you contemplate for a long time like that, you correspond to the Buddha. Every thought I have is Amitābha Buddha, I turn into Amitābha Buddha. You are already in the world of Ultimate Bliss; That's a little more penetrating. However, when people listen to these kinds of words, after hearing them for a long time, they will be able to understand them. Opening your mouth to curse others, listening to dirty words, is very familiar. That is because the energy is very deep from countless lifetimes. Whenever it appears, it is because it is ripe. But when you hear this, you don't know how many lifetimes you haven't heard it. You hear these words, but you still cannot enter. You think this dharma is very simple, just count the numbers and see, it's not very simple! Ten times is fine, but twenty, thirty times, you are already in chaos, already in chaos! If you can't count numbers fluently, practice like that every day. If you can't practice diligently, set aside an hour or half an hour every day. When first practicing, don't sit for too long, don't be too greedy. That is also greed. If you are too greedy, you won't be able to do anything. Why? You say: "I must sit for three hours!" Do you have time? When you begin to meditate, first sit for ten minutes, or fifteen minutes. If you feel uncomfortable or your thoughts are scattered, you have to stand up, don't sit anymore! If you have time, sit for another ten minutes. Gradually increase, you sit longer. Increase it by one minute, increase it to twenty minutes, increase it to half an hour, gradually increase it more. There was a Dharma friend who, with Tet coming up, was about to go into seclusion, I said: "Don't go into seclusion, you're busy with a lot of things, wait until you have a chance to discuss it again." In the morning, when his disciples arrived, they discovered the old master had fallen and rolled on the ground, asking what had happened? Due to tripping! They took him to the hospital for treatment. There are things that cannot be forced. Being diligent is good, making up your mind is good, but you have to consider your circumstances and your own strength to progress gradually. We cannot import it. When practicing, don't be greedy. There are many Dharma friends who also practice sitting in the lotus position, that is natural. Being able to sit cross-legged is quite good, but it's not a day or two of effort. You sit cross-legged, you can't sit for long, your legs are very painful! Just being able to sit is enough! You must focus on the mind, not on the form. There are many Dharma friends who pay attention to form. When looking at others, they also look at form, to see whether their posture is good or not, whether they are sitting properly or not! Whenever it comes to quiet meditation, ask first whether that person can sit in the lotus position or not? [Rather], you should ask whether that person can cultivate a good mind or not? But what's the use of sitting in a lotus position? When sitting in the lotus position, you just need to sit firmly! Don't seek the appearance of sitting, must seek practicality!

Learning a sutra must be practical, not based on appearance. After listening to a certain sutra, after listening to a certain sutra, what effect will it have? What does that sutra say? Speaking of cutting off the Ten Evils and practicing the Ten Virtues, can you cut them off or not? Throughout the day, review, seek reality, first of all, consider and think. If we hope to achieve something, we must first consider the intermediate obstacles to see if we can actually do it or not? If you can't reach it, set your standards a little lower, don't set your standards too high. Don't you want to practice? [Isn't it] hoping to go deeper, hoping to see through birth and death?
