I. Induction stories of the twentieth century

1. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's grace bestowed upon me

Shaman Tam Nhien writes

In the summer of the 35th year of the Republic (1946), I studied at the Shurangama Buddhist Institute in Shanghai. One night, due to sleeping late, he caught a bad cold. At that time, although he was diagnosed at the hospital, it soon turned into a very severe case of whooping cough. Almost every hour, I coughed dozens of times. Every time I cough until my chest is tight and I choke on air, it won't stop! Every time I take the medicine, I vomit every time. Every time the injection came back, it was ineffective. For three meals, I only drink liquid rice water, I can't swallow other hard or dry foods! Every night I have trouble sleeping, it's very painful! During the summer vacation, there were monks discussing the matter of worshiping the relics of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at Nine Flowers Mountain. I thought to myself: "If this useless physical body dies of illness in Shanghai, how about sacrificing while worshiping Bodhisattva will have a richer meaning!" Therefore, I decided to join their team on the road, brace myself, and drag my weakened body along with them. Of course, when traveling, most people are in cars or boats; Otherwise, I can't go!

A group of us monks took the train, car, passed through Nanjing, Wuhu, then took the train, or took people's boats, headed straight to Dai Dong, Thanh Thanh. Even though the road was long and winding and the sun was shining brightly in the air, we did not rest because of the hardship. All the way, I silently recited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's holy name, single-mindedly persevering. As the journey continued, the road got closer and closer to the Bodhisattva's ashram, my inner courage and joy grew little by little. Even though I only drink a few cups of liquid milk every day, my body and mind are happy and can fight without falling down. On Truong Giang, while the ship was being buffeted by waves, most travelers were tired and wanted to fall asleep. While I was confused, I suddenly saw an ascetic monk approaching, saying: "There's no need to worry about asthma! Eat a lot of cold things like watermelon, ice water, etc., and it will heal itself." After saying that, I couldn't see anywhere anymore. Not long after, suddenly there was a piece of delicious, fresh pink watermelon in front of me. I suddenly picked it up and tried it, and immediately felt my whole body feel unusually comfortable and refreshed! But at that time, I heard my own snoring, so I woke up and looked, coincidentally, the monks were also eating watermelon. Naturally, I was like a scene in a dream, conveniently holding and eating. Unexpectedly, because of that, I suddenly slept unusually well that night. The next day, my coughing was much less, making me bold enough to continue eating cold food. What a miracle.

From Dai Dong to Thanh Thanh, one must follow the waterway which is a zigzag branch, narrow, not too short. On the waterway, there are boat people, there are fellow students who make their own bamboo oars, help each other row the boat, so progress is like flying. The only part of the road is a wet, slippery field road, so traveling is quite difficult! Especially for people with physical illnesses like me, it feels even more serious than before, becoming a big trouble for my companions! Therefore, at night, when I asked to sleep at a temple at the southern gate of Thanh Thanh, I had a severe cough! A few interested fellow students came to the Bodhisattva statue in the front hall to ask for a tattoo, and received the following tattoo: "The wide sea meets a fierce wind, big waves hit the boat, the boat capsizes and falls down, it's terrifying if it doesn't sink". After praying, they showed me the hexagram. I saw it and was very enlightened, so I told them: "On the way, I constantly reverently chanted the Bodhisattva's holy name, giving rise to an extremely strong will. Currently, although there is a very dangerous scene, I am confident that it will be like an army's armored ship safely crossing the river, please don't worry!" Sure enough, at midnight, the cough immediately stopped. The next morning, I especially felt hungry, after eating two bowls of porridge in a row I felt full, and my whole body's strength also increased a lot! From Thanh Thanh to Cuu Hoa Son, more than sixty miles of mountain road, I was able to follow the ranks and not fall too far behind. That is the second miracle.

Advancing along the mountain road, we passed the large-scale Long An pagoda, two holy huts in the style of thatched tents, one tuc hut, Tieu Kieu Am and Dai Kieu Am with wonderful scenery. In it, there is the Bodhisattva body of the most recent date. Cam Lo Pagoda is covered with green bamboo, in it there are all Sutras of the Tang and Song dynasties, there is a Ban Tieu pavilion to welcome the wind, and the taste of tea permeates people's hearts. In those places, we have stayed and visited. Although I also had the mentality to enjoy the scenery, due to time constraints, I was completely in no mood to meditate and admire the wind and moon. Finally, pay your respects to Ky Vien pagoda, at the right time that pagoda has a Dharma lecture. We went to visit around, and we all slept at Bach Tue Palace. At that time, during the day, I only coughed a few times per hour!

For the first time, sleeping in the holy place, everyone was filled with joy that was beyond words. The Director of the temple welcomed us warmly and thoughtfully, causing our group to sleep so soundly that we didn't know it was dawn. By the time I got out of bed, my classmates had divided into groups to worship the relics in the holy land. I can endure the fatigue of traveling thousands of miles to the holy land, of course I won't be able to recover alone anymore! Therefore, he also brought along medical equipment (a robe and a crouching blanket), from Hoa Thanh pagoda to the tower worshiping the Bodhisattva's body at Than Quang range to pay homage, bowing at each step. While paying homage, I thought to myself of the spirit of devotion, every step of the way, bowing to the four great famous mountains of those who have been cultivating their minds for a long time, and suddenly felt extremely ashamed! How can a small action like mine express my respect and repay a portion of the Bodhisattva's ten thousand virtues?

Each step, each bow, pass the Nam Thien Mon, pass the Ten Kings Palace covered with shady trees, to reach the stone steps leading up to the steep and high Bodhisattva Tower. At that time, I was panting like a buffalo, sweating like rain, but my mind was as calm as a mirror, my body was as light as the wind, there was a kind of state of mind"a hundred veins are open, a hundred thoughts are swept away", which is truly indescribable. So he quickly arrived in front of the Bodhisattva's tower. After continuing to bow forty-eight times, my whole body was in high spirits. Not only was there no fatigue, from then on, the painful cough was completely eliminated. That is the third miracle!

In Cuu Hoa Son for a few days, I worshiped all the holy relics of the ashrams, visited many statues of the ancestors' bodies, even the highest place was Ksitigarbha on top of Thien Dai mountain, a straight line to the sky, the U Minh bell weighing eighty-four thousand kilograms on the top of the mountain, beautiful and dangerous landscapes, all reached without fail. When I returned to Shanghai, I transformed into a flexible, healthy body, making others dare not believe that I was a weak person who couldn't stand the wind. Who gave the reward? By whose power did this happen? It is due to the loving kindness of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and the grace of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Otherwise, I would have died of illness in Shanghai soon! Namo great vow Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

2. The ceremony of reciting the holy name cures serious illnesses

Lam Chan Hung writes

My youngest daughter a few years ago (from 6th grade until now 12th grade) has kidney disease. Because the treatment did not help, the family was short of money, so the treatment had to be stopped for a while. I waited patiently until mid-September of the 67th year of the Republic of Korea (1978), when I noticed that my child's face was swollen and felt very wrong, so I took him to see a doctor. The autopsy results showed that the condition was worse than before. Although it's not very serious, the situation is not light. At that time, my mind was very depressed. If you have to go to the doctor every day (or every two days), family life will become even more difficult. How to do this? I can only ask the doctor for help; Fortunately, the doctor was very sympathetic to my situation and immediately recommended a medicine and told me to buy it and treat it for half a year to see if it worked. After that, I thought: "There is no way to just take medicine, because in the past, when the disease first appeared, it was not curable. Isn't it even more difficult to treat now?" Therefore, right then I thought: "It's still better to pray to Buddha and Bodhisattva." So on the one hand, on the one hand, I buy the medicine myself and take it, and on the other hand, I teach my grandchild to ask for Buddha's power every morning and night. Unexpectedly, kidney disease has been difficult to treat for many years, but in just over two short months, it has completely cured. Who can believe this kind of miracle? To be honest, even the doctor found it very strange! I think if it weren't for praying to Buddha and Bodhisattvas for help and treatment, I'm afraid it wouldn't be any better now. Therefore, I am very grateful to Buddha.

How did that little girl pray to Buddha for treatment? At first, I was afraid that children would not be patient and would not worship every day. So I told him in advance about the boundless power of Buddha. For the sake of life, there is only one way to pray to Buddha and Bodhisattva. At the same time, encourage and teach it the simplest and most convenient method. In the morning, after brushing your teeth and washing your face, go to the Buddha's table and wholeheartedly recite “Namo Amitābha Buddha” six bows, recite “Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva” six bows, a total of twelve bows. After that, kneel and recite “Namo Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara)” one hundred times. At night, before going to sleep, recite “Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva” three times, then kneel and recite “Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva” one hundred times. Every day, just chanting and praying like that, in just over two months, the disease was completely cured. It's truly inconceivable!

3. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's inspiration to save suffering

Hoang Tri Duc writes

When I was a child, others called me Khoai Lac Fairy Tu, and in school my nickname was Tieu Khi Hoan (anti-anger medicine). It doesn't matter whether the sky falls or the mountains collapse. Live happily, carefree, carefree like a small bird flying in the air, where is there sadness and suffering? But now that I'm old and have life experience, in general, I have more suffering and less joy! If there is no suffering, why do we cry endlessly at birth? That is the beginning of suffering. The Buddha taught: “Or karma is the cause, resulting in suffering in human life”. I once heard the old Dharma Master Thuy Kim give his teachings. The Master said: "Human life is like a white cloth, smeared with ink and polluted. We need to use clean water to wash it gradually to become pure. Therefore, we must often recite Buddha's name. Buddha has mercy on living beings, causing the evil nature in human life to gradually gradually become purer

to be pure, you can leave suffering".

Last August, Tri Nhi came home, her friend Doctor Ly came to visit. I took the opportunity to ask him: "My neck feels like I can't breathe. Sometimes I can't even swallow a mouthful of water. Is that why?" Doctor Ly observed carefully and said: "It's best to go to the hospital for a check-up." I followed Dr. Ly's advice to Sung Hoa Hospital and was examined by Dr. Duong Man. He said all body parts were normal, it would be best to have an X-ray of the throat to know. When I got the X-ray, oh my! It's so embarrassing. The conclusion is that between the esophagus and the trachea, an unknown mass has developed. After being diagnosed by three specialists, in the end, it was decided that it was impossible not to have surgery. I just heard that surgery is required, and I can't help but be scared! I thought to myself: "I'm over sixty years old, but I still have to undergo surgery. It's really dangerous. Let's just go with nature!" Go home, tell your children about the situation. Vi Nu said: "No matter what, we should inform Hoc Nhi and Ms. Ung" (they are both my daughters). But the children unanimously advocated listening to the doctor's dissecting opinion. I can't shake them. Hoc Nhi returned that day and decided to take me to the hospital. Going to the hospital is a series of bowel movements, temperature checks, and all kinds of procedures. At nine o'clock the next morning, he was taken to the operating room and passed through Tu Mon Gate. Five doctors and two nurses told me to lie on a cold bed, my arms and legs tied tightly, I couldn't move even if I wanted to. Close your eyes tightly and recite Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. At nine fifteen, Dr. Hermosisima came in, gave me an injection of anesthetic, and I fell asleep. After that, Dr. Hermosisima dissected, meticulously examined, and finally removed the obstruction. It took more than four hours to complete the surgery, and the object was more than seven inches long. After that, I gradually regained consciousness, opened my eyes and saw myself lying in the hospital room. Surrounded on all sides were several daughters and friends. I let out a sigh to myself! It's truly thrilling to live another life again. I opened my mouth to speak, but couldn't make a sound. Tears immediately filled my eyes! Hoc Nhi quickly came forward to comfort me, wanting me to calm down and rest. At that time, I knew that a hole had been cut in my neck, at the throat, and a round metal device was placed there, which could help me breathe, but I felt extremely uncomfortable. According to the doctor: After surgery, you will feel extremely frustrated. Tich Hy was very careful to stay with me all night. Luckily, I slept peacefully until morning. While in the hospital, nurses and daughters took turns taking care of me day and night.

On the morning of the 18th day, the doctor went to check on the patient, in

my hospital room, said: "Your surgery process was quite smooth, very good. You are also very brave, rest for a few days and you will recover." What else do I have to say? Just laugh bitterly! During my stay at the hospital, being visited by Dharma Master Duy Tu, Priest Tham from Thanh Tam High School, close friends, and good Buddhist friends, deeply engraved it in my heart. There were also friends from the Freedom Fatherland group who sent letters of comfort, hoping that when my body was healthy again, they would make a trip to Taiwan. I was very happy and accepted her invitation, because I had planned to visit Maitreya Internal Palace in Tich Chi to admire the full body of Master Tu Hang[52]. That is also one of my wishes.

On the eighth day, the doctor allowed me to be discharged from the hospital and rest at home, but still needed electrotherapy. Electrologist Canoy observed carefully and said: "It's best to check again. X-ray, blood test, based on age ratio, and test results, twenty days of electrotherapy is needed. Every day is ten minutes, don't interrupt." At eight o'clock every morning, Ung Nu took me for treatment. I remember that after using electrotherapy for ten days, my body was weak, my mind was exhausted, my limbs were weak, my throat was damaged, and I couldn't even drink a sip of water! My strength and strength were exhausted, I couldn't stand it, I felt like a dead person, my body lost thirty pounds. Everyone was worried about me, and I didn't want to continue the treatment, but the two doctors in charge refused. If we stop, wouldn't it be a waste of our previous efforts? After that, they repeated the research, prescribed tonic injections to help increase physical strength, and continued electrotherapy until the twentieth day. This suffering is truly indescribable!

One ​​life after another, there is still another life waiting, when will the metal breathing device attached to the neck be removed? It's been more than five months, the doctor still says it can't be removed, and I feel very worried! Finally, when can I quit? Very concerned! During those days of worry, the only way is to use a sincere heart to pray and pray to Buddha to have mercy and pardon my sins. I remember early in the morning of the 20th day of the first lunar month, I sat by the chair, closed my eyes and chanted the Chuan De mantra, and suddenly heard someone say to me: "Boi Hanh! Your karma has not been eliminated yet!" I opened my eyes in horror. Oh! That was Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, but very quickly, the Bodhisattva image was no longer seen. Therefore, I quickly knelt down in front of the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, sincerely praying for repentance and praying to the compassionate Bodhisattva to pardon my bad karma! At that time, I immediately made a vow to recite ten sets of Ksitigarbha Sutra, praying to the Bodhisattva to eliminate my karma.

From the twenty-sixth day of January, I started chanting silently. It was truly miraculous. When I recited the fifth set, the respiratory device on my neck was removed. When the doctor removed the breathing apparatus, I was extremely nervous, my emotions were both scared and excited, hard to describe! On the first day of February, I went to Dinh Hue Pagoda, where Dharma Master Duy Tu compassionately prayed for me in front of the Buddha hall. At that time, the wound was completely healed. From then on, every morning and evening I paid homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, thanking Bodhisattva for his grace in rescuing suffering. There is boundless joy and comfort in my heart!

4. Dreaming about my grandmother who passed away

Nai Vien write

Remembering my grandmother who passed away many years ago, she was not like the old lady described in the novel, "enjoying God's blessings, holding candy and playing with her grandchildren". In his old age, due to not being careful, he tripped and fell and lay sick in bed for many years. Eating, drinking, moving, all must be taken care of by our descendants in order to live out the rest of our lives. When I was in the sixth grade of Primary School[53], my eldest sister, who was studying at Trung Nguyen University, brought back precious Buddhist scriptures from the Buddhist Study Society, and also told us about Buddhism that we had never heard of. At that time, I was extremely interested. Every night, I set myself to recite the Pho Mon chapter, the Great Compassion mantra, or recite a few hundred verses of the Buddha's name. After worshiping Buddha, do your homework. Feeling very happy in my heart, I often turned to a few close classmates to preach about the greatness and depth of Buddhism. For a long time, after school or on holidays, those girls sometimes came to my house to recite Buddha's name, worship Buddha, and chant sutras.

One ​​night, when I was in seventh grade, I dreamed that my grandmother had passed away and came to find me. She carried a big belly as if she was about to give birth. I immediately thought of the Pho Mon chapter that said: "If a woman has a weak desire to seek a man, worship and make offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, she will easily give birth to merit and virtue, the male branch of wisdom. Set a desire to seek a woman, and be born with a righteous and righteous form, a female branch, be full of her own virtues, all human beings will love her" (If there is a woman who wishes to give birth to a son, worship and make offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, she will give birth to a son of merit and wisdom. If you want to give birth to a daughter, you will give birth to a virtuous daughter with a virtuous appearance, having planted the roots of virtue in advance, and everyone will love and respect you.) I was extremely happy and quickly told my grandmother who had been separated for a year: "You must quickly recite the holy name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. That way the baby will be born fat and lovely." Grandma asked me: "How to chant, I don't know!" I clasped my hands together and said: "You must be very sincere in reciting Namo, great compassion, great compassion, relief from suffering, great inspiration, Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara)..." Unexpectedly, he actually recited after me, but after reciting only a few sentences, he stopped reciting. Suddenly, his face turned pale, his eye sockets turned black, revealing a fierce, scary expression, reaching out with both hands to grab my neck and not let go. I was so scared that I fell to the ground, struggling to get away from her. Now that I think about it, he is a hungry ghost with a throat as small as a needle and a belly as big as a jar! When I woke up, my mind was still very scared. Wait until dawn, urgently ask your eldest sister about seeing her grandmother in her dream last night. She said: "Maybe after my grandmother passed away, she was still in the devil's path or hell suffering, knowing that I recite the sutra every day, so I came to tell her in my dream, hoping to save her. I can recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra to dedicate to my grandmother."

In the Sutra Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, it is said: “If in the future, all sentient beings, whether dreaming, or delusional, seeing ghosts and spirits, seeing ghosts, seeing images, or being sad, or worried, or sad, or lamenting, or dreading, or dying, will try to explain one birth, ten beings, hundreds of beings, and heavens. "In the past, parents, men, women, younger siblings, husbands, wives, relatives, in evil places, they were released from evil, hoping for salvation in the land of good fortune, in the present world, using means, vowing to leave the evil destinies." Husbands, wives, and relatives in one lifetime, ten lifetimes, thousands of lifetimes in the past, have no place to pray for blessings to save them, come and report to relatives in previous lives so that they can create the means and vow to leave the evil destinies). After watching this episode, [remember] when my grandmother passed away, gritting my teeth, gnashing my teeth, the pitiful appearance appeared before my eyes again. In the evening, before her grandmother passed away, she dreamed that her grandfather had passed away on the other side of the river calling her, waving his hand at her, wanting her to come over there. Grandma really rolled up her pant legs and waded through.

Ksitigarbha Sutra teaches: “The person who does good in Jambudvipa, at the end of his or her life, will overcome hundreds of thousands of evil destiniess and ghosts, or the changes of parents and relatives, leading the dead and spirits into the evil destinies” (The person who does good in this realm of Jambudvipa, when his life is about to end, will still have hundreds of thousands of ghosts and spirits." in the evil destinies, or turn into parents, or even relatives, to guide the deceased, causing that person to fall into the evil destinies). The next morning, he told us about his dream that his grandfather had passed away. At that time, we had not yet studied Buddhism, and we did not know at all that this was a sign that our grandmother was about to die.

Early in the morning of the next day, before I bring breakfast, I have to lift the mosquito net first. When I lifted the mosquito net to clean up, I noticed that my grandmother's face was not right: Her eyes were wide open, showing anger, her teeth were clenched in hatred, and she was breathing heavily. At that time, I was only in fifth or sixth grade of elementary school. A feeling of panic enveloped my heart. I quickly ran out the door and ran upstairs to tell my father. Dad went downstairs and saw that grandma had such a different attitude than usual. He was worried and spoke softly to her. It seemed as if she wanted to speak, as if her teeth were tightly clenched by force, unable to open. She became more and more painful, her breathing became more and more difficult, her expression became more and more unsightly, making others afraid... Because her grandmother had had her grandfather call her for many years, and then used her appearance when she died to judge, she was definitely in an evil destinies of suffering, who could have expected it!

When my grandmother passed away, I had not yet studied Buddhism, so I did not know how to quickly support rebirth. After death, within forty-nine days, one does not ask a high-ranking monk to attain transcendence and advancement. Now that I know where my grandmother was born, my heart feels miserable and painful. Therefore, he decided to save his grandmother from the deep water and fire, so that her consciousness could escape the path of suffering. I practice according to the teachings in the Ksitigarbha Sutra: "If you try the sutra with your own mind, or ask for poison, the number will change three or seven times. As if you are familiar with the evil destinies, the clear sutra will definitely change, and you will attain liberation" (If you have a single mind, read this sutra yourself, or ask someone else to read it, three times or seven times. Belonging to such an evil destinies, when the sound of chanting the sutra is heard enough times, you will be liberated). From that day on, every night after eating and showering, I made sure to brush my teeth, wash my hands, burn incense, sincerely pray, and every day faithfully chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows. After reciting each volume, be sure to dedicate it to your grandmother, praying for Buddha's light to be blessed, soon to be liberated, and to be reborn in a good way. Chanting like that about a dozen times, at night I no longer dream of my grandmother's resentful appearance!

Thanks to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's compassionate and saving power, and also grateful to Buddhist leader Śākyamuni Buddha for declaring eighty-four thousand dharma methods to adapt to the different needs and temperaments of sentient beings, we will know in the next life that the great Bodhisattvas, the ones with great compassion, are Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the one with great will. The great vow is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the great wisdom Manjushri Bodhisattva, the great vow Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, etc. to teach and save all living beings in this world of extreme suffering. Luckily in this life, I was able to study Buddhism, understand Buddha's teachings, and then be able to chant sutras to dedicate to my grandmother. But there are too many people on earth, along with the reincarnated beings in the six paths, and too few people who can hear about Buddha Dharma! Buddha once said: “Gaining a human body is like the claws on earth, losing a human body is like the great earth” (Gaining a human body is like the soil on the fingernails, losing a human body is like soil on the great earth). You should know: Once you lose your human body, you will never be able to get it back! In the three evil destiniess, wanting to study Buddha and practice diligently is as difficult as trying to ascend from the ground to heaven. How sad! Writing here, I remember the great master Thanh Khai made a great vow: “I hope that forever in the world of Sa Ba, I will save sentient beings, work as a street sweeper, clean up the filth of the human world, until fifty-six billion seven thousand years later, forming a Pure Land in the human world, welcoming Maitreya Bodhisattva to descend to the world to become Buddha”. Every time I think about this, I can't help but feel moved inside. Thinking of the Bodhisattva path, which is difficult to practice, and sentient beings who are difficult to save ("one's own internal sentient beings" and "external sentient beings" i.e., external sentient beings), when one's mind is wandering, one only needs to think of the great Bodhisattva's spirit of not being afraid of hardships, "can endure what is difficult to endure, can practice what is difficult to practice", in my heart there is truly an unspeakable shame and admiration, so I quickly work harder and always admonish. remind yourself. Life is lost drop by drop with each step, day after day, through many years, my grandmother passed away six or seven years ago. I only pray that the old man will soon be reborn, be born in a good place, and diligently study Buddhism in his next life. Also pray that in this life and the next life, until in the future life, there will be more and more thousands of street sweepers, together cleaning up the dirt in the human world, promoting the truth of Buddha Dharma, hoping that Buddha Dharma will be like sweet rain in times of drought sprinkled throughout the three thousand great thousand worlds.

5. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's dream

Thanh Ha writes

Last summer, I followed my mother to the Central region to visit my aunt whom I hadn't seen for many years. As soon as you enter the door, you see in the middle of the altar in front of the hall, worshiping two holy statues of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In front of the statue, incense smoke wafts, creating a very solemn atmosphere. I immediately clasped my hands in reverence and headed towards Bodhisattva's monastery, feeling happy in my heart because my cousin knew how to worship Bodhisattva. After the ceremony, he immediately sat on the chair and asked his aunt: "Auntie! How long has it been since you took refuge in the Three Jewels?" She looked happy, smiled and said: "It is true that I thank the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions. If it were not for the relationship with the Buddha, my old life would have gone to hell!" I didn't understand what she meant, looked at my cousin with suspicious eyes, and asked: "What was the cause that made you take refuge in the Three Jewels? I didn't expect that in a few years, my cousin would change so much!" She silently looked at the holy statue of Bodhisattva, remembered, and told: "That was a few years ago. My aunt went to visit her friend's house and noticed that her house had a holy statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In her heart, she was extremely happy and unconsciously clasped her hands together to worship. Then she forgot about it!"

She said: "Every year, no matter which god's birthday it is, we always kill a lot of animals to make offerings. The twenty-third day of the third lunar month two years ago was the birthday of Ma To Thanh Mau (Thien Hau Nguyen Quan), every family kills animals to worship. We are rich people and are devout followers of God. Ma To, of course, killed more chickens and ducks than other families, cooking up to twenty delicious salty dishes to treat to his friends. She was naturally very excited, thinking: "This time, if I hold a big party for my friends, even if I have fully devoted myself as a believer, Ma To will secretly bless and bless my whole family." Everyone enjoyed themselves, eating and drinking happily until after eight o'clock, the guests all went home Then, because of entertaining guests, calling here, calling there, busy all day, she was really tired. After bathing with warm water, she went to bed, but for some reason, she tossed and turned, still unable to sleep! It was a deep, quiet night. Suddenly, there was heavy rain and thunder, and in her mind, she suddenly felt the smell of blood in the house, and she seemed to hear the sound of chickens, ducks, and geese squawking loudly. into her ears. She felt like vomiting, had difficulty breathing, wanted to scream but couldn't make a sound! Her whole body felt numb, she couldn't sleep, and unconsciously passed out!

When I woke up early the next morning, I only felt pain all over my body, my limbs were powerless, I couldn't move, my eyes were black, my face was green, just like that I fell seriously ill. Confused, unconscious on the hospital bed, barely breathing. While unconscious, she seemed to fall into a bottomless, dark hole. She was horrified, scared, crying loudly and plaintively. Suddenly, from the top of the deep hole, a ray of light shot straight into her body, making her less afraid and at peace. A monk, with a face like a full moon and a body covered in ca-sa robes, descended from the rays of light, held her hand, and saved her from a deep pit. She followed the monk to a bright, open place. He softly told his aunt: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, whom you respectfully worshiped at your friend's house a few years ago. Because of your serious crime of killing, the animals sought your life, they did not spare you! After death, you deserve to fall into hell, suffering immeasurable suffering. Because of you with a single sincere thought, by admiring the Bodhisattva saint's statue, you will not fall into hell and suffer the retributions of suffering. Now you still have excess sins in your body, from now on, be strong. Repent of your sins, don't create killing karma. Be compassionate towards living beings, give alms generously, and accumulate merit!" Having finished speaking, I was nowhere to be found.

When she woke up, she immediately told her family about the dream situation. Everyone was skeptical, not knowing if it was real or fake. But seeing that the next day, her serious illness was able to revive from death, which can be said to be a miracle. From then on, she went to the temple to take refuge in the Three Jewels and invited the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to worship. Every day, morning and night, we worship, recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and at night reverently recite a volume of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, dedicating it to the animals that were unjustly killed early on to attain a good birth. From then on, he no longer raised animals or slaughtered living beings, and also regularly made offerings to the Three Jewels, listened to Buddha's teachings, printed and donated Buddhist scriptures to widen the Buddha's relationship, did not do evil things, did good things, and often advised others to do good things. The whole family, big and small, lived happily, and was also praised as a model family, becoming the object of admiration of the surrounding neighbors. I'm really excited, but also very embarrassed!”

Speaking of this, their aunt grinned excitedly. I heard her tell the story of her experience, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in a dream advising people to abstain from killing, causing me to naturally feel fear and do the same. Here, I respectfully advise the housewives, it is better not to kill and worship! Otherwise, the murdered living beings, in general, will one day turn to you to demand their life debt. At that time, you enter hell. If you don't have a relationship with Buddha, how can you ask Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to come and save you?

6. Great Vow to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to hear the sound of relief from suffering

Hanh Ngoc write

The twenty-first day of January, the 49th year of the Republic of China (1960), although it was winter, did not feel cold at all. I was only wearing a goat fur coat. I felt very hot, but I couldn't take it off because I had signs of catching a cold. Not long after I left for work, I suddenly received news from a certain Venerable in Taipei telling me to go to the editorial office of Bo De Thu magazine and request a book on Buddhism Questions and Answers by Mr. Ly Binh Nam. I'm an impatient person, and when it comes to things that need to be done, I can't help but do them right away. So, I took an hour and a half break, dragged my tired body to the editorial office of Bo De Thu magazine. The harsh sunlight burned, making my back drenched in sweat. I thought to myself: "My whole body is drenched in sweat. It might help me with my cold." Therefore, I still did not dare to take off that fur coat, went to the editorial office of Bo De Thu magazine, found Venerable Chau Phi and asked for the book Buddhist Studies Questions and Answers by Mr. Ly Binh Nam, which made me very disappointed that there was no longer that book there.

Going by Lien Xa, wanting to step in, I saw old layman Lai Luong Dong walking out with a bicycle. When he saw me coming in, he immediately turned the car around and said, "I'm looking for you to make merit." At the same time, he took out the Dan Thanh Daily (Tieng Dan newspaper) of the same day, and pointed to the second page and told me to look. I replied: "You are really difficult to fathom! If you want me to come, I will. If there's anything, just tell me!" But he insisted that I sit down and read the newspaper. Because I had to rush back to work, I didn't have the heart to read the newspaper. After all, I thought people wanted me to donate; Therefore, impatiently said: "Mr. Lai! If you want me to write a little, there is no problem, but if you want me to go out and make love, I have no choice!" Mr. Lai said: "Please sit down and see (he pointed to the newspaper) what kind of merit is needed?" I said: "If you don't want me to write a little, then what merit can I do?" Mr. Lai didn't wait for me to finish, then interrupted: "I saw that on Trung Phat Nguyet San, there was an article praising your story of inspiration about Ksitigarbha Sutra. Now there is a fellow layperson named Ky Tam Toan, whose family background is extremely poor. He rides a tricycle and works as an electrical worker. After the flood on August 7 (1959), his father passed away immediately afterward. At that time, he tried every means, trying his best to resolve the funeral peacefully. Therefore, there is no way to pay off the debt! Isn't it just a matter of suffering? Recently, when he was working on an electric pole that was more than two feet high, he accidentally fell down. Oh my, this person's karma is so heavy, please pray for him to relieve him of misfortune, it's truly immeasurable merit! then”. I heard Mr. Lai compassionately speak in detail like that, and I couldn't bear the pain in my heart. Therefore, from tomorrow I agree to receive the Eight Precepts and recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra for that strange lay associate Ky Tam Toan, helping him to heal soon.

Around nine o'clock in the morning on the twenty-second day, I went to Trung Thanh surgical hospital on Binh Dang street to visit layperson Ky. This was the first time in my life that I went to a surgical hospital to visit patients. It was as stressful as going directly to hell. In it, strange situations appear in all shapes and sizes; especially the unpleasant smell that pervades everywhere. I had to impolitely use a handkerchief to cover my nose. Under that situation, I really didn't want to stay long, but I couldn't help but try my best to endure. I went to hospital room number thirty and saw a few patients lying there. I didn't recognize Layman Ky. Seeing an old lady come over and ask, I found out that she was layman Ky's mother. She told me about layman Ky's hospital bed. Seeing him lying motionless on the bed, I silently recited the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, then went to layman Ky's bed and asked: "Are you vegetarian or not?" He replied: "I only eat clams on the first and full moon days." He was skinny and his voice was very weak. Seeing his appearance, if it were before I believed in Buddha, I would definitely panic and run away! I said: "If you can make up your mind to eat the Ten Trai (ten-day vegetarian diet), recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at the same time, or recite it softly, or loudly, or silently; but the essential thing is to be sincere and earnest. Only then can you be able to induce communication. Now I will recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra for you, continuing to chant until you are completely cured!"

Because of my sincerity, at that time, he was deeply moved and immediately accepted my opinion very respectfully, wanting me to write down ten days for him. I said; "Tomorrow is the Twenty-Fourth day of December, you should start eating Ten Trai!" I turned to Mrs. Ky again and said: "Your family has a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In the future, please worship more, recite more, pray to Bodhisattva to be merciful and compassionate, to bless the lay people of Ky so that they will not be disabled." I spoke mixed with Taiwanese, and he could naturally understand. "A family of eight lives depends entirely on it for its livelihood." As Mrs. Ky spoke, she showed me layperson Ky's injured left arm from a fall. I felt like I was being electrocuted, I was so scared that I could barely stand! Seeing that arm, flesh and blood were mixed together, as serious as meat sauce, red blood mixed with green color kept leaking out. His wife stood next to him and used toilet paper to soak up the blood. I thought: “Can it be cured?” I was in a heavy mood and hurried back to work.

While I was chanting at night, I suddenly felt a pain in my stomach as if I had been bitten. This is a phenomenon I have never encountered before since I started chanting the sutras until now; But I still endured the pain and chanted until the end. After chanting, my stomach pain was gone. Sometimes due to busy work, as well as busy family matters, I was often tired and exhausted, and I really couldn't lift my spirits, but when I thought of the scene of layman Ky lying on the hospital bed, moaning for help, I finally lifted my spirits and respectfully chanted the Ksitigarbha Sutra.

At noon on the twenty-fifth day of the lunar calendar, I invited a scroll painting of the holy statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to the Chengqing surgical hospital. Another patient saw the solemn statue of the Bodhisattva and was sincerely happy and praised. He was filled with joy, so I gave the holy statue to him, and explained the ten benefits of worshiping the holy image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: “First, the land is fertile; second, a home of peace and prosperity; third, the dead are reborn in heaven; fourth, the living increase their lifespan; fifth, the fulfillment of their wishes; sixth, freedom from disasters of fire and water; seventh, the cessation of damage; eight, the cessation of nightmares; ninth, the presence of divine protection in entering and exiting. guard; ten is to often encounter the cause of the saints". For what I said, that person not only believed, but also continuously thanked me: "Thank you very much."

I went to old lady Ky and asked her: "Is layperson Ky's injury any better?" Mrs. Ky's face was full of joy and she replied: "Tam Toan's injuries are quite many." As he spoke, he showed me the wound. When I saw it, I was so happy that I almost jumped up. I held my heart in joy, praised, and blurted out: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is so powerful, truly so powerful, isn't that so? Apparently, he fell to the point where his arm was injured, flesh and blood mixed together. In less than a few days, the arm's parts suddenly became clearly identifiable, and at the same time, blood and pus stopped flowing out. This is truly inconceivable!" To be honest, if we only relied on medicine, we wouldn't be able to recover that quickly! Several patients in the same room also cheered in unison. Layperson Ky looked surprised and grateful and told me: "Every day I recite the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva more than three hundred sentences." I said: "It is best to recite at every moment." Finally, I left Trung Thanh Surgical Hospital with a happy feeling.

Every Sunday, Mr. Lai and Venerable Hac An Hong periodically go to Taichung prison to propagate the Dharma. When I saw Mr. Lai, I immediately asked Layman Ky if he was feeling well? He said: "It's much better. However, according to the doctor, I still have to take X-rays and have to have two surgeries to connect the bones. Whether it will heal or not is still uncertain, but Layman Ky has no money..." Hearing his meaning, I was quite moved. Layperson Ky's illness was not cured, and in my mind there was infinite guilt and personal suffering. Because from an economic point of view, my mind is abundant, but my strength is not enough. Motivated by humanitarian sentiment, why doesn't it make me "sad and miserable?" After returning home, I didn't want to do anything, so I kept thinking, is there any way to keep Ky lay people from having to have surgery? I said to myself: "King Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! I thank the old man for blessing the lay practitioner Ky Tam Toan to recover from his external injuries, but right now his left hand still cannot function. According to the doctor, he still needs to have two surgeries, but he is still not sure that he will completely recover. The lay practitioner Ky is so pitiful, the disciple who prayed to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva instead felt compassion and used his inconceivable supernatural power to bless the lay practitioner Ky Ksitigarbha without the need for surgery." I pray and repeat that every day.

One ​​Wednesday night, I listened to the sutra at Tu Quang Do Library and heard my friends say that he was looking for me. I thought about it, wondering if Layman Ky had recovered from his illness or not. I looked for Mr. Lai, and without waiting for him to open his mouth, I quickly asked: "Has the layperson been discharged from the hospital?" (I felt reassured when I saw him smile). He replied: "The lay practitioner has been discharged from the hospital." I asked again: "Is it surgery or not?" He replied: "It's very strange to say this! There was no surgery! Suddenly I met an old man who connected the bones and massaged them several times before they healed completely. Is it true that you are addressing Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? Ky Tam Toan wants to come and thank you." Let me tell you the story of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva praying to you! He was already smiling, but he laughed even happier, took off his glasses, and said directly: "No wonder! It's really no wonder!"

“Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva uses his supernatural powers to manifest the image of Shravaka, the treasury of wonderful merits, the birthplace of the precious treasures of liberation, the clear bright eyes of Bodhisattvas, the guiding eyes to Nirvana of noble people, like the Wish-fulfilling Pearl, whose all kinds of treasures according to one's wishes are satisfied and illuminated. Those who do good are like the radiant sun, illuminating those who have lost their way like a torch, dispelling heat and afflictions like the clear moon, making bridges to cross the four streams, making boats to reach the opposite shore, subduing pagans like a king lion, subduing heavenly demons like the great dragon [sword]; protecting those who are afraid like relatives and friends, fending off enemies like moats and citadels, saving from danger like parents. Just as it is written in chapter thirteen of the Sutra, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Vows: "At the same time, the World-Honored One made a golden gesture, and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva spoke: - Ksitigarbha! Ksitigarbha! What powers are inconceivable, what compassion is inconceivable, what wisdom is inconceivable, what eloquence is inconceivable. The true history The Buddhas of the ten directions, extolled and expounded the teachings of the impersonal factors that, throughout thousands of kalpas, cannot be fully attained" (At that time, the World-Honored One raised his golden arm, rubbed the head of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva, and said thus: - Ksitigarbha! Ksitigarbha! Your divine power is inconceivable, your compassion is inconceivable, your wisdom is inconceivable. Your eloquence is inconceivable. Suppose in the ten directions The Buddhas praised him and declared that his inconceivable story could not be explained in a thousand lifetimes).

Smiling and saying goodbye to Mr. Lai, even though it was late at night, I respectfully faced the Buddha and bowed forty-eight times towards Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. After that, she shed tears, the kindness of parents is difficult to repay, but the great kindness of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot be limited, there is no way to repay, only single-mindedly reciting the Buddha's name, vowing to preserve the two words Trai Precepts, respectfully facing the Western Buddhaland, attaining Nirvana. Therefore, I definitely pay my respects. May readers recite together: “Namo the great vow of great compassion and compassion to overcome the sufferings of the deity Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva! Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva!”

7. Namo Minh Duong Great Vow Master Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva

Hanh Ngoc says

Great vows Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Guan Yin Bodhisattva (Avalokiteśvara) are both fathers and mothers of suffering beings, a refuge for both human world and hell at this time, in this life. Every time I hear the sound of a fire truck blowing its siren, I immediately feel uneasy as if I am experiencing that scene myself. Those gamblers really harm people to no end! In the 42nd year of the Republic of China (1953), our lives were miserable, our children were young, our bodies were weak, our spirits were crushed. Basically, it's full of dharma joy!

1. On the first day of the first month of the 45th Republic of China (1956), I obeyed the order to take over the retail store of the Taichung Prison Camp (store at No. 86 Tu Do Street, Taichung, opposite the court). All products made by prisoners such as rattan furniture, woodwork, grass weaving, weaving, etc. are sold there. The store's architecture is ten parts simple. I eat at the store, almost doing business myself. Although the bedroom is small, I put a single bed, the remaining space is for worshiping Buddha, using a cloth curtain to divide it. The kitchen is small and narrow, in front of the kitchen door is a large table for working, next to it is a price ticket of 250 VND. At that time, I used an old-style kerosene stove. One afternoon, I accidentally filled the stove with oil. The stove is old and about to become waste, but I still can't bear to throw it away. I lit the fire to cook rice and went to the back to wash the vegetables. After washing the vegetables, I saw a blazing fire, so I was in such a hurry that I put the stove next to my desk. While pointing at the curtain to hang the bell, suddenly the eldest child rushed forward, grabbed the military blanket from the bed, wrapped it around the stove, and threw it out the door. The fire was still burning fiercely, and passersby stood with their arms crossed, watching. Suddenly, a young man about twenty years old ran over, quietly exhausted his efforts to help, and even more courageous than my eldest child, extinguished the fire. Viewers all praised it. When I wanted to thank that young man, he was nowhere to be found!

When I panicked and placed the burning stove next to the work table, the oil from the stove was full and spilled all over the ground, all four sides were items for sale. The fire scorched a corner of the price slip at the desk. The table was not damaged at all, and any of the public items were not damaged at all. If that young man is not the reincarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, then what is he? Every month I worship Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Chapter twelve of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra says: "If in the future, good men and good women, in the present and future desires, hundreds of thousands of millions of wishes, hundreds of thousands of millions of equal wishes, taking refuge, worshiping, making offerings, praising the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, such as the wish for all stages to be fulfilled. Fulfilling the vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is great compassion, forever supporting the self. Do you see? "If in the future, there are good men and good women who should only take refuge, worship, make offerings, and praise the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and all such wishes will be fulfilled. Again, I pray that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva will be willing to be very compassionate and forever support me. While dreaming, the Bodhisattva immediately patted his head and received the prediction." It was twenty years ago, and when I write down this premonition, I still remember everything clearly in my mind as before. If a big fire burns away all the goods on sale and spreads to neighboring rooms, I will definitely be convicted and spend my life behind bars, leaving behind my poor child, which is truly unthinkable! Due to this event, I have never received any reprimand from my superiors. Writing here, tears of gratitude flow!

2. On May 1, Republic of Korea 57 (1968), I applied to be assigned as a warden at the detention center of the Taipei court. My colleagues agreed that I should have surgery to ease my suffering: “Nhat labor forever” (Tired for a while, at ease forever). My children saw that my illness was serious and strongly agreed that I should have surgery. I would rather die, still afraid of surgery. The doctor saw that I refused surgery and told me to go home. I just had to go home and lie in bed, my whole body was in pain. I regretted why I didn't have the surgery, and wanted to have the surgery. In short, being entangled in conflicts and insecurities!

Moving from Taichung to Taipei, the furniture is messy, the rooms are small and narrow, the Bodhisattva statue I worship has not been worshiped, and this suffering doesn't know when it will end. While my mind was confused, I saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva giving me a book of Ksitigarbha's Original Vows Sutra. I suddenly had a great realization: Hoping to be assigned to work as a warden at the Taipei courthouse, I made a vow to the Bodhisattva to recite one hundred and eight sets of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra. I prayed to Bodhisattva: "Please don't test me anymore. Even though there are mountains of knives and cauldrons of oil, I still firmly believe in Buddha. I also wholeheartedly advise others to believe in Buddha. I pray to Bodhisattva of great compassion to help me heal quickly." I lay in bed all day moaning, saying to myself, my illness gets better every day, my body recovers. Recite all 108 sets of Earth Store Vows Sutra. Until today, every day I recite at least one set, the inspiration is inconceivable. In my mind, every moment is the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Without reciting it, my body is healthy, better than all the nutrients in the world. Due to many previous lives, I have owed my life, or my spiritual debt, in this life I am protected by the Bodhisattva, paying off all my debts. I am single-minded and steadfast in praying to escape birth and death and to be liberated and free. “Namo Minh Duong Great Vow Master Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Mahasattva!”

8. Commemorating the kindness of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Hanh Ngoc write

Quickly, in the blink of an eye, the thirty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month is the holy birthday of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Everyone knows that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is in hell saving and teaching sentient beings who have committed serious crimes. Everyone who respects and worships Him should learn from His great saving spirit. I vow to practice meditation throughout the seventh lunar month, to express my devotion to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Furthermore, I also want to learn from His spirit in order to skillfully educate female compatriots who commit crimes, making them accept Buddhism, eliminate evil, and turn to goodness. Sure enough, layperson Lam (Ms. Lam Khan Tri) brought two fellow practitioners along. They saw the prisoners' fervent belief in Buddhism, so they praised me and called me Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. I was scared, ashamed, and told them what I had experienced at work due to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's predestined inspiration, making them extremely surprised and praising me! The situation of receiving my grace is like a person who has lost his way and suddenly has a bright place to return to and reside in, like a person who has been sick for a long time and is suddenly healed. Now I can only respectfully recount the memorable things I have experienced as follows:

I can work at the prison, so I should sincerely appreciate Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's inspiration. I remember last fall, I was groaning on the hospital bed, unable to sit, and unable to stand. Unfavorable circumstances and an unstable life cannot make me feel free and at ease. Precisely because I am a Buddhist, every time I encounter troubles with no way to escape, I cry sadly in front of the Buddha, in front of the holy image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, repenting, realizing that I have created all kinds of evil in the past, that's why I have to suffer such suffering in this life! Time passed very quickly, my suffering became deeper, my only solution was to pray to Buddha and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to liberate me. The work of relying on others to introduce me a few times, every time I felt hopeful, in a moment of excitement, eventually became an illusion, making me no longer have the courage to pray to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, but who else can I rely on? In the world, who is the most honest supporter? Think about it, think back, console yourself, naturally develop constant and steadfast faith without being lazy, sincerely pray unceasingly before the holy statues of Buddha and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

One ​​weekend evening, there was a loud knock at the door, then someone called me. When I opened the door, it turned out to be a lay follower from Lien Xa returning from listening to the Sutra. His attitude was very urgent. He gave me a small piece of paper. Without waiting for me to thank him, he left. On the piece of paper was printed the word Summons to Take the Exam to Be a Warden of Taichung Prison. The registration deadline was noon the next day. At 8:00 a.m. the next day, exams will begin in the subjects of National Literature, the teachings of the Father of the Nation (Sun Dat Tien), history, civics, and math. I am a person who has been out of school for more than ten years, and I have completely forgotten everything I learned! Therefore, I worry all night and cannot sleep. The next day, at ten o'clock, I went to the market, passed by layperson Cam's house, and was cheered a few times by her, wanting me to register. Thinh Tinh couldn't refuse, so she had to drag her body there that had been sick for a long time and wasn't completely healthy. Oh my god! The registration area was crowded with men and women. It was said that women only recruited one person. What credentials do I have to take the exam? Then, think again, still give it a try! Therefore, I borrowed some books from high school students and read them quickly. I worked hard for half a day and a night, without eating or sleeping. I thought I had thoroughly memorized all the topics and had some understanding of taking the exam. Only then did I reluctantly take the exam. The result did not disappoint the suffering people. I was sick and could not take medicine to get better. I was also sent to serve in the prison where the sinners and suffering beings in the world live, allowing me to solve the problems in life. Therefore, I more respectfully imitate the vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and also learn from his spirit of generosity to sinful and suffering sentient beings.

I remember the day before I came to work at the prison, one morning around seven o'clock, while dreaming, it seemed like I was sleeping but not sleeping. I dreamed that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's instructions were not at all different from the truth in the present. Thinking back to such inconceivable divine power made me a glutton, without salty food I would not be able to swallow. At that time, I passionately resolved to fast every month on the first and full moon days. Gradually increased to Quan Am Trai and then to Thap Trai. I am confident that I will soon start becoming a vegetarian in the future. Many friends who do not believe in Buddha say: "Don't be afraid to believe in Buddha, just be afraid of being vegetarian!" I explained to them: Believing in Buddha absolutely does not prohibit us from eating salty foods. We are vegetarian because when we believe to the level of sincerity (believing in the six paths of reincarnation, not being able to eat the flesh of living beings), we will naturally want to be vegetarian. Speaking according to worldly dharma, when you encounter difficulties, your friends help you solve them. When your own situation gets better, of course you will definitely buy gifts within your means to give to people, or give them favorite things. We should learn from the Buddha's compassion, loving the lives of living beings as much as our own lives.

Layman Duong Tuong Thanh once imitated the great spirit of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, served in Hsinchu prison in Taichung for many years, educated, advised, and guided sentient beings who suffered in prison because of their crimes. Many people were influenced by him and painstakingly corrected their previous mistakes and took refuge in the Three Jewels. Last year, Duong layman was honored to be a military judge; Not only do we Buddhist friends feel extremely happy, but it can be said that the military branch is fortunate to know how to use people. I strongly believe that the lay people will be able to rely on the spirit of justice and integrity, so that criminals who have made mistakes and broken the law will be judged fairly and peacefully, without being unjustly wronged. His wife is also a devout Buddhist, keeps the precepts, is stoic, treats others kindly, has a spirit of great compassion, sacrifices herself to save others, truly makes others incredibly impressed! Isn't that the reincarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva? Now, because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's holy birthday is coming, to commemorate the Bodhisattva's kindness, I especially respectfully narrate my experiences to demonstrate his virtue, to express my deep inner appreciation.

9. The recent premonition story of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Hanh Ngoc write

September 8th is the day I'm on duty. At seven o'clock in the afternoon, it was windy, accompanied by light rain. Colleagues brought a female prisoner, numbered 15, named Truong Bich Van, twenty-six years old, and carrying a yellow-haired, skinny little girl who was always crying and crying. I don't know what disease it is? I thought he had a very dangerous form of epilepsy, so I immediately rang the phone bell to call the chief medical officer. The class leader said: "It's childhood paralysis, there's no other way to treat it. As long as there's no fever, there's no problem!" I asked: "Headmaster! This child won't stop whining, very pitiful. Is there any medicine to take, or an injection that will prevent the child from getting sprained?" The class leader replied: "There is no way to cure it!"

I asked prisoner number 15: "Where are you from? What crime did you commit? How long will you be in prison? Is there anyone in the house?" She replied: "I'm from Wufeng village, Taichung district. I was at home cooking some rice wine for my father to drink. Someone else denounced me and was imprisoned for three months. The baby is already three years old. Just a few days after being born, he got this disease. He spent a lot of money on treatment but couldn't get better. My husband is in the army." I smiled and said: "If you have a relationship with Buddha, your mind will be at peace." I immediately wrote the name of the child (Cao Tu Nguyet, three years old) and placed it in front of the Buddha statue. In the middle of the night, I heard crying. When I went to look, I saw number 15 holding a crying child. The prisoners in the same room all sat up, chanting Buddha in low voices. I think this child has a sprained tendon, there is no other way to cure it, I tell you to recite Buddha's name and dedicate it to Buddha and Bodhisattva!

A few days passed like that. Number 7 and number 11, who were in the same room as number 15, said to me: "Supervisor! This child is truly pitiful, his tendons are pulled three or four times a night. Each time can take up to thirty minutes. We can't sleep, we sit up and recite Buddha's name." I told everyone: "Tell me, what crime did a three-year-old child commit? He was born with this incurable disease, was unable to walk or sit freely, and was still suffering from cramped tendons, as if he was being tortured in hell. Isn't that the evil karma created in his previous life? Cause and effect are laid out before your eyes, don't be greedy for temporary glory and create karma, fall into the Hell of No Interruption, with no hope of ever escaping! This example is worthy of everyone's vigilance. Be sure to believe in Buddha, chant Buddha's name to escape birth and death!"

One ​​day at nine o'clock in the evening, the baby's tendons were pulled, he cried without a sound, his eyes rolled white for several dozen minutes, and he looked like he was about to die. Prisoner number 15 was screaming and crying. I invited the head nurse and the three nurses on duty to come and take a look. They said: "There is no medicine that can cure it!" Tell me to recite Buddha's name! After they left, I led number 15 in front of the Buddha, chanting the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for more than ten minutes. That night, the child was very peaceful and slept soundly. Every time I heard the baby's cry like that, I felt miserable in my heart, intending to chant Buddha's name to pray for her, but I couldn't help but doubt, fearing that chanting Buddha's name would not relieve the baby's illness and would create a negative reaction for the girls. I kept thinking and thinking, the suffering made me unable to bear it, finally I developed courage, faced the Buddha, respectfully clasped my hands, loudly chanting the holy name "Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva". Three minutes later, the baby stopped crying. Therefore, towards the Buddha, pray to recite the three Ksitigarbha Sutras and dedicate them to the child's hearing. Every time I chant, I shed tears.

Once, while washing my hands at the sink, I saw number 15 washing clothes, and I asked her: "Number 15! Is your child better?" She smiled and replied: "It helps a lot!" I still didn't believe it, so I asked again: "How much better?" She replied: "I don't get cramps as many times as before. Sometimes I get them once or twice a day, but not at night. The time I get cramps is not that long! Before, I get cramps three or four times a night, five or six times during the day. When I get cramps, I clench my arms and legs towards my head. Muscles all over my body are pulled by tendons, and even though it's cold, my hair is still sweaty." It's been like that for the past three years." After listening, I felt strange. I had not finished reciting three sets of sutras but I had a premonition so quickly. Before I had eaten lunch, I lit incense before the Buddha, with a sincere heart, thanking Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for his inconceivable mighty power to save sentient beings who were drowning in the sea of ​​suffering. I had nothing to give in return, so I made a vow that every time the Ten Trai recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, I would respectfully stand upright (reciting one set takes ninety minutes). While chanting, I heard the baby crying again. I called number 15 and took the baby to the Buddha's table. I respectfully clasped my hands and loudly chanted the holy name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, simply wanting to call on Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to respond; I couldn't hold back my sadness and burst into tears. Number 15 also cried. But I cried and sadly prayed: "Please, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, please bless this child to be free from suffering." In less than two minutes, the baby stopped crying. Accidentally hearing the child's cry, I immediately began to repent, hating myself for not cultivating properly, ashamed and in tears, hoping to never hear the child's cry like that again! Maybe it's a psychological effect, sometimes when another baby cries, I also think it's crying. I looked at him in panic, his mother was holding him and smiling. The baby was raised fat, number 15's face was filled with joy.

I only chanted six sets of sutras, day and night, without hearing the baby's cry anymore. But I was still worried, every time I entered the door, I asked everyone: "Is number 15's baby okay?" Everyone responded in unison: "The supervisor's merit is great! For such a suffering child, after you chanted the Ksitigarbha Sutra, he got better. The child is much prettier than before and can also walk. Number 15 entering this place is even more fun than winning the special lottery!" Every day she would grin and ask: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva takes care of hell, so why does he still take care of us?" I explained: - Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's vow is that the hell will not be empty, and he will not become a Buddha. Not only does he often stay in hell, but he also adorns hell and saves sinners and suffering beings in hell. At the same time, it also saves all sentient beings in the six paths, as the chapter Confessing the Buddha's Name in the Ksitigarbha Sutra teaches: "Buddha announces to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: With the golden desire to bring compassion, save all sentient beings from sin and suffering in the six paths, speaking inconceivably" (Buddha told Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: - Now you want to arouse compassion, save all sinful and suffering sentient beings in the six paths, speaking inconceivable things). From there, we can know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva was entrusted by the Buddha to save all sentient beings in the six paths, and is not limited to sentient beings in hell. As long as you sincerely recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, there is no place where he will not appear and save you. The Praying for Falling Causes and Heavens chapter of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra reads: "All sentient beings in Nam Jambudvipa are indeterminate in nature, with bad habits, they develop good minds, and when they practice wandering, they retreat. When they encounter evil conditions, their thoughts increase. Di ṃṭṣaṇā, the corn dharma divides hundreds of thousands of billions of teachings, depending on their nature, they are liberated" There are many evils, even if you develop a good mind in an instant, if you encounter evil conditions, your thoughts will increase. For that reason, I divide this body into hundreds of thousands of billions of people and teach them, depending on their nature. This proves Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's great compassionate wish to save sentient beings. He has indescribable and endless magical powers!

After listening, you will probably think it sounds like a myth;

but this is a true story in our prison, you can inquire. Or if there are people who are skeptical about believing in Buddha, whether they need to invite a doctor or not, I can also advise you: People who believe in Buddha very deeply will not need to invite a doctor. Because that person believes deeply, feels the way, if there is a feeling, there will be a response. Suffering or happiness is completely caused by karma. Therefore, we can be single-minded in the path and save sentient beings. For example, if you wear clothes, if they tear a piece, then patch it again, then tear it again, then patch it again, until it can't be patched anymore, so it's okay to throw it away! In short, when we study Buddhism, we must be sincere and earnest, repent and recite the Buddha's name, then we can be inspired by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. If you cannot achieve inspiration, it is because you do not repent urgently, or because you are greedy, or because the karma of life is too deep. If you can use a sincere heart to pay respect to the Bodhisattva, you will definitely be able to turn big things into small things, and small things into nothing. Since you are disciples who have taken refuge in the Three Jewels, you must clearly understand the cause and effect of the three lifetimes and master this period of no freedom. This is truly a good opportunity to practice reciting the Buddha's name. Just like a Buddhist shaman in seclusion, at every moment do not forget to recite the Buddha's name and pray to be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, then you will be eternally happy!

Like Vong Ngon writes

Huizhou Record

18. Create a premonition statue

La Vien Dieu records

The fairy mother is Lady Ly Thai. From the age of sixty, every Winter period, her legs were numb, sore, unable to walk, and healed on their own in the Spring. In the 12th year of the Republic of China (1923), my mother was sixty-nine years old, her calf pain became worse, she groaned and lay in bed for more than a month, with no relief from treatment. Vien Dieu only knows how to recite the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra every day to ask for His mercy and blessings. One day, recite to the Tathagata Praise chapter: “Or hold on to the patient's favorite object, or clothes, treasures, manors, houses, speak to the patient in a high voice, speak in a high voice, and treat the patient with money in front of the sutras and objects, or make offerings to the sutras and images, or create Buddha or Bodhisattva images” (Or take the patient's favorite things, or clothes, treasures, farms, gardens temple, house, in front of the patient, loudly chanting: "My name is... for this patient, in front of sutras and statues, give up all kinds of objects to make offerings to sutras, statues, or create images of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas"), and then it seemed like he was at a loss! After reciting, the Buddha made a vow to create a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for his mother, and even ran to tell his mother. Mother happily said: "Sickness is nothing but karma. You need to rely on the Buddha's family equipment. Now you have made a vow to create an image, which is in accordance with my wishes. I was given a pure, round, bright pearl by your grandmother. Because I miss my grandmother, I treasure it very much. Is it okay to offer that pearl to the Bodhisattva now?"

I then relied on the famous statue master in Bac Binh (Beijing), Mr. Canh Son, to follow the correct method of sculpting statues with bronze and gilded with gold. The pearl is inlaid between the eyebrows to symbolize the white pride. Twenty days later, the statue was carved. Mr. Canh brought it, his appearance was dignified, compassionate and joyful. Mr. Canh said that since the statue was carved until now, unprecedented things have happened. Vien Dieu quickly told his mother. After hearing this, the pain immediately went away, she got out of bed, entered the Buddha hall, prostrated, and knelt down like someone who was not sick. This is a long-term illness that quickly goes away. Those who saw and those who heard all lamented the Bodhisattva's inconceivably quick and compassionate response! Therefore, I have relied on Mr. Canh to create more than dozens of Bodhisattva statues. My mother was a vegetarian and recited Buddha's name; From then on, I became more diligent and moved faster than before. Until the twenty-first day of December, the 18th year of the Republic of Korea (1929), when he was seventy-five years old, he recited Buddha's name and returned to the West. La Vien Dieu in Bao Tinh district, Hunan province respectfully recorded.
