In general, the writer has a spirit of atonement, is only ashamed of himself, does not dare to omit every point, every drop in the holy teachings of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra, all of which are respectfully and carefully followed. Recalling my mother's illness for six years, almost being locked up in prison, I felt even more miserable and indescribable! From the effect, refer to the cause, you will know that up and down in the cold family are deeply sorry, and feel the retribution of suffering. If the writer does not completely regret, become enlightened, take refuge, believe in the Three Jewels, and rely on Buddha's grace, I am afraid that the suffering may not be just like that. In particular, the mother's body was strong, lying in bed for fourteen days, with absolutely no other signs of illness (no fever, no pain. Later, because she lay for a long time, her body was in pain when moved). At the time of death, there was not the slightest bit of pain, eyes looked at the statue of the Western Three Saints, ears heard the Buddha's name, peacefully stopped breathing, as if entering a dreamland. If not blessed by Buddha and Bodhisattva's compassion, how could such a thing happen? Even if I cannot be born in the West, I also pray that in my next life I will be reincarnated into a house of good knowledge, soon hear the Buddha's teachings, and be diligent on the path to Bodhi.

32. Broken mirror heals

Hue Tu write

About two months ago, I noticed my husband was behaving strangely

After searching, after silently investigating and listening, I found out that he was a bit sneaky on the outside. I think if we don't expose this matter too much, we will avoid a deadlock situation. Who would have thought that it wasn't simple, they had a plan to force me to divorce. The family was originally happy and harmonious, but because a third person intervened, we were often noisy and unable to talk. My husband was confused and dizzy. In order to achieve his goal, he had no way to control his wandering mind! One day, while I was cleaning in the Buddhist hall, he took the mop, beat me, and forced me to agree to a divorce! Because of the child, I did not agree, he immediately strangled me with the intention of using death as a threat. While the crossbow was at full strength, I let go of the ten thousand conditions, recited the holy name Ksitigarbha, and single-mindedly turned my attention to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Perhaps because I was single-minded, I didn't feel any pain, but he fell back to the ground for no reason, making him even more angry. I remember my master once told me that arguing will nourish anger, so I didn't make a fuss, nor did I want to tell anyone, and I didn't want to use tears to gain his approval. Every time I feel sad and want to cry, I sadly face the Buddha and beg for repentance.

At the end of the month, I and a few lay people went to Ksitigarbha Monastery to attend the Ksitigarbha dharma conference. Entering the main hall, remembering the Bodhisattva's compassion, tears suddenly fell down his face, sincerely repenting of his own deep karma. Suddenly, I saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva facing me and smiled. Thinking I was dizzy, I carefully focused and looked, it was true! I couldn't help but feel a rushing stream of clear water inside. At two o'clock in the afternoon, the sound of breaking sound began to resound, everyone seemed to be bathing in a sea of ​​pure Dharma, an atmosphere of harmony. Recite the text of the Ksitigarbha Sutra until the paragraph: "The greatest karma can rival Meru, it can penetrate the vast ocean, it can obstruct the holy path. Let all sentient beings despise small evils, be innocent, death will be repaid, the family will live happily, father and son will be close to each other, the paths will be completely separate, they will meet each other, there will be no great life" (Karma is very much, it can be bigger than Mount Meru, it can be deep in the ocean, it can obstruct the holy path. Because Therefore, sentient beings should not ignore small evils, thinking that there is no sin. After death, there will be retribution, even if each person meets, they will not bear the blame for each other. Deeply feel that the cause and effect is not wrong, be brave to face it, and encourage yourself not to create new karma or create bad relationships. If it is true that the relationship with her husband has ended, I only hope that Bodhisattva will compassionately point out the direction of survival for mother and child. Because of that, the inner mind gradually heals

gradually calm down.

On the same day of the Dharma conference, he and the other woman went to the ballroom. When he returned in the middle of the night, he immediately told me that someone urged him to go home. At first, I didn't care. It was like that for four days in a row, he even turned to me to explain and ask for forgiveness. I was surprised and immediately invited him to repent before Buddha. Later, he recounted that in the ballroom, there was a very tall man who passed in front of him and immediately disappeared, but in his ear, someone seemed to whisper in his ear: "Go home quickly! Don't hang out with that woman anymore! Go back and apologize to them and their mother." But the other person also dreamed that someone said: "Destroying the family, causing others to separate from their wife and children, will suffer very severe consequences. Don't be so delusional that you won't be enlightened anymore!" The two of them reminisced, feeling very scared in their hearts. Therefore, automatically break up!

This storm in our family has been stabilized. It can truly be said that it is due to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's majestic and inconceivable power of compassion. Because my husband realized his previous mistakes, he now loves and cares for his family twice as much, and also often reads Buddhist books, and feels even more that Buddhist principles are an indispensable guideline for how to behave and be human. Because of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we have established a Buddhist family like today.

noi_dung:
II. Premonitions before the nineteenth century

1. Recording the radiant inspiration of the Ksitigarbha painting from the Liang Dynasty at Thien Tich Pagoda

During the Liang Dynasty, at Thien Tich Pagoda in Duong District, Hanzhou (now Guanghan District, Sichuan Province), on the wall of the east corridor, there were statues of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha and Avalokiteshvara by Truong Tang Dieu[62] painted, shaped like a monk sitting solemnly. People at that time admired, worshiped, and radiated strange light. In the year of Lan Duc (663), the monks in the pagoda worshiped, admired, and praised it as strange and unusual. Therefore, using silk to apply to the wall to recreate it and worship it in other places also radiates light just like the original statue. Contemporaries took turns drawing and imitating them in large numbers. In the third year of Lan Duc (665), when Vuong Ky came to be the Governor of Tu Chau, he often painted and reproduced it and diligently made offerings. There were ten boats traveling together, suddenly encountered a storm in the middle of the road, nine of them sank. Encountering that fierce wave, only Vuong Ky's boat was not afraid at all, immediately knowing that it was due to Bodhisattva's great compassion that it had such power! In the third year of Thuy Cung (687), the queen (Vu Tac Thien) heard about it and immediately ordered the artist to paint and adapt it, the painting shined as before, just like the painting being worshiped at the ashram [Thien Tich Pagoda]. In the year of the Great Lich (766), a monk at Bao Tho pagoda in the ashram saw a strange light emitting light and wrote a report. The king then respectfully bowed and praised that light! When the Bodhisattva appears, the country is often peaceful and more auspicious.

There was a merchant's wife, who was pregnant for twenty-eight months without giving birth. One day, suddenly seeing the light of the Bodhisattva, she immediately drew an image and made a single-minded vow to the Bodhisattva. That same night, a son was born, his appearance was dignified, everyone who saw him was happy. Therefore, the whole world calls [that statue] the Radiant Bodhisattva.

2. Notes on the Ksitigarbha painting releasing light at the Phap Tu Pagoda of the Tang Dynasty

During the Tang Dynasty, Phap Tu Pagoda at Quach Ha in Ich Chau had a statue depicting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva sitting on a rope bed[63], with his legs hanging down. down, eight inches and six centimeters tall. That statue was originally painted by Truong Tang Dieu. In the seventh month of the second year of Lan Duc, the monks in the pagoda drew an imitation of a copy, and the statue immediately shone like a golden ring, suddenly emanating, suddenly disappearing. Draw so many copies one after another, they all emit the same light. In August of that year, he was ordered to present a copy to the palace for offerings. All monks and laymen inside and outside the capital, painting and making offerings, also saw the radiance and believed that the Buddha's power was beyond measure. Each artist adapted a separate version, achieving an impression that cannot be completely recorded!

3. Records of Ksitigarbha saving suffering for the Ly family in Ho district during the Tang Dynasty

During the Tang Dynasty, in Ho district in Ung Chau, there was a girl with the Ly family name, very faithful and obedient to men's precepts. In the house, worship the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva carved in wood, one meter six inches high, bright, lively, and quite strange. Ms. Ly had a servant in her fifties who had wrong views and did not believe in the Dharma. One day, Ly Thi went to another place, she moved the statue and threw it out into the wilderness behind the house. Ly Thi returned home, crying and looking for her. The statue radiates light in the wilderness. Ly Thi happily welcomes it back, not knowing why the servant did it. The next day, the servant suddenly fainted and fell unconscious. Next, he suddenly woke up, cried and repented, and told himself the story in the dark place as follows:

- When I died, I suddenly saw two mandarins riding horses, taking the mandarin's message themselves, and told the mandarin to read it again. The messenger said: "The servant who desecrated the holy statue and threw it into the wilderness has committed a great crime and must be arrested and taken to the king's palace." After reading the official message, he was tied up and taken to the King's Palace. Arriving in front of the palace, I saw countless people with shackles, shackles, shackles, and chains restraining their bodies. The king angrily said: "You are a foolish servant, you disgraced the saint's image, threw it into the wilderness behind the house, you must suffer retribution. In the house, you indulged, worshiped gods, ignored the holy statues, and still had wrong views, did not believe in the Dharma, you deserve to be imprisoned in the great hell." At that time, a monk suddenly arrived in front of the hall. The king immediately stepped down from the pedestal and was very respectful. The king asked: "Why have you come?" The monk said: "This servant is a maid in my benefactor's house. Even though I hate my statue, I will not leave it. I hope the king will have mercy and grant him a long life." The king said: "Please follow my orders." At that time, after listening, I felt repentant and suddenly chanted: “Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva”. Immediately, depending on the chanting sound, the sinners present in the hall, wherever the chanting sound reached, the shackles, shackles, shackles, chains all freed themselves, their bodies were nowhere to be seen. At that time, the King Yama sat and looked stunned. The monk immediately took my hand and led me out

hall. Immediately, I came back to life.

When Ly Thi heard that, she respected that statue even more. Therefore, in an entire district, everyone has trust and admiration.

4. Records of the golden statue of Ksitigarbha saving the To family's parents in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty

Tang Dynasty, Prime Minister[64] The Patriarch's faith in Phu Chau was true and solid, but his parents did not believe very much. The Patriarch family, for the sake of their parents, created a standing statue of the golden-colored Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, three meters high, with a halo surrounding his body, devoted wholeheartedly, respectfully worshiping and meditating. At that time, his father was from Duong Do and had to temporarily leave, so his mother stayed home alone. At night, there was an evil thief peeking through the door, trying to steal clothes, but only saw Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva sitting, [so he did not dare to enter]. The next day, the enemy changed his clothes, went to that house, and saw the old lady sitting there neatly dressed, but did not see the saint's statue. The thief's heart was surprised, so he confessed his guilt, to express his shame and remorse, and recounted what he had seen in the night. Father returned home, mother told the story above, and together they considered the reason.

Later, my father went to Phu Chau. On the way, he met a resentful family member who pulled out a sharp knife and rushed to slash. Suddenly, a monk with a sharp golden body used his hand to block the tip of the knife, used his head to receive the tip of the knife, and the victim fell to the ground. At that time, the resentful person thought he had killed them, so he ran away. His father avoided being killed, feeling very strange! Going to the Patriarch's house, telling the above story in detail, gave birth to a rare feeling. Together, we went to the place where the statue was worshiped to worship. We saw three knife marks on the statue's head. The yellow color changed a little, as if it was bleeding. The Patriarch immediately knew that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva had endured the execution and saved his father from danger. His father immediately had faith, and the To family welcomed his mother into their home. Three people lived in Phu Chau, worshiping day and night. His father did not pass away until he was seventy-nine years old.

For thirty-five days, the Patriarch dreamed that his father had a luminous body, flying freely in the air, flying back and forth. He was born with a rare heart, vainly asking where his father was born? Answer: "I was born in the fourth heaven, guided by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and serving the Bodhisattva Bodhisattva. Most of the people who were born in that heaven were guided by the Great Being. The Great Being (Maitreya Bodhisattva) praised: 'The Great Being does not overlook those who deserve to be saved by the Buddhas' form. Again: "Thirteen years later, your mother will be born at the end of her lifespan." "And I was born twenty-five years later. My wife and I were born twenty-eight years later." After saying those words, he disappeared and did not appear. Later, the To family's mother and husband were exactly as their father said. You should know that a person who creates a statue and his relatives will all benefit in the present life. From then on, in the entire continent, there were many people creating statues, painting statues, worshiping, and making offerings, and many people were inspired.

5. Recording the story of the induction of the monk in the capital, Tang Tuan

During the Song Dynasty, Thich Tang Tuan, whose real name was Vuong, was from the capital. After becoming a monk, he took care of the Sangha's affairs, wasted a lot of money, neglected his three karmas, and never cultivated good deeds. He had no moral precepts and had never practiced good deeds. He contracted a minor illness and died. His sides were still warm, three days later he came back to life, cried, threw himself on the ground, and told the story in detail as follows:

- When he was about to die, two officials from the underworld chased him to the door of a large citadel. Suddenly a monk said: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. When you were in the capital, you drew and adapted one of my paintings. Even though you never worshiped or made offerings and left it behind a large temple, I still repay your merit by repainting the statue. Since you are a monk of the Avatamsaka sect, I will teach you a verse as follows: - Weakness in human desires and enlightenment, the three worlds are necessarily Buddhas, the mind is like seeing, the mind creates Tathagatas (if anyone wants to know) clearly, all the Buddhas of the three generations, you should contemplate like this: The mind creates the Tathagatas)”. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught that verse and said: “Reciting that verse can close the gates of hell, can open the wayg to the Pure Land, can communicate with the lives achieved by karma”.

Afterwards, arriving before King Yama, Tang Tuan recited that verse, then entered the city and met King Yama. The king asked: "If you encounter the Dharma in this life, do you have any merit?" Answer: "Only receive and recite a four-line verse." The king said: "Can you recite now?" Said: "I am stupid, careless, unable to cultivate goodness, dedicated to temple work, unable to keep the precepts, only to accept and recite a four-line verse." The king asked: "Can you recite now?" Answered: "I know it by heart", then recited the entire verse above. At that time, wherever the chanting came, the suffering people were liberated. The king said: "Stop! Stop! No need to say anymore, let him return to the human world." Because of that fate, he was resurrected. He told the shaman in the Hoa Nghiem sect, the monk Nghia Hoc. The monk looked up the verses and learned that it was taken from the twelfth volume of the Avatamsaka Sutra, which is the sutra that records the verses spoken when countless Bodhisattvas gathered in the Da Ma heaven. That is Bodhisattva Giac Lam's poem praising Buddha. Monk Tuan often told the monks in the temple. Those who heard it all raised their minds and believed in the Avatamsaka Sutra.

6. Record of inspiration caused by drawing and adapting the Ksitigarbha statue of monk Dinh Phap at Khong Quan Pagoda

During the Song Dynasty, monk Thich Dinh Phap of Khong Quan Pagoda had inspiration by drawing an image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva like Tang Tuan. For that Bodhisattva, the Master devoted his whole heart and sincere reliance. On the first day of each month, the Master draws a representation of the Ksitigarbha statue, worships, makes offerings, and requests to see the Bodhisattva manifest in this life. After three years, [one day] a young monk asked to stay in the temple hallway. When Dinh Phap heard the story, he respectfully left the room to say hello and talk a few words, but suddenly he couldn't see [the young monk] anywhere. Everyone was surprised and asked Dinh Phap: "What did the monk say?" Answer: "The monk said: The wonderful vow has been fulfilled, why is the will so short?" The listeners all said: "You seek to see Ksitigarbha, but do not remember the essence, so why does the Bodhisattva manifest and speak with such short-lived energy?" Dharma Dharma says: 'Having been fulfilled, I will develop Bodhi mind and happily seek the unsurpassed enlightenment.

Indeed, the Master dreamed and saw the Bodhisattva saying: "That monk is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. You prayed to see me appear, but did not develop the Bodhi mind. Therefore, I came to enlighten you. You drew many imitations of me, and will never fall into the three evil realms. If you let go, you will be born in Tushita. Heaven, when the Venerable Maitreya is born, you will be prophesied to become a Buddha. I follow you like a shadow follows the shape, like water follows the shape of the container and has different shapes.". The monk woke up, was grateful, shed tears like rain, immediately removed his robe, bowl, and personal money, created a Bodhisattva statue as tall as a human body, sculpted the statue's beautiful body, and also collected the statues he had drawn and imitated for many years to worship and make offerings.

7. Records of the story of the layman Ly Tin Tu who escaped evil by worshiping Ksitigarbha.

During the Tang Dynasty, layman Ly Tin Tu was from Lo Thuy. The men and women in his house were all harassed and harmed by evil spirits. Thirty or so people suddenly lay limp in pain, either spitting out blood, or most of them fainted. At that time, Tin Tu was worried and sad and asked the Sangha how to rescue him. The monk thought for a long time and said: "Once upon a time, when the Tathagata was in the world, at the foot of Vipula mountain in the country of Magadha, in the wealthy Kieu De family, the wealthy Kieu De family was also afflicted by evil spirits and lost their vital energy. All five hundred people in that family fainted and did not wake up for ten days. At that time, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva traveled all over the world, came to the wealthy family's house, had great compassion, and recited the mantra to save him. In an instant After a while, everything will be cleansed. You should do it that way, take refuge in Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha, and single-mindedly recite the name.". At that time, Tin Tu happily followed suit and painted a Bodhisattva statue. Since then, Lo Thuy district has been free from the fear of disease for fifty years. That sacred statue still exists.

8. Record of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's inspiration to save sentient beings in hell at Khai Thien Pagoda

During the Tang Dynasty, Khai Thien Pagoda in Chung Son had a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva three meters high, with light surrounding a body four meters and five inches wide. Because it has been many years, we do not know who created the statue. Later, the Admiral of Duong Chau, Dang Tong, at the age of sixty-one, suffered from a mild illness and died. Because the heart is still warm, [family members] have not yet been buried. After a day and night, he came back to life, sad and crying without saying anything. He ordered his children and grandchildren to help him to Khai Thien Pagoda and told the monks: "In this pagoda there is a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva about three meters high, with a light of four meters and five meters. inch or not? I want to worship and make offerings." The monks did not know where it was, so they followed what Dang Tong said, searched among the holy statues, and found the statue exactly as told. Deng Tong paid his respects, but the White Monk wanted to request that statue. The monk asked him what he cherished, he replied:

- When I died, I saw a fourth-rank mandarin dragging me to the door of a large citadel. Suddenly shocked, the official entered the city, then came out and said: "You can come to the front of the hall." I immediately went before the king. The king said: "You cannot die. Because you take serving Buddhism as your inheritance, you should return to the human world soon, but the underworld is scary, people do not know. Do you want to see hell or not?" Answer: "I want to see." The king immediately ordered a green-shirted mandarin to take him to see: "You lead Dang Tong into hell and show him the appearance of the execution tools." I followed the official out of the city. About five or six miles to the Northeast, there is a large iron citadel. The [official] opened the closed iron door. Gradually approaching, I saw a fierce fire shining in the city, the fire seemed to be burning. Hundreds of thousands of sinners suffer there. At that time, a monk entered the prison, controlled the evil fire, taught and cajoled the sinners, and the fire temporarily extinguished.

Move forward again to an iron citadel, eighteen hells in it. The state of suffering cannot be fully described. [Again, I saw] the monk admonishing the sinners there as before. I went to see each place and then returned. The monk returned from hell and asked: "Do you know who I am?" Answer: "I don't know". The monk said: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva at Khai Thien pagoda. Once upon a time there was a monk named Tri Tang. His disciple was the monk Tri Man. In order to save sentient beings suffering in the three paths, he carved a statue of me. I followed the monk's request and, every day at a time, I entered the eighteen hells and countless sub-hells, teaching and advising. Those who had planted good roots in the past, their good force was quite strong, as soon as they raised their mind, they were immediately freed. Next, those with weaker good powers only plant the weak roots of good, even those who have broken good roots and wrong views, will not know or know, and will not have the mind to escape suffering. If they are weak in the human world, if someone falls into the evil destinies, the holy power cannot save them, because they are as inert as those who are not enlightened, waiting until they escape "If you are a person [with good roots] who is a little strong, when you first enter the [evil destinies], you will be able to repent by obeying the Dharma and escape the suffering of hell. Please return to the human world soon and announce this matter." Therefore, I raised my eyes to admire the monk, [seeing him] three meters high, with radiant light surrounding his body. The monk immediately gave him two verses as follows:

Weaknesses in the human world can cultivate the Way,

The chandis with the upper mind can develop,

If you enter the evil destinies, your karma will mature,

The mind is indifferent and cannot be saved.

As human aging progresses,

Weakness and flexibility,

Weaknesses: immobility, inadequate power,

Sentient beings are surprised by their karma.

(If in the human world it is easy to cultivate the Way,

Xiande can still develop the mind,

If you follow an evil destinies, your karma will ripen,

An indifferent mind cannot be saved.

Like an old and weak person wanting to go on the road,

If your legs move, you can help them walk,

If you lie motionless, you won't be able to help

The same is true for living beings who determine their karma).

After saying the verse, suddenly I couldn't see it anymore! While I was dreaming, I remembered that story well. Afraid of not knowing whether it was real or not, I didn't tell anyone else. Now I see this statue, exactly the same as I saw it. Because of that cause and effect, I wanted to request it." After listening, the monk happily said: "How wonderful! Believing in the heart and feeling of a saint's prophet. I can only draw and adapt it, I can't ask for it!” He then trusted a skilled craftsman to sculpt an imitation and left the old statue there.

9. Record of the impact of the Ksitigarbha statue on the head of the staff at the house of the Dang family mandarin in Jianzhou during the Tang Dynasty

During the Tang Dynasty, in Jinshui district of Jianzhou, there was a mandarin with the surname Dang. He saw on the side of the road a broken stick, carved with the image of a monk. He did not know what kind of statue it was. The maid originally believed in Buddha, so she took it home, put it on the wall, respected it, and then left, not remembering it anymore. Three years later, he suddenly fell ill and died, his chest was still warm, his family was suspicious and did not bury him. After a day and night, he came back to life and said with tears in his eyes:

- When I first died, two men riding horses from the underworld chased me to the door of a large citadel. They got off their horses and dragged me into the city. Arriving in front of the king's hall, he saw hundreds of thousands of people in shackles in the yard. The king is angry and wants to reprimand me. At that time, a monk with an ugly appearance, like a ghost, came to the front of the hall. The king saw from afar, respectfully, stood up from the throne, clasped his hands, knelt down, and said: "Great saint! Why did you suddenly come here?" The monk said: "The maid is my benefactor. Because you want to repay your kindness, you should grant me amnesty." The king replied: "The karma has been decided, both life and fortune are gone, this is difficult to do." The monk said: "Once upon a time, in the Good Dharma Hall of the Thirty-Third Heavens, I was entrusted by the Buddha to be able to save evil sentient beings with fixed karma. Isn't it just now that I can do that? What's more, the maid hasn't committed a serious crime, so shouldn't she help?" The king said: "The great man vows, solid and immovable, like a diamond mountain, to release him to the human world. Because his fortune has ended, I give him a red bean."

The monk was happy, held his wife's hand, and led him onto the path of life. When about to say goodbye, the maid asked the monk: "Please wait a moment. Who are you to save me?" The monk replied: "Don't you know? I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Once upon a time, in the human world, you saw my statue on the side of the road without realizing it. You took it home and put it in the wall. It was because a child was playing around with carving the tip of a stick to make a statue, only the head and face were carved, without any other features, so the appearance was ugly. Can you remember?" After saying those words, suddenly I was nowhere to be found!

After waking up, the maid saw the statue on a stick in the corner of the wall in the house. The stick was broken in the middle, so he carved and modified it, using sandalwood to join it, creating a statue five inches high. At that time, the statue emitted light, illuminating the whole house. The maid created a statue as large as a human body, placed a small statue inside, turned the house into a pagoda, and named it Ksitigarbha. People from near and far came to admire it in large numbers! Ksitigarbha's teachings create inconceivable benefits!

10. Records of the story of monk Thich Phap Thuong at Hue Nhat Pagoda in Huazhou during the Tang Dynasty received sympathy from Ksitigarbha

Monk Thich Phap Thuong at Hue Nhat pagoda, ordained at the age of thirty-seven. In the past, when he was still at home, he used to go hunting. Going to the forest to play, I saw a few rays of light shining out in the bushes outside the wild forest. I was surprised, so I tied my horse and went in to look for it myself. I only saw a piece of rotten wood more than a meter long, so I took it home and put it in the house. The next day, he saw that the grove of trees was still shining like before, so he used his spear to wipe away all the bushes, there was absolutely nothing. He was surprised and returned. The next time I went hunting, I thought that the last time the grove of trees emitted the same light as before. My mind was surprised, I put the rotten core of wood on the tree stump and returned. On the way, he encountered a herd of tigers. He spurred his horse to chase and shoot. The bowstring was broken, and when I touched the bowstring bag, there was no string to replace. The tiger turned back to chase. He ran away in fear, his horse bucked, causing him to fall off the horse. He thought to himself that he would probably be chewed by a tiger. He was lost as if in a dream and saw a person like a monk coming to chase away an angry tiger. He asked: “Who are you?” Answer: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. You were in the grove and saw that the rotten piece of wood was my body. Your great-grandfather built a temple and carved a statue of me there. The temple was in ruins, my statue was rotten, only the wooden core remained. You are my great-grandson and saw my light, so now I save you."

After a while, he woke up and saw a horse neighing [nearby]. The tiger is nowhere to be found. He deeply repented himself, so he built a monastery at the place where the light shined before. From a block of rotten wood covered in mud, he carved a statue of Ksitigarbha, followed by a dharma lamp, [building a pagoda] called Hue Nhat Monastery. When Phap Thuong was seventy-eight years old, on the twenty-fourth day of the second month of that year, the Master told his companions:

- Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva came to my house and said: "You are the one who will attain enlightenment in the second assembly of the three Dharma teaching assembly of Tu Thi Tathagata. Today, when he gives up his life, he will immediately be born in Dao Loi". I told the Great Master: "The realm of the five desires in heaven is incomparably happy, I have lost my Bodhi mind. If I want to meet the Buddha again in the future, it will still be a long time. I only wish to be born in the Western world of Peace and Bliss." The Bodhisattva replied: "According to your wishes. If you want to be reborn in the Pure Land, you should recite Amitābha Buddha for one day and one night, concentrate on reciting Buddha's name, and immediately be reborn". I followed that teaching, starting from yesterday, specializing in reciting the Buddha's name in the West, and now I am reborn in the Pure Land.

After speaking, the Master clasped his hands facing the West and passed away. Those who saw it said it was a rare auspicious omen. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva released light [to guide him] to the Pure Land.

11. Sympathetic story of creating a Ksitigarbha statue to save the mother of Tran Do Doc's daughter

During the Tang Dynasty, the youngest daughter (name lost) of the Tran admiral lost her mother at a young age, day and night she loved her but could not see her. The Admiral advised: "Dad is also your relative. Even though your mother has passed away, your father is still alive. Why don't you care about eating and drinking and want to seek your own death? If you remember your deceased mother, you should create a holy statue of Ksitigarbha to pray for relief from her suffering." She immediately spent five hundred dong, hired a craftsman to respectfully carve the statue three meters high, and took the statue to her father's house. The girl told her father: "I just want to put the statue where my mother was before. If I want to see my mother, I will immediately see this statue." Father felt pity and ordered the bedroom to be removed to place that statue. The girl worshiped, made offerings, and prayed to save her mother's suffering day and night. Dreaming of a monk telling Ms. Tran: "Your mother is in Tieu Heat hell. When I was a woman, my father's name was Thi La Thien Hien, my mother's name was Duyet De Loi. Looking for the place where my mother was born, seeing that she was suffering, I developed the Bodhi mind to help sentient beings. I was moved by your filial heart. I personally went to hell and preached the Dharma with light. Your mother was freed from suffering and was born in Dao Loi heaven." The girl named Tran saw the monk's clothes burning and asked the reason. The monk replied: "When going to hell, fierce fire burns out." The girl named Tran woke up, uncontrollably sad and happy! People in the house gathered and saw the statue's clothes changing color as if it had been burned, and they all complained about how rare it was! Listeners recounted that many stars painted that statue to save their parents' suffering.

12. Records of the story of a girl named Truong in Duong Chau obeying her mother's instructions and carving a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to save her mother's suffering

Miss Truong was the daughter of Governor Duong Chau Truong Kien Tin. After her mother passed away, she was warned by her mother in a dream: "For the sake of raising my child, my mother indulged in excessive greed and pride. Therefore, the feeling of becoming a hungry ghost is unbearable!" The girl asked about her miserable condition. The mother replied: "I am a child of a demon, living and dying day and night [many times]. Why is that? The retribution of hungry ghosts is mostly to eat their own children, and as soon as they are born, they eat them. Seeing my birth mother is like seeing a great devil; but in every month of the human world, there is one day that cannot eat me. That was the twenty-fourth day of the month, early in the morning a monk entered the city, giving food until it was full. Other days cannot avoid this suffering. On that day, the monk chanted. that: ‘I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, now entering the hungry ghost city, you should develop the Bodhi mind'. Although you are bound by karma, you cannot develop the mind to eat enough for your mother. You should create a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. After her mother said those words, the girl woke up from her dream and used all her mother's assets to create a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as tall as a human body. She dreamed again of her mother, her body radiating light, standing in the void, saying: "I will soon be born in heaven thanks to your merit and virtue. Use your heart to reverently worship and make offerings, and in the future we will [meet] together at the place of Tu Thi Bodhisattva, together we will see the Buddha and hear the Dharma." She woke up, feeling extremely sad! Everyone who heard the story came to worship, everyone benefited!

13. The story of the inspiration caused by the painting of Ksitigarbha by Prime Minister Chau Khang Cu Thong

The Emperor of Lo Chau is Khang Cu Thong, a sincere believer who has served Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for many years. He even had the heart to paint a statue of the Bodhisattva. Even though he had not yet colored it, it was already radiant. Therefore, Cu Thong's faith became even stronger and more dedicated. He accidentally dreamed that two soldiers were chasing him on horseback. At that time, Cu Thong could not escape, so he stood trembling in fear. The soldiers dismounted and said: "We were wrong! You are Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's harp. My king will not besiege Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's harp!" Having finished speaking, he disappeared. He woke up from his dream, worshiped even more deeply, worshiped, and made offerings.

In the first year of Quang Minh (880) under the reign of Emperor Duong Hy Tong (Ly Huyen), demons rose up to riot, there was a plague in the country, the dead piled up like a mountain. Cu Thong dreamed of hundreds of thousands of green demons passing through his door and said: "This house is the home of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. We, our subordinates, should be careful and do not enter the door." He woke up very happy, the whole family was free from evil.

During the Trung Hoa era[67], he had to go far away, encountered heavy snow on the way, and got lost. [So] chanting Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, suddenly I saw a parrot jumping on the snow. He was surprised, followed it, and soon found the right path. That is the Bodhisattva's touch. By the reign of Quang Khai, he was eighty-seven years old, suffered from a mild illness, and sincerely prayed for recovery. In the dream, a young monk said: "You killed a green goose[68], deserving of hell, now let you repay that karma, only suffer a little for a day or two. After tomorrow, you will be born in the Pure Land." After hearing this, he immediately woke up, joyfully worshiped, and his illness was completely cured. On that day, his illness was completely cured, and he passed away mindfully.

14. Records of the miracle caused by the creation of a three-inch tall statue of Ksitigarbha made of sandalwood by mandarin Biet Gia Kien Khat in Ung Chau

During the Tang Dynasty, the king of the Buddha[69] Sustained Thirsting for a pure mind, wholeheartedly believing in and serving the Buddha Dharma. One day, he asked the Sangha: "Which Buddha or Bodhisattva should lay people worship?" Each monk spoke differently, [some said]: "We should worship Avalokiteshvara because He is the Fearless Giver in the Sa Ba world." Or say: "Worship the Medicine Buddha because he vows to benefit [living beings] in this world." Or say: "Worshiping Maitreya is worshiping the Teacher." Or say: "Worship Ksitigarbha, because he has accepted Buddha's decree." Kien Khat thought to himself: "We should worship Ksitigarbha, because he has received the Buddha's decree, should he abandon us?" Immediately find sandalwood, create a three-inch tall statue, tuck it in a bun, walk, stand, lie down, sit, and recite the name. During the Thien Thanh era of the Tang Dynasty (Ly Ton Huc), the world was in war and chaos. Kien Khat was surrounded by enemy troops, he didn't know where to hide, and in a moment he would die. As soon as he thought of the Ksitigarbha statue he was carrying [in his bun], the general who was leading the cavalry suddenly panicked, sheathed his sword, and told his comrades: "We are besieging Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, should we make the mistake of destroying the sages?", and immediately ran away. Kien Khat said it was a rare thing. After calming the chaos, he asked the monks about this cause and effect, and everyone who heard them complained. During Truong Hung's reign[70], when he arrived at his office, the enemy heard the news, attempted to harm him, and hid and waited by the dangerous roadside. He only saw a monk passing by, but did not see Kien Khat. Later, when I heard he had passed, I apologized, said goodbye, and let go of my resentment. One time on the way, the night he slept in a motel, it rained heavily and all the lights went out. The statue of the saint in a bun of hair shines, illuminating the night as clearly as day. Suddenly there was a soft sound like a child's voice saying: "Leave soon, leave soon!" He was horrified, followed the guiding light, and went to spend the night elsewhere. The next day, the flood surged, the place where he was staying before was flooded, it was unknown how deep it sank. He said to himself: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva saves and protects." In the second year of Thanh Thai (935), he passed away at the age of seventy-eight. When dying, the statue in the bun radiates light. He clasped his hands and recited Buddha's name as he passed away. That light shined straight into the sky for a moment. Everyone said that when the light sent Kien Khat away, he would definitely be born in heaven!

15. Record of the story of Ksitigarbha's induction by Admiral Truong An Thoi Ly He of the Song Dynasty

Cui Ly He is Admiral Truong An, younger brother of Minister Thoi Long. In the second year of Khai Bao (969), he died for two days and then came back to life, telling the following story in the underworld:

- When I first died, two people carried me under my arms. I saw a good ghost in the shape of a white horse chasing me for several miles, arriving at a large citadel in the Northeast. Entering from the black door in the South, you will see the East, entering from the black door in the West, you will see the South gate. Following the black door in the North to enter the city, you will see a dozen tiled houses. Each apartment has a dozen rooms. In there, there are thousands of painted pillars and the crowns of the mandarins are all black. On both sides of the tiled house there are more than thirty servants, all saying: "I am [a subordinate of] the military palace." Go to the southwest again, more than fifty steps, there are more than fifty houses. Ly He came before the military palace, the military palace asked: "What do you serve?" Ly He replied: "I serve Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and make offerings to the monks." The palace army said again: "You have worshiped the great saint, that is a blessing from heaven." Then he asked the minor servants: "Is this person's life over yet?" The army immediately took a book to read for himself and told Ly He: "Your life is not over yet, thanks to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to save and protect you." Calling the low-ranking servants again, they shouted: "Why are you taking the lives of people from the Buddha family?" Immediately reprimanded the prisoner in the shape of a white horse and sentenced him to be tied to a post for one day. Asked again: "Do you want to go home or not?" Answer: "Yes, I want to". Asked again: "Do you want to see the underworld?" Answer: "I want to see". The military palace gave him a horse, and sent two servants to lead him away. Going out from the Northeast, about five or six miles, we saw a large iron citadel, several dozen miles square. There is an iron house, filled with boiling liquid iron water, blazing with fire. Next, we came to a tile-roofed house using iron as a door. The official of the underworld opened the door and told him to look and saw that his grandfather, great-grandfather, etc. were all in that city, all with shackles, shackles, and chains binding their bodies. Fierce fire plays around the body, burning, the body is burned and cracked. When they saw Ly He, they shed tears and said, "You should help." Ly He said: "You should recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva".

Going forward, you see a citadel with a bed, court, and bed made of hot iron. The monks he had met before were sitting there, their bodies like coals, the fierce fire shining brightly. He asked: "Master, you practice holy life, why is it like this now?" The monk replied: "For the sake of fame and profit, we practice holy conduct. Because our inner and outer conducts do not correspond, the sleeping tools, beds, chairs, etc. that we received in the past have now turned into huge instruments of execution. Clothes, food, etc. have turned into iron clothes and boiling copper water. Please save us." He replied: "You should recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva." He saw dozens of hells, each filled with tortured sinners, all of whom he had met in life. Come to the red sand prison, there are trees full of swords, bronze pillars, hundreds of thousands of sinners up there. When they saw Ly He, they all shed tears and said, "Please save us." Answer: "You should often recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name." The seven prisons of yellow sand, white sand, burning sand, etc. are all the same as seen. He then returned.

I saw a glittering green tiled house, with precious trees and various fruits alternating on both sides of the road. Immediately asking the two monks again, they replied: "Among the disciples of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, who still paint statues, most of them are born in the Pure Land, or are born in the Tusita heaven, everyone has their wish fulfilled. Those who do not believe in painting statues, but serve, mostly stay here." Therefore, he entered and saw that in the large citadel, there was a large treasure palace. Hundreds of millions of men and women play in it. Again, I saw my parents, relatives, etc. happily greeting me. The men and women said: "Previously, we were in hell. Thanks to you, thanks to you who taught us how to chant Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, we were able to escape suffering and be born in this great hall!" My parents, brothers, and six relatives happily told me: "Thanks to your kindness, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva taught me and left suffering to be born here." He asked again: "Where is this place?" Answer: "This place is called a blessed abode, with a long life span and separation from all kinds of suffering. Even though one is born here, one will certainly meet the three councils of Maitreya Buddha and end all sufferings." Ly He asked which realm? They said: "Once upon a time, when Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva was in the world, he accepted the Tathagata's blessing and told the Buddha: 'I will definitely not let the four disciples fall into the evil destinies.' Before Maitreya Buddha appeared, the interval between the two Buddhas was fifty-six billion seven thousand ten thousand years. If there were sentient beings who wished to be born in the Pure Land and the Four Heavens, those with less merit would come to this merit, and would not return to the evil destinies until they became Buddhas. just new". He returned to the military headquarters, and the king immediately sent two people up there to take him back to his hometown.

16. Records of the story of the inspiration to create a Ksitigarbha statue by Ich Chau's First Minister, Quach Tu An

During the Great Han Dynasty, the Governor of Ich Chau, Quach Tu An, did not believe in the Three Jewels and especially respected Lao Tzu. In the middle of the leap year of the third year of Qianhuu (950)[71], he contracted an illness and was treated with all sorts of things that did not cure him. His wife worshiped Buddha, looking for a happy day, she said: "You can make a vow to create a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in one day to cure your illness, don't delay!" Tu An lay on the hospital bed, still not believing, saying: "Do I need to make a vow? If I have sympathy, I will believe immediately." One day, he suddenly fainted. The wife raised her face to the sky, cried, shed tears, her heart was broken, praying to the gods to help him come back to life. After three sessions (six hours), Tu An regained consciousness, threw himself on the ground, demanded a sharp knife, and attempted to cut his tongue. Everyone who saw him thought he was hysterical. His wife comforted him, and he calmed down, saying: "You are a great wise man, you can prolong my life, you can eliminate the suffering of hell, you can give joy to heaven, you can teach the way of liberation." The wife said: "Please tell me the beginning and the end." Tu An burst into tears and said:

- I was sent by the King Yama about seven or eight people, each claiming to be the god of fortune (governing fortune), all riding green horses, flying like the wind. Two people holding bows and arrows, two people holding swords, two people holding sticks, one person holding a rope, chased me northeast, to the door of a large citadel. In the city, there were hundreds of thousands of people, standing on both sides. The official got off his horse and asked the king. The king said: "Why arrest people who have not completed their charity?" The king became angry and ordered him to use an iron rod to punish him. Quan Tu Loc screamed loudly, his clothes were soaked in blood. The king went to the door and told Tu An: "Thanks to your wife, you made a vow to create a statue of the Great Being. I, on the throne, truly in order to make sentient beings pay for their sins, incarnate the King Yama, is actually the king of dharma. If there are sentient beings who take refuge in Ksitigarbha, their wishes will be fulfilled. Please return to the human world soon to complete that vow." The king immediately sent someone to bring him back. Now awakened. My mind does not believe, slanders the great saint, wants to cut out my tongue to repent.

The wife said: "Cutting your tongue is not repentance. If you fall to the ground, you still have to stand up on the ground. You should take refuge with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and repent." He immediately did as his wife said. Create the statue in one day, deeply regret your previous mistake. Every day, he worships and makes offerings, considers it a family tradition, diligently advises the rich and the poor to serve Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

17. Records of the sympathy caused by the creation of the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva by Minister Ba Duyet of Dai Chau Dynasty for his wife

Dai Chau Dynasty[72], Minister Ba Duyet was a mandarin who was awarded by the king to wear a bag embroidered with goldfish, and believed very much in the Three Jewels. His wife died due to childbirth. He wept in pain, practiced merit and dedicated it, created a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as tall as his wife's body, established an association of monks, and poured his heart out to worship and make offerings. He dreamed that his wife was wearing new clean clothes and told Ba Duyet: "I used to be someone else's wife and had no children. My husband often lamented that he had no children. I immediately told my husband to marry me. Not long after, she became pregnant. My husband loved and respected his new wife. I gave birth to another woman, pretended to be close, used delicious food mixed with poison to kill their mother and child. Because of that, I fell into the Vo Gian prison for six lives. Reborn in the human world, because of giving birth, I died fifty-seven years ago. Once, I have always been your wife and endured that great suffering. Now that you have created a holy statue for me, that karma has been destroyed, and you will be born in the Dao Loi heaven, more majestic than before. After being born as the consort of a god, you will forever be in the body of a woman. In that heaven's Good Dharma Hall, on the twenty-fourth day of each month, countless incarnations of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the three thousand great worlds will gather there. everywhere under the Vo Uu tree, preaching the Dharma for the benefit of birth. [Those incarnations] all had the appearance of a golden monk. At one time, he preached the Dharma for me: ‘You and your husband, when you create an image, practice according to the Dharma, and will be freed from the path of suffering'. Ba Duyet woke up, mixed with joy and sadness!

18. Records of monk Hue Tan in the capital chanting the Lotus Sutra to appreciate Ksitigarbha

Thich Hue Tan from Lac Duong, became a monk at a young age, sought Dharma in other countries, preached Hien and Mat. In it there is a collection of Dharma Flowers, the text and meaning of which are extremely mysterious. The Master recites it day and night silently, never dissolving or abandoning it. The monk is respected by everyone as a teacher, and is called a magician in the world. During the reign of Hien Duc of the Dai Chau dynasty, there was a novice monk, claiming to be from the Western Regions, who worshiped Hue Tan as his teacher and served as a free servant for three years. Hue Tan was surprised and promised to give him a full life. The novice said: "I respect the person who chants the Lotus Flower, but he cannot become a great monk." After that, Hui Tan stopped reciting the Lotus Sutra and taught the Mahayana Sutra[73]. The novice said to his teacher: "I returned to my country, you changed the way, it's not what I like." Then he disappeared, not knowing where he went. Hue Tan said to himself: "Because I stopped reciting, it became like this. Novice monks did not know how to think deeply and worship reciting. Now I change my practice and eagerly practice the secret dharma, what difference does it make?"

The monk thought about it, and at night he dreamed that the novice was Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva emitting light illuminating Hue Tan. The master was frightened, clasped his hands, and apologized. The Bodhisattva told Hui Tan: "I have a great compassionate vow to help the people of Xiandi. Obeying the Buddha's advice, I will maintain the teachings, guide, and benefit all living beings. The Great Master Thich Ton once lived on Thuu Mountain for eight years preaching the Lotus Sutra. As my guardian, twenty thousand Bodhisattvas such as the Medicine King, etc., all obeyed the teachings, and were personally advised by the Buddha to protect and maintain them. He gave a sincere, solid, and excellent advice: In an impure life, those who temporarily uphold the Lotus Sutra are The most difficult thing. Due to the Master's noble karma of reciting the Dharma Flower, I followed him as a free servant and stopped reciting. Hue Tan shed tears of repentance. Again asked: "Can I leave birth and death?" Answer: "In the Buddha's past, Buddha's present, or after the Buddha's nirvana, if he listens to the Lotus Sutra, he will all attain Buddhahood. Only if the mind is pure or impure, [will leave birth and death] quickly or slowly!" Having finished speaking, suddenly he was nowhere to be seen. The monk woke up, repented, and recited the Lotus Sutra as before.

19. Recorded about the story of a girl in Vi Chau who stayed at Mantra Ksitigarbha's house to educate her.

During the Dai Chau era, at Mr. Dang's house in Vi Chau, there was a niece (name unknown) who lost her mother at a young age, and was raised by her uncle. She missed her mother day and night, asking the monk: "How can I see my mother's face again?" The monk said: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has the original vow of great compassion. If you recite with all your heart, you will see again." She then confessed her name day and night. Later, he told the monk: "Thanks to you, I can see your face again. I respectfully offer a set of clothes." The monk asked questions in detail, and she said: "I dreamed of following a monk and flying up to the sky. I saw a forty-nine-storey mani palace filled with deities. Mother was among the people outside. I went to the place, bowed and asked questions. Mother said: 'I recited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, brought me to this heaven, and met you again, it was personally arranged by the Holy One'. I immediately woke up, my mind had no thoughts. It's inconceivable that such a profound connection is thanks to the teacher! The monk was filled with joy and said: "If it weren't for my own deep faith, I wouldn't have been able to have that transformation." I heard it personally and wrote it down.

20. Records of the story of Nhan Hung in Kinh Chau, thanks to the merit of taking refuge in Ksitigarbha, he escaped the suffering of hell

During the Five Dynasties period, in Kinh Chau, there was a man who lived by hunting swallows, famous throughout the world, called Nhan Hung. At the age of fifty-one, he died from miasma and his wife left his body in a grave to raise tigers and wolves. Three days later, he came back to life and returned to his old home. His wife and children were frightened and thought he had turned into a crazy ghost. Nhan Hung told in detail:

- When I died, a fiery car came to pick me up and was burned by fierce fire. There was a monk who used water to pour water on his car. The fire goes out, the body cools down, and a rare thought arises! Next, go to the king (King Yama). Pigs, goats, chickens, pheasants, thousands of animals came to tell the king: "He took my life, please punish Nhan Hung for his crime." The Great King replied: "You have denounced, Nhan Hung must be an evil person. Only his ancestors took refuge in Ksitigarbha, and their descendants will be freed from burning suffering." Nhan Hung saw that situation and single-mindedly proclaimed the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Birds and animals in the temple all turned into human shapes. The king immediately released me. Therefore, be resurrected.

21. Record of the story of the child using his fingernail to draw a picture of Ksitigarbha and gaining longevity

During the Song Dynasty, monk Thich Hue On of Khai Bao pagoda raised a boy, whose name is unknown, just fourteen years old. General Kien Chan looked at it and said: "This child's life is very short, he only has one more month to live!" The Master listened to Kien Chan's words and sent him home. At that time, it was raining heavily and travel was difficult. He slept at a painter's house, saw him drawing a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, so he used his fingernails to imitate him and draw on the wall. When the weather stopped, I went home.

More than a month later, the child returned to Khai Bao pagoda. Hue On was happy and told Kien Chan to talk nonsense. Immediately called Kien Chan to come see the baby. He was surprised and said: "Life expectancy increased by fifty years. This is rare, I don't know why." The child said to himself: "I used my fingernail to draw the image of Ksitigarbha. That night, a monk told me in my sleep: 'You are fifty, fifty'. Praise two or three times like that. Apart from that, do not practice any other good deeds." Hue On and the fortune teller both lamented: "The holy power is inconceivable!" Later, the child became a monk, received the Full Precepts, and was named Dharma Master Hue Tang.

22. Records of the auspicious manifestation of Ksitigarbha in Liaocheng during the Song Dynasty

During the Song Dynasty, in the countryside of Liaocheng, in the past there were more than a thousand houses, recently there were more than two thousand houses, all worshiping Buddha Dharma, and believing in Quan Am and Ksitigarbha. They attach great importance to the Avalokitesvara Sutra, Ksitigarbha Sutra, and Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sūtra. There is an ancient pagoda with three rooms and four wings, green tile roofs, and leaf walls. On both sides are statues of Guan Yin and Ksitigarbha, seven meters and five inches high. In the middle is a statue of Amitābha Buddha, one meter six meters high, often with auspicious premonitions, the statue was created by Dang Do in the past. During the Thai Binh Hung Quoc era of the Song Thai Tong dynasty, epidemics were widespread and many villages died prematurely. The master of the island prayed to the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. The statue radiated light into the village, everyone recovered, and those who had died prematurely were brought back to life. There was a medium who did not believe in Buddhism. She fell ill and died one day before coming back to life. She came to the monastery and paid homage to Ksitigarbha, crying and begging to become a monk. Everyone was surprised and asked why. The psychic said:

- I was bound by the devil. Even though I called the god I worshiped to save me, he saw that the devil had been influenced by the monk, so he left me. At that time, the monk said: "You are a foolish woman, relying on the divine path in vain, not believing in Buddhism. I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in the great temple. At the request of the city lord, I saved you foolish woman. I give you my life to build a temple in the village to directly protect them." I quit my evil mind and no longer control ghosts. Demons are your own karma, not caused by anyone else. Having seen and heard this story, she was able to survive and reform her evil ways, so she asked to become a monk." Everyone who heard this was happy and agreed to let her become a nun.

23. Notes on the sympathy of the Ksitigarbha statue of Thien Phuoc pagoda

During the Song Dynasty, in the northeast corner of Thien Phuoc Pagoda, there was a statue of Ksitigarbha, one meter six inches high, it is unknown who created it and in what era it appeared. However, legend has it that it is extremely strange. Anyone who comes to ask to stay over for repentance will certainly be understood. At that time, there was a layperson who, at the age of thirty-seven, had no teeth left. He went to the statue, fasted, became pure, and prayed. In the middle of the night, I had a dream and saw a statue rubbing my head, my whole body felt light and happy. Waking up, thirty-eight teeth have grown. People who see and hear strange things, draw imitations of statues to worship, are sympathized.

24. Record of inspiration from the painting Ksitigarbha by nun Tri Tang in Thai Nguyen, Tinh Chau

During the Song Dynasty, nun Tri Tang in Thai Nguyen especially served Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, preferring to seek birth in the Western Pure Land. She spent two hundred dong to paint a statue of Amitābha Buddha, on both sides were painted Ksitigarbha and Avalokiteshvara as attendants, placed in the room, worshiped and made offerings with faith. In the year of Canh Thin (980) in the fifth year of Thai Binh Hung Quoc, a whirlwind blew the house and the nunnery were all damaged. The next day, looking for the statue and not knowing where it was lost, my heart was filled with sadness! She prayed, recited Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name, contemplated the void, and saw in the distance an object floating in the air, radiating several rays of light like lightning. When it fell, it was the statue she was looking for. She was happy and still placed it in the room as before. On the twenty-third day of the second month of the seventh [Thai Binh Hung Quoc] year (982), she told her friends: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva guides me to the Pure Land, tomorrow I will definitely be reborn." She lit incense, scattered flowers, chanted the names of the three monks, each name one hundred and eight times, sat upright facing the West, clasped her hands, and passed away.

25. Record of the strange manifestation of the Ksitigarbha painting on the west wall of Ngoa Quan Pagoda in Kim Thanh

On the west wall of Ngoa Quan pagoda, there is a painting of the holy statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, looking like a middle-aged monk, wearing a brightly colored kasaya. Every day at the beginning of the fifth watch, light is emitted. Out of ten people, only one or two can see it. Recently, a monk from Thien Truc, Hoa Thien, quite miraculously, requested to be inspired by the holy image, to see the full light, saying: "This statue is because in the past, Zen master Tri Khai of Sui country drew this statue in order to save sentient beings who are suffering in the three paths. After hearing this story, more people worshiped and made offerings!

26. Record of the induction of Ksitigarbha by the monk Tri Huu of Thanh Thai pagoda

During the Song Dynasty, the monk Tri Huu was from West India, went to China during the Thien Phuoc era, and stayed at Thanh Thai pagoda. In the sutra that the Master brought with him, there was a statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and a Sanskrit version of the Sutra of the Original Vows of Merit. In that statue, in the middle circle, there is a Bodhisattva statue, on both sides there are ten saintly statues wearing crowns and holding treasures. On the left are five people: One is Qin Quang Vuong, two is So Giang Vuong, three is Song De Vuong, four is Ngu Quan Vuong, and fifth is Diem La Vuong. On the right there are five: One is Bien Thanh Vuong, two is Thai Son Vuong, three is Equal Equality King, four is Do Thi Vuong, fifth is Five Paths Turning the Wheel. Each of them has [subordinates] such as private life, private fortune, military palace, dignitary, etc. The monk himself said dependent origination as follows:

- Once upon a time, in West India, there was a compassionate Bodhisattva who saved the world and made a great vow. In order to save sentient beings suffering in the three paths, he drew a statue of Ksitigarbha, facing the ten royal cities, teaching: "Now I vow to save the suffering of the three paths, please create benefits." The ten kings all clasped their hands together, respectfully responded, and said to the painted statue: "All sentient beings hope to be taught by the great saint. We respectfully act as companions and assistants." At that time, the statue smiled and said: "How good! The sins of sentient beings will soon be alleviated." Immediately magnify the light, illuminating the three sufferings. All sentient beings who are illuminated will end their suffering. That is the Bodhisattva in India who entered the Samadhi of Benefiting Living Beings, asking the great kings to bestow great benefits. That Bodhisattva himself drew what he saw, so he painted ten more kings next to the statue of Ksitigarbha.

Mr. Tri Huu said again:

- I was in Luu Sa, encountered demonic demons, so I prayed and recited Bodhisattva's name, so Bodhisattva held a staff to chase them away. Again at night, when heavy rain poured down, miserable because there was no light, I didn't know what to do, fierce beasts roared, both people and horses lost their way. This statue radiated light as bright as day, the fierce beasts fled, and the path was clear again. Again, I encountered a big river, the waves were rolling, I didn't know how deep it was. That water is very weak, it cannot support a leaf, let alone a boat? I prayed to the holy image and immediately saw a monk and two disciples, one holding a phan, the other rowing a boat. The monk held a Sanskrit sutra in his hand and immediately took us across the river. Having arrived at the East Coast, when he was about to say goodbye, he gave me a Sanskrit sutra book, telling the Sangha that the customs in this world could be copied. Therefore, everyone scrambled to copy it, feeling many strange things.

Three years later, without knowing where Tri Huu and the statue were, everyone suspected he had returned to India. Surely the monk Tri Huu is the reincarnation of Ksitigarbha.

27. Record of the story of the fisherman in Minh Chau feeling the Buddha Ksitigarbha

Fishermen in Minh Chau, I don't know their names, go to the sea to catch fish. In the net, a statue resembling a monk was caught. Not knowing the reason, he left it on the shore. At night, I dreamed of a monk with a bright body, telling the fisherman: "Why did you leave me?" The fisherman said: “Who are you?” Answer: "I am Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva who has been in the ocean for a long time, saving the water tribe, half of whom were born in heaven. Now for you, I sacrifice myself in the net." That person woke up, repented, built a monastery, and established that image. The fishermen there still worship to this day, and the relief they receive is endless!

28. Record of sympathy by Tran Kien in Taizhou for his parents creating a statue of Ksitigarbha

Tran Kien in Taizhou is always upright and filial, surpassing others. He built a house to raise his parents, and for his parents created two statues of Ksitigarbha and Guan Yin, each three meters high. In the fourth year of Can Duc (966), he suffered from a mild illness and suddenly fainted. Parents cried. Four hours later, he woke up, worshiped his parents, and said:

- A child dies and leaves behind his parents, not yet fully filial. Suddenly arriving in front of the Palace of King Yama, I saw two statues that I had made, standing in the palace. The king headed there to worship. Seeing his son coming, the king took the hands of the two Bodhisattva statues to support his waist and led him up to the hall. The statue said in a gentle voice: "Dan-Viet has not satisfied his filial piety, please let your king release him back to the human world." The king said to the statue: "This man's karmic life is over, his parents' lives are long." The statue said: "The lifespan is uncertain, depending on the conditions, it can change and change. If Dan-Viet cultivates good karma, why won't he return?" The king checked a book and said: "If anyone is filial and creates or paints a statue, his life will be long. You can increase your lifespan by forty years, twenty years of filial piety, twenty years later you will be repaid by your filial son." An official wearing a green shirt opened the book and told the king: "Mr. Kien's son only lives ten years, who will be filial?" The King said: "The King of Dharma does not say two words. Please increase the life span of your child." After hearing those words, I woke up.

Everyone who heard the story complained that it was "unprecedented"!

29. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva wears a straw hat (Japanese legend)

Cao Ngoc My writes

A long time ago, there was an old couple living in a certain place. Due to extreme poverty, every day we have to live very hard. One year, on Tru Tich day (thirtieth day of Tet), the old man lamented to the old woman: "Oh! Although tomorrow is the first day of Tet, we have no way to prepare banh day (mochi)[74]!" “That's right!” "If there is something that can be exchanged for thick cake, that's fine." As the old man spoke, he searched around the house, but couldn't find anything! “Is it really nothing?” The old lady asked, suddenly going to the storage room to take a look. In a corner of the storage room, there is still a pile of grass cut from the summer. "Old man! Take that grass and weave it into a straw hat. If you take it into the city, you can exchange it for money!" "Oh! Oh! That's fine." Therefore, the two old men went into the storage room, tidied up the messy pile of grass, and seriously began braiding the grass into straw hats. After finishing the work, the old man took it and said: "I will exchange it for money, I will buy a lot of rice cakes, and also buy radishes and burdock." After speaking, he left.

The bustling Tet market in the city, everywhere is bustling with Tet shoppers. There are shops that sell mortars and pestles to pound [thick cakes], and there are also people who cut pinewood[76] down from the mountains to sell, shouting loudly: "Hey! Do you want to buy pinewood or not? Do you want to use pinewood to decorate or not?" The old man did not give up and loudly announced: "Hey, hey, hey! Here's a straw hat, do you want to buy a straw hat or not?" But no one stopped to buy, so the old man had no choice but to collect all the money and return, [muttering]: "No one buys straw hats on New Year's Eve! Oh! If I don't bring the cake home, I wonder how upset the old lady will be?" Unconsciously, the sky was already dark, the old man bowed his head sadly and walked out of the city, going all the way to the wilderness outside the village. The wind blew and formed a fierce blizzard. Suddenly, the old man saw six statues of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva standing on the side of the road, with nothing to cover their chests, and no trees to block them. In the blizzard-torn wilderness, the statue of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva was half buried by heavy snow.

“Oh! How pitiful, it must be so cold!” The old man brushed the snow off the head of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's head: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's cheeks are both frozen, why is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's nose hanging down with a stick of ice like this?" The old man stroked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's cold and wet back. “Then let's get a straw hat and put it on them!” The old man took a straw hat and placed it on the head of each Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva statue, and also tied the [hat strap] tightly under the chin to prevent the wind from blowing it away. But there are six statues of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and only five straw hats, so it is impossible to wear one statue. “Even though my handkerchief isn't great, it can still withstand the wind and snow!” The old man took his own patched handkerchief and covered the head of the last Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva statue. “That's okay, that's okay.” After that, he felt secure and returned home. "Old lady! Old lady! I'm home!" "Ah! That old man! Must be very cold? Have you sold all your straw hats yet?" “It can be said that it is all sold!” He told the story of seeing Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva buried in snow on the road. “So I put straw hats on everyone!” After listening, the old woman not only did not show an annoyed expression, but also said: "That's right! You have done some good things. I think Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva must be very cold too! Hey! Old man, quickly come to the warm bed!" The old man immediately sat on the bed and warmed his ice-cold body!

“Hmm! Finally, we have to spend a night in Tru Tich without rice cake. If that's the case, then I'll imitate the person pounding rice cake." After the old man finished speaking, he pretended to be pounding rice and sticky rice to make banh day, [as if] pounding a pestle into a mortar by tapping the side of the furnace bed. Therefore, the old lady also laughed. After that, the two of them drank some cooked soup before going to rest. Around midnight, in the snowy night, the sound of a sleigh could be heard. The old man asked: "Old woman! Who is it at this hour? It's probably a young person from nearby who went to carry Tet goods and only came back at this hour." “Probably!” But the sound of the sled did not go anywhere else, but gradually came closer. Listening carefully, someone joined in singing: "Bring straw hats to the six Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, where is the old man's house? Where is the old woman's house?" The old man couldn't help but cry out: "Here, here!"

Then the singing fell silent. Then, there was the sound of something heavy being dropped. The old man propped up the window and saw five Ksitigarbha Bodhisattvas wearing straw hats and one wearing a scarf pulling a sleigh back. Under the eaves are placed sticky rice cakes, corn cakes, wrapped with straw. In addition to those things, there are also bean paste, Burdock, radish, pine wood for decoration, etc. Finally, the old man and woman can celebrate a good new year.

Due to the large number of monks who had fled from mainland China, and disagreements with Mr. Dieu Qua, the Master handed over the academy to the shaman Vien Minh to take over, leading a number of monks to Linh Tuyen Pagoda in Keelung, to join the Linh Tuyen Buddhist Academy. After being released from prison, his life was very difficult. His followers invited him to return to Indonesia, but he could not leave the monkhood. In 1950, at the invitation of Bhikkhunī Huyen Quang of Tinh Tu Zen Monastery, she went there to teach and founded Maitreya Noi Monastery. It was the largest Buddhist Institute in Taiwan at that time. [61] Ma Loi Chi Thien (Marīci), translated as Yang Yan, Dreadful Light, Yang Light, Ma Loi Chi Thien Bodhisattva, Nhat Tien Bodhisattva, Accumulation of Light Bodhisattva, Mother of Light Buddha, Mother of Light Buddha. etc. belong to the Tathagata family in Esoteric Buddhism. He is considered the reincarnation of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, with the original vow to eliminate disasters, increase blessings, and satisfy sentient beings. His statue is often carved in the form of a goddess, with three faces, each face has three eyes, eight arms, standing on a pig, or sitting on three sharp golden pigs. Sometimes it's sitting on a treasure cart pulled by seven sharp golden pigs. In Esoteric Buddhism, he is one of the Da La Three Venerable, i.e. Tara Bodhisattva (Tara, Mother Goddess), Magi Chi Deva, and One-Kyeka Raksha King (Ekajatā-raksha). Master An Quang taught: "Although Ma Loi Chi Thien appears in the form of heaven, he is truly a Bodhisattva. Due to his earnest mind to save suffering, he recites this mantra to be the root of salvation. If one recites this mantra as often as possible every day, the better. Even when encountering disasters like water, fire, swordsmen, etc., evil will turn to good". There are many mantras of Ma Loi Chi Thien, but the one most recited is the mantra: “Namah samanta buddhānām. Om, Marīcī svāhā” (Namo tam man da da dan nan, court, ma loi chi sa ha). Patriarch An Quang further taught: “If you are illiterate, have no memory, and just sincerely recite namo Ma Loi Chi Thien Bodhisattva, the benefits are the same as reciting mantras”.

[62] Truong Tang Dieu (479-?) was a famous painter of the Liang Dynasty, once appointed Vu Lang Vuong Quoc Thi Lang, specializing in managing royal paintings. He has a knack for drawing Buddhist paintings, especially paintings on walls. His way of painting portraits of Buddha, Bodhisattva, and saints has formed a separate school called Truong Gia Dang, which is considered the standard model for Buddhist paintings. His paintings of dragons, birds, flowers, grass, and mountains are also very famous. He painted dragons so vividly that there is a legend: Tang Dieu painted four dragons on the wall of An Lac Pagoda in Kim Lang. When he pointed the eye (drawing the dragon's eyes), two of them flew into the sky. His two children, Thien Qua and Nhu Dong, studied painting with him and were also prominent painters at that time.

Quach Oai was originally a powerful minister of the Later Han Dynasty, achieving many victories, high power, and high positions. When the Han lord Liu Zhiyuan died, his son Liu Chenghuu succeeded the throne. Seeing that the great mandarins held military power too strong, he plotted to kill the great mandarins. The throne must be passed to Quach Oai's adopted son, Sai Vinh, also known as Chau The Tong. Due to constant wars and lack of money, Chau The Tong listened to the taoist's gossip, abolished Buddhism, destroyed pagodas, ordered Buddha statues and bronze bells to be melted down to mint money, creating a dharma disaster for Chinese Buddhism. It was he who ordered the destruction of 30,336 pagodas and sent sixty thousand monks and nuns back to life. In June 959, Chau The Tong died of illness at the age of 38. His son, Sai Tong Huan, was only seven years old when he ascended the throne, becoming Hau Chau Cung Emperor. In less than a year, in January 960, Zhao Kuangyin's Imperial Palace usurped the throne, establishing the Song Dynasty, and the Hau Chau Dynasty perished! Hien Duc is the era name of Sai Vinh.

[74] Mochi is the way the Japanese read the word Binh (cake), this word refers to cakes made of sticky rice or cornstarch. Sticky rice cooked into sticky rice is pounded into a sticky dough like the way Vietnamese people make thick cakes, then shaped into a circle, or use a mold to create the desired shape. Although it can be made and eaten all year round, during Tet, Mochi is a must-have dish. Usually, Mochi is filled with red beans or green beans, and comes in many different shapes. Another type of cake with a similar shape and material is Dangoo, but Dangoo is made of rice flour, while Mochi is made from crushed sticky rice. The type of Mochi commonly used during Tet is called Kinako Mochi. After the cake is made, it is grilled over fire and rolled through a layer of soybean shell powder. On Tet, offerings to ancestors must include two large pieces of cake, stacked on top of each other, with a slice of orange or tangerine on top. Sometimes they also have miso soup cooked with thick slices of cake.

[76] Pine wood is a necessary material mainly for traditional Japanese decoration, called Kadomatsu. This decorative object is often made in pairs and placed in front of the house, symbolizing welcoming ancestors and gods. The pine tree is usually made of pine branches, bamboo and peach or plum blossom branches. The required part is three slanted bamboo tubes of different heights, representing Heaven, Earth, and Humanity, with fresh pine or pine branches placed on both sides. Three bamboo tubes tied with ropes with many tassels. The outside is tied with straw and woven into a basket, sometimes with flowers and leaves, including painted fans. After the full moon day of the first lunar month, the pine tree will be burned.
